items.title: 2022年12月六级第1套 · 长对话 1
items.transcript:
M: How's your dissertation going? I'm proofreading my first draft and will submit it to my professor tomorrow.

W: Oh, I haven't even started writing mine yet, so I'm really worried about finishing by the end of next semester.

M: You mean you haven't even begun yours yet? The final draft is due in five months.

W: Of course I've started it, but I can't get to the writing yet as I haven't found enough resources to use, so I'm still researching the topic.

M: Maybe the problem is the way you're doing your research. I started by talking to my professor about where to look for information, and based on that, I found books in the library and a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet.

W: I've tried all that, but don't have enough to write the dissertation as my department's minimum length is 70 pages. I think the problem is that my topic isn't viable. And honestly, my professor did warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material. But I was so interested in the topic that I didn't let his advice turn me.

M: Well, I suggest you find a new topic. After all, our professors are here to guide us, so it's best to listen to them.

W: In retrospect, I wish I had listened to him, but I didn't. And now I don't want to give up my topic as I've already invested so much time and energy.

M: If you're committed to your current topic, maybe you could make some adjustments rather than abandon it completely. What is your topic?

W: It's "Depictions of Femininity in Folklore from the South of the Country".

M: That's pretty narrow. You could find more material if you made the topic broader, maybe by including other kinds of depictions.

W: Broadening the topic is a great idea, I'll start by including folklore from other regions of the country.

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about her dissertation?

options.text: She hasn't started writing it.
She hasn't decided on a topic.
She is proofreading the first draft.
She is working on the references.

questions.shortExplanation: W: Oh, I haven't even started writing mine yet, so I'm really worried about finishing by the end of next semester.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） She hasn't started writing it.

【定位】 W: Oh, I haven't even started writing mine yet, so I'm really worried about finishing by the end of next semester.

女：哦，我连写都还没开始呢，所以我真的很担心能不能在下学期末之前完成。

【信号】 被问者的直接应答。男生先问 How's your dissertation going，女生张口第一句 I haven't even started writing mine yet 就是对提问的直接应答，对话题的答案就落在被问者这第一反应上。

【替换】 I haven't even started writing mine yet↔She hasn't started writing it. 去掉 even 的同义压缩

【排除】 B) 偷换概念

She hasn't decided on a topic. 听着也像『没进展』，但女生说的是还没开始写，topic 在后文 I'm still researching the topic 里指『还在查资料』，并非『没定下题目』，属偷换概念。 借⽤原⽂： I'm still researching the topic C) 张冠李戴

She is proofreading the first draft. 里 proofreading the first draft 确在录音中出现，但说这话的是男生 I'm proofreading my first draft，不是女生，张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： I'm proofreading my first draft D) 未提及

She is working on the references. 说她在弄参考文献，意味着正文已近完成，与她『还没动笔』完全矛盾，录音里也没说她在做文献，属未提及。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the man say about his professor?

options.text: He lent many books to the man for reference.
He offered the man advice on resource hunting
He published a lot in a number of reputable journals.
He told the man to be selective when using e-resources.

questions.shortExplanation: M: I started by talking to my professor about where to look for information, and based on that, I found books in the library and a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） He offered the man advice on resource hunting

【定位】 M: I started by talking to my professor about where to look for information, and based on that, I found books in the library and a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet.

男：我一开始是去找我教授聊该上哪儿找资料，在这个基础上，我在图书馆找到了书，还在网上找到很多有声望的期刊文章。

【信号】 经过句里的求助动作。男生回顾自己怎么做研究，关键在 I started by talking to my professor about where to look for information——他教授给的正是『去哪找资料』的指点，这句叙述里藏着教授的作为。

【替换】 talking to my professor about where to look for information↔ He offered the man advice on resource hunting

把『聊去哪找资料』概括为『给找资料建议』

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

He lent many books to the man for reference. 里 books 确在录音出现，但 I found books in the library 是男生自己在图书馆找到的书，不是教授借给他的，原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： I found books in the library C) 原词陷阱

He published a lot in a number of reputable journals. 用了原词 reputable journal，但 a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet 说的是男生在网上找到这些文章来读，而非教授在期刊上发表论文，原词陷阱兼无中生有。 借⽤原⽂： a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet D) 未提及

He told the man to be selective when using e-resources. 说教授叮嘱『用电子资源要有选择』，但录音里教授只指点了去哪找，从未提『要挑着用』，selective 是未提及。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about her professor?

options.text: He didn't think her dissertation topic viable.
He wasn't interested in her dissertation topic.
He didn't want her to rush through her dissertation.
He wasn't specific about the length of her dissertation.

questions.shortExplanation: W: And honestly, my professor did warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material. 女：说实话，我教授一开始就警告过我，我可能找不到足够的材料。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） He didn't think her dissertation topic viable.

【定位】 W: And honestly, my professor did warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material. 女：说实话，我教授一开始就警告过我，我可能找不到足够的材料。

【信号】 引述动词 warn 引出原话。女生用 my professor did warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material 转述教授当初的警告，引述动词 warn 后面那句就是教授的态度，是答案句。

【替换】 warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material↔ He didn't think her dissertation topic viable. 『找不到材料』即『选题不可行』

【排除】 B) 张冠李戴

He wasn't interested in her dissertation topic. 把 interested 安在教授身上，但录音里 I was so interested in the topic 说有兴趣的是女生自己，教授只是警告找不到料，张冠李戴又偷换。 借⽤原⽂： I was so interested in the topic

C) 未提及

He didn't want her to rush through her dissertation. 说教授不想她赶工，但教授只警告材料不够，从没说过快慢、赶不赶的事，未提及。

D) 原词陷阱 He wasn't specific about the length of her dissertation. 提到 length，录音里 length 出现在 my department's minimum length is 70 pages，那是系里的规定，与教授说没说清篇幅无关，原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： my department's minimum length is 70 pages
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What do we learn the woman will do to complete her dissertation?

options.text: Change her research methodology.
Narrow down her dissertation topic.
Consult her professor more.
Follow the man's advice.

questions.shortExplanation: W: Broadening the topic is a great idea, I'll start by including folklore from other regions of the country.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Follow the man's advice.

【定位】 W: Broadening the topic is a great idea, I'll start by including folklore from other regions of the country.

女：把题目扩大是个好主意，我打算先把全国其他地区的民间传说也纳进来。

【信号】 结尾采纳建议的应答。男生上一句建议 You could find more material if you made the topic broader，女生末句 Broadening the topic is a great idea 当即采纳，结尾这句『接受建议』就是答案句。

【替换】 Broadening the topic is a great idea ↔ Follow the man's advice.

采纳男生提议=照他建议办

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

Change her research methodology. 沾了男生那句 Maybe the problem is the way you're doing your research，但女生最终决定的是扩大题目，并没说要换研究方法，原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： Maybe the problem is the way you're doing your research B) 与原文相反

Narrow down her dissertation topic. 与女生的决定正好相反——男生说题目 That's pretty narrow，建议 made the topic broader，女生要做的是 broaden（扩大）而非 narrow（缩小），与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： That's pretty narrow C) 原词陷阱

Consult her professor more. 里 professor 全程反复出现，诱人选；但女生采纳的是男生当下的建议，并未表示要再去多问教授，原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： our professors are here to guide us

items.title: 2022年12月六级第1套 · 长对话 2
items.transcript:
W: Today, on Book Talk, we are lucky enough to host John Robbins and discuss his new book, Why Americans Are Fat and How We Can Lose Weight. John isn't just a respected writer; he's also one of the rare celebrity authors writing about science today.

M: Thanks for having me, Rebecca, but I'm hardly a celebrity.

W: That's very modest of you to say, considering that your four books have sold a total of seven million copies worldwide, and they've been translated into 12 different languages. What makes people so fascinated with your work?

M: Well, people read my books because more than 60% of Americans are overweight, or obese. And other countries are facing similar problems. Basically, we all want to know how to fix things.

W: We certainly do. I've read your new book, and it's fabulous, especially when it comes to the way you make difficult science easy for laymen to understand. That's no small achievement.

M: I'm glad to hear you find my work accessible, because I was worried when I wrote it that discussing the science might make the book more suited for a specialist audience. My last book was written primarily for the medical community. But this time, I want to help ordinary people take control of their weight.

W: And how do you suggest they do that? Can you give us the basics of your advice for people who want to lose weight?

M: Briefly, I argue that every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body's needs. I don't advocate one single diet. Some people should eat more carbohydrates than others. And different people need different amounts of protein and fat.

W: But you do have some recommendations for everyone, including eating ten servings of vegetables and three of fruit a day. We'll talk about those recommendations next, but now we need to take a short break for a message from our sponsor.

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about the man in her introduction?

options.text: He has translated 12 books.
He is a well-known nutritionist.
His books sell well worldwide.
His latest book sold a million copies.

questions.shortExplanation: That's very modest of you to say, considering that your four books have sold a total of seven million copies worldwide, and they've been translated into 12 different languages.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） His books sell well worldwide.

【定位】 That's very modest of you to say, considering that your four books have sold a total of seven million copies worldwide, and they've been translated into 12 different languages.

您这么说太谦虚了，毕竟您的四本书在全球总共卖出了七百万册，还被翻译成了 12 种不同的语言。

【信号】 主持人介绍嘉宾的成就陈述句。答案信号是主持人介绍环节里铺陈嘉宾业绩的那句 your four books have sold a total of seven million copies worldwide——访谈开场的 "夸业绩" 句往往就是 introduction 题的答案句。

【替换】 sold a total of seven million copies worldwide↔His books sell well worldwide "全球卖出七百万册" 概括为 "全球畅销"

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱录音说 translated into 12 different languages(译成 12 种语言)，A 却说 He has translated 12 books.(翻译了 12 本书)——盗用了原文数字 12，却把对象从 "语言" 换成 "书"，且作者是 "被翻译" 不是 "去翻译"，听到 12 就选必中招。 借⽤原⽂： translated into 12 different languages B) 未提及

录音介绍他是 a respected writer 和写科学的 celebrity authors，从没说他是 a well-known nutritionist.(知名营养师)。营养师是顺着 "减肥饮食" 话题脑补出来的，原文未提及。

D) 原词陷阱

录音是 your four books have sold a total of seven million copies(四本书合计七百万册)，D 说 His latest book sold a million copies.(最新一本卖了一百万册)——盗用 "百万册级销量" 的语感，却把 "四本合计七百万" 偷换成 "单本一百万"，数字与范围全错。 借⽤原⽂： your four books have sold a total of seven million copies
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What has motivated the man to write his books?

options.text: The desire of Americans to try exotic cuisines.
The demand for information about food safety.
The fact that over half of Americans are overweight.
The fact that science books are difficult to read.

questions.shortExplanation: Well, people read my books because more than 60% of Americans are overweight, or obese. 嗯，人们读我的书，是因为超过 60% 的美国人超重，甚至肥胖。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） The fact that over half of Americans are overweight.

【定位】 Well, people read my books because more than 60% of Americans are overweight, or obese. 嗯，人们读我的书，是因为超过 60% 的美国人超重，甚至肥胖。

【信号】 因果连接词 because 引出原因。答案信号是显性因果词 because：people read my books because more than 60% of Americans are overweight，because 后面那句现象即为写书/读书的动机。

【替换】 more than 60% of Americans are overweight, or obese↔ The fact that over half of Americans are overweight

"超 60%" 等价于 "过半"

【排除】 A) 未提及 The desire of Americans to try exotic cuisines.(想尝异国菜)在整段对话里没有任何对应，纯属话题跑偏的捏造，与减肥饮食主线无关。

B) 未提及

The demand for information about food safety.(对食品安全信息的需求)听上去与饮食沾边，但录音给的动机是 "超重"，从未谈 food safety，属顺着话题脑补的未提及项。

D) 与原文相反

录音里 "科学难懂" 是被作者 make difficult science easy for laymen to understand 克服的难点、是卖点，而非写书动机；D 却把 science books are difficult to read. 说成动机， 盗用了 "difficult science" 的字眼却把作用讲反了。 借⽤原⽂： make difficult science easy for laymen to understand
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: Who does the man say his last book was mainly written for?

options.text: The general public.
Those who are overweight.
Those who want to lose weight.
The medical community.

questions.shortExplanation: My last book was written primarily for the medical community. But this time, I want to help ordinary people take control of their weight. 我上一本书主要是为医学界写的。但这一次，我想帮助普通人掌控自己的体重。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） The medical community.

【定位】 My last book was written primarily for the medical community. But this time, I want to help ordinary people take control of their weight. 我上一本书主要是为医学界写的。但这一次，我想帮助普通人掌控自己的体重。

【信号】 限定词 last + 受众句，并与 "this time" 对照。答案信号是 My last book was written primarily for the medical community 这句明确的 "上一本 written for 谁"，紧接的 But this time 形成 "上一本 vs 这一本" 对照，提醒要选 last 对应的那一群。

【替换】 My last book was written primarily for the medical community↔The medical community

受众原词直接对应

【排除】 A) 张冠李戴

The general public. 对应的是 this time, I want to help ordinary people——那是 "这一本(新书)" 的受众。把 this time 的受众安到 last book 头上，正是没分清两本书的张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： this time, I want to help ordinary people take control of their weight B) 原词陷阱

Those who are overweight. 借了通篇出现的 overweight 一词，但录音从没说哪本书是 "为超重者" 而写；它只是话题词，不是 last book 的受众。 借⽤原⽂： more than 60% of Americans are overweight C) 答非所问

Those who want to lose weight. 贴合全场减肥主题、最顺耳，但录音说 last book 是写给 medical community 的；"想减肥的人" 从未被点名为某本书的受众，是借主题诱选。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the man recommend people do?

options.text: Switch to a vegetarian diet.
Follow a personalized diet.
Adhere to doctors' advice.
Cut carbohydrate intake.

questions.shortExplanation: Briefly, I argue that every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body's needs. I don't advocate one single diet.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Follow a personalized diet.

【定位】 Briefly, I argue that every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body's needs. I don't advocate one single diet.

简单说，我主张每个人都要考虑自己的新陈代谢，吃适合自己身体需求的东西。我不提倡某一种单一的食谱。

【信号】 主张句 I argue + 否定 I don't advocate 立反差。答案信号是主张句 I argue that every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body's needs， 再以 I don't advocate one single diet 否定 "单一食谱"——一立一否，强调的正是 "因人而异"。

【替换】 every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body's needs↔ Follow a personalized diet

"按各自身体需求吃" 概括为 "个性化饮食" I don't advocate one single diet↔Follow a personalized diet

"不主张单一食谱" 反面印证 "个性化"

【排除】 A) 未提及

Switch to a vegetarian diet.(改吃素)在对话里没有依据；录音末尾虽提到多吃蔬果，但那是补充建议，从没让人 "改成素食"，属未提及的绝对化主张。

C) 原词陷阱

Adhere to doctors' advice. 借了前文 the medical community 留下的 "医学" 印象，但作者建议的是按自身代谢来，从没让普通人 "遵医嘱"，是盗用医学语感的诱选。 借⽤原⽂： My last book was written primarily for the medical community D) 与原文相反

录音说 Some people should eat more carbohydrates than others(有些人该比别人多吃碳水)，是 "碳水因人而异"；D 却笼统说 Cut carbohydrate intake.(减少碳水)，盗用 carbohydrate 一词，却把 "看人而定" 讲成了 "一律削减"，方向相反。 借⽤原⽂： Some people should eat more carbohydrates than others

items.title: 2022年12月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 1
items.transcript:
Stress is often depicted as negative, but research shows that moderate amounts of it can be beneficial for your brain and your body.

First, the benefits for the brain. Studies have shown that short periods of stress can actually bolster cognitive functioning. Researchers discovered that placing rats in a stressful situation for just a few hours doubled the growth of new brain cells. The rats also did better on a memory test later on. Scientists think the same thing happens in humans. But how does stress improve memory? It's simple. When your brain cells multiply, your memory can improve. Viewed from a biological perspective, this makes sense, because animals that are better at remembering dangerous situations can avoid them in the future. If an animal encounters a predator and escapes, for example, it's important to remember where and when that encounter happened. Experts assert that the same principle applies to humans.

Now, let's turn to how stress benefits the body. This may come as a surprise to laymen. But experts say that stress can keep you from getting sick. Scientists concede that chronic stress can make you more prone to illness. But research shows that short periods of stress can actually provide some protection against getting sick, because it increases your immune functioning. One study shows that rats that experienced brief stress had a surge of immune cell response, which makes the immune system better prepared to fight illness. For humans, there's even evidence that experiencing stress before getting vaccinated could help make vaccines more effective.

questions.prompt: What did researchers discover about rats placed briefly in a stressful situation?

options.text: The rate of their growth increased dramatically.
The growth of their new brain cells doubled.
They began to show signs of depression.
They began to get irritated and restless.

questions.shortExplanation: Researchers discovered that placing rats in a stressful situation for just a few hours doubled the growth of new brain cells. 研究者发现，把大鼠置于压力情境中仅仅几个小时，就使其新脑细胞的生长翻了一倍。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） The growth of their new brain cells doubled.

【定位】 Researchers discovered that placing rats in a stressful situation for just a few hours doubled the growth of new brain cells. 研究者发现，把大鼠置于压力情境中仅仅几个小时，就使其新脑细胞的生长翻了一倍。

【信号】 discovered 后接发现内容。答案句由 Researchers discovered that 引出，研究动词 discovered 后面紧跟的就是题干要的发现，是天然的答案信号；同时 doubled the growth of new brain cells 给出明确的量化结果，更确认这就是落点。

【替换】 doubled the growth of new brain cells ↔ The growth of their new brain cells doubled.

主被动语序调换

【排除】 A) 偷换概念

A 说 rate of their growth increased dramatically（成长速率剧增），但录音说的是生长翻倍（数量翻番），讲的是结果量而非速率；它盗用了原文 growth 一词，却把翻倍偷换成速率剧增，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： doubled the growth of new brain cells C) 未提及

C 说大鼠出现 signs of depression（抑郁迹象），但录音通篇讲的是适度压力的好处，从未提大鼠抑郁，属于无中生有。

D) 未提及

D 说大鼠变得 irritated and restless（烦躁不安），录音只说短暂压力让脑细胞翻倍、记忆变好，没说大鼠情绪烦躁，是凭压力等于负面的常识硬加的，未提及。

items.title: 2022年12月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 2
items.transcript:
For many managers and people who work in leadership positions, dealing with emails is a dilemma. It's likely the "unpredictable, uncontrollable and ongoing nature of day-to-day email in terms of volume, importance and urgency" contributes to their levels of anxiety and to diminished leadership skills.

That's because it's not unusual for many leaders to prioritize email management over people management. An obsession with managing their inbox prevents them from dealing with their employees. As a result, they ignore the issues that might only be mild problems at first, until unfortunately, they inevitably transform into a major problem or crisis by virtue of neglect.

As leaders, they are expected to motivate and inspire their team in pursuit of longer-term strategic goals and also, less ambitiously but more practically, to monitor their daily output, to set clear expectations and to give regular feedback.

When presented with a choice between the appeal of their inbox and other more important activities, many sacrifice the latter. Daily email demands have a negative impact on their goal progress. This is because leaders must divert resources from other tasks to check, filter and respond to emails.

The solution is cultivating self-control which is like a muscle—it can be strengthened or improved over time through exercise. Some suggestions include making space in your diary for the only periods during which you'll be checking emails, setting a timer for yourself so you don't become distracted by your inbox for too long, turning off email alerts so you're not interrupted by them.

【定位】 When presented with a choice between the appeal of their inbox and other more important activities, many sacrifice the latter. Daily email demands have a negative impact on their goal progress. 当要在收件箱的诱惑与其他更重要的事务之间做选择时，许多人牺牲了后者（更重要的事）。每天的邮件需求对他们的目标推进产生了负面影响。

【信号】 概括管理者通病的陈述句。这句不是靠某个转折词跳出来，而是全篇反复落到同一点：管理者把精力压在邮箱上而牺牲更重要的事。many sacrifice the latter 与 prioritize email management over people management 互相印证，共同指向"花太多时间在邮件上"这个通病。

"邮件占用精力"换说成"花太多时间处理邮件"

【排除】 A) 偷换概念

录音说的是管理者把邮件管理置于人员管理之上 prioritize email management over people management，置于上面的是"邮件"而非"自身利益"；A 把 over...staff 的句式留下，却换成 own interests，是偷换。 借⽤原⽂： prioritize email management over people management B) 原词陷阱

录音强调的是被"邮件"困住，未说被泛泛的"日常事务（daily routines）"压垮；B 借了 day-to-day 的感觉 day-to-day email，却把焦点从"邮件"扩大成"日常琐事"，范围被放大。 借⽤原⽂： day-to-day email C) 过度推断录音只说管理者沉迷邮箱、忽视员工 prevents them from dealing with their employees，是"没空管"，并未说他们"缺乏与员工共情的能力（relate to staff）"；从"没空管"推到"没能力"是多走了一步。 借⽤原⽂： prevents them from dealing with their employees

items.title: 2022年12月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 1
items.transcript:
In last week's lecture, we talked about the problems caused by poor eating habits, focusing on how medical professionals are trying to solve these problems. Today, we'll continue with the topic, but focus on research from a different field—marketing.

Now, what can marketing tell us about improving nutrition? Well, a team of marketing professors has studied the importance of the visual aspect of food and how that influences food choices.

Those marketing experts assert that the impact of the appearance of food is greater than we might presume, and might hold the key to encouraging better eating. So how important is the appearance of food?

Research shows that just seeing an appealing photograph of a hamburger in an advertisement, for example, can cause individuals to imagine the taste or smell of that hamburger. This can make them more likely to purchase and consume it. Of course, that's the point of advertisements. So isn't that a good thing?

Well, the marketing professors argue that this is actually a problem, because the combination of pleasing aesthetics of and easy access to unhealthy foods, such as hamburgers and pizza, may be contributing to a worldwide health crisis. In fact, statistics show that 39% of all adults in the world weigh too much and another 13% are obese.

Now, as we discussed last time, medical professionals have tried to fight the obesity epidemic by focusing on the nutrients found in different foods, emphasizing things like carbohydrate, fat, sugar and calorie content. But they've had limited success.

The marketing professors believe that the real solution to obesity is making food look appealing and focusing on the pleasure of both looking at and eating that food. That pleasure can be used as a tool to promote healthy food choices. In fact, the research done by the team showed that associating healthy food with pleasant images, experiences and emotions led to greater interest in purchasing or eating it. "This is a better strategy," they claim, than reminding consumers that a certain food is good for them. But are they right?

Well, the researchers cited a marketing campaign designed to reverse the sales decline of carrots. The campaign didn't emphasize the carrots' healthy qualities, but embraced their beauty and the pleasure derived from eating them. For example, the ads focused on the bright, beautiful orange color and crisp texture of the carrots. The campaign led to an impressive increase in product sales of more than 10%. The researchers believe that other companies could bolster sales of healthy foods with similar ads, depicting their products as attractive and a source of pleasure.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say a team of marketing professors has studied?

questions.detailedExplanation:

【定位】 Well, a team of marketing professors has studied the importance of the visual aspect of food and how that influences food choices.

嗯，一组营销学教授研究了食物视觉方面的重要性，以及它如何影响食物选择。

【信号】 题干原词 studied 在原文直接出现。录音 a team of marketing professors has studied the importance of the visual aspect of food 与题干同用 studied，是对研究对象的直接交代，定位信号明确，无需转折或推断。

【替换】 the importance of the visual aspect of food↔The importance of the appearance of food. visual aspect 同义改写为 appearance

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

选项把录音多次提到的 healthy 拼成 increasing healthy food supply，但录音研究的是外观对选择的影响，从未谈增加健康食品的供给量，属听到 healthy 就想选的原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： promote healthy food choices B) 原词陷阱

录音确实在 seeing an appealing photograph of a hamburger in an advertisement 提到广告，但那是用来举例说明外观如何起作用，不是这组学者研究的对象；选项把举例细节当成研究主题，属原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： an appealing photograph of a hamburger in an advertisement

items.title: 2022年12月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 2
items.transcript:
The household cleaning products industry really began to take off in the 1950s. Prior to that, resourceful housewives who had grown up in a less prosperous era relied on substances that they used in their kitchens such as vinegar used to clean windows.

Today, the household cleaning products industry is worth billions of dollars a year and is dominated by large global companies. In recent years, however, many countries have witnessed a surge in the number of small businesses and companies offering more environment-friendly cleaning products, and they're doing good business too.

One reason for this is that consumers are becoming more aware of environment and sustainability issues. They also want to make their home a safe place, free from toxic chemicals. The third reason is people's awareness of and knowledge about technology has never been greater. In the past, people might have been skeptical of a new product claimed to be able to achieve amazing cleaning results, but they now have faith in technology's ability to do what was once thought impossible.

There is perhaps no better example of this than a patented cloth sold by one company, which remarkably uses only water rather than traditional cleaning products. The company claims its cloth lifts, traps and removes dirt and bacteria. And considering that people don't see these products in shops, or advertised on TV or in the press, it has been a pretty steep rise.

Many of the people behind these companies began testing the viability of their products by selling them at local markets. Then, in many cases, customers are doing the marketing for these products by leaving threads of comments on social media, praising their virtues. There are also TV shows and books dedicated to maintaining home tidiness and cleanliness and the benefits of having a clean home.

Having a safe and clean home might be one thing people feel they can control in an increasingly out-of-control world. And there are social media celebrities. One woman in Britain has become a social media sensation with more than two million followers for her cleaning tips page.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about the cleaning products industry in recent years?

options.text: It has witnessed a spectacular surge in demand.

【替换】 a surge in the number of small businesses and companies offering more environment-friendly cleaning products

选项 much criticism from environmentalists 在录音里找不到任何对应——原文讲的是环保产品走红、生意红火，从无"被批评"之说，属凭空捏造。 D) 原词陷阱

录音第2段确有 large global companies，选项 fierce competition among global companies 借这个词造出"全球公司竞争加剧"，可原文只说大公司"主导"行业，没说它们之间竞争更激烈。 借⽤原⽂： dominated by large global companies

items.title: 2022年12月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 3
items.transcript:
Throwing spare change into a fountain is a time-honored ritual: throw a penny into the water, and your wish might come true. But all that money has to go somewhere. Otherwise, the growing piles of pennies, quarters and euros could clog up the fountains' works. Today, I'm going to talk about where all the coins go.

Well, the coins collected can go to all sorts of different places—from fountain maintenance to charity or public service. In New York City, for example, coins collected from fountains in public parks often go towards the fountains' maintenance itself, though entrepreneurs who don't mind getting their hands wet often get to it first. There are over 50 beautiful decorative display fountains in New York City parks. They are cleaned by the parks' staff every few weeks. But most of the coins have already been removed by entrepreneurial New Yorkers and there is not a significant amount left to be collected.

Other cities, though, can pull in a much more serious haul. Take for example, Rome's famous Trevi fountain: for hundreds of years, visitors have thrown coins over their shoulder into the fountain to ensure that they will return. So many tourists toss in coins that Roman officials have the fountain cleaned every night, reportedly getting as much as $4,000 in loose change from around the world each day. Most of the money collected each night goes towards running a supermarket for the needy. And collecting that cash is serious business. Roman officials have been known to be tough on anyone caught skimming coins from the fountain. In one case in 2005, police arrested four fountain cleaners after they were spotted slipping coins into their own pockets after collecting them. Authorities finally caught one notorious thief named Thomas Morgan and banned him from the fountain after he fished out thousands of dollars in change over 34 years using a magnetic stick.

For the most part, money collected from privately-owned fountains in the United States also goes to charity. The fountain in New York City's Bryant Park is owned and operated by a not-for-profit corporation, which puts the cash collected by cleaners towards the fountain's own maintenance. Tens of thousands of dollars in coins removed from wishing wells, fountains and ponds in Florida's Walt Disney World are donated each year to support foster children living in the state. Whether or not your wish comes true after tossing a coin into a fountain, you can rest assured knowing that the change is likely going to someone who needs it.

questions.prompt: What problem might be caused by the growing piles of coins in fountains?

options.text: Increasing cleaners' workload.
Blocking the fountains' works.
Breaking a time-honored ritual.
Polluting the fountains' water.

questions.shortExplanation: Otherwise, the growing piles of pennies, quarters and euros could clog up the fountains' works.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Blocking the fountains' works.

【定位】 Otherwise, the growing piles of pennies, quarters and euros could clog up the fountains' works.

否则，越堆越多的便士、25 美分和欧元硬币可能会堵塞喷泉的运作机件。

【信号】 Otherwise 引出假设后果。信号是 Otherwise（否则）——它引出"如果钱不被运走会怎样"的假设性后果，正对题干问的"会造成什么问题"，紧跟其后的 could clog up the fountains' works 就是答案句的核心。

【替换】 clog up the fountains' works↔ Blocking the fountains' works clog up = Blocking 同义替换

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

选项 Increasing cleaners' workload 里的 cleaners 在后文确实反复出现（喷泉由 staff 清理），但录音从没说"硬币堆积会加重清洁工负担"，是借后文的"清洁"话题诱你听到 cleaners 就选。 借⽤原⽂： They are cleaned by the parks' staff every few weeks.

C) 原词陷阱

选项 Breaking a time-honored ritual 直接搬了录音第一句的 time-honored ritual，但那句是说"投币许愿是个老传统"，是引入话题，根本不是在讲"硬币堆积造成的问题"——典型的把开头原词拿来骗。 借⽤原⽂： Throwing spare change into a fountain is a time-honored ritual D) 未提及

选项 Polluting the fountains' water 听起来"硬币泡水里好像会污染"很合常识，但录音通篇没提水质污染，是用生活常识替文本作答的典型坑。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about the coins collected from New York City's park fountains?

options.text: They are occasionally retrieved by curious tourists.
They are regularly donated to charity organizations.
They are mostly used for the fountains' maintenance.
They are usually used as wages for fountain cleaners.

questions.shortExplanation: But most of the coins have already been removed by entrepreneurial New Yorkers and there is not a significant amount left to be collected.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） They are mostly used for the fountains' maintenance.

【定位】 But most of the coins have already been removed by entrepreneurial New Yorkers and there is not a significant amount left to be collected.

但大部分硬币已经被有生意头脑的纽约人捞走了，剩下能被收走的已所剩无几。

【信号】 转折 But 后才是真意。信号是 But——前半句说"市政人员每几周清理一次"是表面信息，转折 But 之后的 most of the coins have already been removed by entrepreneurial New Yorkers 才是录音真正想强调的实情，这正是答案落点。

【替换】 go towards the fountains' maintenance itself↔used for the fountains' maintenance go towards=used for 同指用途

【排除】 A) 张冠李戴

选项 occasionally retrieved by curious tourists 看似对上"硬币被人提前取走"，但录音说取走硬币的是 entrepreneurial New Yorkers（有生意头脑的纽约人），不是 curious tourists（好奇游客）——把取走者的身份偷换了，属张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： most of the coins have already been removed by entrepreneurial New Yorkers B) 张冠李戴

选项 donated to charity organizations 里的 charity 录音确有（罗马的钱办惠民超市、迪士尼捐寄养儿童），但那是罗马和迪士尼喷泉的事，不是本题问的纽约公园喷泉——张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： Tens of thousands of dollars in coins removed from wishing wells, fountains and ponds in Florida's Walt Disney World are donated each year to support foster children D) 未提及

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the money collected from Rome's Trevi Fountain?

【定位】 Most of the money collected each night goes towards running a supermarket for the needy. 每晚收上来的钱，大部分用于运营一家面向困难群体的超市。

【信号】 goes towards 点明用途。信号是表用途的 goes towards（用于……）——它直接交代这笔钱的去向，紧跟其后的 running a supermarket for the needy 就是答案。听到 goes towards 这类"用于"的短语就锁定其后内容。

【替换】 running a supermarket for the needy↔ run a supermarket for the needy

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

选项 invested in a series of businesses 里 business(es) 一词录音确有（serious business 指"收钱是件正经事"），但那是形容"这事很严肃"，根本不是说钱拿去"投资做生意"——盗用 business 一词制造误会。 借⽤原⽂： collecting that cash is serious business B) 张冠李戴

选项 about $40,000 a month 把数字改了：录音说的是 as much as $4,000 in loose change from around the world each day（每天约 4000 美元），选项改成"每月 4 万"——金额和时间单位都被动了手脚，是典型数字陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： getting as much as $4,000 in loose change from around the world each day

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about Thomas Morgan?

options.text: He was arrested for stealing money from four fountain cleaners.
He was sentenced to 34 years' imprisonment.
He collected rare coins from around the world.
He stole a lot of money from a fountain with a magnetic stick.

questions.shortExplanation: Authorities finally caught one notorious thief named Thomas Morgan and banned him from the fountain after he fished out thousands of dollars in change over 34 years using a magnetic stick.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） He stole a lot of money from a fountain with a magnetic stick.

【定位】 Authorities finally caught one notorious thief named Thomas Morgan and banned him from the fountain after he fished out thousands of dollars in change over 34 years using a magnetic stick.

当局最终抓获一名臭名昭著、名叫 Thomas Morgan 的小偷，并禁止他靠近喷泉——此前他用一根磁棒在 34 年间钓走了数千美元的零钱。

【替换】 fished out thousands of dollars in change↔stole a lot of money from a fountain fished out=stole 概括偷取 using a magnetic stick↔ with a magnetic stick using=with 同指工具

选项 arrested for stealing money from four fountain cleaners 里的 four fountain cleaners 录音确有，但那是 2005 年警方抓的"四名监守自盗的清洁工"，是另一桩案子，跟 Thomas Morgan 无关——把别人的事安到他头上，还把"四名清洁工"从"被抓的人"偷换成"被偷的对象"。 借⽤原⽂： police arrested four fountain cleaners after they were spotted slipping coins into their own pockets B) 原词陷阱

选项 sentenced to 34 years' imprisonment 盗用录音的数字 34 years，但录音说的是他 over 34 years 间一直作案，结果只是被 banned from the fountain（禁入喷泉），并没有"判刑 34 年"——把"作案时长"偷换成"刑期"。 借⽤原⽂： banned him from the fountain after he fished out thousands of dollars in change over 34 years C) 原词陷阱

items.title: 2022年12月六级第2套 · 长对话 1
items.transcript:
M: Welcome to the Book Club. Today's guest is Susan Lane, the author of a new book on personal finances that has already sold half a million copies. Hi, Susan, your book is extremely successful. Why do you think that is?

W: I think that's because of my message, which is making happiness a priority over money. So many of us in my generation have spent decades trying to earn more money, just to consume more, but it made us more miserable.

M: You yourself were once caught in that cycle, working for two decades as an executive and earning a high salary, but still accumulating debt.

W: I most certainly was. I earned millions, but by the time I quit my job four years ago to become a writer, I owed over $30,000.

M: So how did you escape that pattern? And what would you advise other people to do?

W: The first change is in what we value. We need to emphasize things that actually make us happy, like relationships, the environment or even our hobbies. Once we make the right things our priority, our goals will change and so will our financial behavior.

M: How does that translate into practical action? Can you give our audience examples of what you are talking about on an everyday basis?

W: The major areas for action are usually housing, food and transportation. So people might share a home with friends instead of living on their own, bring lunch from home instead of going to restaurants, and use public transport instead of owning a car.

M: Those sound like major sacrifices, I could never share my home, I need my own space.

W: But they aren't sacrifices. When people change their values, their desires change. So in the example of housing, if we value relationships, sharing a home isn't depriving ourselves of space, but giving us an opportunity to spend more time with our loved ones.

M: Indeed it is.

questions.prompt: What message does the woman convey in her book?

options.text: Prioritizing happiness over money.
Joining the club to get her new book.
Managing one's personal finances wisely.
Consuming more only when earning more.

questions.shortExplanation: I think that's because of my message, which is making happiness a priority over money.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Prioritizing happiness over money.

【定位】 I think that's because of my message, which is making happiness a priority over money.

我想那是因为我书里的核心讯息——把幸福置于金钱之上。

【信号】 my message is 自报主旨。女方用 that's because of my message, which is making happiness a priority over money 亲口点出 my message（我的核心讯息），这种受访者自报观点的句子就是答案信号，无需再推。

【替换】 making happiness a priority over money↔Prioritizing happiness over money 短语换说法、意思全等

【排除】 B) 未提及

录音里男方说 Welcome to the Book Club 又提 a new book，B 借「book/club」这两个原词诱你联想「入会拿书」，但全篇没有任何「加入俱乐部以获取她新书」的内容，是凭原词拼出的假选项。 借⽤原⽂： Welcome to the Book Club C) 原词陷阱

Managing one's personal finances wisely 用了书的主题词 personal finances（原文 a new book on personal finances），听着像那么回事，但女方的核心讯息是「幸福优先于金钱」这个价值排序，而非笼统的「明智理财」，C 用原词把观点稀释成了空泛口号。 借⽤原⽂： a new book on personal finances

D) 与原文相反

Consuming more only when earning more 盗用原文 trying to earn more money, just to consume more 的 earn / consume，但那是女方批判的旧循环（结果让人更痛苦）， 不是她要传达的讯息，正话被反着取了。 借⽤原⽂： trying to earn more money, just to consume more, but it made us more miserable

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the woman before she became a writer?

options.text: She was in debt.
She was a financial adviser.
She earned $30,000 a month.
She enjoyed a happy life.

questions.shortExplanation: I earned millions, but by the time I quit my job four years ago to become a writer, I owed over $30,000.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） She was in debt.

【定位】 I earned millions, but by the time I quit my job four years ago to become a writer, I owed over $30,000.

我挣过数百万，但等到四年前我辞职去当作家时，我已欠债超过 3 万美元。

【信号】 转折 but 后才是真处境。句中 I earned millions, but by the time I quit my job…I owed over \$30,000 用 but 转折，前半「挣过数百万」是铺垫，转折后的「欠债三万」才是她当作家前的真实处境，转折后即落点。

【替换】 I owed over \$30,000↔ She was in debt owe 概括为 in debt

【排除】 B) 偷换概念 She was a financial adviser 借书谈 personal finances 的「financial」联想出「理财顾问」，但原文说她过去是 working for two decades as an executive（高管），不是理财顾问，职业被张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： working for two decades as an executive C) 原词陷阱

She earned \$30,000 a month 直接搬来原文数字 \$30,000，但原文 \$30,000 是 I owed over \$30,000 的「欠债额」，不是月收入；她的收入原文说的是 earned millions。数字对、名目全错。 借⽤原⽂： I owed over \$30,000 D) 与原文相反

She enjoyed a happy life 与原文相反：女方说当年那段循环 made us more miserable （更痛苦），过去并不幸福，D 反了极性。 借⽤原⽂： but it made us more miserable

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about one's financial behavior?

options.text: It reflects one's earning power.
It varies with one's environment.

questions.shortExplanation: Once we make the right things our priority, our goals will change and so will our financial behavior. 一旦我们把对的事情当作优先项，我们的目标就会改变，财务行为也随之改变。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） It changes with one's goals in life.

【定位】 Once we make the right things our priority, our goals will change and so will our financial behavior. 一旦我们把对的事情当作优先项，我们的目标就会改变，财务行为也随之改变。

【信号】 Once…and so will 的因果链。Once we make the right things our priority, our goals will change and so will our financial behavior 用 Once（一旦）引导条件、so will 承接连锁：目标改变带动财务行为改变，财务行为是被「目标」牵着走的，因果链尾即答案。

【替换】 our goals will change and so will our financial behavior↔It changes with one's goals in life

so will 还原成 changes with goals

【排除】 A) 偷换概念

It reflects one's earning power 蹭了全篇 earn / earned 的高频词，但原文说财务行为由 goals 决定，从未说它「反映挣钱能力」，归因对象被换掉了。 借⽤原⽂： trying to earn more money B) 原词陷阱

It varies with one's environment 的 environment 确实在原文出现过——但那是 relationships, the environment or even our hobbies 里「值得珍视的事物」之一，不是决定财务行为的因素，词对、关系错。 借⽤原⽂： like relationships, the environment or even our hobbies C) 未提及

It varies with one's environment 与 B 同样把 environment 当成变量来源，原文从未说财务行为随环境变化，纯属拼词造句。 借⽤原⽂： like relationships, the environment or even our hobbies

questions.prompt: What does the man say about sharing a home?

【定位】 Those sound like major sacrifices, I could never share my home, I need my own space.

那些听起来像是重大的牺牲，我绝不可能跟人合住，我需要自己的空间。

【信号】 男方直接应答表态。在女方讲完合住等做法后，男方紧接着应答 Those sound like major sacrifices, I could never share my home, I need my own space，这是被问者本人的直接表态，态度题的答案就落在这句应答上。

【替换】 Those sound like major sacrifices↔ It would mean major sacrifices for him

几乎原词、补出主语 for him

【排除】 A) 张冠李戴

It would give him more time to be with his loved ones 来自女方 giving us an opportunity to spend more time with our loved ones，那是女方反驳时说的合住好处， 不是男方的看法，主体说反了。 借⽤原⽂： giving us an opportunity to spend more time with our loved ones B) 张冠李戴

It would be good for those who value relationships 对应女方观点 if we value relationships, sharing a home isn't depriving ourselves of space，仍是女方的论调而非男方所说，归属错位。 借⽤原⽂： if we value relationships, sharing a home isn't depriving ourselves of space D) 原词陷阱 It would deprive him of his individuality 蹭了女方原文 sharing a home isn't depriving ourselves of space 的 depriving，但原文说的是「不会剥夺空间」且是女方所言，D 既盗词又把否定说成肯定、还安到男方头上。 借⽤原⽂： sharing a home isn't depriving ourselves of space

items.title: 2022年12月六级第2套 · 长对话 2
items.transcript:
W: Thank you for inviting me to the gallery, Christopher. I haven't visited here since your predecessor's retirement function.

M: Would you like to see the newest additions to our collection first, Catherine?

W: Are those the landscapes by Danielle Gregory? I absolutely adore her work.

M: This first piece was a gift to the gallery from the artist herself, and it's quite exquisite.

W: I love how she depicts the barren landscape. The colors complement each other perfectly.

M: You can sense the desolation in the picture. This piece was inspired by Gregory's recent trek in the Gobi Desert.

W: And how did you obtain her other piece over here?

M: It was purchased at auction by an anonymous collector who lent it to the gallery for display. This composition is one of her most acclaimed paintings.

W: It must have cost that collector a small fortune to purchase this.

M: Obviously, I can't disclose the exact amount he paid, but it was substantial.

W: There's so much detail in this painting. I feel like I can really immerse myself in the scene. I particularly like the symmetry created by the reflection of the mountain in the lake.

M: This particular piece was the one that was nominated for a Gateway Award. I was lucky enough to attend the award ceremony as Gregory's guest.

W: So you know her personally. I assume she's an eccentric artist.

M: Quite the opposite. In fact, she's not at all eccentric. I would say she's one of the most easygoing and intelligent people I know.

W: I'd love to be able to meet her. There are so many questions I'd like to ask.

M: What a coincidence! I'm meeting her for dinner tonight. Would you like to come along?

W: I'd love to. Thank you.

这第一幅是艺术家本人赠送给画廊的，相当精美。

【替换】 a gift to the gallery from the artist herself↔donated by the artist herself a gift = donated 同义改写

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱录音里女士提到 those the landscapes by Danielle Gregory，男士又说 This first piece，选项 A 把 first 与 landscape 拼成『这是她的第一幅风景画』，但 first 只是『第一幅展品』之序，原文从未说是画家生涯首作。 借⽤原⽂： This first piece B) 张冠李戴

Christopher 是开头女士称呼的画廊负责人（Thank you for inviting me to the gallery, Christopher.），画作者是 Danielle Gregory；选项 B 把这画说成 Christopher 所画，属张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： Christopher D) 原词陷阱

items.title: 2022年12月六级第2套 · 听力篇章 1
items.transcript:
Forgiveness is the release of resentment or anger. Forgiveness doesn't mean reconciliation. We don't have to return to the same relationship, nor do we have to accept the same harmful behaviors from an offender. Forgiveness is vitally important for the mental health of certain victims. It propels people forward rather than keeping them emotionally engaged in an injustice or trauma. Carrying the hurt or anger of an offense leads the body to release stress chemicals. Eliminating the perpetual flow of those chemicals may also explain why forgiveness provides physical health benefits.

There are scenarios in which forgiveness is not the best course. Sometimes the victim becomes more empowered when they give themselves permission not to forgive. Forgiveness can be challenging. This is especially true when the offending party offers an insincere apology, or maybe they haven't offered anything at all. However, it's often the healthiest path forward. It's important to cultivate forgiveness by developing compassion for the offender, reflect on whether the act was due to malicious intent, or whether it was caused by challenging circumstances in the offender's life.

What about forgiving ourselves? We sometimes need to take responsibility for mistakes, but intense guilt and shame aren't a desirable outcome in the long run. Forgiving yourself may seem like an ambiguous process. You can begin by acknowledging that you are at fault, taking responsibility for the hurt you caused, then reflecting on why the event occurred. Draw the lessons you learned and try to avoid committing a similar offense in the future.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about forgiveness?

options.text: It is vital to one's mental health.
It leads to reconciliation and peace.
It promotes interpersonal relationship.
It keeps one from traumatic experience.

questions.shortExplanation: Forgiveness is vitally important for the mental health of certain victims. 对某些受害者而言，宽恕对其心理健康至关重要。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） It is vital to one's mental health.

【定位】 Forgiveness is vitally important for the mental health of certain victims. 对某些受害者而言，宽恕对其心理健康至关重要。

【信号】 正面界定句 is vitally important for。录音里 Forgiveness is vitally important for the mental health of certain victims. 用'X is important for…'的正面陈述直接给宽恕定价值， 是典型的'下定义/给判断'信号句，细节定义题的答案就落在这种句子上。

【替换】 vitally important for the mental health ↔ vital to one's mental health

副词转形容词、介词换说法

【排除】 B) 与原文相反

It leads to reconciliation and peace. 看似命中 reconciliation，但录音 Forgiveness doesn't mean reconciliation. 恰恰说宽恕'不等于'和解，选项把被否定的词当成正面结论， 方向相反。 借⽤原⽂： Forgiveness doesn't mean reconciliation. C) 未提及

It promotes interpersonal relationship. 与原文相反：录音 We don't have to return to the same relationship 说宽恕后不必回到原来的关系，根本没说宽恕能'促进'人际关系， promotes 是无中生有又恰好反向。 借⽤原⽂： We don't have to return to the same relationship D) 原词陷阱 It keeps one from traumatic experience. 借了录音里的 trauma 一词，但原文 keeping them emotionally engaged in an injustice or trauma 说的是'宽恕让人不再深陷于创伤情绪'，不是'让人远离/避免创伤经历(keeps one from traumatic experience)'，偷换了 trauma 的语境。 借⽤原⽂： keeping them emotionally engaged in an injustice or trauma
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: When is forgiveness especially challenging?

options.text: When the offender has power over the victim.
When the offender is not willing to apologize.
When the offender is not duly penalized.
When the offender adds insult to injury.

questions.shortExplanation: This is especially true when the offending party offers an insincere apology, or maybe they haven't offered anything at all.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） When the offender is not willing to apologize.

【定位】 This is especially true when the offending party offers an insincere apology, or maybe they haven't offered anything at all.

尤其当冒犯方道歉并不真诚，或者干脆什么都没表示时，更是如此。

【信号】 especially true when 引出难点条件。录音 This is especially true when the offending party offers an insincere apology, or maybe they haven't offered anything at all. 紧接在 'Forgiveness can be challenging.' 之后，用 especially true when 把'最难'的条件点名，正是题干 especially challenging 的答案信号句。

【替换】 they haven't offered anything at all↔not willing to apologize

'压根没道歉'=不愿道歉 offers an insincere apology↔ not willing to apologize '道歉不真诚'≈无诚意道歉

【排除】 A) 张冠李戴

When the offender has power over the victim. 里的'权力'像呼应录音 the victim becomes more empowered，但原文 empowered 说的是'受害者更有力量(选择不宽恕)'，恰恰是 victim 被赋权，而非 offender 对 victim 有权力，主体被掉包。 借⽤原⽂： the victim becomes more empowered when they give themselves permission not to forgive C) 未提及

When the offender is not duly penalized. 讲'冒犯者没被适当惩罚'，录音通篇谈道歉是否真诚、动机是否恶意，从没提'惩罚(penalize)'这一维度，属凭常识脑补的未提及项。

D) 过度推断

When the offender adds insult to injury.('火上浇油/雪上加霜')听起来也像'让宽恕更难'的情形，但录音点名的难点只有'道歉不真诚或不道歉'，并未提冒犯者'再次加害'，属过度推断。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What should one do in order to forgive the offender?

options.text: Talk with the offender calmly.
Accept the offender's apology.
Find out why he committed the offense.
Determine how serious the offense was.

questions.shortExplanation: It's important to cultivate forgiveness by developing compassion for the offender, reflect on whether the act was due to malicious intent, or whether it was caused by challenging circumstances in the offender's life.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Find out why he committed the offense.

【定位】 It's important to cultivate forgiveness by developing compassion for the offender, reflect on whether the act was due to malicious intent, or whether it was caused by challenging circumstances in the offender's life.

重要的是要通过对冒犯者培养同情心来培育宽恕，去反思那件事究竟是出于恶意，还是由冒犯者生活中的艰难处境所致。

【信号】 It's important to…by… 引出方法。录音 It's important to cultivate forgiveness by developing compassion for the offender, reflect on whether the act was due to malicious intent, or whether it was caused by challenging circumstances 用 'It's important to…by + 做法' 的建议句式直接给出培养宽恕的方法，是方法题的答案信号句。

【替换】 reflect on whether the act was due to malicious intent, or whether it was caused by challenging circumstances in the offender's life ↔ Find out why he committed the offense

'反思动机是恶意还是处境'=弄清原因

【排除】 A) 未提及

Talk with the offender calmly. 听上去是化解冲突的好办法，但录音讲的方法是'对冒犯者培养同情、反思其动机'，从没提'与对方平静交谈(talk with…calmly)'，属合理却未提及的脑补做法。 B) 原词陷阱

Accept the offender's apology. 借了录音里的 apology 一词，但原文 the offending party offers an insincere apology, or maybe they haven't offered anything at all 说的是道歉往往不真诚甚至没有道歉，宽恕并不以'接受道歉'为前提，选项与文意相悖。 借⽤原⽂： This is especially true when the offending party offers an insincere apology, or maybe they haven't offered anything at all. D) 原词陷阱 Determine how serious the offense was. 借了录音里反复出现的 offense，但原文要人反思的是冒犯的'原因(why/intent)'，不是冒犯的'严重程度(how serious)'，偷换了反思的对象。 借⽤原⽂： reflect on whether the act was due to malicious intent, or whether it was caused by challenging circumstances in the offender's life
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

items.title: 2022年12月六级第2套 · 听力篇章 2
items.transcript:
The Glasgow subway first opened in 1896 as a cable-hauled system. It is generally recognised as the world's third underground railway, after London and Budapest. In its long history, it has never been expanded, remaining as a single loop line with a mere 15 stations. At its peak, it served the shipyard workers on the south side of the city. In the 1960s, there was a decline in the shipbuilding industry and the popularity of private transport grew. As a result, the subway saw a rapid decline in ridership.

It ran with little further change until 1977 when its new operators closed it for major modernisation investment. Carriages were replaced, ventilation was improved, and the main depot was also renovated and fitted with connecting tracks to replace the outdated crane transfer mechanism. The subway in its present form reopened for operation in April 1980. Since its relaunch, the subway has seen a revival in its fortunes. It serves as a viable alternative to other forms of transport and has gone a long way to alleviate traffic jams in the city centre. In 1996, the system reached an important milestone—100 years. To commemorate this special event, the colour scheme of the train carriages was updated.

Recently, high-tech systems such as smart card ticketing machines and smart gates are used across all subway stations. The smart card provides more convenient travel, and passengers simply top up their cards and tap them to get in and out the subway. Since its launch, the technology has been adopted by more than 100,000 subway customers.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about the Glasgow subway in the 1960s?

options.text: The number of passengers dropped sharply.
It served more and more commuters.
The number of stations increased to 50.
It became the longest in the United Kingdom.

questions.shortExplanation: In the 1960s, there was a decline in the shipbuilding industry and the popularity of private transport grew. As a result, the subway saw a rapid decline in ridership. 在 20 世纪 60 年代，造船业衰退、私人交通工具日益普及。结果，地铁的客流量急剧下降。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） The number of passengers dropped sharply.

【定位】 In the 1960s, there was a decline in the shipbuilding industry and the popularity of private transport grew. As a result, the subway saw a rapid decline in ridership. 在 20 世纪 60 年代，造船业衰退、私人交通工具日益普及。结果，地铁的客流量急剧下降。

【信号】 时间词 + 因果信号 As a result。听到 In the 1960s 锁定时间，再抓住因果信号 As a result，结果句 the subway saw a rapid decline in ridership 才是承载答案的落点——这是篇章题靠因果结论句定位的典型。

【替换】 a rapid decline in ridership ↔ The number of passengers dropped sharply

同义改写：ridership=客流人数，rapid decline=dropped sharply

【排除】 B) 与原文相反

It served more and more commuters. 把方向反了——原文 1960 年代是 a rapid decline in ridership（客流骤降），B 却说服务越来越多通勤者，正好相反。"客流增多" 是录音里别的时期（早年高峰）的情形，被挪到 1960 年代头上。 借⽤原⽂： a rapid decline in ridership C) 未提及

The number of stations increased to 50. 凭空捏造。原文明说 it has never been expanded, remaining as a single loop line with a mere 15 stations，站数一直是 15 且从未扩建，根本没有增到 50 一说。 D) 原词陷阱

It became the longest in the United Kingdom. 借 "最长" 这类醒目说法制造诱惑，但原文谈的是它是 the world's third underground railway（世界第三条地下铁），讲的是 "第三早" 而非 "全英最长"，把 "第三" 偷换成 "最长"、把 "世界范围的早" 偷换成 "英国范围的长"。 借⽤原⽂： the world's third underground railway, after London and Budapest
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: Why was the Glasgow subway closed in 1977?

options.text: To increase capacity to meet growing needs.
To make way for other means of transport.
To have its systems modernised.
To avoid further financial losses.

questions.shortExplanation: It ran with little further change until 1977 when its new operators closed it for major modernisation investment. 它一直没怎么变，直到 1977 年新运营方将其关闭，以进行大规模的现代化改造投资。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） To have its systems modernised.

【定位】 It ran with little further change until 1977 when its new operators closed it for major modernisation investment. 它一直没怎么变，直到 1977 年新运营方将其关闭，以进行大规模的现代化改造投资。

【信号】 目的信号 for + 时间词 1977。听到 until 1977 锁定时间后，紧跟的介词 for major modernisation investment 里的 for 正是表目的的信号词，for 后面的成分就是关闭的原因。

【替换】 for major modernisation investment↔ To have its systems modernised

同根词改写：modernisation→modernised，名词转动词被动

【排除】 A) 未提及

To increase capacity to meet growing needs. 录音没有依据。原文反而强调它 has never been expanded（从未扩建），与 "增加运力" 相悖，更没说是为应对需求增长而关闭。

B) 未提及

To make way for other means of transport. 是无中生有。原文后文只说改造后地铁成了 a viable alternative to other forms of transport（其他交通的替代选择），是 "地铁替代别的交通"，绝非 "为别的交通让路"，B 把关系搞反且与 1977 关闭目的无关。 借⽤原⽂： a viable alternative to other forms of transport D) 原词陷阱

To avoid further financial losses. 听感上呼应了前文客流下降，像是 "亏损"，但原文从未把关闭归因于避免财务亏损，1977 关闭明确是 for major modernisation investment。它借第一段衰退的语境制造 "亏损" 联想，属过度推断式的原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： a rapid decline in ridership
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: Why does the Glasgow subway remain important today?

options.text: It is generally recognised as a world heritage site.
It is the fastest way to reach the city's south side.
It constitutes a source of revenue for the city.
It helps reduce traffic jams in the city centre.

questions.shortExplanation: It serves as a viable alternative to other forms of transport and has gone a long way to alleviate traffic jams in the city centre.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） It helps reduce traffic jams in the city centre.

【定位】 It serves as a viable alternative to other forms of transport and has gone a long way to alleviate traffic jams in the city centre.

它成为其他交通方式的一个可行替代选择，并在很大程度上缓解了市中心的交通拥堵。

【信号】 作用信号 serves as / alleviate。听到 It serves as a viable alternative 与 alleviate traffic jams in the city centre 这类讲贡献作用的动词，就是承载 "为何重要" 的答案句。

【替换】 alleviate traffic jams in the city centre↔helps reduce traffic jams in the city centre 近义词替换：alleviate=help reduce

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

It is generally recognised as a world heritage site. 盗用了原文 It is generally recognised as the world's third underground railway 的 "generally recognised as" 整个句式，但原文认的是 "世界第三条地下铁"，不是 "世界遗产"，把 third underground railway 偷换成 world heritage site。这也答非所问：该句讲历史地位，并非它 today 重要的原因。 借⽤原⽂： It is generally recognised as the world's third underground railway B) 原词陷阱

It is the fastest way to reach the city's south side. 借了原文 the shipyard workers on the south side of the city 的 south side 字眼，但原文只说早年它服务南区造船工人，从未说它是去南区 "最快" 的方式，fastest 是凭空添加的最高级。 借⽤原⽂： the shipyard workers on the south side of the city C) 未提及 It constitutes a source of revenue for the city. 录音通篇没有提到地铁为城市创收/带来财政收入，是无中生有的功能。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about all subway stations in Glasgow nowadays?

options.text: They are usually crowded.
They use high-tech systems.
They accept smartcards only.
They are colourfully decorated.

questions.shortExplanation: Recently, high-tech systems such as smart card ticketing machines and smart gates are used across all subway stations. 近来，诸如智能卡售票机和智能闸机之类的高科技系统已在所有地铁站投入使用。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） They use high-tech systems.

【定位】 Recently, high-tech systems such as smart card ticketing machines and smart gates are used across all subway stations. 近来，诸如智能卡售票机和智能闸机之类的高科技系统已在所有地铁站投入使用。

【信号】 现状信号 Recently + 范围词 all stations。听到 Recently 即进入讲现状的部分，high-tech systems such as smart card ticketing machines and smart gates are used across all subway stations 里 all subway stations 与题干 all stations 对应，正是答案句。

【替换】 high-tech systems such as smart card ticketing machines and smart gates↔ They use high-tech systems 概括替换：列举的具体例子→上位概括 high-tech systems

【排除】 A) 未提及

They are usually crowded. 录音从未提到车站拥挤，是无中生有。原文末段讲的是高科技系统，与拥挤无关。

C) 原词陷阱

They accept smartcards only. 盗用原文 smart card ticketing machines 的 smart card，但原文只说智能卡是高科技系统之一、很方便，从未说车站 "只收" 智能卡。only 是凭空加的绝对范围词，把 "用了智能卡" 偷改成 "只收智能卡"。 借⽤原⽂： smart card ticketing machines and smart gates D) 张冠李戴

They are colourfully decorated. 借了原文 the colour scheme of the train carriages was updated 的 colour 字眼，但那是为纪念百年更新了"车厢"的配色，对象是 train carriages，且属 1996 年的旧事，并非如今 "所有车站" 装饰艳丽，对象和时间都被张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： the colour scheme of the train carriages was updated
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

items.title: 2022年12月六级第2套 · 讲座与讲话 1
items.transcript:
If you visit the Great Smoky Mountains National Park, chances are you will remember the roadside or campground bears above all else. Bears are the most popular animals in a number of our national parks. In these mountains, where the population of bears runs into the hundreds, opportunities to observe these large wild animals are plentiful during the summer.

Since national parks are wildlife sanctuaries where no disturbance of the native animals is allowed, years of protection have served to break down the wild bears' fear of humans. Now, instead of depending on their own resources for a living, many bears patrol park roads and campgrounds. They give the garbage cans a frequent going over. An occasional offer of food from a park visitor, an illegal and dangerous practice, makes beggars of them. Bears are very often hungry and since they will feed on almost any kind of plant or animal, garbage is quite acceptable.

Feeding them, however, represents misguided kindness because the bears come to expect such generosity from everyone and consequently, trouble could lie ahead. Park rules prohibit the feeding of bears. Violators are arrested. Every year, doctors who have offices near the park treat a number of cases of bear bites and bear scratches. Some of the accidents have come about in strange ways.

One man was in the process of feeding two small cubs, when the mother bear appeared and insisted upon having some of the food. Shoving the big bear aside with one hand, the man continued feeding the cubs when suddenly he was struck a fierce blow in the face. A bear, prompted by the food that a lady kept offering to him, entered the car where the generous person was sitting. Her efforts to push the bear out of the car resulted in injuries. A man required medical attention after he applied a lighted cigarette to a bear's nose. Another man tried to boost a bear into the front seat of his car so that he might take a picture of a bear sitting beside his wife who was behind the wheel.

Because bears prefer roads and campgrounds, the possibility of a hiker meeting up with a bear along park trails is small, but there's always that chance, for a bear seems to know if you are carrying a lunch or a candy bar. He may even insist on taking it.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about the bears in national parks now?

options.text: They are quite friendly to humans.
They are shrinking in numbers.
They are unafraid of humans.
They are especially fond of garbage.

questions.shortExplanation: Since national parks are wildlife sanctuaries where no disturbance of the native animals is allowed, years of protection have served to break down the wild bears' fear of humans. 由于国家公园是禁止任何打扰本地动物的野生动物保护区，多年的保护已经逐渐瓦解了野生熊对人类的恐惧。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） They are unafraid of humans.

【定位】 Since national parks are wildlife sanctuaries where no disturbance of the native animals is allowed, years of protection have served to break down the wild bears' fear of humans. 由于国家公园是禁止任何打扰本地动物的野生动物保护区，多年的保护已经逐渐瓦解了野生熊对人类的恐惧。

【信号】 因果句的结果落点。years of protection have served to break down the wild bears' fear of humans 是"多年保护"导致的结果，"瓦解了对人的恐惧"正是对熊现状的概括，这种"原因—结果"句的结果端就是答案落点。

【替换】 break down the wild bears' fear of humans↔They are unafraid of humans. "瓦解恐惧"="不再害怕"

【排除】 A) 过度推断原文只说熊 break down the wild bears' fear of humans（不再怕人），但"不怕"不等于"友好"——后文讲熊咬人抓人，恰恰说明它们并不友好。They are quite friendly to humans. 是把"不怕"硬升级成"友好"，推过了头。 借⽤原⽂： break down the wild bears' fear of humans B) 与原文相反

录音里只在第一段说 the population of bears runs into the hundreds（熊有成百上千），根本没说数量在减少。They are shrinking in numbers. 与原文给出的"数量众多"印象相反，属与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： the population of bears runs into the hundreds D) 原词陷阱

录音确实念到 garbage is quite acceptable（垃圾它们也吃），They are especially fond of garbage. 就盗用了 garbage 这个原词。但原文是说熊"几乎什么都吃，垃圾也接受"，并非"特别偏爱垃圾"，更不是对熊"现状"的总概括，是答非所问的原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： garbage is quite acceptable
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about visitors feeding bears in national parks?

options.text: It is strictly forbidden.
It is an uncommon sight.
It is a gesture of human generosity.
It is allowed only in certain areas.

questions.shortExplanation: An occasional offer of food from a park visitor, an illegal and dangerous practice, makes beggars of them. 公园游客偶尔给熊喂食，这是一种违法又危险的行为，会把熊变成乞食者。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） It is strictly forbidden.

【定位】 An occasional offer of food from a park visitor, an illegal and dangerous practice, makes beggars of them. 公园游客偶尔给熊喂食，这是一种违法又危险的行为，会把熊变成乞食者。

【信号】 插入语直接定性 illegal。an illegal and dangerous practice 是夹在句中的插入语，直接给"游客喂食"贴上"违法且危险"的定性标签，这种紧贴行为的评判性插入语就是答案信号； 第三段 Park rules prohibit the feeding of bears. 再次印证。

【替换】 an illegal and dangerous practice↔It is strictly forbidden.

illegal/prohibit = strictly forbidden

【排除】 B) 答非所问

原文说游客喂食只是 An occasional offer of food（偶尔给食），但整段都在讲熊巡逻、讨食、被喂出问题，可见这事并不罕见；题问的也是"喂熊"的性质（违法），而非它"常不常见"。It is an uncommon sight. 答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： An occasional offer of food from a park visitor C) 与原文相反

录音第三段确实出现 misguided kindness（误导的善意），并提到熊指望"这种慷慨"， generosity 一词录音真念过，于是 It is a gesture of human generosity. 把它正面化。但作者明说这是"misguided（错误的）"善意，是正话反说，并非赞许喂熊是慷慨之举。 借⽤原⽂： misguided kindness D) 与原文相反

原文是 Park rules prohibit the feeding of bears.（规定禁止喂熊），全面禁止、没有任何"某些区域可以喂"的说法。It is allowed only in certain areas. 凭空造出"分区允许"，与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： Park rules prohibit the feeding of bears.
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's advice to people who carry some food while hiking on a park trail?

options.text: Share their food with the bear they see.
Be prepared to run into a hungry bear.
Try to be friendly with the bear they meet.
Refrain from teasing bears with cubs.

questions.shortExplanation: Because bears prefer roads and campgrounds, the possibility of a hiker meeting up with a bear along park trails is small, but there's always that chance, for a bear seems to know if you are carrying a lunch or a candy bar. He may even insist on taking it.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Be prepared to run into a hungry bear.

【定位】 Because bears prefer roads and campgrounds, the possibility of a hiker meeting up with a bear along park trails is small, but there's always that chance, for a bear seems to know if you are carrying a lunch or a candy bar. He may even insist on taking it.

由于熊更喜欢马路和营地，徒步者在公园小径上遇到熊的可能性很小，但总有那么一点几率，因为熊似乎能察觉你是否带着午餐或糖果。它甚至可能非要把它抢走。

【信号】 转折 but 之后才是真意。前半 the possibility of a hiker meeting up with a bear along park trails is small 是铺垫，but there's always that chance 的 but 一转，才点出"仍有可能遇上、且熊会盯上你的食物甚至抢走"——转折后这层提醒就是 advice 的落点。

【替换】 there's always that chance ↔ Be prepared to run into a hungry bear.

"总有机会遇上"="要有遇熊的准备" He may even insist on taking it ↔ a hungry bear

"非要抢食"印证"饿熊"

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

Share their food with the bear they see. 是"主动喂熊"，但全文反复说喂熊违法危险（an illegal and dangerous practice、Park rules prohibit the feeding of bears.），作者绝不会建议分食物给熊，与原文立场相反。 借⽤原⽂： Park rules prohibit the feeding of bears. C) 与原文相反

Try to be friendly with the bear they meet. 让人主动亲近熊，但录音通篇在讲熊咬人抓人、会抢食，提醒的是"提防"而非"友好"。这是把第 16 题埋的 friendly 一词挪过来制造的诱惑，与作者本意相反。 借⽤原⽂： He may even insist on taking it D) 原词陷阱

录音第四段确有带幼崽的母熊伤人的例子（the mother bear appeared），cubs 的画面录音真出现过，Refrain from teasing bears with cubs. 就借此设套。但那只是"事故举例"， 作者末段给徒步者的建议并不是"别逗带崽的熊"，属答非所问的原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： One man was in the process of feeding two small cubs
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

items.title: 2022年12月六级第2套 · 讲座与讲话 2
items.transcript:
Why do we form opinions or attitudes about someone or something without really knowing much about them? Just hearing something good or bad about a person, a place or thing can influence our opinions positively or negatively. But letting the opinions of another person determine what our opinions will be is dangerous. Forming opinions about someone or something before really knowing them well is called prejudice. "Pre-" means before, and "judice" refers to judgment. Hence, prejudice means to judge before having adequate knowledge.

We can be prejudiced toward or against someone or something. In either case, we are only allowing ourselves to see half of the picture. Very few people or things in this world are all good or all bad. Prejudiced attitudes are usually based on myths, half-truths or incorrect information, and they are dangerous because they can keep us from learning the truth about someone or something. People form prejudices against others for many reasons—differences in their race, religion, gender, or occupation. Prejudices keep people apart. They keep us from really knowing and understanding each other.

We should feel proud of who we are and the group of people we represent. If feelings of pride begin to turn to feelings of superiority when we think that our group or our beliefs are better than those around us, however, then we begin to develop prejudiced attitudes that can be harmful. For example, the prejudiced attitudes of one group may keep another group from attending certain schools, from living in any neighborhood they want, or from getting a job or a promotion. Extreme feelings of prejudice have caused the deaths of innocent people. We are responsible for our own thoughts and opinions. When we let someone else tell us what to think about someone or something, we are giving up some control of our own lives.

Before you form an attitude or opinion, find out for yourself about the person or the thing in question. Sometimes we don't realize that we hold prejudiced attitudes toward or against someone or something. We need to carefully examine our lives and our fears, and to ask ourselves whether our attitudes come from our personal knowledge and experience or from rumors and fear of the unknown. The good news about prejudice is that we are not born with it. Prejudiced attitudes and opinions develop over time. But with education and knowledge, we can replace our prejudices with cooperation and understanding.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about prejudice?

options.text: It refers to opinions that are radical and widespread.
It means making judgments without adequate knowledge.
It refers to deep-rooted beliefs about someone or something.
It means sticking to one's judgments even when proved wrong.

questions.shortExplanation: Forming opinions about someone or something before really knowing them well is called prejudice. "Pre-" means before, and "judice" refers to judgment. Hence, prejudice means to judge before having adequate knowledge. 在真正了解某人或某物之前就对其形成看法，这叫作偏见。"Pre-"意为"之前"，"judice"指"判断"。因此，偏见就是在没有足够认识之前就下判断。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） It means making judgments without adequate knowledge.

【定位】 Forming opinions about someone or something before really knowing them well is called prejudice. "Pre-" means before, and "judice" refers to judgment. Hence, prejudice means to judge before having adequate knowledge. 在真正了解某人或某物之前就对其形成看法，这叫作偏见。"Pre-"意为"之前"，"judice"指"判断"。因此，偏见就是在没有足够认识之前就下判断。

【信号】 定义标志is called与Hence总结。is called prejudice 给出概念名称、紧接 Hence, prejudice means to judge before having adequate knowledge 用 Hence 收束成一句完整定义，这个"下定义+总结"信号让它成为答案句。

【替换】 to judge before having adequate knowledge↔ making judgments without adequate knowledge

judge=making judgments且before=without

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

opinions that are radical and widespread 借了录音里的 opinions 一词，但原文从未说偏见是"激进而广泛的（radical and widespread）"观点，激进/广泛是凭空加的限定，属听到 opinions 就想选的原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： hearing something good or bad about a person, a place or thing can influence our opinions C) 偷换概念

deep-rooted beliefs about someone or something 蹭了原文反复出现的 about someone or something，但把偏见说成"根深蒂固的信念"，而原文定义强调的是"了解/认识之前"就下判断，时间点完全不同，属偷换概念。 借⽤原⽂： Forming opinions about someone or something before really knowing them well D) 答非所问

sticking to one's judgments even when proved wrong 用了 judgments 一词，但说的是"被证明错了仍坚持"，是事后固执；原文定义说的是"了解之前"就下判断，是事前，与原文相反/错位。 借⽤原⽂： prejudice means to judge before having adequate knowledge
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker say prejudiced attitudes are dangerous?

options.text: They often lead to war between religious groups.
They keep certain occupations from thriving.
They allow myths and half-truths to persist.
They prevent us from getting to the truth.

questions.shortExplanation: Prejudiced attitudes are usually based on myths, half-truths or incorrect information, and they are dangerous because they can keep us from learning the truth about someone or something.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） They prevent us from getting to the truth.

【定位】 Prejudiced attitudes are usually based on myths, half-truths or incorrect information, and they are dangerous because they can keep us from learning the truth about someone or something.

偏见态度通常建立在谬误、半真半假的说法或错误信息之上，它们之所以危险，是因为它们会妨碍我们了解关于某人或某物的真相。

【信号】 dangerous because因果信号。they are dangerous because they can keep us from learning the truth 里 dangerous 后跟 because，因果信号直接把"危险的原因"端出来， because 之后那半句就是答案句。

【替换】 keep us from learning the truth↔prevent us from getting to the truth keep from=prevent from且learning=getting to

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

war between religious groups 借了原文 religion/后文 religious 的影子，但原文此处说危害是"妨碍了解真相"，并未说偏见"导致宗教群体间的战争"；战争是过度引申，原文只说极端偏见 caused deaths，没说"宗教群体间开战"。 借⽤原⽂： differences in their race, religion, gender, or occupation B) 张冠李戴

keep certain occupations from thriving 蹭了原文 occupation 一词，但原文说偏见 keep people apart（让人彼此疏远），第三段说妨碍人 getting a job or a promotion（找工作/晋升），从没说让"某些职业无法繁荣"，属张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： from getting a job or a promotion C) 原词陷阱

allow myths and half-truths to persist 直接盗用原文 myths, half-truths，极具迷惑性； 但原文说偏见是"基于（based on）myths/half-truths"，谬误是偏见的成因/来源，不是 because 后给出的"危险原因"，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： Prejudiced attitudes are usually based on myths, half-truths or incorrect information

questions.prompt: When does the speaker say we begin to develop prejudiced attitudes?

options.text: When we start to feel superior.
When we mix with prejudiced people.
When we live in an isolated neighborhood.
When we try to keep up with those around us.

questions.shortExplanation: If feelings of pride begin to turn to feelings of superiority when we think that our group or our beliefs are better than those around us, however, then we begin to develop prejudiced attitudes that can be harmful.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） When we start to feel superior.

【定位】 If feelings of pride begin to turn to feelings of superiority when we think that our group or our beliefs are better than those around us, however, then we begin to develop prejudiced attitudes that can be harmful.

如果自豪感开始转变为优越感——当我们认为自己的群体或信念比周围人更好时——然而， 那时我们就开始发展出可能有害的偏见态度。

【信号】 If…turn to superiority条件信号。If feelings of pride begin to turn to feelings of superiority 用 If 引出条件、then we begin to develop prejudiced attitudes 给出结果， 这个"条件→产生偏见"的因果/条件信号让它成为答案句。

【替换】 feelings of pride begin to turn to feelings of superiority ↔ When we start to feel superior turn to feelings of superiority=start to feel superior

【排除】 B) 未提及

When we mix with prejudiced people（与有偏见的人来往时）听上去合理，但原文给的触发条件是"自豪转为优越感"，从没说"和有偏见的人相处"会让我们产生偏见，属未提及。 C) 原词陷阱

live in an isolated neighborhood 盗用了原文 living in any neighborhood 的 neighborhood 一词；但原文里 neighborhood 出现在"偏见使某群体无法随意居住"的危害举例中，是偏见的后果，不是产生偏见的条件，张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： from living in any neighborhood they want D) 与原文相反

When we try to keep up with those around us（努力跟上周围人）与原文 better than those around us（觉得自己比周围人更好）方向相反：原文是"自觉高人一等"，选项却是"努力追赶别人"，与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： our group or our beliefs are better than those around us

items.title: 2022年12月六级第2套 · 讲座与讲话 3
items.transcript:
When I started high school, it was a shock. I had spent eight years fighting my way to be the most popular kid in the Catholic school student body. I had been a big, tough 8th grader and suddenly I was a lonely 9th grader bullied by the big, tough 12th grade seniors who ran the high school. I realized then that it's nice to strive for something, but that you also have to enjoy the moment you're in and be happy where you are. Rock and roll had always been an important part of my life. I remember my friends and I used to drive around until the late hours of the nights listening to the music of Rock and Roll legends. During those teenage years, I built friendships that I thought would last a lifetime. Most people that age think the same thing, but people drift apart. Jobs, families and tragedies separate people from those lasting friendships.

The tragedy that separated me from my friends forever was the Vietnam War. A year after I graduated from high school, I left for Vietnam. I came back, burned out, and tired, as though I had lived 10 lifetimes in the short span of 14 months, the 14 months I was in the war. I couldn't relate to the friends I had had in high school. They still seemed childish, concerned with childish things that weren't important to me. I was still trying to cope with the death, destruction and evil I had seen in Vietnam. I felt like we had done terrible things to innocent people there and in turn, I had seen terrible things done to my friends.

I withdrew from my friends and started college. Then I quit college and took many different jobs. I spent a lot of my time and money on alcohol and other drugs. Finally, in an effort to get my life going in the right direction again, I sold everything and took what little money I had and bought myself an airplane ticket to Israel. I went there to study history. While studying at Haifa University, I met my wife, who was also an American student.

I now teach in a high school back in America. I look at my students and see them struggling with many of the very things I struggled with many years ago. As a teacher, I try to help them over the rough spots as best I can.

questions.prompt: How did the speaker feel when he started high school?

options.text: Motivated.
Disappointed.
Perplexed.
Shocked.

questions.shortExplanation: When I started high school, it was a shock.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （态度观点题） Shocked.

【定位】 When I started high school, it was a shock.

我上高中的时候，那真是一记冲击。

【信号】 直陈感受句 it was a shock。开篇第一句 it was a shock 就用 it was + 情绪名词直接定调入学感受，这种讲者自陈心情的句子就是态度题的答案句。

【替换】 it was a shock↔ Shocked.

名词 shock 转形容词 Shocked

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

Motivated. 是被激励的积极情绪，而原文 it was a shock 是负面冲击，方向相反。 借⽤原⽂： it was a shock B) 偷换概念

Disappointed. 是失望，原文是 shock（震惊冲击），二者都偏负面但情绪类型不同，原文没有“期望落空”的意思。

C) 偷换概念

Perplexed. 是困惑、想不明白，原文 shock 强调的是突然的强烈冲击，并非智力上的困惑。

questions.prompt: What did the speaker once think of teenage friendships?

options.text: They would change with the passage of time.
They would benefit young people's adult life.
They would help kids grow.
They would last a lifetime.

questions.shortExplanation: During those teenage years, I built friendships that I thought would last a lifetime. 在那些青少年岁月里，我建立了一些我以为会维系一辈子的友谊。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） They would last a lifetime.

【定位】 During those teenage years, I built friendships that I thought would last a lifetime. 在那些青少年岁月里，我建立了一些我以为会维系一辈子的友谊。

【信号】 I thought 引出当初的判断。that I thought would last a lifetime 里的 I thought（我当初以为）正对题干的 once think，是讲者亲口给出的当年看法，定为答案句。

【替换】 would last a lifetime↔They would last a lifetime. 几乎原句照搬

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

They would change with the passage of time. 说友谊会随时间改变，这恰恰是讲者后来才发现的现实（people drift apart），不是他当初 thought 的看法，张冠李戴了时间点。 借⽤原⽂： people drift apart B) 未提及

They would benefit young people's adult life. 谈友谊对成年生活的好处，录音只说他以为友谊会持久，从未谈“对成年生活有益”，属无中生有。 C) 未提及

They would help kids grow. 说友谊帮孩子成长，录音里讲者对青少年友谊的判断只有“会持续一辈子”，没有“助成长”这一层。
