questions.prompt: What do we learn about the speaker when he returned from the Vietnam War?

options.text: He had become mature.
He suffered poor health.
He had lots of stories to tell.
He regretted leaving Vietnam.

questions.shortExplanation: I couldn't relate to the friends I had had in high school. They still seemed childish, concerned with childish things that weren't important to me. 我没法再和高中时的那些朋友产生共鸣了。他们在我看来还是很幼稚，只在意一些对我而言已不重要的幼稚事情。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （推断题） He had become mature.

【定位】 I couldn't relate to the friends I had had in high school. They still seemed childish, concerned with childish things that weren't important to me. 我没法再和高中时的那些朋友产生共鸣了。他们在我看来还是很幼稚，只在意一些对我而言已不重要的幼稚事情。

【信号】 以朋友的“幼稚”反衬自己的成熟。讲者说朋友 still seemed childish、还在关心 childish things that weren't important to me，用对方的幼稚反衬出自己已经变了——经历战争后心智超前于同龄人，这处对比就是归纳点。

【替换】 They still seemed childish, concerned with childish things that weren't important to me↔ He had become mature. “别人幼稚”反向等于“我成熟”

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

讲者说自己 burned out, and tired，He suffered poor health. 盗用这种“累、垮”的字眼当身体得病，但 burned out 指心力交瘁，原文并未说他身体患病。 借⽤原⽂： burned out, and tired C) 过度推断

He had lots of stories to tell. 看似贴合“经历越战、活了十辈子”，但原文 as though I had lived 10 lifetimes 是形容沧桑成熟，不是说他爱讲故事、有谈资，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： as though I had lived 10 lifetimes

D) 未提及 He regretted leaving Vietnam. 说他后悔离开越南，原文只讲他对在越南的所见所为感到痛苦，从没说后悔离开那里，属无中生有且方向也不对。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker try to do as a teacher?

options.text: Make friends with his students.
Show his students how to do their best.
Help his students get through the growing pains.
Share his personal experience with his students.

questions.shortExplanation: I look at my students and see them struggling with many of the very things I struggled with many years ago. As a teacher, I try to help them over the rough spots as best I can.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （目的题） Help his students get through the growing pains.

【定位】 I look at my students and see them struggling with many of the very things I struggled with many years ago. As a teacher, I try to help them over the rough spots as best I can.

我看着我的学生，看到他们正为许多当年我也挣扎过的同样的事而苦苦挣扎。作为一名老师，我尽我所能帮他们渡过那些艰难的关口。

【信号】 As a teacher, I try to… 的收束主句。结尾 As a teacher, I try to help them over the rough spots 用 I try to help… 直陈自己当老师的做法，是全篇落点句，正对题干 try to do。

【替换】 help them over the rough spots↔ Help his students get through the growing pains. rough spots = growing pains struggling with many of the very things I struggled with↔ Help his students get through the growing pains.

学生的挣扎即成长之痛

【排除】 A) 未提及

Make friends with his students. 说和学生交朋友，结尾只说 I try to help them over the rough spots（帮他们渡难关），从没说要与学生做朋友，无中生有。

B) 偷换概念

Show his students how to do their best. 说教学生如何做到最好，原文是 help…over the rough spots（帮他们渡过难关），偏向陪伴扶持，不是示范如何取得最好表现，偷换了做法。 D) 原词陷阱

Share his personal experience with his students. 借前文大段个人经历制造诱惑，但结尾的做法是 help them over the rough spots，是“帮”不是“讲给学生听”，他回顾经历只为解释自己懂学生的处境，并未说要把经历分享给学生，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： I look at my students and see them struggling with many of the very things I struggled with many years ago

items.title: 2022年6月六级第1套 · 长对话 1
items.transcript:
W: Mr. David Jackson, a staff writer at the New Yorker, is known for his non-fiction books of adventure. Today, we go on a different kind of adventure: Jackson's life of parenting his offspring. David, as a parent of an 11- and a 14-year-old, what is the most interesting issue you are dealing with right now?

M: It's easy to focus on the challenges, but so far, I find these ages to be kind of wonderful. They are independent, and they have their own curiosities and obsessions. You can talk to them about fairly sophisticated subject matter such as politics.

W: Yes, that does sound refreshing compared with talking to younger children. Do they ask you to proofread their essays?

M: Certainly, with writing they do. I really just try to be encouraging. I think at this age, editorial guidance is less important than encouragement.

W: Are there books that you think are important that your children read, and that all children read?

M: My general thought is to read widely and to incorporate a love for reading. Learning to love to read, I think, is the optimal thing, because it gives you a skill you can take anywhere.

W: So you're not too concerned like some parents with the content they're reading? I know I have some worries about that.

M: Yeah, read what you like. If a child loves graphic novels or comic books, whatever it is, that is turning them on to read and turning on their imagination.

W: I feel that children's tastes in books change as they reach adolescence. I know that mine certainly did when I was a teenager. What do you think?

M: I think it's especially important as they get older to read subject matter that'll open their eyes to the world and people. So I think both fiction and non-fiction are really important because they give you the power to begin to perceive the world through the lives of others.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about David Jackson from the conversation?

options.text: He is a staff writer.
He is an adventurer.
He is an author of fiction.
He is a father of four kids.

questions.shortExplanation: Mr. David Jackson, a staff writer at the New Yorker, is known for his non-fiction books of adventure. David Jackson 先生，《纽约客》的专职撰稿人，以其纪实类冒险题材的书而闻名。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） He is a staff writer.

【定位】 Mr. David Jackson, a staff writer at the New Yorker, is known for his non-fiction books of adventure. David Jackson 先生，《纽约客》的专职撰稿人，以其纪实类冒险题材的书而闻名。

【信号】 开场介绍句直接报身份。主持人开场第一句就用同位语把人物头衔报全：a staff writer at the New Yorker。人物介绍题的答案信号就是这种"姓名 + 同位语头衔"的引入句，听到立刻锁定。

【替换】 a staff writer at the New Yorker↔He is a staff writer.

原句同位语→选项主系表，几乎原词对应

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

原文说他 is known for his non-fiction books of adventure——写冒险题材的书，是"写冒险的人"不是"亲历冒险的人"。He is an adventurer. 盗用 adventure 一词，把"写冒险书"偷换成"他本人是冒险家"，听到 adventure 就选会中招。 借⽤原⽂： is known for his non-fiction books of adventure C) 与原文相反

原文明确是 non-fiction books（纪实/非虚构），He is an author of fiction. 却说他写 fiction（虚构小说），正好把 non-fiction 的 non 抹掉、极性反了。听到 fiction 这半个原词就选，等于没听清前面的否定前缀。 借⽤原⽂： non-fiction books of adventure D) 未提及

原文只说他有 an 11- and a 14-year-old（一个 11 岁、一个 14 岁，共两个孩子），He is a father of four kids. 凭空说"四个孩子"。four 这个数字原文从未出现，是偷改数字的陷阱。

【答案】 B （态度观点题） They are curious and autonomous.

【定位】 They are independent, and they have their own curiosities and obsessions. 他们很独立，有自己的好奇心和着迷的东西。

【信号】 被问者的正面评价应答。女方问他这阶段孩子的情况，男方应答先说 I find these ages to be kind of wonderful，再具体说 They are independent, and they have their own curiosities。对话题答案落在被问者的应答里，wonderful 与 independent、curiosities 是定调的正面信号。

【替换】 They are independent↔ They are curious and autonomous. independent=autonomous 同义替换 their own curiosities↔curious

名词 curiosities→形容词 curious 词形转换

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

原文说能和孩子聊 sophisticated subject matter such as politics，即谈"成熟话题如政治"，反衬他们不幼稚；They are interested in fairy tales. 童话与原文要表达的"能聊成熟话题"恰恰相反，且 fairy tales 原文根本没提，是借"孩子"语境硬造的话题。 借⽤原⽂： sophisticated subject matter such as politics C) 与原文相反

男方明明说 I find these ages to be kind of wonderful（觉得这年纪很好），They are a headache to their parents. 却说孩子让父母头疼，与他的正面评价完全相反。这是把褒义答案反向设成贬义的陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： I find these ages to be kind of wonderful

D) 原词陷阱

原文说能和孩子聊 politics，恰恰说明他们"懂/能聊政治"；They are ignorant of politics. 盗用 politics 原词，却说他们"对政治无知"，意思正好反过来。听到 politics 就选会直接掉坑。 借⽤原⽂： such as politics
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: How does the man help his kids with their essays?

options.text: He offers them ample editorial guidance.
He recommends model essays to them.
He gives them encouragement.
He teaches them proofreading.

questions.shortExplanation: I really just try to be encouraging. I think at this age, editorial guidance is less important than encouragement.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） He gives them encouragement.

【定位】 I really just try to be encouraging. I think at this age, editorial guidance is less important than encouragement.

我真的只是尽量给予鼓励。我觉得在这个年纪，编辑式的指导不如鼓励来得重要。

【信号】 取舍句 less important than 落在后半。男方先表态 I really just try to be encouraging，再用取舍句 editorial guidance is less important than encouragement。"A is less important than B" 的信号是：被贬低的 A（指导）是陪衬， 强调的 B（鼓励）才是答案。

【替换】 I really just try to be encouraging↔He gives them encouragement. be encouraging→give encouragement 形容词转名词

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

选项 He offers them ample editorial guidance. 盗用原文 editorial guidance 原词，可原文恰恰说它 less important than encouragement——他不强调指导。听到 editorial guidance 就选，正好掉进"被贬低项"的坑，且 ample（大量）更与他"只是尽量鼓励"的克制相反。 借⽤原⽂： editorial guidance is less important than encouragement

B) 未提及 He recommends model essays to them. 借了 essays 这个语境词（女方确实问到 proofread their essays），但"推荐范文（model essays）"这件事男方从没说过，是凭"帮写作"语境硬造的做法。

D) 张冠李戴

proofread 这个词确实出现，但它出自女方提问 Do they ask you to proofread their essays?，是"孩子请他校对"，并非"他教孩子校对"。He teaches them proofreading. 把女方问句里的词搬来、又改成"他教校对"，既盗原词又错了施动方。 借⽤原⽂： Do they ask you to proofread their essays?
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about herself when she was a teenager?

options.text: Her tastes in books changed.
She realized the power of reading.
Her reading opened her eyes to the world.
She began to perceive the world differently.

questions.shortExplanation: I feel that children's tastes in books change as they reach adolescence. I know that mine certainly did when I was a teenager.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Her tastes in books changed.

【定位】 I feel that children's tastes in books change as they reach adolescence. I know that mine certainly did when I was a teenager.

我觉得孩子的读书口味会随着进入青春期而改变。我知道我自己当年读中学时口味确实变了。

【信号】 mine + when I was a teenager 锁定她谈自己。女方说 I know that mine certainly did when I was a teenager，mine 回指 tastes in books，when I was a teenager 正对题干限定。第一人称 mine/I 加"少年时"，是"她说自己"的答案信号。

【替换】 children's tastes in books change ↔ Her tastes in books changed. mine did 还原为 her tastes changed

【排除】 B) 张冠李戴 She realized the power of reading. 里的 power 出自男方 they give you the power to begin to perceive the world，是男方谈读书的话，不是女方说自己；且女方从没说她"意识到读书的力量"。既错主语又属未提及。 借⽤原⽂： they give you the power to begin to perceive the world C) 张冠李戴

Her reading opened her eyes to the world. 盗用男方 read subject matter that'll open their eyes to the world 的原词 open eyes to the world，但这是男方对"孩子该读什么"的看法，主语既不是"她"、内容也非她自述。听到 open eyes 就选会被男方的话误导。 借⽤原⽂： open their eyes to the world D) 原词陷阱

She began to perceive the world differently. 盗用男方 to perceive the world through the lives of others 的 perceive the world，但这同样是男方对读书意义的论述，非女方谈自己。与 C 是一对孪生干扰，靠"主语是谁"才能切开。 借⽤原⽂： perceive the world through the lives of others

items.title: 2022年6月六级第1套 · 长对话 2
items.transcript:
M: In this episode of Money Talks, our guest is Molly Sanders, a university student and a successful young entrepreneur. Molly, tell us about your business.

W: Well, I sell specialty clothes through a website, mainly for women who have trouble finding suitable clothes in main street shops because of their height or weight. But I do some men's clothes too.

M: How did you get started in this business at such a young age? Are you studying fashion design?

W: Actually, I'm majoring in finance, but I've always loved clothes. And I started making my own at 14.

M: Did you have any sort of training in design or sewing? Or was it a natural ability?

W: I'd have to say no to both. No one taught me to make clothes and most of the things I made at first were disasters.

M: Why did you persevere? I think most people would give up if they kept failing, especially at that age.

W: I kept on out of necessity. As you can see, I'm very tall and I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops. So I kept trying and developed my skills over time.

M: Well, my notes say you earned $50,000 in profits last year, an extraordinary amount for a 20-year-old student. How did that happen? Did you see a gap in the market and decide to fill it?

W: No. When I started university, some classmates complimented my clothes. And when I said I made them myself, other tall women started asking if I would make theirs. And I did. And before I knew it, I was an entrepreneur.

M: So what are your plans for the future? Do you intend to open a physical store?

W: No. I'll keep things online to keep costs down. But I will add more clothes for children, both girls and boys, and possibly even for infants. And I hope to add to my range of designs for men.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the woman?

options.text: She is a website designer.
She is a university graduate.
She is a main street store owner.
She is a successful entrepreneur.

questions.shortExplanation: In this episode of Money Talks, our guest is Molly Sanders, a university student and a successful young entrepreneur.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） She is a successful entrepreneur.

【定位】 In this episode of Money Talks, our guest is Molly Sanders, a university student and a successful young entrepreneur.

在本期《财富对话》中，我们的嘉宾是莫莉·桑德斯，一名大学生，也是一位成功的年轻创业者。

【信号】 主持人开场介绍嘉宾的同位语。答案信号是开场白里介绍嘉宾身份的同位语 a university student and a successful young entrepreneur——访谈类听力里，嘉宾身份几乎都在主持人开场这句 our guest is… 后面交代。

【替换】 a successful young entrepreneur↔She is a successful entrepreneur. 近乎同词，只省去 young

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

录音确实说她是 a university student，She is a university graduate. 借此设套；但一来题问我们了解到什么，主持人重点捧的是 successful entrepreneur，二来 student（在读）不等于 graduate（已毕业），身份还被偷改了。 借⽤原⽂： a university student A) 过度推断

后文她说 I sell specialty clothes through a website，但用网站卖衣服不等于她是做网站的设计师，She is a website designer. 是从 website 一词过度联想出来的。 借⽤原⽂： I sell specialty clothes through a website

C) 与原文相反

她明确说将来 I'll keep things online to keep costs down，根本不开实体店，She is a main street store owner. 与原文相反；main street 还是她顾客买不到衣服的地方，并非她开店之处。 借⽤原⽂： I'll keep things online to keep costs down
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about the clothes she made at first?

options.text: They were repeatedly rejected by shops.
They were popular with her classmates.
They showed her natural talent.
They were mostly failures.

questions.shortExplanation: No one taught me to make clothes and most of the things I made at first were disasters.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） They were mostly failures.

【定位】 No one taught me to make clothes and most of the things I made at first were disasters.

没人教过我做衣服，而且我最初做的大多数东西都是惨不忍睹的失败品。

【信号】 被问者直接应答里的自我评价词。主持人问她是否有天赋，她应答中的 most of the things I made at first were disasters 是直接评价句，disasters 这个强贬义词就是答案信号。

【替换】 were disasters↔ They were mostly failures.

disasters 约等于 failures 的同义替换

【排除】 C) 原词陷阱

主持人问 Or was it a natural ability?，They showed her natural talent. 盗用了 natural 一词；但她明确回答 I'd have to say no to both（天赋、培训都没有），所以显出天赋恰与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： Or was it a natural ability? A) 未提及

They were repeatedly rejected by shops. 听着像创业故事，但录音从没说她最初的衣服被商店反复拒收；她说的是顾客在 main street shops 买不到合身的，张冠李戴了。

B) 张冠李戴

同学称赞她衣服确有其事——some classmates complimented my clothes，They were popular with her classmates. 借此设套；但那是她上大学后的事，不是最初（14岁）做的，时间错位。 借⽤原⽂： some classmates complimented my clothes
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: Why did the woman persevere in making clothes for herself?

options.text: She had a strong interest in doing it.
She did not like ready-made clothes.
She could not find clothes of her size.
She found clothes in shops unaffordable.

questions.shortExplanation: I kept on out of necessity. As you can see, I'm very tall and I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops. 我是出于无奈才坚持下来的。如你所见，我个子很高，在普通商店里找不到合身的衣服。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） She could not find clothes of her size.

【定位】 I kept on out of necessity. As you can see, I'm very tall and I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops. 我是出于无奈才坚持下来的。如你所见，我个子很高，在普通商店里找不到合身的衣服。

【信号】 原因短语 out of necessity 引出理由。答案信号是因果短语 out of necessity（出于必需），其后紧跟的 I'm very tall and I couldn't find clothes that fit me 就是真正原因。

【替换】 I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops↔She could not find clothes of her size.

fit me 约等于 of her size 的同义改写

【排除】 A) 答非所问

她确说过 I've always loved clothes，She had a strong interest in doing it. 借喜爱设套；但那解释的是她为何开始做衣服，题问的是为何坚持，她坚持的理由是无奈，不是兴趣。 借⽤原⽂： I've always loved clothes D) 未提及

She found clothes in shops unaffordable. 与C都涉及商店的衣服，迷惑性强；但录音说的是找不到合身的，从未提到买不起、太贵，价格问题纯属杜撰。

B) 未提及

She did not like ready-made clothes. 听着合理，但录音只说商店里没有合她身的，从没说她不喜欢现成衣服；她做衣服是因买不到，不是因厌恶成衣。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the woman plan to do in the future?

options.text: Study fashion design at college.
Improve her marketing strategy.
Add designs for women.
Expand her business.

questions.shortExplanation: But I will add more clothes for children, both girls and boys, and possibly even for infants. And I hope to add to my range of designs for men. 不过我会增加儿童服装，男孩女孩都做，可能还会做婴幼儿的。我也希望扩充我给男士设计的产品线。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Expand her business.

【定位】 But I will add more clothes for children, both girls and boys, and possibly even for infants. And I hope to add to my range of designs for men. 不过我会增加儿童服装，男孩女孩都做，可能还会做婴幼儿的。我也希望扩充我给男士设计的产品线。

【信号】 将来意图信号 I will 与 I hope to。答案信号是 I will add more clothes for children 与 I hope to add to my range of designs for men 里的 will、hope to——它们标志将来计划，后接的增加品类即答案。

【替换】 add more clothes for children↔Expand her business. 具体加品类等于概括的扩展生意

【排除】 C) 偷换概念

她确说 add to my range of designs for men，Add designs for women. 却把对象由 men（男士）偷换成 women（女士），方向都改错了，且她加的远不止男装。 借⽤原⽂： add to my range of designs for men A) 原词陷阱

前文主持人问 Are you studying fashion design?，Study fashion design at college. 盗用了 fashion design；但她回答 I'm majoring in finance，学的是金融，更没把学时装设计当未来计划。 借⽤原⽂： Are you studying fashion design? B) 未提及

Improve her marketing strategy. 听着像生意人会做的事，但录音谈未来时只说加品类、 保持线上控成本，从没提改进营销策略。

items.title: 2022年6月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 1
items.transcript:
Researchers have identified a potent new antibiotic compound using artificial intelligence. The antibiotic can kill very dangerous bacteria. According to a study published in the journal Cell, the compound successfully removed deadly strains of bacteria in mice which are resistant to all known antibiotics.

The researchers say this is the first time that artificial intelligence has been used to find a powerful new antibiotic molecule. Why does this matter? The answer is antibiotic resistance. This happens when bacteria develop the ability to survive the medications designed to kill them. Antibiotic resistance is a serious threat to health and the problem is growing. This makes finding new antibiotics very important. However, in recent decades, very few have been developed, and those that have tend to be very similar to drugs already available. The searches also tend to only focus on a narrow spectrum of chemical compounds, but this is where artificial intelligence comes in. Why? To find new drugs, scientists screen molecules to predict how effective they might be. Typically, such screening is done by humans in the lab, which is both costly and slow. Artificial intelligence is different. It's fast, and it can process a high volume. It can screen hundreds of millions of compounds to identify a few interesting candidates that require experimental testing. Artificial intelligence is also able to predict if compounds are likely to be toxic. Some experts assert that this work signifies a paradigm shift in antibiotic discovery. It could change drug discovery more generally.

questions.prompt: What have researchers done for the first time in history?

options.text: Utilizing artificial intelligence to find a powerful new antibiotic.
Discovering bacteria which are resistant to all known antibiotics.
Identifying bacterial strains that are most harmful to human health.
Removing a deadly strain of bacteria in humans with a new antibiotic.

questions.shortExplanation: The researchers say this is the first time that artificial intelligence has been used to find a powerful new antibiotic molecule. 研究者表示，这是首次有人用人工智能来发现一种强效的新型抗生素分子。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Utilizing artificial intelligence to find a powerful new antibiotic.

【定位】 The researchers say this is the first time that artificial intelligence has been used to find a powerful new antibiotic molecule. 研究者表示，这是首次有人用人工智能来发现一种强效的新型抗生素分子。

【信号】 first time 与题干同标志。录音里 this is the first time that artificial intelligence has been used to find a powerful new antibiotic molecule 出现了与题干 for the first time 完全对应的标志短语 the first time，听到这个标志就锁定这句是答案句。

【替换】 artificial intelligence has been used to find a powerful new antibiotic molecule↔ Utilizing artificial intelligence to find a powerful new antibiotic 被动转主动/同义改写

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

B 项 Discovering bacteria which are resistant to all known antibiotics 盗用了录音第一段 resistant to all known antibiotics 这串原词，但录音说的是新抗生素清除了这些耐药菌、不是去发现耐药菌，听到熟悉的 resistant 就选会落入陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： resistant to all known antibiotics C) 未提及

C 项 Identifying bacterial strains that are most harmful to human health 说识别最有害的菌株，录音通篇没说研究者去给菌株按危害排序或识别哪种最有害，属未提及。

D) 原词陷阱

D 项 Removing a deadly strain of bacteria in humans with a new antibiotic 盗用了第一段 removed deadly strains of bacteria 的原词，但录音说清除发生在 in mice（小鼠） 身上、不是 in humans，且本题问的首次成就是用 AI 找药、不是清除细菌，原词对、主体与考点都错。 借⽤原⽂： removed deadly strains of bacteria in mice
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What makes it important to find new antibiotic drugs?

options.text: Ever-increasing strains of bacteria.
Bacteria's resistance to antibiotics.
The similarity between known drugs.
The growing threat of bacteria to health.

questions.shortExplanation: Why does this matter? The answer is antibiotic resistance. This happens when bacteria develop the ability to survive the medications designed to kill them. 这为什么重要？答案是抗生素耐药性。当细菌发展出在那些本该杀死它们的药物下存活的能力时，耐药性就出现了。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Bacteria's resistance to antibiotics.

【定位】 Why does this matter? The answer is antibiotic resistance. This happens when bacteria develop the ability to survive the medications designed to kill them. 这为什么重要？答案是抗生素耐药性。当细菌发展出在那些本该杀死它们的药物下存活的能力时，耐药性就出现了。

【信号】 自问自答的因果信号。录音用一个自设问 Why does this matter? 紧跟一句直答 The answer is antibiotic resistance，这种自问自答正是篇章独白明示原因的强信号，答案就藏在 The answer is 之后。

【替换】 The answer is antibiotic resistance↔Bacteria's resistance to antibiotics

同义短语换序表述

【排除】 A) 未提及

A 项 Ever-increasing strains of bacteria 说细菌菌株不断增多，录音只说耐药性问题在加重（the problem is growing），从未说菌株数量在增加，属未提及。

C) 原词陷阱

C 项 The similarity between known drugs 盗用了录音 tend to be very similar to drugs already available 里的 similar，但录音说新药彼此相似是研发不足的表现、不是让找新药变重要的原因，原词对、角色错。 借⽤原⽂： tend to be very similar to drugs already available D) 偷换概念

D 项 The growing threat of bacteria to health 盗用了录音 Antibiotic resistance is a serious threat to health and the problem is growing 里的 threat 与 growing，但录音说的是耐药性对健康是威胁、主语是耐药性，选项却换成 bacteria 对健康的威胁，把本题原因从耐药性偷换成笼统的细菌威胁。 借⽤原⽂： Antibiotic resistance is a serious threat to health and the problem is growing
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the passage say artificial intelligence is able to do in antibiotic research?

options.text: Dispense with experimental testing.
Predict whether compounds are toxic.
Foresee human reaction to antibiotics.
Combat bacteria's resistance to antibiotics.

questions.shortExplanation: Artificial intelligence is also able to predict if compounds are likely to be toxic. 人工智能还能够预测某些化合物是否可能有毒。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Predict whether compounds are toxic.

【定位】 Artificial intelligence is also able to predict if compounds are likely to be toxic. 人工智能还能够预测某些化合物是否可能有毒。

【信号】 able to 直陈功能。录音 Artificial intelligence is also able to predict if compounds are likely to be toxic 里 is also able to 与题干 is able to 直接呼应，是明示 AI 一项能力的功能句，听到 able to 即锁定。

【替换】 predict if compounds are likely to be toxic↔Predict whether compounds are toxic

if 换 whether 的近原词改写

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

items.title: 2022年6月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 2
items.transcript:
A recent study overturned what we think we know about lying. Most of us have a theory about how to tell if someone is telling a lie. We may develop that theory from observations of those people we know well and see regularly, but we tend to generalize what we gather from that unscientific daily research and make it a universal theory.

So we might imagine that liars have evasive eyes, or the opposite—they simply stare at you. Or perhaps it is more generally nervous behavior we associate with lies. Whatever the particular theory, it's usually based on close observation of people we know. And we get lots of practice. On average, we're lied to some 200 times per day. These are mostly harmless lies, but lies nonetheless.

But there's a problem with our theories, even though they're based on all these observations. The average person—you and me—tested rigorously on how well we detect lies fails to do better than chance. That's well established over many studies and lots of attempts by researchers to work out reliable ways to detect lies. It's even relatively easy to fool lie detectors, the gold standard of lie detection, by training yourself in breathing techniques and symptom suppression.

Is there any way to get better at detecting lies? The new research offers some surprising advice. Stop looking and listen instead. It turns out that if we're unable to see the face, but rather focus on the voice of the person in question, our accuracy rate improves considerably.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how do most people detect lying?

options.text: By theorization.
By generalization.
By observation.
By conversation.

questions.shortExplanation: We may develop that theory from observations of those people we know well and see regularly, but we tend to generalize what we gather from that unscientific daily research and make it a universal theory. 我们可能是从对身边熟识、常见之人的观察中形成那套"看人说谎"的理论的，但我们往往会把从这种不科学的日常观察里得来的东西加以归纳，把它当成放之四海皆准的理论。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） By observation.

【定位】 We may develop that theory from observations of those people we know well and see regularly, but we tend to generalize what we gather from that unscientific daily research and make it a universal theory. 我们可能是从对身边熟识、常见之人的观察中形成那套"看人说谎"的理论的，但我们往往会把从这种不科学的日常观察里得来的东西加以归纳，把它当成放之四海皆准的理论。

【信号】 起源信号 develop … from。develop that theory from observations 里的 develop … from 点明"这套判断说谎的理论来自哪里"，正是"靠什么方式"的答案落点；后面虽有 generalize，但那是把观察所得再加工，最初的获取方式仍是 observations。

【替换】 from observations of those people we know well↔ By observation. 复数 observations 概括为 observation

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

录音反复出现 theory、universal theory，A 项 By theorization.（靠理论化）就是拿这个原词来骗；但录音说理论是"从观察中得来"，获取方式是观察，不是"靠理论化"去判断说谎。 借⽤原⽂： make it a universal theory B) 原词陷阱

录音确实说了 we tend to generalize，B 项 By generalization. 就盗这个词；但 generalize 是"把观察所得再归纳推广"的后续动作，不是"多数人最初靠什么发现说谎"—— 题问的是 detect 的方式，那是观察。 借⽤原⽂： we tend to generalize what we gather D) 未提及 By conversation.（靠交谈）与 observation 词形相近，最易听混，但录音通篇没说人们靠"交谈"来识谎，属未提及。

items.title: 2022年6月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 1
items.transcript:
Appear to be submissive, humble, grateful and undemanding; show great pleasure when a doctor comes into your room, even if the visit is brief and useless. Don't challenge anyone with authority unless you are famous or very rich.

Those are a few strategies for dealing with today's American medical establishment. What patients want is to be treated with respect and consideration. But in my experience, too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that. In his book, A Whole New Life, novelist Reynolds Price recalls that his doctors chose a crowded hallway as the place to tell him he might have a tumor on his spinal cord. It did not occur to the two physicians that a hallway was not the most appropriate place for that particular piece of news.

My surgeon, who is in his mid-thirties, looks tired. He has been overwhelmed with patients who have fallen on the winter ice. He is a witty man, but sometimes his wit is unwelcome.

"The health insurance company Blue Cross wants me to put you out in the snow tomorrow afternoon," he tells me after I have been in the hospital for more than a week. I'm terrified because I have no idea where to go. I cannot walk or even lift my leg a few inches. The hospital social worker strikes me as an idiot. But my complaints about her only annoy my surgeon. "I have to work with these people," he tells my friend, Dr. Karen Brudney, when she mercifully intervenes on my behalf and arranges for me to be transferred to another hospital.

"If you say one negative thing, they get defensive," she tells me later. "They have this kind of institutional loyalty. Always bring an advocate, that is, any other person with you to the hospital, and write down every single question and the answer, the name of every doctor and nurse. When people know you have their names, they behave better. And," Brudney adds, "if you, as a patient, suggest that you might like to control even part of the situation or be consulted or informed, then you are considered difficult. They want you to be totally passive. The entire health care system, particularly hospitals and nursing homes, exists for reasons that have nothing to do with taking care of patients. Patients are incidental."

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about most American hospitals?

options.text: They don't treat patients with due respect.
They witness a lot of doctor-patient conflicts.
They have to deal with social workers' strikes.
They don't care how much patients have to pay.

questions.shortExplanation: What patients want is to be treated with respect and consideration. But in my experience, too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （态度观点题） They don't treat patients with due respect.

【定位】 What patients want is to be treated with respect and consideration. But in my experience, too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that.

病人想要的是被尊重、被体谅地对待。但据我的经验，愿意这样做的医院和医生太少了。

【信号】 转折 But + 程度词 too few。答案落在转折词后：But in my experience, too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that。前半句说『病人想被尊重』是铺垫，But 之后才是主讲人的真实判断——能做到的医院太少，这正是定性句。

【替换】 too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that↔They don't treat patients with due respect. 肯否定转换：很少做到=不做到 treated with respect and consideration↔with due respect

同义改写：respect=due respect

【排除】 B) 未提及

They witness a lot of doctor-patient conflicts. 借用了全篇的医患话题，听着像在讲医患关系，但原文只说医院少有尊重病人，从没说医院『目睹大量医患冲突』，属于顺着话题硬编。

C) 原词陷阱 They have to deal with social workers' strikes. 盗了后文出现的 social worker 一词，制造『听到原词就想选』的诱惑。但原文 The hospital social worker strikes me as an idiot 里 strikes 是『让我觉得』之意（strike sb as），与『罢工 strike』完全无关，且这是讲个人遭遇，不是医院的总体特征。 借⽤原⽂： The hospital social worker strikes me as an idiot D) 未提及

They don't care how much patients have to pay. 把话题引向『收费』，但全篇主讲人谈的是尊重、知情、被动顺从，从未谈医院在不在乎病人花多少钱，费用维度是凭空添加的。

questions.prompt: What does Karen Brudney suggest patients do?

options.text: Appear submissive and grateful to doctors and nurses.
Express a strong desire to be consulted or informed.

questions.shortExplanation: Always bring an advocate, that is, any other person with you to the hospital, and write down every single question and the answer, the name of every doctor and nurse. When people know you have their names, they behave better.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Note down the names of all the doctors and nurses.

【定位】 Always bring an advocate, that is, any other person with you to the hospital, and write down every single question and the answer, the name of every doctor and nurse. When people know you have their names, they behave better.

一定要带一个能为你说话的人，也就是任何别的人，陪你去医院，并且把每一个问题和答案、每一位医生和护士的名字都写下来。当别人知道你掌握着他们的名字时，他们就会表现得更好。

【信号】 建议句信号 Always / write down。建议落在祈使句信号词上：Always bring an advocate 和 write down ... the name of every doctor and nurse。Always 开头的祈使句、write down 都是典型的建议语气，是答案句的标志。

【替换】 write down ... the name of every doctor and nurse↔ Note down the names of all the doctors and nurses.

同义词替换 write down=Note down

【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 Appear submissive and grateful to doctors and nurses. 盗用了开篇 Appear to be submissive, humble, grateful and undemanding 的原词。但那是主讲人反讽地复述『医院想要病人怎样』，并非 Brudney 给病人的建议；Brudney 恰恰主张病人要主动（带人、 记名字），与顺从感恩相反。 借⽤原⽂： Appear to be submissive, humble, grateful and undemanding B) 原词陷阱

Express a strong desire to be consulted or informed. 盗用了 be consulted or informed 原词。但 Brudney 说的是：病人若表现出想被咨询或知情，反而会被当成难缠的人——这是在描述后果，不是建议病人去这么做。 借⽤原⽂： if you, as a patient, suggest that you might like to control even part of the situation or be consulted or informed, then you are considered difficult C) 原词陷阱

Refrain from saying anything that sounds negative. 与原文 If you say one negative thing, they get defensive 的 negative 一词呼应，听着像建议别说负面话。但原文只是陈述『说一句负面话他们就会防备』这一现象，Brudney 并没有把『别说负面话』作为建议给出，本题问的建议是记名字。 借⽤原⽂： If you say one negative thing, they get defensive

questions.prompt: What do American doctors expect their patients to be, according to Karen Brudney?

options.text: Cooperative.
Appreciative.
Passive.

questions.shortExplanation: They want you to be totally passive. 他们想要你完全被动顺从。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Passive.

【定位】 They want you to be totally passive. 他们想要你完全被动顺从。

【信号】 want 表期望 + totally 强调。答案句以 They want you to be totally passive 直白给出期望：want 正对题干 expect，totally 加重语气强调这正是医院想要的状态，是明确的答案落点。

【替换】 They want you to be totally passive ↔ Passive.

【排除】 A) 偷换概念

Cooperative. 听感上像『听话配合』，与 passive 沾边，易误选。但原文用的是 passive （被动顺从），强调的是『别插手、别要求』，而非主动『配合』；cooperative 是录音没有的词。

B) 原词陷阱 Appreciative.（感激的）与开篇 grateful 含义呼应，易让听过 grateful 的人误选。但本题问的是答案句 They want you to be totally passive 给出的特质，是 passive 不是感激； appreciative 并非此句所述。 借⽤原⽂： grateful D) 与原文相反

Responsive.（主动回应的）正是 Passive 的反义。原文明说医院要病人 totally passive （完全被动），responsive 取了相反方向；它恰恰是病人想被知情、被咨询那种主动姿态，而那会被医院当成难缠。 借⽤原⽂： They want you to be totally passive

items.title: 2022年6月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 2
items.transcript:
There are probably teams you've worked with but you never want to work with again. But there must have also been other teams that you would prize reuniting with professionally. In other words, your team had vitality. Vitality comes about when the ties people form with their fellow team members are such that they stay connected even after the team breaks up.

What characteristics of a team make its members more likely to stay in contact despite no longer working together? This question has been answered recently in a study published in a business journal.

One of the two key factors the research team discovered is sameness. Specifically, sharing the same gender or ethnic origin. The more members of a team share similar demographics, the more inclined they will be to remain associates long after the team has served its purpose. After ties are established, similarity strengthens them. As a result, they regard these individuals with greater trust and mutual understanding, which motivates them to seek further opportunities for collaboration. In effect, people tend to create stronger and longer-lasting connections with similar others. Someone who looks and sounds different from us may have the resources we need to be more successful. Yet, we find them to be significantly less credible simply because they are different. If you are a fierce advocate of workplace diversity, you'll no doubt be horrified by such a revelation.

The second factor identified by the researchers is the quality of the relationships among the team members. The more they trust one another, share the same goals and depend on each other for the achievement of those goals, the stronger their chances of maintaining their connections, despite no longer working as one team. Teams with quality relationships have a shared belief that it's safe to take risks with each other, and their members are obliged to share the workload and help out.

From personal experience, I can see both the truth and the inconsistency of such studies. The truth is some of my closest friendships were formed as a result of having worked together on teams, and I actively seek opportunities to work with them again. The inconsistency, though, is that I've never worked for a team more successful and cohesive than the one of which I am a member right now. And yet, the four of us have very little in common and are completely different demographically. So I am unlikely to question the value of a diverse workforce.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about a team with vitality?

options.text: Its members work together despite risks of failure.
It prioritizes recruiting young energetic members.
Its members stay in touch even after it breaks up.
It grows more and more mature professionally.

questions.shortExplanation: Vitality comes about when the ties people form with their fellow team members are such that they stay connected even after the team breaks up.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Its members stay in touch even after it breaks up.

【定位】 Vitality comes about when the ties people form with their fellow team members are such that they stay connected even after the team breaks up.

当人们与团队同伴结成的纽带强到即使团队解散后仍保持联系时，活力（vitality）便由此产生。

【信号】 下定义句 "Vitality comes about when…"。录音用 Vitality comes about when 给"活力"正式下定义，紧跟其后的 they stay connected even after the team breaks up 就是这一概念的核心内容，定义句即答案句。

【替换】 they stay connected even after the team breaks up↔ Its members stay in touch even after it breaks up

stay connected = stay in touch

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

A 的 risks of failure 借用了第 4 段 safe to take risks with each other 里的 risks 一词， 但那是讲"优质关系"、不是 vitality 的定义，听到 risk 就选会偏题。 借⽤原⽂： safe to take risks with each other B) 未提及

B 说团队 prioritizes recruiting young energetic members（优先招募有活力的年轻成员），录音通篇没说招募，纯属臆造，多半是被 vitality 的"活力"联想出来的。

D) 过度推断

D 称团队 grows more and more mature professionally，录音定义 vitality 时只字未提"专业上越来越成熟"，这是顺着"好团队"想当然推出来的，原文无据。

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Their similarity is conducive to future collaboration.

【定位】 After ties are established, similarity strengthens them. As a result, they regard these individuals with greater trust and mutual understanding, which motivates them to seek further opportunities for collaboration.

在纽带建立之后，相似性会强化这些纽带。结果，人们会以更大的信任和相互理解看待这些相似的人，这促使他们去寻求更多合作的机会。

【信号】 因果信号 "As a result…seek…collaboration"。录音先说 similarity strengthens them，再用因果词 As a result 引出 motivates them to seek further opportunities for collaboration，"相似→促成合作"这条因果链就是研究结论的落点。

【替换】 similarity strengthens them↔ Their similarity is conducive to strengthens = conducive to seek further opportunities for collaboration↔future collaboration seek further…collaboration = future collaboration

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

A 称 differences are likely to impact productivity，但录音研究结论强调的是相似 similarity strengthens them，A 取了相反的一极（differences），且 productivity 录音根本没提，方向与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： similarity strengthens them C) 偷换概念

C 说 connections strengthen with the passage of time，借了录音 similarity strengthens them 的 strengthen 一词，却把原因偷换成"随时间推移"——录音说让纽带变牢的是相似，不是时间。 借⽤原⽂： similarity strengthens them D) 原词陷阱

D 说 mutual understanding stems from a common goal，mutual understanding 确实出自录音 greater trust and mutual understanding，但录音说相互理解来自"相似"、不是来自"共同目标"（common goal 属第 4 段另一因素），强加了错误因果。 借⽤原⽂： greater trust and mutual understanding

items.title: 2022年6月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 3
items.transcript:
An American researcher who studied 600 millionaires found how rich you can get comes down to six wealth factors. She found that six behaviors are related to net worth potential, regardless of age or income. These were thriftiness, confidence, responsibility, planning, focus and social indifference.

Being thrifty comes as no great surprise. Spending above your means, spending instead of saving for retirement, spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy, makes you a slave to the paycheck. "Even with an astronomical level of income," she wrote, "to properly build wealth, experts recommend saving 20% of your income and living off the remaining 80%."

Having confidence is another key characteristic, as it helps people to be thrifty. It takes confidence to live within your means. It also takes confidence to invest properly. Instead of making investing decisions with your emotions, financial planners advise that you should leave your investments alone and focus on a long-term investment plan. But people can't invest or manage their own money without accepting responsibility for the outcomes. Many millionaires take on personal responsibility, and most also happen to be self-made, meaning they didn't acquire their wealth through luck. Millionaires don't count on anyone else to make them rich, and they don't blame anyone else if they fall short. They focus on things they can control and align their daily habits to the goals they have set for themselves. They tend to be goal-oriented and hard workers, which enables them to plan financially and focus on seeing those plans through. 92% of the millionaires surveyed developed a long term plan for their money and 97% almost always achieved the goals they set for themselves.

And it is these behaviors that make it easy for them to be socially indifferent. They resist lifestyle creep, the tendency to spend more whenever one earns more. Essentially, they don't yield to pressure to buy the latest thing or to keep up with others or what they have acquired. Instead of being focused on what might make them happy today, they're focused on their long-term wealth-building plan.

questions.prompt: What do experts recommend concerning being thrifty?

options.text: Putting aside twenty percent of one's earnings.
Spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy.
Living off a small proportion of one's income.
Saving as much as one can possibly manage.

questions.shortExplanation: "Even with an astronomical level of income," she wrote, "to properly build wealth, experts recommend saving 20% of your income and living off the remaining 80%." 她写道："即便收入高得惊人，要想真正积累财富，专家也建议把收入的 20% 存起来，靠剩下的 80% 生活。"
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Putting aside twenty percent of one's earnings.

【定位】 "Even with an astronomical level of income," she wrote, "to properly build wealth, experts recommend saving 20% of your income and living off the remaining 80%." 她写道："即便收入高得惊人，要想真正积累财富，专家也建议把收入的 20% 存起来，靠剩下的 80% 生活。"

【信号】 原词 recommend 直接领出建议。答案句直接出现题干同款词 experts recommend，紧跟其后的 saving 20% of your income 就是被推荐的做法——"建议/推荐"类动词后面那句即答案落点。

【替换】 saving 20% of your income↔ Putting aside twenty percent of one's earnings 同义改写 save=put aside、income=earnings

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 的 Spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy 几乎照搬原文 spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy，但原文是把它当作让人沦为"工资奴隶"的反面行为来批评，不是专家推荐的做法，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy C) 与原文相反

C 说靠 a small proportion of one's income（一小部分收入）过活，而原文是靠 the remaining 80%（大头）生活、只存 20%，C 把"靠大部分生活"偷换成"靠一小部分生活"， 与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： living off the remaining 80% D) 偷换概念

D 的 Saving as much as one can possibly manage（尽量多存）听上去合理，但原文给的是精确的"存 20%"，并非"能存多少存多少"，D 用模糊的最大化偷换了专家给出的确切比例。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: How does confidence help people to be thrifty?

options.text: It empowers them to cope with irrational emotions.
It will guarantee the profits from their investments.
It will turn them into successful financial planners.
It enables them to focus on long-term investments.

questions.shortExplanation: It also takes confidence to invest properly. Instead of making investing decisions with your emotions, financial planners advise that you should leave your investments alone and focus on a long-term investment plan. 正确投资同样需要信心。理财规划师建议，不要凭情绪做投资决策，而应让投资保持不动、 专注于一个长期投资计划。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） It enables them to focus on long-term investments.

【定位】 It also takes confidence to invest properly. Instead of making investing decisions with your emotions, financial planners advise that you should leave your investments alone and focus on a long-term investment plan. 正确投资同样需要信心。理财规划师建议，不要凭情绪做投资决策，而应让投资保持不动、 专注于一个长期投资计划。

【信号】 Instead of 否定情绪、转出正解。答案句用 Instead of making investing decisions with your emotions 先否定"凭情绪投资"，转折出真正建议的做法——专注长期投资计划；"Instead of A, do B"里 B 才是落点。

【替换】 focus on a long-term investment plan↔ focus on long-term investments

近乎同义、概括复述 leave your investments alone↔ enables them to focus on long-term investments

详述→概括

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

A 说信心"使人应对 irrational emotions"，盗用了原文的 emotions 一词，但原文是说"不要用情绪做决策"（避开情绪），并非"赋予人应对非理性情绪的能力"，把"绕开情绪"偷换成"驾驭情绪"。 借⽤原⽂： making investing decisions with your emotions B) 过度推断

B 说信心 guarantee the profits from their investments（保证投资盈利），原文从未承诺"保证收益"，只说专注长期计划，guarantee 是过度拔高的绝对化表述。

C) 张冠李戴

C 说信心 turn them into successful financial planners，盗用了原文出现的 financial planners，但原文里 financial planners 是"给出建议的人"，不是说有信心就能"变成"理财规划师，把建议者的身份安到了普通人身上。 借⽤原⽂： financial planners advise

questions.prompt: How do millionaires react when they fail in their investment?

options.text: They count on others to take the responsibility.
They change their investment strategy in time.
They think they themselves are to blame.
They persist rather than get discouraged.

questions.shortExplanation: Millionaires don't count on anyone else to make them rich, and they don't blame anyone else if they fall short.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） They think they themselves are to blame.

【定位】 Millionaires don't count on anyone else to make them rich, and they don't blame anyone else if they fall short.

百万富翁不指望别人让自己变富，达不到目标时也不怪罪任何人。

【信号】 两个 don't…anyone else 否定推责。答案句连用 don't count on anyone else 和 don't blame anyone else 两重否定，把责任牢牢落回自己身上——否定"怪别人"等于肯定"怪自己"，这是答案落点。

【替换】 they don't blame anyone else if they fall short↔They think they themselves are to blame 否定他人=肯定自身（肯否转换）

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

A 说他们 count on others to take the responsibility，盗用了原文的 count on anyone else 和 responsibility，但原文明明是"don't count on anyone else"——加了否定。A 把原文的否定句正过来用，与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： don't count on anyone else B) 未提及

B 说他们 change their investment strategy in time（及时改投资策略），原文谈的是"失利时不怪别人/担责"，从没说他们会"改策略"，属凭常识脑补的未提及项。

D) 答非所问

D 的 persist rather than get discouraged（坚持不气馁）说的是"态度上是否泄气"，原文这句讲的是"责任归谁"，D 答的是另一个维度，与本题问的"react when they fail"对不上。

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker say millionaires are socially indifferent?

options.text: They do not resist novel lifestyles.
They do not try to keep up with others.
They do not care what they have acquired.
They do not pressure themselves to get rich.

questions.shortExplanation: Essentially, they don't yield to pressure to buy the latest thing or to keep up with others or what they have acquired. 本质上，他们不会屈服于"去买最新潮的东西、或与他人攀比所拥有之物"的压力。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） They do not try to keep up with others.

【定位】 Essentially, they don't yield to pressure to buy the latest thing or to keep up with others or what they have acquired. 本质上，他们不会屈服于"去买最新潮的东西、或与他人攀比所拥有之物"的压力。

【信号】 Essentially 引出本质解释。答案句以 Essentially 领出对"社会冷漠"的本质性解释，其中 keep up with others 直接说明缘由——他们不攀比，这是答案落点。

【替换】 they don't yield to pressure to buy the latest thing or to keep up with others↔ They do not try to keep up with others

近乎同词、概括复述

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

A 说他们 do not resist novel lifestyles（不抗拒新潮生活），原文提到的是 lifestyle creep（消费随收入膨胀），并说他们 resist lifestyle creep——是"抗拒"，A 借 lifestyle 一词却把"抗拒"说成"不抗拒"，与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： They resist lifestyle creep C) 偷换概念

C 说他们 do not care what they have acquired（不在乎自己拥有什么），盗用了原文 what they have acquired，但原文是说他们"不为攀比别人所拥有的而买买买"，并非"不在乎自己的所有物"，把宾语对象偷换了。 借⽤原⽂： keep up with others or what they have acquired D) 偷换概念 D 说他们 do not pressure themselves to get rich（不逼自己变富），原文讲的 pressure 是"买最新潮的、与人攀比"的外部压力，不是"逼自己变富"的内部压力，D 把压力的对象配错了。 借⽤原⽂： they don't yield to pressure to buy the latest thing

items.title: 2022年9月六级第1套 · 长对话 1
items.transcript:
W: Welcome to Money Matters, a weekly program that helps you manage your money. Tonight, I'll be talking to Mary Johnson about budgeting.

M: Hello, everyone.

W: There's a magic about money. When it's not planned for, tracked and kept a record of, it literally disappears. What are some of the steps we can take to prevent this from happening?

M: Well, it's all about keeping track of your money. If you don't do that, you'll never be able to set any goals for your budget or have the discipline to stick to them.

W: That's easier said than done. I read recently that only 41% of Americans adhere to a budget.

M: Yes, but knowing what you earn and what you spend can give you reassurance that you won't get into debt in the first place. You can do this by adding up all of your sources of income you have and writing them all down on a piece of paper. On the same page, write down all of your monthly expenses.

W: I'm always amazed at how much my expenses add up. But designating each item as an income or an expense really helps me have a much better sense of all my spending.

M: Right, most people have no idea how much they spend each day, let alone each week or month, no matter how careful they are. Next, subtract your monthly expenses from income. If the result is positive, you are living within your means. If the result is a negative number, you're going to have to cut back on your spending.

W: I'm usually a negative number. I just can't resist the allure of all those prestigious goods.

M: Well, it's not a catastrophe. But you do have to make some changes. Try cutting back on those non-essential items, sell some stuff in your attic, or shop online to avoid unnecessary temptations like chocolate. Failing that you can always find yourself a part-time job.

【答案】 C （细节题） It helps people with budgeting.

【定位】 Welcome to Money Matters, a weekly program that helps you manage your money. Tonight, I'll be talking to Mary Johnson about budgeting. 欢迎收听《金钱要事》，这是一档帮你管理钱财的每周节目。今晚，我将和玛丽·约翰逊聊聊预算的话题。

【信号】 开场点题句。节目开头的自我介绍 a weekly program that helps you manage your money 加上 talking to Mary Johnson about budgeting，是典型的"开场点题"信号—— 节目类录音常在第一两句报出自己是干嘛的，这句就是定位锚。

录音说节目"helps you manage your money"（帮你管钱），不是帮你"earn more money"（赚更多钱）；管钱 ≠ 赚钱，方向被偷换。 借⽤原⽂： helps you manage your money B) 未提及

录音谈的是 budgeting（预算/记账），并没说节目"teaches the importance of financing"（讲融资/理财的重要性）；financing 与 budgeting 是相近理财词，盗用相近概念来诱选，原文未提"重要性"这一说法。

D) 原词陷阱

items.transcript:
M: Hi there, I've come to see the flat. My name is Mark Adams. We spoke on the phone on Wednesday.

W: Hi, Mark, come on up. I'll buzz you in. Green door on the second floor on the right side. Nice to meet you, I spoke to all your references and they all checked out okay. So let me show you around. The place actually belongs to my mother, but her health isn't great, so we finally managed to persuade her to move in with us and rent this old place out.

M: It's a great size. Plenty of space. Very versatile. I think it's a winner for us.

W: Yes, all the appliances are brand-new. There's a washing machine and a tumble dryer in the utility room next to the kitchen.

M: Lots of closet space too, which is fabulous. My wife has a ridiculous number of shoes. Now, the big question: What about noise and the neighbours?

W: Well, all the neighbours are elderly, so no noisy kids. And the back of the house overlooks a clear and peaceful pond, so it's perfect if tranquility is what you are looking for.

M: That's good news. We've been living in a less than glamorous part of Aberdeen, constantly harassed day and night by noisy neighbours. Getting to work was a nightmare too, as we only have one car and my wife has to use it as she works nights at the hospital.

W: Well, if you like the place, it's yours, as soon as I get a contract drawn up with the solicitor. The first month's rent and a deposit are mandatory on signing the contract. Then we can work out when is the best day for you to pay rent each month.

M: We'll be incredibly happy to be your new tenants. Thank you so much, My wife will be thrilled to get out of the shabby place we are now in, and start filling those wardrobes with all those shoes.

items.title: 2022年9月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 1
items.transcript:
A new study has found a positive correlation between how much television children watch and their parents' stress levels. Why? Because the more television kids watch, the more they're exposed to advertising. The more advertising they see, the more likely they are to insist on purchasing items when they go with their parents to the store. This could generate conflict if the parents refuse. All that, researchers say, can contribute to parents' overall stress levels.

What's the solution? Perhaps the most obvious is curtailing screen time. Commercial content is there for a reason: to elicit purchasing behavior. So parents might want to shut off the TV. Researchers concede that this is easier said than done. So they suggest another option. Parents can change how they talk to their kids about purchases.

The researchers suggest that parents seek input from their children on family purchasing decisions. They shouldn't try to control all purchases. Instead, parents might tell their children things like "I will listen to your advice on certain products or brands." This type of communication, the researchers assert, can lead to children making fewer purchasing demands. That means less parents' stress.

However, the protective effect of this kind of communication diminishes with greater exposure to television. This is because advertising aimed at children is especially persuasive. Advertisers use an assortment of tactics, such as bright colors, happy music and celebrity endorsements to appeal to children. Plus, children don't have the cognitive ability to fully understand advertising's intent. That makes them particularly vulnerable to advertisements.

questions.prompt: What has the new study found about children watching television?

options.text: The more commercials they see, the more brands they get to know.
The more commercials they see, the more they adore celebrities.
The more television they watch, the fewer conflicts in the family.
The more television they watch, the greater their parents' stress.

questions.shortExplanation: A new study has found a positive correlation between how much television children watch and their parents' stress levels.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） The more television they watch, the greater their parents' stress.

【定位】 A new study has found a positive correlation between how much television children watch and their parents' stress levels.

一项新研究发现，孩子看电视的多少与其家长的压力水平之间存在正相关。

【信号】 开头点题句即研究结论。篇章独白常在第一句就抛出研究核心，本段开头 A new study has found a positive correlation 用 "研究发现" 直接报出结论，是典型的开头点题信号，听到 "A new study has found" 就该锁定这句为答案句。

【替换】 a positive correlation between how much television children watch and their parents' stress levels ↔ The more television they watch, the greater their parents' stress

正相关改写成 "越多越大"

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

录音确说看电视越多 the more they're exposed to advertising，但谈的是接触广告进而吵架、增压，并非 "认识更多品牌"；A 借 commercials 这个真出现过的话题词，把结果偷换成认识品牌，是听到原词就想选的原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： the more they're exposed to advertising B) 张冠李戴

明星 celebrity endorsements 确在录音里出现，但那是第 4 段讲广告手段时说的，与本题问的 "研究发现" 无关；B 把后文一个原词搬来当本题结论，属张冠李戴式的原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： celebrity endorsements C) 与原文相反

录音说看电视多会 generate conflict（产生冲突、增加压力），C 却说 "家庭冲突更少"， 把录音的因果方向整个反了过来，属与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： This could generate conflict if the parents refuse

items.title: 2022年9月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 2
items.transcript:
Everyone is supposed to cheer for good guys, and we should only punish the bad guys. But that's not what we always do. Most of the time, we do indeed reward good people. We also often punish people who harm others, or who aren't good team players. But sometimes, the good guys also get punished or criticized, specifically because they are so good.

This seems baffling, because it's detrimental to group cooperation. However, the phenomenon has been discovered in multiple fields, and it has been found in every society. Why does this happen? Research suggests a simple reason. When one person looks really good, others look bad by comparison. Those others then have an incentive in stopping that person from looking good, especially if they can't or won't compete. After all, we're all judged in comparison with others.

When faced with someone better, what can a normal person do? One option is to actively compete. A second option is to bring that person down; that is, to suppress their cooperation or work ethic, infer selfish motives for their actions, or imply real or imagined hypocrisy. Other tactics include attacking them on unrelated dimensions, or punishing them outright.

Why does this matter? Critics often attack the motives of people who protect the environment, donate money, or work too hard. Such good deeds are dismissed as naive or hypocritical by those who do not perform those deeds. This criticism may ultimately discourage people from doing good deeds. So it's important to recognize these attacks for what they are.

questions.prompt: What baffling phenomenon is discussed in the passage?

options.text: Bad guys may do good deeds.
Bad guys may go unpunished.
Good guys may not always cooperate.
Good guys may get unfair treatment.

questions.shortExplanation: But sometimes, the good guys also get punished or criticized, specifically because they are so good.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Good guys may get unfair treatment.

【定位】 But sometimes, the good guys also get punished or criticized, specifically because they are so good.

但有时候，好人也会仅仅因为他们太好，而恰恰因此受到惩罚或批评。

【信号】 转折 But 后才是真意。前文先说 we do indeed reward good people（确实奖励好人）做铺垫，紧接 But sometimes, the good guys also get punished or criticized 用 But 一转，转折之后才是作者真正要立的反常现象——这句就是答案句。

【替换】 the good guys also get punished or criticized↔Good guys may get unfair treatment 被罚被批=不公待遇

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

选项把录音里的 bad guys 搬来拼成「坏人也会做好事」，但录音从没说坏人做好事，只说 we should only punish the bad guys；听到 bad guys 就选会中招。 借⽤原⽂： we should only punish the bad guys B) 与原文相反录音说坏人「会被」惩罚（often punish people who harm others），选项却说坏人「逃脱」惩罚（go unpunished），把极性反了；盗用 punish 一词却改了方向。 借⽤原⽂： We also often punish people who harm others C) 张冠李戴

选项说「好人不总愿合作」，盗用了 aren't good team players 里的合作意味，但录音说的是不合作的人会被罚，没说好人不合作；这是把别处的合作话题安到「好人」头上。 借⽤原⽂： who aren't good team players

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） In comparison with others.

【定位】 After all, we're all judged in comparison with others. 毕竟，我们所有人都是在与他人的比较中被评判的。

【信号】 judged 原词直接应答。题干问 how are we judged，录音 we're all judged in comparison with others 里 judged 一词与题干正面咬合，是直接给出依据的应答句；句首 After all（毕竟）是收束总结语气，更确认这是作者下的判定。

【替换】 in comparison with others↔In comparison with others

近乎原句对应

【排除】 A) 答非所问选项「凭我们做什么」看似呼应录音里 stopping that person from looking good 的行为话题，但题干问的是评判依据，录音明说依据是「比较」不是「我们做的事」；用行为话题误导。 借⽤原⽂： incentive in stopping that person from looking good B) 未提及

选项「靠公正评价」里的 fair（公正）录音通篇没出现，是凭「评判」话题臆造出的好听说法；录音说的是与人比较，并未强调公正。 D) 与原文相反

选项「按固定标准」恰与录音「与他人比较」相对立——录音明确说是相对的比较，不是绝对的标准；这是给出与答案句直接相反的另一极。 借⽤原⽂： we're all judged in comparison with others
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What can a normal person do when faced with people who perform better?

options.text: Learn from them earnestly.
Compete with them actively.
Leave them alone temporarily.
Cooperate with them sincerely.

questions.shortExplanation: When faced with someone better, what can a normal person do? One option is to actively compete.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Compete with them actively.

【定位】 When faced with someone better, what can a normal person do? One option is to actively compete.

面对比自己更强的人，一个普通人能做什么呢？一个选择是积极地去竞争。

【信号】 设问后第一答 One option。录音用 what can a normal person do? 自设问，紧接 One option is to actively compete 给出第一个、也是唯一正面的做法；One option 是列举做法的起始信号，作者把「主动竞争」摆在首位，正是答案句。

【替换】 One option is to actively compete↔Compete with them actively compete/actively 同义重组

【排除】 A) 未提及

「向他们认真学习」是面对强者最符合常识的反应，但录音列举的做法里只有竞争和打压， 没有 learn；这是用常识替文本，录音根本没念。

C) 未提及

「暂时不理他们」录音从未提及，作者给的第二选择是 bring that person down（打压），不是回避；这是凭想象补的做法。 借⽤原⽂： A second option is to bring that person down D) 原词陷阱

选项「真诚地与他们合作」盗用了录音里 suppress their cooperation 的 cooperation 一词，但录音说的是「压制别人的合作」，方向恰恰相反，绝非自己去真诚合作。 借⽤原⽂： suppress their cooperation or work ethic
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What may discourage people from performing good deeds?

options.text: Being dismissed as hypocritical.
Not getting the reward they deserve.
Having to make too many sacrifices.
Being misunderstood by people around.

questions.shortExplanation: Such good deeds are dismissed as naive or hypocritical by those who do not perform those deeds. This criticism may ultimately discourage people from doing good deeds.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Being dismissed as hypocritical.

【定位】 Such good deeds are dismissed as naive or hypocritical by those who do not perform those deeds. This criticism may ultimately discourage people from doing good deeds.

这样的善行被那些自己不做这些事的人贬斥为天真或虚伪。这种批评最终可能打消人们行善的念头。

【信号】 discourage 前一句即诱因。题干的 discourage 在 This criticism may ultimately discourage people from doing good deeds 原词复现，而 This criticism 回指上一句 dismissed as naive or hypocritical；指代回指处的那项批评（被斥为伪善）就是打击行善的因素，是答案句。

【替换】 dismissed as naive or hypocritical ↔ Being dismissed as hypocritical 近义并保留 hypocritical

【排除】 B) 张冠李戴

「得不到应有回报」呼应录音前文 reward good people 的奖励话题，但那是开头铺垫，并非第 4 段 discourage 的诱因；把别段的内容安到本题头上。 借⽤原⽂： we do indeed reward good people C) 未提及

「不得不做太多牺牲」录音通篇没提 sacrifice，是对行善代价的常识联想；录音说的打击是被斥伪善，不是牺牲过多。 D) 偷换概念

「被周围人误解」听着像 dismissed as hypocritical，但「误解」是中性的认知偏差，录音说的是被恶意贬斥为伪善，程度与性质都不同，属把「被斥伪善」悄悄换成更轻的「被误解」。 借⽤原⽂： dismissed as naive or hypocritical by those who do not perform those deeds

items.title: 2022年9月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 1
items.transcript:
In America, most researchers concede that boys and girls are brought up in different ways, taught different skills and rewarded for different acts. Women, it is agreed, excel at certain tasks, men at others. There's little argument that some personality traits appear more dominant in one sex than in the other. All of this notwithstanding, gender differences are very much in the media these days. Since the rise of the women's movement, gender role behavior has come under closer scrutiny. How has this affected friendship? How do the sexes differ in their friendship relations?

Most preteen children have a best friend who is usually someone of the same sex and similar age. Both sexes share an essentially positive recollection of these childhood friendships; they do not differ in this respect. However, the type of play engaged in during these early friendships is telling of the difference to come. Boys tend to form play groups that are competitive in nature; girls' groups more frequently revolve around cooperative enterprises. Thus, at an early age, boys become concerned with trying hard and winning while girls, by contrast, play house and school, engaging in roles that require complementary support.

Speaking of their childhood, men recall being highly responsive to and aware of the gender-role opinions of other boys. Girls in preteen years appear to be less susceptible to gender-role pressure. It is not until the dating years that women report being concerned with feminine behavior. Males, for the most part, are responsive to the suggestion that their behavior is unmanly at almost any age.

These early attitudes, reinforced by social conditioning, continue to play an active part in the friendships of both sexes during adolescence. This is a period when the majority of males once again report a close alliance with same-sex friends. Now, however, with heightened intensity, considerable energy is devoted to competing for position and a definite undercurrent of competition permeates the relationship. Although in dissimilar fashion, females share equally fragile relationships at this age. For them, the bond of loyalty extends only to the line of romantic involvement. This is most apt to be the case in late adolescence, when dating and relationships with boys take sharp precedence over sisterhood. Actually, dating dilutes the intensity of same sex friendships for men also. For the majority of us, the moment we begin to date seriously, there's a competition between romance and friendship.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about most preteen children?

options.text: They are increasingly aware of gender differences.
They engage themselves in positive recollection.
They begin to see the importance of friendship.
They make friends with peers of the same sex.

questions.shortExplanation: Most preteen children have a best friend who is usually someone of the same sex and similar age.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） They make friends with peers of the same sex.

【定位】 Most preteen children have a best friend who is usually someone of the same sex and similar age.

大多数青春期前的孩子都有一个最好的朋友，这个朋友通常是同性、年龄相仿的。

【信号】 总括词most + 段首点题。这句出现在第二段段首，且以题干同款的 Most preteen children 开头，是讲者对该群体的总括陈述；听到 most 这种总括词紧跟题目所问对象，就该锁定其后内容为答案句。

【替换】 a best friend who is usually someone of the same sex↔make friends with peers of the same sex have a best friend概括为make friends

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

gender differences 借用了第一段反复出现的 gender differences 一词，但那是讲者引出全文话题的背景，并非对 preteen children 的描述；说 preteen 孩子『越来越意识到性别差异』在该年龄段段落里并无对应。 借⽤原⽂： gender differences are very much in the media these days

B) 原词陷阱

positive recollection 与录音 positive recollection of these childhood friendships 几乎原词照搬，极具迷惑性；但原文说的是『两性都对这些童年友谊有正面回忆』，主体是回忆童年的成年视角，并非在讲 preteen 孩子当下『正在进行正面回忆』这一行为，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： Both sexes share an essentially positive recollection of these childhood friendships C) 未提及

see the importance of friendship 听上去合情合理，但录音在描述 preteen children 时只说他们有同性好友、玩不同性质的游戏，从未说他们『开始认识到友谊的重要性』，属于无中生有。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What do most males devote much of their energy to during adolescence?

options.text: Competing for position.
Forging close ties with friends.
Pursuing fashion.
Fulfilling family obligations.

questions.shortExplanation: Now, however, with heightened intensity, considerable energy is devoted to competing for position and a definite undercurrent of competition permeates the relationship. 然而此时，随着强度增加，大量精力被投入到争夺地位上，一股明确的竞争暗流贯穿于这段关系之中。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Competing for position.

【定位】 Now, however, with heightened intensity, considerable energy is devoted to competing for position and a definite undercurrent of competition permeates the relationship. 然而此时，随着强度增加，大量精力被投入到争夺地位上，一股明确的竞争暗流贯穿于这段关系之中。

【信号】 转折however后 + energy is devoted to原词。本句以转折词 however 引出青春期男性的真实状态，并直接出现题干同款短语 considerable energy is devoted to competing for position；转折之后才是讲者要强调的结论，加上 devoted to 这一投入信号，定位即落于此。

【替换】 considerable energy is devoted to competing for position↔Competing for position

几乎原词对应、仅句式调整

【排除】 B) 与原文相反

Forging close ties with friends 借用了同段 a close alliance with same-sex friends，但那是 however 转折之前的铺垫（青春期男性又一次与同性结盟），讲者随即用 however 转折强调真正投入的是竞争；取转折前的信息即答错方向。 借⽤原⽂： the majority of males once again report a close alliance with same-sex friends C) 未提及

Pursuing fashion 在整篇录音里没有任何对应，讲者谈的是友谊、竞争、恋爱，从未提及时尚，是凭空添加的干扰项。

D) 未提及

Fulfilling family obligations 同样在录音中无对应，讲者讨论的是同伴友谊与竞争，与家庭义务无关，属无中生有。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What do children do when they reach late adolescence?

options.text: They prioritize romance over friendship.
They try to strengthen same-sex friendships.
They begin to take friendship more seriously.
They compete intensely for romantic partners.

questions.shortExplanation: This is most apt to be the case in late adolescence, when dating and relationships with boys take sharp precedence over sisterhood.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） They prioritize romance over friendship.

【定位】 This is most apt to be the case in late adolescence, when dating and relationships with boys take sharp precedence over sisterhood.

在青春期后期最容易出现这种情况，那时约会和与男生的关系会明显优先于姐妹情谊。

【信号】 时间标志late adolescence + 优先级信号take precedence over。句中 in late adolescence 正是题干同款时间标志，紧跟 take sharp precedence over sisterhood 给出明确的优先级判断；时间标志加『谁优先于谁』信号叠加，即为答案句。

【替换】 dating and relationships with boys take sharp precedence over sisterhood ↔ prioritize romance over friendship

take precedence over等于prioritize over

【排除】 B) 与原文相反 strengthen same-sex friendships 借用了原文反复出现的 same-sex friendships，但本句说的是恋爱『压过』姐妹情、即同性友谊被稀释，并非『加强』；方向恰好相反。 借⽤原⽂： dating dilutes the intensity of same sex friendships C) 与原文相反

take friendship more seriously 与录音 take sharp precedence over sisterhood 的取向正相反——原文是恋爱优先、友谊退居其次，而非更看重友谊。 借⽤原⽂： dating and relationships with boys take sharp precedence over sisterhood D) 原词陷阱

compete intensely for romantic partners 把前文讲青春期男性的 competition 一词移花接木到『争夺恋爱对象』上；原文从未说他们激烈争夺恋爱伴侣，只说恋爱与友谊之间存在竞争，属偷换概念。 借⽤原⽂： there's a competition between romance and friendship
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

items.title: 2022年9月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 2
items.transcript:
Good afternoon. In today's lecture, we'll be talking about how and when to disclose a disability when applying for a job. On average, about 20% of the population has some form of disability. Most countries these days have equal opportunity and non-discrimination laws. Yet, disabled people often find it hard to decide when, how, and if at all to raise their disability problem with the potential employer. There is uncertainty about how a recruiter will perceive their disability.

As such, many candidates fear they wouldn't be considered for a position, as a result of disclosing this personal information. And research has validated this as a genuine concern for many job applicants. It's a natural reaction, but it shouldn't be a reason to stay quiet. People need to remember that they are applying for a position they have the skills and experience to excel in. Discussing a disability with the potential employer may help them make reasonable workplace adjustments in their favor.

It's most appropriate to discuss a disability when they reply to confirm an interview. This information needn't be put up front in their cover letter or resumé, because it's probably not relevant to the position itself. Candidates with disabilities should feel they have the power to make their own decisions around sharing this information free from prejudice. If they find an organization that doesn't celebrate diversity and inclusion, it could say a lot about the company's culture. Perhaps the organization isn't the right fit. It's important for them to remember that they are seeking a manager and employer that's going to be supportive and continue to give them a great employment experience.

Companies sometimes offer candidates the chance to disclose disabilities on their application form, but people shouldn't feel restricted by this method or timing. People should avoid sharing the name of their disability or condition. There is always the risk that the recruiter will research information that is inaccurate or irrelevant. If people don't think their disability will impact their ability to perform in the advertised position, then it's entirely their entitlement to choose when, and whether to share this information.

questions.prompt: Why do disabled job applicants feel reluctant to disclose their disability information?

options.text: They regard it as a matter of sheer privacy.
They are worried about being turned down.
They fear that their condition will be made widely known.
They are afraid to be discriminated against once recruited.

questions.shortExplanation: As such, many candidates fear they wouldn't be considered for a position, as a result of disclosing this personal information.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） They are worried about being turned down.

【定位】 As such, many candidates fear they wouldn't be considered for a position, as a result of disclosing this personal information.

正因如此，许多求职者害怕：一旦透露这一个人信息，自己就不会被某职位纳入考虑（即落选）。

【信号】 fear + as a result 双重信号。many candidates fear they wouldn't be considered for a position 中的 fear 直接对应题干的 feel reluctant 的心理，as a result of disclosing 又点出『因披露而……』的因果，这两个信号合起来标定它就是答案句。

【替换】 fear they wouldn't be considered for a position↔worried about being turned down 怕不被考虑 = 怕被拒

【排除】 C) 原词陷阱

录音说的是怕『不被考虑』，并未说怕病情被广泛知晓；C 借 this personal information 这个原词诱你联想到『隐私外泄』，但 made widely known（被广泛传开）是录音没说的内容，属原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： as a result of disclosing this personal information D) 过度推断

录音的担忧发生在『还没被考虑、怕落选』阶段；D 说 once recruited（一旦被录用后）被歧视，把时间挪到了入职之后，与录音 they wouldn't be considered for a position（怕进不去）方向相反，属过度推断兼时间偷换。 借⽤原⽂： they wouldn't be considered for a position A) 未提及

A 说他们把这当作 a matter of sheer privacy（纯属隐私问题），但录音给的理由是『怕落选』这一现实顾虑，并没说他们当作纯隐私来回避，属录音未提及的说法。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: When does the speaker suggest applicants reveal their disability information?

options.text: After receiving a job offer.
During a job interview.
When confirming an interview.
Upon completing a cover letter.

questions.shortExplanation: It's most appropriate to discuss a disability when they reply to confirm an interview.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） When confirming an interview.

【定位】 It's most appropriate to discuss a disability when they reply to confirm an interview.

最合适的（披露）时机，是在他们回复确认面试的时候。

【信号】 most appropriate 推荐句。It's most appropriate to discuss a disability when they reply to confirm an interview 用最高级 most appropriate 直接给出『最佳时机』，这种带推荐色彩的句子就是『何时』题的答案信号。

【替换】 when they reply to confirm an interview↔ When confirming an interview 确认面试时 = confirm an interview

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱录音说的是『确认面试时(confirm an interview)』而非『面试过程中(during)』；B 借 confirm an interview 里的 interview 原词，把时点偷换成 During a job interview，与录音差一个动作环节，属原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： when they reply to confirm an interview D) 与原文相反

录音明确说残疾信息 needn't be put up front in their cover letter or resumé（不必放进求职信），D 却让人在 completing a cover letter 时披露，正好取了录音否定掉的那个时点，与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： This information needn't be put up front in their cover letter or resumé A) 未提及

A 说在 After receiving a job offer（收到录用通知后）披露，但录音推荐的是确认面试阶段，全篇没说要等到拿 offer 之后，属录音未提及的时点。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What are people advised to do when filling out their job application form?

options.text: Describe the true state of their health.
Provide all the information required.
Stress the irrelevance of their disability to the job.
Avoid mentioning the name of their disability.

questions.shortExplanation: People should avoid sharing the name of their disability or condition. 人们应当避免说出自己残疾或病症的具体名称。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Avoid mentioning the name of their disability.

【定位】 People should avoid sharing the name of their disability or condition. 人们应当避免说出自己残疾或病症的具体名称。

【信号】 should avoid 告诫句。People should avoid sharing the name of their disability or condition 用 should avoid 直接给出告诫，这种 should/avoid 的建议措辞就是『建议做什么』题的答案信号。

【替换】 should avoid sharing the name of their disability or condition↔ Avoid mentioning the name of their disability

避免说出名称 = avoid mentioning the name

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

A 让人 Describe the true state of their health（如实描述健康状况），录音却劝人 avoid sharing the name of their disability or condition（避免说出名称），方向正好相反，是与原文相反的干扰。 借⽤原⽂： People should avoid sharing the name of their disability or condition B) 原词陷阱

录音说人们『不应被表格的方式或时机限制』，并未要求 Provide all the information required（提供所有被要求的信息）；B 借录音反复出现的 information 一词诱你选『信息全交』，但全篇恰恰在讲可以有所保留，属原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： people shouldn't feel restricted by this method or timing C) 未提及 C 让人 Stress the irrelevance of their disability to the job（强调残疾与岗位无关）；录音填表那段只说『避免说出名称』，并未建议在表格里强调残疾与工作无关，属录音未提及的做法。
