items.title: 2022年9月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 3
items.transcript:
Smartphones distract attention and reduce learning because of their potential to offer activities more inviting than study. But what about background sound alone?

A group of American researchers compared students' comprehension of verbal material when reading in the presence of background speech, instrumental music or general noise. General noise is neutral, such as that from the sound of an air conditioner or fan. Students' scores were most depressed in the presence of background speech. Comprehension was slightly better with the presence of music than with speech. However, when they were asked to identify melodies rather than understand text, background music interfered more. When the background speech was in a language unfamiliar to participants, there was little if any hindrance of reading comprehension.

British researchers compared the effects of background speech, vocal music, instrumental music, general background noise and silence on short-term memory. Background speech had the biggest negative effect; vocal music was slightly more disruptive than instrumental; and general background noise and silence were least disruptive. It seems the degree of interference from background noise depends on the overlap between the processing required on the task and the processing required to screen out the background noise.

The studies suggest that when people read and when they try to remember any verbal material, background speech will inhibit their ability. Instrumental music will have at worst a slight effect. When students write essays, however, other research has found it is best to reduce all background noise as much as possible.

Not everyone reacts in the same way to distractions. Other studies suggest some aspects of personality may make a difference. The researchers subjected shy quiet people and confident outgoing ones to high arousal or low arousal background music, general noise or silence while asking them to remember words. Everyone performed best in the silent condition, but less sociable people were more negatively affected by each of the distractions. So when children are reading and trying to incorporate new material, parents could consider allowing some background music, particularly if it's instrumental and their child is the outgoing type.

questions.prompt: What did some American researchers find about students' reading comprehension in the presence of background noise?

options.text: Their scores were least affected by music with speech.
It was the poorest when there was background speech.
Their scores were most depressed with instrumental music.
It was disrupted by the sound of an air conditioner or fan.

questions.shortExplanation: Students' scores were most depressed in the presence of background speech. Comprehension was slightly better with the presence of music than with speech. 在有背景人声（说话声）的情况下，学生的成绩下降得最厉害。有音乐时的理解力比有说话声时稍好一些。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） It was the poorest when there was background speech.

【定位】 Students' scores were most depressed in the presence of background speech. Comprehension was slightly better with the presence of music than with speech. 在有背景人声（说话声）的情况下，学生的成绩下降得最厉害。有音乐时的理解力比有说话声时稍好一些。

【信号】 程度极值 most depressed。答案句靠程度极值信号锁定：scores were most depressed in the presence of background speech 中的 most depressed（下降最厉害）直接回应 “成绩最差出现在哪种声音下”，极值词就是听力比较题的落点。

【替换】 scores were most depressed in the presence of background speech ↔ It was the poorest when there was background speech most depressed = poorest

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

录音说有 When the background speech was in a language unfamiliar to participants, there was little if any hindrance，是“陌生语言的人声几乎不干扰”，A 却笼统说成绩受人声影响“最小（least affected）”，偷换并反了极值方向，原文是“最差”才对。 借⽤原⽂： there was little if any hindrance of reading comprehension

C) 原词陷阱

录音里 most depressed 是接 background speech 的，C 却把 most depressed 安到了 instrumental music 头上。instrumental music 在录音里反而是 Comprehension was slightly better with the presence of music，C 盗用了真实出现过的极值词却配错了对象。 借⽤原⽂： Students' scores were most depressed in the presence of background speech D) 原词陷阱

air conditioner or fan 确在录音中出现，但那是用来定义 General noise is neutral, such as that from the sound of an air conditioner or fan（举例说明什么叫一般噪音），并非说阅读理解被它“扰乱”，D 借这个原词制造熟耳朵的诱惑，其实答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： General noise is neutral, such as that from the sound of an air conditioner or fan
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the British researchers about the degree of interference from background noise?

options.text: It has to do with the type and volume of the background noise.
It has to do with short-term memory for listening comprehension.
It depends on the overlap in processing different kinds of information.
It depends on the participants' ability to concentrate on the task at hand.

questions.shortExplanation: It seems the degree of interference from background noise depends on the overlap between the processing required on the task and the processing required to screen out the background noise.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） It depends on the overlap in processing different kinds of information.

【定位】 It seems the degree of interference from background noise depends on the overlap between the processing required on the task and the processing required to screen out the background noise.

看来，背景噪音造成的干扰程度，取决于“完成任务所需的信息处理”与“屏蔽背景噪音所需的信息处理”这两者之间的重叠。

【信号】 因果信号 depends on。答案句靠归因信号锁定：depends on the overlap between the processing required on the task and the processing required to screen out the background noise 中的 depends on 直接给出“干扰程度由什么决定”，原因题的落点就在 depends on 之后。

【替换】 the overlap between the processing required on the task and the processing required to screen out the background noise

↔ the overlap in processing different kinds of information

两种处理 = 不同信息处理

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

the type and volume of the background noise 把决定因素说成“噪音的类型和音量”。录音确实念了 background noise，但从没说取决于其 type and volume，volume（音量） 更是录音未提，A 借熟词拼了个原文没有的归因。 借⽤原⽂： the degree of interference from background noise depends on the overlap B) 原词陷阱

short-term memory 来自录音 British researchers compared the effects… on short-term memory，那是英国研究的“测试对象/实验任务”，B 把它偷换成“干扰程度取决于短期记忆”，张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： compared the effects of background speech, vocal music, instrumental music, general background noise and silence on short-term memory D) 未提及

the participants' ability to concentrate on the task at hand 听着合理，但英国研究者那段从没说干扰程度取决于“专注能力”，这是录音未提的常识性臆测。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What is best for students to do when writing essays according to some research?

options.text: Keep everything as quiet as possible.
Play nothing but instrumental music.
Use vocal material as little as possible.
Wear a pair of earphones or headphones.

questions.shortExplanation: When students write essays, however, other research has found it is best to reduce all background noise as much as possible.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Keep everything as quiet as possible.

【定位】 When students write essays, however, other research has found it is best to reduce all background noise as much as possible.

然而，当学生写作文时，另有研究发现，最好尽可能减少一切背景噪音。

【信号】 转折 however + 建议 it is best to。答案句双信号锁定：转折词 however 提示前面（读书可放纯音乐）之外另起一种场景，紧接的 it is best to reduce all background noise as much as possible 是建议句，转折后的建议正是写作文场景的落点。

【替换】 reduce all background noise as much as possible↔Keep everything as quiet as possible. 减一切噪音 = 保持安静

【排除】 B) 张冠李戴

Play nothing but instrumental music. 里的 instrumental music 来自录音 Instrumental music will have at worst a slight effect，但那是针对“读书/记忆”场景说的；写作文场景明确要求“减少一切噪音”，B 把读书场景的纯音乐建议张冠李戴到写作文上。 借⽤原⽂： Instrumental music will have at worst a slight effect C) 原词陷阱

Use vocal material as little as possible. 中 vocal 来自英国研究那段 vocal music was slightly more disruptive than instrumental，写作文场景要求的是“减少一切噪音”而非单单“少用人声”，C 借 vocal 这个原词缩小了范围、答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： vocal music was slightly more disruptive than instrumental

D) 未提及

Wear a pair of earphones or headphones. 戴耳机听着像隔音的合理办法，但录音从头到尾没提 earphones / headphones，属凭常识臆造。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: How do people of different personalities react to distractions according to other studies?

options.text: Sociable people were immune to all distractions.
Shy quiet people were most adversely impacted.
Less outgoing people were more affected by silence.
Confident people were unaffected by high-arousal music.

questions.shortExplanation: Everyone performed best in the silent condition, but less sociable people were more negatively affected by each of the distractions.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Shy quiet people were most adversely impacted.

【定位】 Everyone performed best in the silent condition, but less sociable people were more negatively affected by each of the distractions.

所有人在安静条件下表现最好，但不那么善于社交（即较内向）的人，受到每一种干扰的负面影响都更大。

【信号】 转折 but 后是真意。答案句靠转折信号锁定：but less sociable people were more negatively affected by each of the distractions 中 but 之后才是关于性格差异的真正结论，前半 Everyone performed best in silence 是共性铺垫，转折后才落到“内向者受影响更大”。

【替换】 less sociable people were more negatively affected by each of the distractions↔ Shy quiet people were most adversely impacted.

less sociable = shy quiet；more affected = most impacted

【排除】 A) 过度推断

Sociable people were immune to all distractions. 中 sociable 来自录音 less sociable， 但录音说外向者“受影响更小”，并未说“对所有干扰免疫”，且 Everyone performed best in the silent condition 表明人人都受干扰（只有安静最好），A 的 immune to all 是绝对化臆断。 借⽤原⽂： Everyone performed best in the silent condition C) 与原文相反

Less outgoing people were more affected by silence. 里 Less outgoing 对得上内向者，但录音说大家在 silent condition 下表现最好，内向者是被“各种干扰”影响更大，而非被“安静”影响更大，C 把受影响的对象由 distractions 偷换成 silence，与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： less sociable people were more negatively affected by each of the distractions

D) 原词陷阱

Confident people were unaffected by high-arousal music. 中 confident、high arousal music 都在录音里出现（subjected shy quiet people and confident outgoing ones to high arousal or low arousal background music），但那只是实验设置，录音没说自信者“不受高唤醒音乐影响”，D 拼接真实原词造了个原文未下的绝对结论。 借⽤原⽂： subjected shy quiet people and confident outgoing ones to high arousal or low arousal background music, general noise or silence
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

items.title: 2023年12月六级第1套 · 长对话 1
items.transcript:
M: Hello, doctor.

W: Hello, please take a seat. I have your test results here, and it's good news. The blood test came back clear. There is no indication of any digestive issues.

M: So then why do I feel so poorly all the time?

W: It's probably due to overwork and stress.

M: No, it can't be. I've always been working hard, but I've never felt stress. Other people suffering complain about that, but I don't. It must be something else.

W: What you have just described is a common sentiment. Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it. You told me you often work long into the night, right?

M: Yes, most days in fact. But I've been doing that for about 20 years now.

W: That doesn't matter. You could have been suffering from stress for 20 years without knowing it, and now it's catching up to you.

M: But what about my feeling tired all the time and not being able to sleep well at night?

W: Those are common consequences of stress. And if you don't sleep well, then of course you will feel fatigued. I'm going to prescribe some special sleeping pills for you. They have a soft, gentle effect and are made from natural ingredients, so your stomach should tolerate them fine, and there shouldn't be any negative side effects. Take one with your dinner and come see me after a month. If there is no improvement, I'll give you something stronger.

M: Thank you, doctor.

W: That's not all. You should try and work less. Is there any way you can decrease your workload?

M: Um, I'd have to think about it. I'm a restaurant manager and this industry is very competitive. There are many things to keep track of and stay on top of.

W: I recommend you think about delegating some responsibilities to someone else. I'm not asking you to retire just to slow down a bit. It's for your own health.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the man from his test results?

options.text: It is clear that he is expected to enjoy a healthy life.
There is nothing wrong with his digestive system.
There is some indication of an issue with his blood circulation.
He doesn't know he has long been suffering from poor health.

questions.shortExplanation: The blood test came back clear. There is no indication of any digestive issues.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） There is nothing wrong with his digestive system.

【定位】 The blood test came back clear. There is no indication of any digestive issues.

血液化验结果是清白的（没问题）。没有任何消化系统问题的迹象。

【信号】 医生宣布结果的直接陈述句。医生一坐下就直接通报结论 The blood test came back clear 并补一句 There is no indication of any digestive issues——这种“医生直接公布检查结果”的陈述就是答案信号，不用等转折。

【替换】 no indication of any digestive issues↔nothing wrong with his digestive system “没有消化问题迹象”=“消化系统没毛病”

【排除】 C) 原词陷阱

录音查的是 blood test 与 digestive issues，an issue with his blood circulation 借用了 “血液 blood”的耳熟感，却把对象偷换成 blood circulation（血液循环），录音从未说循环有问题，且结果是 clear（清白），与“有问题”正好相反。 借⽤原⽂： The blood test came back clear A) 过度推断

录音只说某项检查没问题，It is clear that he is expected to enjoy a healthy life 却推到 “可望享有健康人生”——录音里他正feel poorly、被诊断有压力，谈不上健康一生，是无中生有的拔高。 D) 答非所问

He doesn't know he has long been suffering from poor health 套用了后文“压力潜伏二十年而不自知”的影子，但本题问的是 test results（化验结果），结果恰恰是“清白”，并未说明他长期体弱，错位安插。 借⽤原⽂： You could have been suffering from stress for 20 years without knowing it
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the woman think is a common phenomenon among many people?

options.text: Mistaking symptoms of illness for stress.
Complaining they are being overworked.
Being unaware of the stress they are under.
Suffering from illness without recognising it.

questions.shortExplanation: What you have just described is a common sentiment. Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Being unaware of the stress they are under.

【定位】 What you have just described is a common sentiment. Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it.

你刚才描述的是一种很常见的心态。许多承受压力的人都意识不到自己有压力。

【信号】 含 common / Many people 的概括句。女方用 a common sentiment 与 Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it 对“很多人”下普遍性判断——出现 common、 Many people 这类总括词，就是“普遍现象”题的答案信号。

【替换】 Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it↔ Being unaware of the stress they are under

“承压却没认出”=“没意识到自己身处压力”

【排除】 D) 偷换概念 Suffering from illness without recognising it 与答案句框架一致（都是“X 而不自知”）， 但 X 被换成 illness；录音说的是 suffer from stress fail to recognise it——没认出的是压力不是疾病，差的正是那个核心变量。 借⽤原⽂： Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it A) 与原文相反

Mistaking symptoms of illness for stress 是“把病当成压力”，而录音是“有压力却没认出 （把压力当别的）”，方向恰好反过来；男方原话是 I've never felt stress，是不承认压力， 不是错把病当压力。

B) 原词陷阱

Complaining they are being overworked 蹭了录音 overwork and stress 的 overwork，但女方说的是很多人“没意识到压力”，恰恰不是“抱怨过劳”；男方甚至说 other people complain，他自己不抱怨，与“很多人抱怨”相反。 借⽤原⽂： It's probably due to overwork and stress
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say she will do for the man?

options.text: Prescribe some medication for him.
Give him another physical check-up.
Explain to him the common consequence of stress.
Buy some sleeping pills for him from the drugstore.

questions.shortExplanation: I'm going to prescribe some special sleeping pills for you. 我要给你开一些特制的安眠药。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Prescribe some medication for him.

【定位】 I'm going to prescribe some special sleeping pills for you. 我要给你开一些特制的安眠药。

【信号】 I'm going to + 动词的将来表态句。女方用 I'm going to prescribe some special sleeping pills for you 主动声明下一步动作——I'm going to 这类将来式表态，就是“她将做什么”题的答案信号。

【替换】 prescribe some special sleeping pills↔Prescribe some medication for him “开安眠药”=“开药（medication）”

【排除】 D) 原词陷阱 Buy some sleeping pills for him from the drugstore 盗用了原句的 sleeping pills，却把动作从“医生开处方 prescribe”改成“去药店买 buy from the drugstore”；录音里医生是开方，不是替他去药店买药。 借⽤原⽂： I'm going to prescribe some special sleeping pills for you C) 答非所问

Explain to him the common consequence of stress 蹭了录音 Those are common consequences of stress，但那是医生在解释失眠成因，不是回答“她将为他做什么”这一动作；本题要的是她接下来要做的事，是开药。 借⽤原⽂： Those are common consequences of stress B) 未提及

Give him another physical check-up 录音从未提及再做体检——医生是看着已有的 test results 直接开药，并约一个月后复诊，没有安排再次体检。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the man say about the industry he is engaged in?

options.text: It calls for responsible management.
It proves to be quite profitable.
It is remarkably promising.
It is full of competition.

questions.shortExplanation: I'm a restaurant manager and this industry is very competitive. 我是个餐厅经理，这个行业竞争非常激烈。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） It is full of competition.

【定位】 I'm a restaurant manager and this industry is very competitive. 我是个餐厅经理，这个行业竞争非常激烈。

【信号】 this industry is very + 形容词的直接评价句。男方自陈身份后用 this industry is very competitive 直接评价所在行业——this industry is very + 形容词的结构就是“行业评价” 题的答案信号，落点在 competitive 这个词。

【替换】 this industry is very competitive↔It is full of competition “非常有竞争性”=“充满竞争”

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

It calls for responsible management 蹭了男方自报身份 I'm a restaurant manager 里的 manager/management，但他评价行业用的词是 competitive，从没说这行“需要负责任的管理”，是借身份词造的干扰。 借⽤原⽂： I'm a restaurant manager B) 未提及

It proves to be quite profitable 谈盈利，但男方对行业的描述只有“竞争激烈”和“事务繁多”，从未提到赚钱与否，是无中生有。

C) 未提及

It is remarkably promising 说行业前景可观，但录音里男方谈的是竞争和繁忙、并被建议放慢节奏，全无“前景大好”之意，属凭空添加的正面评价。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

items.title: 2023年12月六级第1套 · 长对话 2
items.transcript:
W: Today on People in the News, our guest is John Williams. The name may not sound familiar to you, but John was once an acclaimed basketball player. John, you stunned fans by leaving the sport at just 25. Why did you retire so early?

M: Meg, I loved being an athlete, but I didn't love being a celebrity. I was in the limelight when I was still a high school student and went professional right after high school graduation, which was a mistake. I was a shy kid and I wasn't ready for all the media attention.

W: But walking away from millions of dollars at the height of your career, most people wouldn't be able to resist the lure of such a high salary. When you left the sport, there was speculation that you were having issues with your teammates or even an injury.

M: Not at all. It was hard to quit. I was tempted to stay in the game, because I love basketball and I loved my team. As for money, I turned professional at 18. So I'd actually earned a lot and saved most of it, because I had great financial advisers. I knew basketball wasn't a career with a lot of longevity for most players, so I wanted to change careers while I was still young.

W: Okay, that was 20 years ago, and you're back in the news. You've created a foundation that works to get more kids playing team sports. Why?

M: I went to university and I studied public health and learned about the seriousness of the obesity epidemic, particularly among kids and adolescents in poor communities. I've spent the last two decades trying to alleviate the problem. The foundation is just the latest attempt.

W: The foundation uses private donations to support basketball teams for girls and boys in primary school, right?

M: Actually, we support teams for secondary school students, too, and also have some public funding.

questions.prompt: Why did John Williams leave the sport of basketball at just 25?

options.text: To avoid being in the limelight.
To seek medical help for his injury.
To pursue a less competitive career.
To stay away from his hostile teammates.

questions.shortExplanation: I loved being an athlete, but I didn't love being a celebrity. I was in the limelight when I was still a high school student and went professional right after high school graduation, which was a mistake. I was a shy kid and I wasn't ready for all the media attention.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） To avoid being in the limelight.

【定位】 I loved being an athlete, but I didn't love being a celebrity. I was in the limelight when I was still a high school student and went professional right after high school graduation, which was a mistake. I was a shy kid and I wasn't ready for all the media attention.

我热爱当运动员，但我不喜欢当名人。我还在念高中时就处在聚光灯下，高中一毕业就转入职业，这是个错误。我是个害羞的孩子，还没准备好应对这一切媒体关注。

【信号】 被问者应答 + 转折 but 见真意。主持人问他为何退役，被问者亲口回答的这句就是答案句；其中 but I didn\'t love being a celebrity 的转折 but 之后才是真正的退役理由，前半 I loved being an athlete 是铺垫干扰。

【替换】 I didn\'t love being a celebrity ↔ To avoid being in the limelight. 不爱当名人=避开聚光灯

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

B 借用了原文里 injury 一词，但那是主持人提出的传闻 you were having issues with your teammates or even an injury，被问者随即以 Not at all 明确否认，故因伤就医并非退役原因。 借⽤原⽂： there was speculation that you were having issues with your teammates or even an injury C) 过度推断

他确实想趁年轻转行，但原文动机是 basketball wasn\'t a career with a lot of longevity （这行干不长），并非为追求「竞争更小」的职业，C 是无中生有地编了个理由。

D) 原词陷阱

D 借用原文 teammates 一词，但 issues with your teammates 同样只是主持人的猜测， 被 Not at all 一并否认，与队友不和并非退役原因。 借⽤原⽂： you were having issues with your teammates

questions.prompt: What does the man say about basketball as a career for most players?

It proves rewarding.
It does not last long.
It is not so profitable.

questions.shortExplanation: I knew basketball wasn't a career with a lot of longevity for most players, so I wanted to change careers while I was still young.

【答案】 C （态度观点题） It does not last long.

【定位】 I knew basketball wasn't a career with a lot of longevity for most players, so I wanted to change careers while I was still young.

我知道对大多数球员来说，篮球不是个能干很久的职业，所以我想趁年轻就转行。

【信号】 被问者亲口下的定性句。这句 basketball wasn\'t a career with a lot of longevity for most players 是男士对篮球职业寿命的直接判断，与题干 for most players 的限定完全对应，是答案句。

缺乏长久性=持续不久

B) 答非所问

他确实说热爱篮球、留恋球队，但这是个人情感，并非说篮球作为职业 proves rewarding （有回报）；B 借了正面语气却与「问职业属性」答非所问。

D) 与原文相反

D 借用了这段反复出现的 money 话题，但原文是 I\'d actually earned a lot and saved most of it，说明他挺赚钱，与 not so profitable（不赚钱）正好相反。 借⽤原⽂： I\'d actually earned a lot and saved most of it

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the woman about John Williams 20 years later?

options.text: He was a financial advisor.
He suffered from poor health.

【答案】 D （细节题） He was back in the news.

【定位】 Okay, that was 20 years ago, and you're back in the news. You've created a foundation that works to get more kids playing team sports. 好，那是二十年前的事了，如今你重回新闻视野。你创立了一个基金会，致力于让更多孩子参与团队运动。

【替换】 you\'re back in the news↔He was back in the news.

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

A 借用了原文 I had great financial advisers 里的 financial，但那说的是他当年请了理财顾问，而非他本人 20 年后成了理财顾问，时间与身份都被错置。 借⽤原⽂： I had great financial advisers B) 张冠李戴

C) 原词陷阱 C 借用反复出现的 basketball，但原文 20 年后他做的是创立基金会推动孩子运动，从未说他 became a basketball coach，教练身份系无中生有。 借⽤原⽂： You\'ve created a foundation that works to get more kids playing team sports

options.text: Study issues of public health.
Alleviate the obesity problem.

Train young basketball players.

【定位】 I studied public health and learned about the seriousness of the obesity epidemic, particularly among kids and adolescents in poor communities. I've spent the last two decades trying to alleviate the problem.

我研究了公共健康，了解到肥胖流行问题的严重性，尤其是在贫困社区的儿童和青少年中。 过去二十年我一直在努力缓解这个问题。

A 借用原文 I studied public health，但研究公共健康是他在大学里的学习，是认识问题的前提，而非他二十年来「致力做」的那件事；真正的长期目标是缓解肥胖。 借⽤原⽂： I studied public health C) 原词陷阱

items.title: 2023年12月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 1
items.transcript:
Kate Atkinson was born in York, England, in 1951. She worked hard to gain her credentials as an author. She studied English Literature at University in Scotland. After graduating in 1974, she researched a doctorate on American Literature. Later, she taught at the university she graduated from, and began writing short stories in 1981. She began writing for women's magazines after winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition. Her first novel, Behind the Scenes at the Museum, won the 1995 UK Book of the Year award. The book is set in Yorkshire and has been adapted for radio, theatre, and TV. She has written two plays for a theatre in Edinburgh—the first was called Nice and the second Abandonment, performed as part of the Edinburgh Festival in August 2000.

Whatever genre Atkinson writes in, her books touch on the themes of love and loss and how to carry on. They are always presented with ingenuity and a wicked sense of humor. Her books tend to be populated by odd, sometimes sinful, and generally flawed eccentrics who become credible by virtue of being so fully realized. Her books have frequently been described as comedies of manners. That is to say, comedies that represent the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour current in fashionable circles of society, where appearances count more than true moral character. A comedy of manners tends to reward its clever and deceitful characters, rather than punish their bad deeds. The humor of a comedy of manners relies on verbal wit and playful teasing.

questions.prompt: When did Kate Atkinson begin to write for women's magazines?

options.text: When she started teaching at Edinburgh University in Scotland.
While she was doing her doctoral studies on American Literature.
After publishing her first novel Behind the Scenes at the Museum.
After winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition.

questions.shortExplanation: She began writing for women's magazines after winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition. 她在赢得 1986 年《Woman's Own》短篇小说大赛之后,开始为女性杂志写作。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） After winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition.

【定位】 She began writing for women's magazines after winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition. 她在赢得 1986 年《Woman's Own》短篇小说大赛之后,开始为女性杂志写作。

【信号】 after 时间标志词直接锁定时点。答案句里 after winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition 的 after 是明确的时间定向词,把"开始为女性杂志写作"这一动作精确挂在"获奖"事件之后——听到"writing for women's magazines"紧跟 after,就锁定这一句。

【替换】 after winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition ↔ After winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition.

原文与选项近乎逐字同形,只需对住事件

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

When she started teaching at Edinburgh University in Scotland. 盗用了原文 she taught at the university she graduated from 这一真实事件来诱选,但任教在前(1981 写短篇之前),并非"为女性杂志写作"的时点;且原文是"母校"而非 Edinburgh University,地点也被偷改。 借⽤原⽂： Later, she taught at the university she graduated from B) 原词陷阱

While she was doing her doctoral studies on American Literature. 借原文 she researched a doctorate on American Literature 设套,读博发生在 1974 年毕业后、远早于 1986 年,并非为女性杂志写作的时间。 借⽤原⽂： After graduating in 1974, she researched a doctorate on American Literature C) 原词陷阱

After publishing her first novel Behind the Scenes at the Museum. 借原文 Her first novel, Behind the Scenes at the Museum, won the 1995 UK Book of the Year award 设套;出版在 1995 年、晚于为女性杂志写作的 1986 年,时序正好反了。 借⽤原⽂： Her first novel, Behind the Scenes at the Museum, won the 1995 UK Book of the Year award

questions.prompt: What did Kate Atkinson's books touch on?

options.text: The themes of love and loss.
The code of human behaviour.
The sins and flaws of eccentrics.
The manners of fashionable circles.

questions.shortExplanation: Whatever genre Atkinson writes in, her books touch on the themes of love and loss and how to carry on.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） The themes of love and loss.

【定位】 Whatever genre Atkinson writes in, her books touch on the themes of love and loss and how to carry on.

无论写什么体裁,阿特金森的书都触及爱与失、以及如何继续生活下去这些主题。

【信号】 题干同词 touch on 领起主题,直给答案。答案句 her books touch on the themes of love and loss 用的动词与题干 touch on 完全同款,等于原文亲口把答案领出来——听到 "her books touch on…" 就锁这句,后面紧跟的主题即答案。

【替换】 the themes of love and loss↔ The themes of love and loss. 主题表述逐字对应

【排除】 B) 答非所问

The code of human behaviour. 取自原文后文 the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour,但那是在解释"风尚喜剧"这一文类的定义,不是回答"her books touch on 什么主题"的内容,答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour current in fashionable circles of society C) 答非所问

The sins and flaws of eccentrics. 拼自原文 sometimes sinful, and generally flawed eccentrics,但那句讲的是书里"住着哪类人物形象",而题目问的是 touch on 的"主题",混淆了"登场人物"与"核心主题"。 借⽤原⽂： populated by odd, sometimes sinful, and generally flawed eccentrics D) 答非所问

The manners of fashionable circles. 取自原文 code of behaviour current in fashionable circles of society 与 comedies of manners,这些是解释"风尚喜剧"文类标签的措辞,而非她书的 touch on 主题。 借⽤原⽂： comedies that represent the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour current in fashionable circles of society

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the clever and deceitful characters in a comedy of manners?

options.text: They are usually ignorant of complex human relations.
They successfully imitate the manners of celebrities.
They often get rewarded instead of being punished.
They are generally looked down upon in society.

questions.shortExplanation: A comedy of manners tends to reward its clever and deceitful characters, rather than punish their bad deeds. 风尚喜剧往往奖赏它那些聪明而狡诈的角色,而不是惩罚他们的恶行。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） They often get rewarded instead of being punished.

【定位】 A comedy of manners tends to reward its clever and deceitful characters, rather than punish their bad deeds. 风尚喜剧往往奖赏它那些聪明而狡诈的角色,而不是惩罚他们的恶行。

【信号】 reward…rather than punish 的对比定向句。答案句用 reward its clever and deceitful characters, rather than punish their bad deeds 这一"奖赏 A、而非惩罚 B"的对比结构直接交代结局——rather than 是关键定向词,把方向钉死在"受赏"一边;听到 reward…rather than punish 就锁这句。

【替换】 reward its clever and deceitful characters, rather than punish their bad deeds↔ They often get rewarded instead of being punished. 主动→被动 + rather than=instead of 同义改写

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

They are usually ignorant of complex human relations. 把原文 the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour 里的 complex 一词揪出来拼成"对复杂人际无知",但原文从未说这些角色"无知",纯属据片词臆造。 借⽤原⽂： the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour B) 未提及

They successfully imitate the manners of celebrities. 借原文 manners 一词造势,但原文只字未提这些角色"成功模仿名人",imitate/celebrities 都无出处,属凭空添加。

D) 与原文相反

They are generally looked down upon in society. 取了"受罚/负面"的方向,正好与原文 reward…rather than punish 的"受赏不受罚"相反——原文明说是被奖赏,本项却说被社会看轻,极性反了。 借⽤原⽂： rather than punish their bad deeds

items.title: 2023年12月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 2
items.transcript:
Why is adaptability an important skill to exercise in the workplace? Simply put, adaptability is a skill employers are increasingly looking for. When you spend time learning a new task rather than resisting it, your productivity goes up. You can also serve as an example to your co-workers who may be having trouble adapting, and can help lead your team forward. Strategy consultant, Dorie Clark, explains it to us this way. "I'd say that adaptability is an important skill in the workplace because frankly, circumstances change. Competitors introduce new products, economy might enter a recession, customer preferences differ over time, and more. If you shake your fist at the sky and say why can't it stay the same, that's not going to do very much good. Instead, you need to recognise when circumstances have changed, so you can take appropriate action based on what is, rather than how you wish the world would be. That enables you to make more accurate, informed and effective choices."

Also, the workplace itself has been evolving. Today's work culture and management style is often based on teamwork, rather than a rigid hierarchy. Brainstorming, which requires creativity, flexibility, and emotional intelligence, is a typical problem-solving technique. Employees who are unable or unwilling to participate will not easily move forward in the company. Employees who are flexible demonstrate other skills too. They can reprioritize quickly when changes occur and suggest additional modifications when something is not working. They can also regroup quickly when a setback occurs, adapting to the new situation confidently and without overreacting.

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker say adaptability is an important skill to exercise in the workplace?

options.text: It is what members use to alleviate tension in a team.
It is what employers are increasingly seeking after.
It is conducive to getting over a recession.
It is necessary for learning a new task.

questions.shortExplanation: Simply put, adaptability is a skill employers are increasingly looking for.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） It is what employers are increasingly seeking after.

【定位】 Simply put, adaptability is a skill employers are increasingly looking for.

简单说，适应力是一种雇主越来越看重的技能。

【信号】 Simply put 引出总论断。开篇自问 Why 之后紧跟 Simply put, adaptability is a skill employers are increasingly looking for，Simply put 是抛出核心结论的信号词，这句就是对 Why 的直接回答。

【替换】 employers are increasingly looking for↔employers are increasingly seeking after looking for 同义于 seeking after

【排除】 A) 未提及

alleviate tension in a team 在录音里根本没出现，适应力被说成雇主看重的技能而非用来化解团队紧张的工具，属凭空捏造。

C) 原词陷阱录音后文确念了 economy might enter a recession，但那是举例说明环境会变，并非说适应力有助于度过衰退；C 盗用 recession 制造听到就想选的诱惑，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： economy might enter a recession

D) 原词陷阱

录音里 learning a new task 是说学新任务时生产力会上升，并非说适应力对学新任务必不可少；D 把这个原词搬来当重要性的理由，错位。 借⽤原⽂： When you spend time learning a new task rather than resisting it, your productivity goes up.

questions.prompt: What does adaptability enable us to do according to strategy consultant Dorie Clark?

options.text: Make better choices.
Follow innovative ideas.
Achieve recognition duly.
Accumulate work experience.

questions.shortExplanation: That enables you to make more accurate, informed and effective choices.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Make better choices.

【定位】 That enables you to make more accurate, informed and effective choices.

这使你能够做出更准确、更明智、更有效的选择。

【信号】 enables you to 的因果落点。Dorie Clark 一番话的收尾句 That enables you to make more accurate, informed and effective choices，enables you to 正是题干 enable us to do 的对应信号，结论就在这句。

【替换】 make more accurate, informed and effective choices↔Make better choices. 三个褒义形容词概括为 better

【排除】 B) 未提及

Follow innovative ideas. 在 Dorie Clark 的话里没有依据，她讲的是认清变化、做出选择，未提跟随创新想法。

C) 未提及

Achieve recognition duly. 谈获得认可，录音从未涉及，是凭空添加的职场正能量诱饵。 D) 答非所问

录音说环境会变、要据实采取行动，并未提积累经验；Accumulate work experience. 借职场话题诱你联想，但答案句讲的是做选择，并非攒经验。 借⽤原⽂： you can take appropriate action based on what is, rather than how you wish the world would be

questions.prompt: What do we learn about today's work culture from the passage?

options.text: Workers show more emotional intelligence.
Workers use brains more than muscles.
People usually work flexible hours.
People often work in teams.

questions.shortExplanation: Today's work culture and management style is often based on teamwork, rather than a rigid hierarchy.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） People often work in teams.

【定位】 Today's work culture and management style is often based on teamwork, rather than a rigid hierarchy.

如今的工作文化和管理方式往往建立在团队合作之上，而非僵化的等级制度。

【信号】 Today's work culture 直接点题。第二段开头 Today's work culture and management style is often based on teamwork 与题干用词几乎一致，是直接点题句，答案就在 based on teamwork。

【替换】 based on teamwork ↔ People often work in teams. 名词 teamwork 转为动作 work in teams

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

录音确念了 emotional intelligence，但那是说头脑风暴需要情商，并非说工作者展现出更多情商；A 把这个原词搬来当工作文化特征，安错了对象。 借⽤原⽂： Brainstorming, which requires creativity, flexibility, and emotional intelligence B) 未提及 Workers use brains more than muscles. 这种脑力对体力的对比录音从没说，是凭空臆造的常识性诱饵。 C) 原词陷阱

录音多次出现 flexibility、flexible，但讲的是员工要灵活应变，并未说大家弹性工时； People usually work flexible hours. 借 flexible 同根词诱你联想到工时，无据。 借⽤原⽂： Employees who are flexible demonstrate other skills too.

questions.prompt: What are employees with adaptability able to do when changes occur?

options.text: Leave the group as soon as possible.
Anticipate setbacks well in advance.
Decide on new priorities speedily.
Stick to original goals confidently.

questions.shortExplanation: They can reprioritize quickly when changes occur and suggest additional modifications when something is not working.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Decide on new priorities speedily.

【定位】 They can reprioritize quickly when changes occur and suggest additional modifications when something is not working.

当变化发生时，他们能迅速重新排定优先级，并在某些做法行不通时提出额外的调整。

【信号】 when changes occur 条件句应答。They can reprioritize quickly when changes occur 与题干 when changes occur 逐词对应，reprioritize quickly 就是对该情形的直接应答， 是答案句。

reprioritize=decide on new priorities，quickly=speedily

B) 原词陷阱

录音后句确念了 regroup quickly when a setback occurs，但说的是挫折发生时迅速重整，并非 well in advance 提前预判；Anticipate setbacks well in advance. 盗用 setback 又把时间偷换成事前。 借⽤原⽂： They can also regroup quickly when a setback occurs D) 与原文相反

录音说 adapting to the new situation confidently，confidently 是修饰适应新情况； Stick to original goals confidently. 搬走 confidently 却接上坚持原目标，恰与适应力相反。 借⽤原⽂： adapting to the new situation confidently and without overreacting

items.title: 2023年12月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 1
items.transcript:
What makes humans different from other species? Some philosophers argue it's morals or ethics, while some scientists assert it's our greater cognitive development. But I argue that the main difference is our desire to combat routine. This makes being creative a biological mandate, as what we seek in art and technology is surprise, not simply a fulfillment of expectations.

As a result, a wild imagination has characterized the history of our species. We build intricate habitats, devise complex recipes for our food, wear clothes that reflect constant changes in fashion, communicate with elaborate signs, symbols, and sounds, and travel between habitats on wings and wheels of our own design. To satisfy our appetite for novelty, innovation is key. But who innovates?

Now, many people, both laymen and experts, believe that only geniuses innovate. But I believe that innovation is not something that only a few people do. The innovative drive lives in every human brain, and the resulting war against the repetitive is what powers the massive changes that distinguish one generation from the next. The drive to create the new is a trait of being human. We build cultures by the hundreds and tell new stories by the millions. We create and surround ourselves with things that have never existed before, while animals do not. But where do our new ideas come from?

According to many, new ideas come from seemingly nowhere to great minds. From this perspective, new ideas are almost like magic. They come in a flash of inspiration to a select few. However, the reality is that, across the spectrum of human activities, prior work propels the creative process. We may think of innovation as being the result of inspiration or genius, but it's really the result of developing the ideas of others further. This happens in technology, where one invention enables or inspires further inventions. And it happens in the arts, as writers, composers, and painters use the work of previous artists in their own work. The human brain works from precedent. We take the ideas we've inherited and put them together into some new shape.

What is a true creator? Is a creator a genius who makes something out of nothing? No. Creators are simply humans who use what they inherit, who absorb the past and manipulate it to create possible futures. Thus, humans are creators as a rule rather than as an exception.

questions.prompt: What question does the speaker address in this talk?

options.text: What differentiates people from animals.
Why philosophers disagree with scientists.
Where humans' great cognitive capacity originates.
When being creative becomes a biological mandate.

questions.shortExplanation: What makes humans different from other species? Some philosophers argue it's morals or ethics, while some scientists assert it's our greater cognitive development. But I argue that the main difference is our desire to combat routine.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （主旨题） What differentiates people from animals.

【定位】 What makes humans different from other species? Some philosophers argue it's morals or ethics, while some scientists assert it's our greater cognitive development. But I argue that the main difference is our desire to combat routine.

是什么让人类区别于其他物种？一些哲学家认为是道德或伦理，而一些科学家断言是我们更高级的认知发展。但我认为，主要区别在于我们对抗常规的渴望。

【信号】 开篇设问 + But I argue 亮主线。第一段以设问 What makes humans different from other species 开场，随后用 But I argue that the main difference is our desire to combat routine 中的转折信号 But 和立场词 I argue 亮出全篇主线——这正是篇章独白"开头点题"的答案信号。

【替换】 What makes humans different from other species↔ What differentiates people from animals 同义改写：different from species = differentiates from animals

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

第一段确实念到 Some philosophers argue it's morals or ethics, while some scientists assert it's our greater cognitive development，选项 Why philosophers disagree with scientists 就盗用了 philosophers 和 scientists 这两个原词；但讲者只是借两派观点引出自己的主张，全篇根本不讨论"他们为何分歧"，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： Some philosophers argue it's morals or ethics, while some scientists assert it's our greater cognitive development C) 原词陷阱

选项 Where humans' great cognitive capacity originates 借用了原文 our greater cognitive development 里的 cognitive；但"认知发展"是讲者复述并随即用 But 推翻的科学家旧观点，讲座既不问它"从哪来"，更没把它当主线，纯属盗词诱选。 借⽤原⽂： our greater cognitive development

D) 偷换概念

选项 When being creative becomes a biological mandate 搬来了原文 This makes being creative a biological mandate 的整串短语；但讲者是把"创造是生物律令"当作结论陈述，从没问它"何时"发生，选项用 When 偷换成一个录音没讨论的时机问题。 借⽤原⽂： This makes being creative a biological mandate

questions.prompt: What does the speaker believe about innovation?

options.text: It is what tells apart two adjacent generations.
It is what sharpens our appetite for novelty.
It is something only geniuses can achieve.
It is something every human being can do.

questions.shortExplanation: Now, many people, both laymen and experts, believe that only geniuses innovate. But I believe that innovation is not something that only a few people do. The innovative drive lives in every human brain. 如今，许多人——无论外行还是专家——都认为只有天才才会创新。但我认为，创新并不是只有少数人才能做的事。创新的驱动力存在于每一个人的大脑中。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （态度观点题） It is something every human being can do.

【定位】 Now, many people, both laymen and experts, believe that only geniuses innovate. But I believe that innovation is not something that only a few people do. The innovative drive lives in every human brain. 如今，许多人——无论外行还是专家——都认为只有天才才会创新。但我认为，创新并不是只有少数人才能做的事。创新的驱动力存在于每一个人的大脑中。

【信号】 But I believe + not… only a few 的立场转折。讲者先用 many people…believe that only geniuses innovate 摆出大众看法，再以 But I believe that innovation is not something that only a few people do 中的 But I believe 强力转折亮出己见——转折后 + I believe 的句子正是观点题的答案信号。

【替换】 innovation is not something that only a few people do↔ It is something every human being can do 否定转肯定：not only a few = every human The innovative drive lives in every human brain↔ every human being can do every human brain = every human being

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

选项 It is what tells apart two adjacent generations 借用了原文 distinguish one generation from the next 里的 generation；但原文说的是"创新所引发的变化"区分了代际，而非"创新本身就是用来区分两代人的"，选项把因果关系改成了创新的定义，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： distinguish one generation from the next B) 原词陷阱

选项 It is what sharpens our appetite for novelty 拼用了第二段的 our appetite for novelty；但原文是"为满足对新奇的渴望，创新是关键"，是渴望催生创新，选项却反过来说"创新激起对新奇的渴望"，因果颠倒、且并非讲者对创新的核心看法。 借⽤原⽂： To satisfy our appetite for novelty, innovation is key C) 与原文相反

选项 It is something only geniuses can achieve 几乎照抄原文 only geniuses innovate；但这恰是讲者用 But I believe 明确推翻的大众看法，是"与原文相反"——把讲者反对的观点当成讲者的观点，正好选反。 借⽤原⽂： many people…believe that only geniuses innovate

questions.prompt: How does the human brain work according to the speaker?

options.text: It seeks inspiration for novel inventions.
It constantly absorbs new information.
It uses existing ideas to create new ones.
It repeats precedent on a regular basis.

questions.shortExplanation: The human brain works from precedent. We take the ideas we've inherited and put them together into some new shape.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） It uses existing ideas to create new ones.

【定位】 The human brain works from precedent. We take the ideas we've inherited and put them together into some new shape.

人脑依凭先例而运作。我们把继承来的想法拿来，重新组合成某种新的形态。

【信号】 直陈机制句 works from + take… put… into new shape。讲者用 The human brain works from precedent 直接点出机制，又以 We take the ideas we've inherited and put them together into some new shape 展开"拿旧的拼成新的"——这种正面解释"怎么运作"的句子就是细节题的答案信号。

【替换】 take the ideas we've inherited and put them together into some new shape↔ uses existing ideas to create new ones

继承的旧想法拼成新形状 = 用已有想法造新的 it's really the result of developing the ideas of others further↔ uses existing ideas to create new ones

在他人想法上further发展 = 用已有想法造新

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

选项 It seeks inspiration for novel inventions 拼用了原文 inspiration 和 one invention enables or inspires further inventions 里的词；但讲者明说新想法"几乎像魔法般灵感闪现"只是大众误解，他真正主张的是"靠先例"，故"四处寻找灵感"并非讲者的机制描述。 借⽤原⽂： They come in a flash of inspiration to a select few B) 偷换概念

选项 constantly absorbs new information 听上去像"大脑怎么运作"的合理答案，且 absorb 一词原文第五段确实念到 absorb the past；但原文说的是"吸收过去/旧的东西"， 选项偷换成"不断吸收新信息"，方向正好相反，差在 past 被改成 new information。 借⽤原⽂： absorb the past and manipulate it to create possible futures D) 与原文相反

选项 repeats precedent on a regular basis 借走了原文 works from precedent 的 precedent；但讲者说的是"依凭先例去拼出新东西"，强调的是"造新"，选项却说成"只是定期重复先例"，把创造性的"用旧造新"歪曲为机械重复，与原意相反。 借⽤原⽂： The human brain works from precedent

items.title: 2023年12月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 2
items.transcript:
Many dog owners would tell you that their dog somehow knows when they're ill or upset, and according to researchers who study dog cognition, those pet owners are right. Dogs do know when their human companions are having a rough time. Not only can your dog sense when you have a cold, but domestic dogs have shown an aptitude for detecting both much smaller mood fluctuations and far more serious physical conditions. This is because dogs are extremely sensitive to changes in the people they're familiar with, and illness causes change. If a person is infected with a virus or bacteria, for example, their odor will be abnormal, and dogs are able to smell that change even if the human can't, because dogs have a much more powerful sense of smell than humans.

Researchers have also found that a person's mood, which can be an indicator of a larger illness, triggers a dog's sense of smell. Human emotions manifest physically in chemical signals that are emitted by the body, and dogs are able to smell those as well. Beyond smell, dogs gather information from a person's voice in order to sense changes.

In 2014, researchers discovered that dogs have an area of the brain similar to one in humans that allows them to understand emotional cues in the tone of a speaker's voice, beyond what they'd be able to pick up from familiar words alone. A person's voice can also carry indicators of illness. What's not understood quite so well is what dogs understand about these changes. Humans send out lots of cues, but whether dogs know some of these cues mean illness isn't clear. What we perceive as concern on a dog's part might be more like increased curiosity or suspicion that something is wrong with us, and sticking close by is a great way to gather more information about the situation.

Some researchers assert dogs will one day help doctors diagnose diseases, as some dogs have already demonstrated the ability to detect an assortment of ailments, including diabetes and certain types of cancer. But those researchers concede that's probably in the distant future. For now, research suggests dog ownership can have an array of benefits in and of itself. Keeping a pet dog has been shown to bolster health and boost mood. Dogs also help people relax, and they can be a particular comfort to those with chronic diseases.

【答案】 A （细节题） Dogs know when their owners are not feeling well.

【定位】 Many dog owners would tell you that their dog somehow knows when they're ill or upset, and according to researchers who study dog cognition, those pet owners are right.

许多狗主人会告诉你，他们的狗不知怎么就能知道他们生病或心烦了；而据研究狗的认知的研究者所言，这些主人是对的。

【信号】 研究者的认定语 those pet owners are right。答案落在研究者对狗主人看法的直接认定 those pet owners are right 上——"研究者支持哪个看法"的答案，就藏在他们说"对"所指向的那句话里，即狗能知道主人 ill or upset。

【替换】 their dog somehow knows when they're ill or upset ↔ Dogs know when their owners are not feeling well ill or upset 概括为 not feeling well

【排除】 B) 未提及

telling right from wrong（分辨对错）说的是道德认知，录音通篇讲狗"感知主人健康/情绪"，从未谈狗能分辨是非，属凭常识脑补。

C) 原词陷阱

items.title: 2023年12月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 3
items.transcript:
Earlier this month, the think-tank called Onward published a report, "A Question of Degree", which argues that degrees in the creative arts are not good value for money. Ministers, according to Onward, should "crack down on courses that offer extremely limited value for money to students ten years after graduation", restricting the ability of such courses to recruit new students, if the average graduate earns below the student loans payment threshold. Courses like science, technology, engineering, and math, and economics, where the average graduate earns a lot, should be favored.

The report provides insight into a government review which looks at how to reform technical education and how to ensure students get good value for money. At first glance, it might even seem like Onward have a point. According to their data, the majority of creative arts students earn less than 25,000 pounds a year, ten years after graduation. The average male creative arts students, indeed, apparently earn much less than they would, had they simply never gone to university. This isn't really good for anyone, and it's certainly no good for graduates, who are forced to endure a lifestyle where they can never save up, never buy a house, never hope to retire.

Onward has identified a real problem. Creative arts graduates from top universities—like Oxford, with a high proportion of privately-educated students—have fairly good work prospects. Well, 40 percent of all graduates—regardless of their degree—are on less than 25,000 pounds a year, 5 years after graduation. This suggests that the problem isn't really to do with specific students studying specific degrees, but really with the economy as a whole. Regardless of what they've studied, young people find it hard to get ahead unless they're lucky enough to be born with successful parents.

If ministers want to make education pay for young people, they need to look beyond the higher education sector, towards the wider world. The rewards that education gives us are not measurable. They are not always instantly obvious, and certainly not always direct. An education makes you a different person from the one you would have been if you hadn't received it. We need to look at the value of education not in the context of a bank balance, but of a life. If we continue to allow ourselves to be distracted with talk of "value for money", we will all be made poorer as a result.

questions.prompt: What does Onward's report propose ministers should do?

options.text: Crack down on courses like science, technology, engineering and math.
Restrict the ability of creative arts courses to recruit new students.
Look at how to reform technical and vocational education.
Ensure creative arts students get better value for money.

questions.shortExplanation: Ministers, according to Onward, should "crack down on courses that offer extremely limited value for money to students ten years after graduation", restricting the ability of such courses to recruit new students, if the average graduate earns below the student loans payment threshold.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Restrict the ability of creative arts courses to recruit new students.

【定位】 Ministers, according to Onward, should "crack down on courses that offer extremely limited value for money to students ten years after graduation", restricting the ability of such courses to recruit new students, if the average graduate earns below the student loans payment threshold.

据 Onward 称，大臣们应当"严打那些在学生毕业十年后仍只能提供极有限性价比的课程"， 即在这类课程毕业生平均收入低于助学贷款偿还门槛时，限制它们招收新生的能力。

【信号】 建议信号 should，紧跟报告主张。Ministers, according to Onward, should 里的 according to Onward + should 双重标记，明确这是"报告建议大臣做什么"，正是题干所问，后半 restricting the ability of such courses to recruit new students 即具体动作。

【替换】 restricting the ability of such courses to recruit new students↔ Restrict the ability of creative arts courses to recruit new students. 几乎原句保留，such courses 具体化为 creative arts courses

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

选项盗用了原文 crack down on courses 和 science, technology, engineering, and math 两处原词，但原文 crack down 针对的是低回报课程，而理工科恰恰是 should be favored（应受青睐）。把"打压"安到理工科头上，正负方向全反。 借⽤原⽂： Courses like science, technology, engineering, and math, and economics, where the average graduate earns a lot, should be favored. C) 张冠李戴

选项盗用了第二段 looks at how to reform technical education 的原词，但那是 a government review（政府评估）的工作内容，并非 Onward 报告"提议大臣做"的事。题干问的是报告 propose 什么，主体被偷换。 借⽤原⽂： The report provides insight into a government review which looks at how to reform technical education D) 偷换概念

选项里 24D 式的 value for money 措辞来自 ensure students get good value for money，但那同样是政府评估关注的目标，且报告主张的是"限制招生"这一具体动作，而非"确保创意艺术学生物有所值"。把整体评估目标偷换成报告的提议。 借⽤原⽂： how to ensure students get good value for money

questions.prompt: What does the speaker think of Onward's arguments?

options.text: Seemingly reasonable.
Clearly well-grounded.
Extremely irrational.
Apparently simplistic.

questions.shortExplanation: At first glance, it might even seem like Onward have a point.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （态度观点题） Seemingly reasonable.

【定位】 At first glance, it might even seem like Onward have a point.

乍一看，Onward 的观点甚至似乎还有几分道理。

【信号】 让步信号 At first glance + might seem，暗示"表面有理"。At first glance, it might even seem like Onward have a point. 中 At first glance（乍看）与 might even seem （似乎）连用，是典型的"表面看…"让步语气，说明作者承认其"看似有理"，但保留实质判断——后文随即用数据与反驳推翻它。

【替换】 At first glance, it might even seem like Onward have a point.↔Seemingly reasonable. seem like...have a point ↔ Seemingly reasonable，详述概括化

【排除】 B)

Clearly well-grounded. 把作者的 seem like（似乎）拔高成 Clearly（明显）、well-grounded（根据充分）。原文有 At first glance\might even seem 的限定，恰恰说明作者认为它经不起推敲，并非"明显有理"。 借⽤原⽂： it might even seem like Onward have a point C) 过度推断

Extremely irrational. 把作者温和的"看似有理但有问题"夸张成"极不理性"。原文是 might even seem like...have a point，承认其表面合理，远没到 extremely irrational 的全盘否定，态度强度严重失真。 D) 未提及

Apparently simplistic. 的 Apparently 蹭了原文"表面看"的味道，但 simplistic（过于简单化）这一评价原文从未给出——作者的批评是"问题不在具体学位而在整体经济"，是归因偏差，而非"简单化"。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about British college graduates five years after graduation?

options.text: A high proportion of them haven't tried to save money.
Most of them never hope to buy a house or to retire.
Forty percent of them earn less than ￡25,000 a year.
The majority of them have fairly well-paying jobs.

questions.shortExplanation: Well, 40 percent of all graduates—regardless of their degree—are on less than 25,000 pounds a year, 5 years after graduation.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Forty percent of them earn less than ￡25,000 a year.

【定位】 Well, 40 percent of all graduates—regardless of their degree—are on less than 25,000 pounds a year, 5 years after graduation.

要知道，所有毕业生中——无论学的什么专业——有 40% 的人在毕业 5 年后年收入低于 25000 英镑。

【信号】 精确限定三连：40% + all graduates + 5 years after。40 percent of all graduates— regardless of their degree—are on less than 25,000 pounds a year, 5 years after graduation. 同时给出百分比、人群（all graduates）、时间（5 years），三项限定与题干 five years after graduation 完全对齐，是唯一匹配句。

【替换】 40 percent of all graduates↔Forty percent of them 数字逐字对应，all graduates ↔ them less than 25,000 pounds a year↔ less than ￡25,000 a year

金额与范围词原样保留

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

选项盗用了 never save up 的原词，但原文是"被迫过上永远存不下钱的生活"，说的是"现状被迫如此"，并非 haven't tried to save money（没尝试去存钱）。把"存不下"偷换成"没去尝试存"，且该描述属 P2 的创意艺术生、非本题 5 年后的全体毕业生。 借⽤原⽂： never save up, never buy a house, never hope to retire B) 原词陷阱

选项盗用 never buy a house never hope to retire 的原词，但原文是"被迫过上永远买不起房、不敢指望退休的生活"，是被环境所迫的处境，不是 never hope to buy a house or to retire（主观上不想买房退休）。且这同样是 P2 描述创意艺术生的，与题干 5 年后全体毕业生不符。 借⽤原⽂： never buy a house, never hope to retire D) 与原文相反

The majority of them have fairly well-paying jobs. 蹭了 P3 fairly good work prospects（顶尖名校创意艺术生前景不错）的原词，但那只针对牛津等顶尖名校的少数人；就全体毕业生而言原文恰恰说 40% 低于 25000，多数收入并不高。把局部的"前景好"放大成整体"多数高薪"，方向相反。 借⽤原⽂： Creative arts graduates from top universities—like Oxford...—have fairly good work prospects.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say actually accounts for the problem identified by Onward?

options.text: The context of a bank balance.
Britain's economy as a whole.
The specific degree a student earns.
Britain's defective educational system.

questions.shortExplanation: This suggests that the problem isn't really to do with specific students studying specific degrees, but really with the economy as a whole.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Britain's economy as a whole.

【定位】 This suggests that the problem isn't really to do with specific students studying specific degrees, but really with the economy as a whole.

这表明，问题其实并不在于具体学生读了什么具体专业，而真正在于整体经济。

【信号】 对照信号 isn't...but...，真因在 but 之后。the problem isn't really to do with specific students studying specific degrees, but really with the economy as a whole. 用 isn't...but... 先否掉"具体专业"这个归因，再把真正原因点在 but 之后的 the economy as a whole，正对题干 actually accounts for。

【替换】 the economy as a whole↔ Britain's economy as a whole. economy as a whole 几乎原词，补限定 Britain's

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

The context of a bank balance. 盗用了 P4 the value of education not in the context of a bank balance 的原词，但原文恰恰说"不要在银行账户的语境里、而要在人生的语境里看教育的价值"，bank balance 是作者要否定的衡量方式，而非问题根源。 借⽤原⽂： not in the context of a bank balance, but of a life C) 原词陷阱

The specific degree a student earns. 盗用 specific students studying specific degrees 的原词，且顺着前文"创意艺术学位不值钱"最像答案；但原文 isn't really to do with specific...degrees 已把它明确否定，真因在 but 之后，故它正是要排的"but 前被否定项"。 借⽤原⽂： the problem isn't really to do with specific students studying specific degrees D) 未提及

Britain's defective educational system. 听着像总结，但原文从未说"英国教育制度有缺陷"是问题根源；作者归因是 the economy as a whole（整体经济），并在 P4 主张到"高等教育之外的更广世界"去看，并未指控教育系统 defective。

items.title: 2023年12月六级第2套 · 长对话 1
items.transcript:
W: So, I've been thinking, this summer, instead of our usual holiday rental, I'd like to try renting a camper van and exploring a bit more.

M: A camper van? You mean to spend the summer living out of a car?

W: Yes, a camper van. And no, it's nothing like living out of a car. These are proper vans with full-size beds to sleep in. Some even have kitchens. This way, we wouldn't have to be locked into one place during our holiday. We'd be able to visit so many more places and travel at our own pace. The rates of most hotels and holiday homes really soar in the summer anyway. We'd probably save a lot of money as well.

M: I think my grandfather had a van like that. It doesn't sound that appealing to me.

W: Today's camper vans are completely different. These days, they're equipped with all the modern comforts. I've seen quite a few with solar panels that provide electricity for when you're stopped. This way, you can still use your computer or charge your phone. And most even have Wi-Fi, so if the weather's not great, you could stream videos.

M: I'm warming up to the idea. Keep talking.

W: Loads of people are committing to this trend full time. Check it out online. Lots of people stream videos of their alternative lifestyles and actually earn a salary. Imagine having that kind of freedom to go anywhere you want and work from anywhere in the world.

M: Okay, we can consider it. As long as the basic needs like toilet and showers are covered, I'm definitely in. Do you think there will be enough room for my mountain bike? What about food delivery? Will we be able to order at the van? Will there be enough space for the dog? We wouldn't want to leave him behind.

W: Slow down. Glad you're excited about it. Let's start by looking at what's available first.

questions.prompt: What has the woman been thinking of doing for this summer?

options.text: Renting a car instead of driving their own.
Surfing online to check out the best deals.
Exploring more summer holiday resorts.
Spending their holidays in a novel way.

questions.shortExplanation: So, I've been thinking, this summer, instead of our usual holiday rental, I'd like to try renting a camper van and exploring a bit more.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Spending their holidays in a novel way.

【定位】 So, I've been thinking, this summer, instead of our usual holiday rental, I'd like to try renting a camper van and exploring a bit more.

嗯，我一直在想，今年夏天，不走我们往常租度假屋那一套，我想试试租一辆房车、多走走看看。

【信号】 意愿句I'd like to。答案信号是女方直接表达意愿的 I'd like to try renting a camper van and exploring a bit more，I'd like to（我想）这类意愿句正是“她想做什么”的落点，紧跟在 I've been thinking 之后，开门见山。

【替换】 renting a camper van and exploring a bit more↔Spending their holidays in a novel way 具体做法概括为“新方式” instead of our usual holiday rental↔in a novel way “不走老一套”=“新方式”

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

选项 Renting a car instead of driving their own. 盗用了原文 renting a camper van 里的 renting，听到“租”就想选；但她租的是 camper van（房车）不是普通 car，更没说“不开自己的车”，是把原词嫁接到一个原文没有的意思上。 借⽤原⽂： renting a camper van B) 原词陷阱

Surfing online to check out the best deals. 里 online 确实在录音里出现过，但那是后文 Check it out online 让对方上网看这种生活方式，并非她“这个夏天想做的事”，时间点和意图都错位。 借⽤原⽂： Check it out online C) 偷换概念

Exploring more summer holiday resorts. 借用了 exploring 和 summer holiday 的字眼，听感很熟；但她说的是 exploring a bit more（多走走看看更多地方），从没提“度假胜地 resorts”，是把模糊的“多探索”偷换成具体的“逛度假村”。 借⽤原⽂： exploring a bit more

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the man's grandfather from the conversation?

options.text: He once owned a van.
He was well travelled.
He did not find holiday homes appealing.
He did not like to be locked into one place.

questions.shortExplanation: M: I think my grandfather had a van like that. It doesn't sound that appealing to me.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） He once owned a van.

【定位】 M: I think my grandfather had a van like that. It doesn't sound that appealing to me.

男：我记得我爷爷有过一辆那样的车。这听着对我没什么吸引力。

【信号】 提到祖父那一句。答案信号就是男方亲口提到祖父的 I think my grandfather had a van like that——题目点名 grandfather，原文唯一讲祖父的就是这句，had a van 直接给出关于祖父的事实。

【替换】 my grandfather had a van like that↔He once owned a van had a van=owned a van

【排除】 B) 未提及

He was well travelled.（他见多识广 / 走过很多地方）原文从未说祖父，是无中生有；对话只说祖父有过车，没说他爱旅行，属未提及的凭空拔高。

C) 张冠李戴

He did not find holiday homes appealing. 盗用了原文 It doesn't sound that appealing to me 里的 appealing；但说“不吸引人”的是男方本人对房车主意的反应，且嫌的是房车不是 holiday homes，把男方的话张冠李戴成祖父的态度。 借⽤原⽂： It doesn't sound that appealing to me D) 张冠李戴

He did not like to be locked into one place. 盗用了 we wouldn't have to be locked into one place 的 locked into one place；但那是女方在讲房车的好处，主语是“我们”， 不是祖父的喜好，人物与语境双重错位。 借⽤原⽂： we wouldn't have to be locked into one place

questions.prompt: What can many camper vans do nowadays according to the woman?

options.text: Ensure the safety of passengers.
Drive under any weather condition.
Receive instructions via computers.
Generate their own electricity.

questions.shortExplanation: I've seen quite a few with solar panels that provide electricity for when you're stopped.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Generate their own electricity.

【定位】 I've seen quite a few with solar panels that provide electricity for when you're stopped.

我见过不少装了太阳能板的，停车时能供电。

【信号】 功能描述provide electricity。答案信号是描述具体功能的 solar panels that provide electricity——provide electricity（提供电力）直接说出房车“能做什么”，是这段功能罗列里与选项对得上的那一句。

【替换】 solar panels that provide electricity↔Generate their own electricity

供电=自己发电

【排除】 A) 未提及

Ensure the safety of passengers. 原文整段讲的是供电、Wi-Fi、看视频这些舒适功能，从未提“保障乘客安全”，是凭常识硬加的功能，属未提及。

B) 原词陷阱

Drive under any weather condition. 利用了原文 if the weather's not great 的 weather；但原文说的是“天气不好时可以看流媒体视频”，是娱乐功能，根本不是“任何天气都能开车”，把 weather 嫁接到一个原文没有的能力上。 借⽤原⽂： if the weather's not great C) 原词陷阱

Receive instructions via computers. 盗用了原文 you can still use your computer 里的 computer；但原文是“你可以用自己的电脑”，主语是人在用电脑，不是房车“通过电脑接收指令”，把人的行为偷换成车的功能。 借⽤原⽂： you can still use your computer

questions.prompt: What idea does the woman find attractive?

options.text: Having one's basic needs covered while away from home.
Enjoying the freedom to choose where to go and work.
Slowing down in one's increasingly hectic life.

questions.shortExplanation: Imagine having that kind of freedom to go anywhere you want and work from anywhere in the world. 想象一下，拥有那种自由——想去哪儿就去哪儿，还能在世界任何地方工作。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （态度观点题） Enjoying the freedom to choose where to go and work.

【定位】 Imagine having that kind of freedom to go anywhere you want and work from anywhere in the world. 想象一下，拥有那种自由——想去哪儿就去哪儿，还能在世界任何地方工作。

【信号】 向往句Imagine having。答案信号是女方满怀憧憬的 Imagine having that kind of freedom——Imagine having（想象一下拥有）是她表达向往的语气，紧跟其后的 freedom 就是她觉得吸引人的那一点。

【替换】 that kind of freedom to go anywhere you want and work from anywhere in the world↔ Enjoying the freedom to choose where to go and work 几乎逐点对应的同义改写

【排除】 A) 张冠李戴

Having one's basic needs covered while away from home. 盗用了原文 the basic needs like toilet and showers are covered；但说在意 basic needs 的是男方（M），不是女方，题目问的是女方觉得什么吸引人，人物错位。 借⽤原⽂： the basic needs like toilet and showers are covered C) 偷换概念

Slowing down in one's increasingly hectic life. 借用了原文 Slow down 里的 slow down；但那是女方让激动的男方“别急、慢点说”，是对话节奏用语，根本不是她觉得吸引人的生活理念，把口语提醒偷换成人生主张。 借⽤原⽂： Slow down D) 张冠李戴 Riding one's mountain bike on vacation. 盗用了原文 my mountain bike；但提山地车的是男方（担心装不装得下），与女方“觉得吸引人”毫无关系，人物和语境都错。 借⽤原⽂： my mountain bike

items.title: 2023年12月六级第2套 · 长对话 2
items.transcript:
W: You wanted to see me?

M: Yes, I'll get straight to the point. Over the past month or so, it has become apparent that your performance has dipped. You've been late to work several times these past few weeks, which is very uncharacteristic of you. But what really concerns me is your curtailed output. Lately, you seem to be constantly one step behind. What's going on?

W: I'm sorry. I'm going through some unfortunate family issues at the moment. It's a personal matter, so if you don't mind, I much prefer we don't get into it. Nevertheless, I expect it to have all blown over in another month or so.

M: Do you need some time off?

W: Actually, yes. Would it be possible to take the next two Mondays off? I was deliberating whether I should ask for this, but now that we're here…

M: Sure thing. But if you needed some leave, why didn't you ask for it earlier?

W: I'm not sure why. I guess I kind of felt bad asking for it.

M: You shouldn't feel bad asking for leave, especially if you need it.

W: I know. You're right. I'm sorry.

M: Look, you've been with us almost five years and I personally really value your proficiency at your job. It makes my job far easier. In addition, I can assure you that management as a whole also holds you in high regard.

W: Thank you.

M: What I need is for you to be back at your 100%. Are you sure taking two Mondays off will suffice?

W: It'll be enough. I'm sure of it.

M: Okay, good. So this is what we're going to do. You will take those days off, and I expect that you will gradually come back to your usual self. Then in two months' time, we will catch up again to see how you are faring.

W: Sounds good. Thank you for your understanding.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the woman from the man's description?

options.text: She has missed several important appointments lately.
Her job performance has worsened over the past month.
She has lagged behind most of her co-workers in output.
Her physical health has deteriorated these past few weeks.

questions.shortExplanation: Over the past month or so, it has become apparent that your performance has dipped. You've been late to work several times these past few weeks, which is very uncharacteristic of you. But what really concerns me is your curtailed output.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Her job performance has worsened over the past month.

【定位】 Over the past month or so, it has become apparent that your performance has dipped. You've been late to work several times these past few weeks, which is very uncharacteristic of you. But what really concerns me is your curtailed output.

在过去一个月左右，很明显你的表现下滑了。这几周你好几次上班迟到，这很不像你。但真正让我担心的是你产出减少了。

【信号】 总起定性句 + 转折强调。男方开口就给总定性 your performance has dipped，又用 But what really concerns me 的转折把重点压到"产出减少"上；"总起判断句 + But 后的强调"正是答案句信号。

【替换】 your performance has dipped↔ Her job performance has worsened dipped=worsened 同义替换 Over the past month or so↔over the past month 时间范围对应

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

原文确说她 late to work several times（多次迟到），A 却说 missed several important appointments（错过重要约会），盗用"several"和"迟到"的影子，把"上班迟到"偷换成"错过约会"，answer非所答。 借⽤原⽂： You've been late to work several times these past few weeks C) 原词陷阱

原文只说她 curtailed output（产出减少），C 用了"output"原词，却擅自加上 lagged behind most of her co-workers（落后于大多数同事），原文从没拿她和同事作比较，属无中生有的范围扩大。 借⽤原⽂： what really concerns me is your curtailed output D) 未提及

原文谈的是工作"表现/产出"下滑，D 却说 physical health has deteriorated（身体健康变差），原文男方描述中根本没提她身体生病，属未提及；这与第6题的健康选项呼应，是跨题混淆。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say she's experiencing at the moment?

options.text: Serious health issues.
Disturbance of her mind.
Some problems at home.
Penalty for curtailed output.

questions.shortExplanation: I'm sorry. I'm going through some unfortunate family issues at the moment. It's a personal matter, so if you don't mind, I much prefer we don't get into it.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Some problems at home.

【定位】 I'm sorry. I'm going through some unfortunate family issues at the moment. It's a personal matter, so if you don't mind, I much prefer we don't get into it.

对不起，我目前正经历一些不幸的家庭问题。这是私人的事，如果你不介意，我更希望我们不要深谈。

【信号】 被问者应答 + I'm going through 自述。男方追问 What's going on? 后，女方的直接应答 I'm going through some unfortunate family issues 就是答案句；"被问者应答"加上 I'm going through 这种亲口陈述原因的句式，是双重定位信号。

【替换】 family issues↔ problems at home family issues=problems at home 同义替换 at the moment↔ Some "some...issues"对"Some problems"

【排除】 A) 未提及

女方从没说自己有 serious health issues（严重健康问题），健康话题是借第5题 D 项的余味来混淆，原文她给的原因是家事不是身体，属未提及。

B) 过度推断 Disturbance of her mind（心神不宁）原文从未出现，可能由"她状态不好"脑补出"心理问题"，但女方明说是 family issues、a personal matter，是家事而非精神疾患，属过度推断。

D) 原词陷阱

D 的 curtailed output 是从男方第2段 curtailed output 原封搬来的原词，但本题问她"在经历什么"，curtailed output 是"表现"不是"原因"，且"Penalty for"（因…受罚）原文根本没有，盗原词来答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： what really concerns me is your curtailed output

questions.prompt: What does the man say makes his job far easier?

options.text: The woman's work proficiency.
The woman's whole-hearted support.
His engaging personality.
His management capability.

questions.shortExplanation: I personally really value your proficiency at your job. It makes my job far easier.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） The woman's work proficiency.

【定位】 I personally really value your proficiency at your job. It makes my job far easier.

我个人非常看重你在工作上的熟练。这让我的工作轻松多了。

【信号】 题干同款短语 makes my job easier。原文 It makes my job far easier 与题干 makes his job far easier 是同一短语，前一句的 your proficiency at your job 就是"It"指代的内容，定位锁这两句。

【替换】 your proficiency at your job↔The woman's work proficiency your=the woman's，视角转换

【排除】 B) 偷换概念原文男方说 I personally really value your proficiency（看重你的熟练），B 借"value/对她的肯定"的影子说成 whole-hearted support（全心全意的支持），但让他工作轻松的是她的"熟练"不是"支持"，原文没说她全力支持他，属偷换概念。 借⽤原⽂： I personally really value your proficiency at your job C) 张冠李戴

His engaging personality（他迷人的性格）讲的是男方自己的特质，但原文让工作轻松的是"你的熟练"即女方，C 把归属从女方错挪到男方，且"魅力"原文从未出现，属张冠李戴。 D) 张冠李戴

His management capability（他的管理能力）原文从未提及，且方向反了——让工作轻松的是女方的熟练，不是男方自己的管理力，既张冠李戴又无中生有。

questions.prompt: What agreement have the speakers reached by the end of the conversation?

options.text: The woman will resume her work in two weeks.
The man will be back at his 100% in a couple of weeks.
The woman will be off work on the next two Mondays.
The man will help the woman get back to her usual self.

questions.shortExplanation: W: Would it be possible to take the next two Mondays off? ... M: Sure thing. ... M: So this is what we're going to do. You will take those days off, and I expect that you will gradually come back to your usual self.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） The woman will be off work on the next two Mondays.

【定位】 W: Would it be possible to take the next two Mondays off? ... M: Sure thing. ... M: So this is what we're going to do. You will take those days off, and I expect that you will gradually come back to your usual self.

女：能让我接下来两个周一请假吗？……男：当然可以。……男：那我们就这么办，你把那两天休掉，我希望你慢慢恢复到平时的状态。

【信号】 请求—应允—拍板三处合一。女方提出 take the next two Mondays off，男方 Sure thing 应允，结尾再 So this is what we're going to do. You will take those days off 拍板；"请求被应允并在结尾确认"是约定题的答案信号。

【替换】 take the next two Mondays off ↔ be off work on the next two Mondays

take...off=be off work 同义替换 You will take those days off ↔ The woman will be off work

结尾确认句坐实主语是女方

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

A 说 resume her work in two weeks（两周后复工），但原文女方只是休"两个周一"、并非停工两周后才回来；"two"原词在，时间概念却被偷换，且 in two months 才是再约谈时间，A 张冠时间。 借⽤原⽂： take the next two Mondays off B) 张冠李戴

B 说 The man will be back at his 100%，但原文 What I need is for you to be back at your 100% 是男方要求"你（女方）"回到100%，主语该是女方不是男方；盗用 100% 原词却把人安反，属张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： What I need is for you to be back at your 100% D) 过度推断

D 说 The man will help the woman get back to her usual self，但原文是男方期望"你会慢慢恢复"you will gradually come back to your usual self，是女方自己恢复，并非男方"帮"她；盗 usual self 原词却脑补出"帮助"，属过度推断。 借⽤原⽂： you will gradually come back to your usual self

items.title: 2023年12月六级第2套 · 听力篇章 1
items.transcript: There are many factors that impact our health. These include our finances, our emotions and the way we work. Education is one such factor. Research suggests that higher levels of education can lead to better health and even greater longevity. But what about the education of your partner? New research seeks to answer this question. Researchers use data from a longitudinal study. The data came from surveys first administered to high school seniors in 1957. The surveys ended in 2011. The team found that a person whose spouse had a higher level of education tended to report better health. This remained the case when adjusting for other factors, such as participants' own education, social background and health status before and after marriage. The authors suggest that high levels of education provide shared social, intellectual, emotional and financial resources. These include things like higher levels of emotional intelligence, particular skills or knowledge, or more money. The researchers concede that an individual's own level of education is clearly important for their health, but they assert that individuals also can reap the benefits of their partner's education. It is noteworthy that the effects vary by gender. For women, health was more closely correlated to their spouse's education than for men. The team suggests this may be related to the time period of the study. Women in this sample had lower levels of education and lower occupational achievements than the men. The researchers' hypothesis is that this made the husband's resources more likely to have a shared impact.

questions.prompt: What does research suggest about a higher level of education?

options.text: It can have an impact on our moods and emotions.
It can enable us to live a healthier and longer life.
It can improve our financial status significantly.
It can help us achieve better work performance.

questions.shortExplanation: Research suggests that higher levels of education can lead to better health and even greater longevity.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） It can enable us to live a healthier and longer life.

【定位】 Research suggests that higher levels of education can lead to better health and even greater longevity.

研究表明，更高的教育水平能带来更好的健康状况，甚至更长的寿命。

【信号】 题干原词在原文的复现句。录音里 Research suggests that higher levels of education 几乎逐字复述了题干 What does research suggest about a higher level of education 的措辞，这种'题干怎么问、原文就怎么开头'的句子就是答案句，紧跟其后的 can lead to better health and even greater longevity 即为结论。

【替换】 better health and even greater longevity↔live a healthier and longer life

名词换成形容词、同义改写

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

录音开头确实念到 our emotions，但那是在列举'影响健康的诸多因素'时提到的，并非说'教育能影响情绪'。选项 have an impact on our moods and emotions 把这个原词搬来，答的却不是题干问的'教育带来什么'。 借⽤原⽂： our finances, our emotions and the way we work C) 原词陷阱

录音里 our finances 同样只是被列为'影响健康的因素'之一，原文从未说'教育能显著改善财务'。选项 improve our financial status significantly 借 finances 这个原词设套，与题干所问无关。 借⽤原⽂： our finances, our emotions and the way we work D) 原词陷阱录音说 the way we work 是影响健康的因素之一，并未说'教育能带来更好的工作表现'。选项 achieve better work performance 用 work 这个原词制造熟悉感，但属无中生有。 借⽤原⽂： the way we work
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the finding of the new research?

options.text: One's health tends to differ before and after marriage.
One's health status is related to one's social background.
The wealthier one's spouse is, the healthier one becomes.
The spouse's level of education can impact one's health.

questions.shortExplanation: The team found that a person whose spouse had a higher level of education tended to report better health.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） The spouse's level of education can impact one's health.

【定位】 The team found that a person whose spouse had a higher level of education tended to report better health.

研究团队发现，配偶受教育水平更高的人，往往报告自己的健康状况更好。

【信号】 The team found 引出研究结论。The team found that 是典型的'结论引导句'，篇章里凡以'研究团队发现……'开头的话，几乎必是某道题的答案句；其后整句就是这项新研究的核心发现。

【替换】 a person whose spouse had a higher level of education tended to report better health↔ The spouse's level of education can impact one's health '配偶教育高→健康好'概括为'配偶教育影响健康'

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

录音里 health status before and after marriage 是作者明确列出的'被调整掉的其他因素'之一，意在说'即便排除它结论依然成立'，根本不是研究发现。选项 One's health tends to differ before and after marriage 反把这个被排除项当成结论。 借⽤原⽂： adjusting for other factors, such as participants' own education, social background and health status before and after marriage B) 原词陷阱

social background 与上一项一样，是被作者 adjusting for 排除掉的干扰因素，原文没说'健康与社会背景有关'是新发现。选项 One's health status is related to one's social background 把被排除项伪装成结论。 借⽤原⽂： adjusting for other factors, such as participants' own education, social background and health status before and after marriage C) 偷换概念

研究讲的是配偶'教育'影响健康，C 却说 The wealthier one's spouse is, the healthier one becomes，把'教育'偷换成'财富'。虽然录音后文提到教育能带来 more money 等资源，但那是教育的衍生好处，原文从未把'配偶越富→本人越健康'立为结论。 借⽤原⽂： more money

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about the men in the sample of the new research?

options.text: They benefited a lot from their career achievements.
They showed interest in their spouse's occupations.
They had much in common with their spouses.
They had more education than their spouses.

questions.shortExplanation: Women in this sample had lower levels of education and lower occupational achievements than the men. 该样本中的女性，其受教育水平和职业成就都低于男性。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） They had more education than their spouses.

【定位】 Women in this sample had lower levels of education and lower occupational achievements than the men. 该样本中的女性，其受教育水平和职业成就都低于男性。

【信号】 比较句 lower…than the men 反推男性更高。答案句以女性为主语作比较——Women in this sample had lower levels of education…than the men，说女性教育水平低于男性， 等于反过来说男性教育水平高于女性。问 men 的题，答案藏在'拿 women 跟 men 比'的这句里，需做一次方向反推。

【替换】 Women in this sample had lower levels of education…than the men↔ They had more education than their spouses '女低于男'与'男多于女'肯否方向对调、等值

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

录音 lower occupational achievements 里确有 achievements 一词，但它是用来说女性'职业成就低'的，并没说男性'从事业成就中获益良多'。选项 benefited a lot from their career achievements 借 achievements 设套，且把描述对象错安到'获益'这一原文没有的意思上。 借⽤原⽂： lower occupational achievements B) 原词陷阱

录音里与 occupation 沾边的只有 occupational achievements，原文从未说男性'对配偶的职业感兴趣'。选项 showed interest in their spouse's occupations 用 occupations 这个原词凑出一个原文没有的行为。 借⽤原⽂： lower occupational achievements C) 与原文相反

原文恰恰在讲男女'教育与职业成就有差距'（女性更低），而 They had much in common with their spouses 说男性'与配偶有很多共同点'，方向正好相反，原文也根本没提共同点。
