items.title: 2023年12月六级第2套 · 听力篇章 2
items.transcript: Climate scientists predict that many parts of the world will be increasingly prone to floods. This is a serious risk to human lives and property. So understanding and accurately forecasting flood risks is a key challenge for vulnerable cities around the globe. In 2017, Derek Loftis of the Virginia Institute of Marine Science started a project called Catch the King. It uses a smartphone app to collect the data of ordinary citizens during high tides. He'll use those data to validate and improve his mathematical flooding model, called TideWatch. Loftis's mission is to know where the water goes before it goes there. But collecting necessary data and then processing that information quickly enough to make usable forecasts is anything but easy. Accurate flood forecasts require an understanding of the situation on the ground. By the early 2000s, supercomputing had advanced enough that scientists could integrate weather forecasting models with such measurements. But they still didn't have the critically important ability to forecast fast-moving floods in real time. So, in 2017, Loftis and colleagues set up a group of 28 Internet-connected water-level sensors throughout the flood risk community of Norfolk, Virginia. The new sensors relayed rough measurements about water height and movement to a computer at the Virginia Institute. Along with those sensors, hundreds of local citizens take photos of rising tides and transmit them in real time to the institute. Scientists hope that the data collected by these citizens can help sharpen the ability to forecast exactly when and where damaging floods will occur.

questions.prompt: What is said to be a key challenge for cities prone to floods?

options.text: Eliminating their root cause.
Forecasting flood risks accurately.
Identifying the cities' geological features.
Finding out the changing climate patterns.

questions.shortExplanation: So understanding and accurately forecasting flood risks is a key challenge for vulnerable cities around the globe. 因此，理解并准确预报洪水风险，对全球易受灾的城市来说是一项关键挑战。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Forecasting flood risks accurately.

【定位】 So understanding and accurately forecasting flood risks is a key challenge for vulnerable cities around the globe. 因此，理解并准确预报洪水风险，对全球易受灾的城市来说是一项关键挑战。

【信号】 原句直接出现 key challenge。这句直接含题干核心名词 a key challenge for vulnerable cities around the globe，且前面有 So 引出结论，是明确的答案句信号——题干名词在录音里几乎原样出现的那一句，就是落点。

【替换】 accurately forecasting flood risks↔Forecasting flood risks accurately

同词换序，意思全等

【排除】 A) 未提及

Eliminating their root cause 谈"消除洪水的根源"，录音通篇讲的是"理解和预报"风险，从未提到消除根源，属凭常识臆想的方向。

C) 答非所问

Identifying the cities' geological features 说挑战是"识别城市地质特征"，录音里 challenge 后面跟的是"预报洪水风险"，根本没提地质特征，方向被岔开。

D) 原词陷阱

Finding out the changing climate patterns 借了录音开头 Climate scientists predict 里的 climate 制造熟耳感，但那只是引出背景的"气候科学家预测"，挑战并非"弄清气候模式变化"，是典型听到原词就想选的陷阱。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: For what purpose does Derek Loftis collect the data of ordinary citizens during high tides?

options.text: To validate his hypothesis about the gravity of floods.
To determine the frequency of high tides causing floods.
To improve his mathematical flooding model.
To see the feasibility of his project on flooding.

questions.shortExplanation: He'll use those data to validate and improve his mathematical flooding model, called TideWatch. 他将用这些数据去验证并改进他那个名为 TideWatch 的数学洪水模型。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （目的题） To improve his mathematical flooding model.

【定位】 He'll use those data to validate and improve his mathematical flooding model, called TideWatch. 他将用这些数据去验证并改进他那个名为 TideWatch 的数学洪水模型。

【信号】 use those data to 引出目的。这句的 use those data to validate and improve his mathematical flooding model 正是目的信号 use… to…，to 后面的动作就是采集数据的目的，是答案句无疑。

【替换】 improve his mathematical flooding model ↔ To improve his mathematical flooding model

几乎原句对应

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

To validate his hypothesis about the gravity of floods 借了录音原词 validate and improve，但录音 validate 的宾语是"数学洪水模型"，不是"关于洪水严重性的假设"——盗了动词、换了宾语。

B) 原词陷阱

To determine the frequency of high tides causing floods 盗用 high tides，但录音里 high tides 是"采集数据的时机"，目的并非"测高潮致洪的频率"，把时间状语硬说成目的。

D) 未提及

To see the feasibility of his project on flooding 说目的是"看项目可行性"，录音从未提 feasibility 或"看可行性"，纯属添加。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the passage say is Derek Loftis's mission?

options.text: To study the consequences of high tides on flooded areas.
To teach local citizens how to collect data of incoming floods.
To forecast rapid floods in real time.
To classify the flooding data processed.

questions.shortExplanation: Loftis's mission is to know where the water goes before it goes there. ... But they still didn't have the critically important ability to forecast fast-moving floods in real time.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） To forecast rapid floods in real time.

【定位】 Loftis's mission is to know where the water goes before it goes there. ... But they still didn't have the critically important ability to forecast fast-moving floods in real time.

Loftis 的使命是：在水流到某处之前，就知道它会去哪里。……但他们仍不具备实时预报快速移动洪水这一至关重要的能力。

【信号】 mission is to + 后文同义解释。信号句 Loftis's mission is to know where the water goes before it goes there 直接点出使命；它较抽象，录音随后用 forecast fast-moving floods in real time 把这一使命具体化，两处合起来锁定答案。

【替换】 to know where the water goes before it goes there↔To forecast rapid floods in real time

形象说法换成专业说法 forecast fast-moving floods in real time↔To forecast rapid floods in real time

fast-moving=rapid，近义词替换

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 To study the consequences of high tides on flooded areas 借了录音的 high tides，但录音说的使命是"实时预报"，不是"研究高潮对淹没区的后果"，study consequences 是录音没有的动作。

B) 张冠李戴

To teach local citizens how to collect data of incoming floods 盗用 citizens、collect data，但录音是"市民帮他采数据"，从没说他的使命是"教市民怎么采数据"——角色与动作都被偷换。

D) 原词陷阱

To classify the flooding data processed 借了录音 processing that information 里的"处理数据"概念，但录音从没说使命是"给处理过的洪水数据分类"，classify 是凭空添加的动作。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What did Loftis and his colleagues do to obtain data about water height and movement?

options.text: They set up Internet-connected water-level sensors.
They tracked the rising tides with video-cameras.
They used newly-developed supercomputing facilities.
They observed the direction of water flow on the spot.

questions.shortExplanation: So, in 2017, Loftis and colleagues set up a group of 28 Internet-connected water-level sensors throughout the flood risk community of Norfolk, Virginia. The new sensors relayed rough measurements about water height and movement to a computer at the Virginia Institute. 于是，2017 年，Loftis 和同事们在弗吉尼亚州诺福克的涝灾社区各处架设了一组共 28 个联网水位传感器。这些新传感器把关于水位高度和水流移动的粗略测量数据传回弗吉尼亚研究所的一台计算机。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） They set up Internet-connected water-level sensors.

【定位】 So, in 2017, Loftis and colleagues set up a group of 28 Internet-connected water-level sensors throughout the flood risk community of Norfolk, Virginia. The new sensors relayed rough measurements about water height and movement to a computer at the Virginia Institute. 于是，2017 年，Loftis 和同事们在弗吉尼亚州诺福克的涝灾社区各处架设了一组共 28 个联网水位传感器。这些新传感器把关于水位高度和水流移动的粗略测量数据传回弗吉尼亚研究所的一台计算机。

【信号】 set up sensors + 紧跟 water height and movement。答案句信号是动作动词 set up a group of 28 Internet-connected water-level sensors，紧接着下一句出现题干的对象词 water height and movement，两句锁死"靠装传感器拿水位数据"。

【替换】 set up a group of 28 Internet-connected water-level sensors ↔ They set up Internet-connected water-level sensors 略去数量，核心动作器材全留

【排除】 B) 偷换概念

They tracked the rising tides with video-cameras 看似对应录音 take photos of rising tides，但那是"市民用（手机）拍照"，不是"用 video-cameras 追踪"，且这是采图片、不是题干问的"水位与水流"数据，器材和数据类型都被换。 C) 原词陷阱

They used newly-developed supercomputing facilities 借了录音 supercomputing had advanced，但录音说超算是用来"整合天气预报模型"的背景能力，不是他们获取水位数据的手段，原词被搬错了位置。 D) 未提及

They observed the direction of water flow on the spot 说他们"实地观察水流方向"，录音获取水流靠的是传感器测量，从没说"实地肉眼观察方向"，属添加动作。

items.title: 2023年12月六级第2套 · 讲座与讲话 1
items.transcript:
Now, it's become something of a ritual to debate the value of a college degree, but as Current Population Survey data show, there has been a sharp decline in employment among men without college degrees compared with those who have them. This decline began in the 1960s and has become more serious over time.

What has actually caused this decline? Well, economists have been working to ascertain the roots of the decline for decades and have come up with several theories. One popular theory is that it's a case of too low wages for jobs that don't require a degree. An alternate theory is that there were more jobs not requiring a college degree in the past than now.

A recent working paper from the National Bureau of Economic Research reviewed those theories and put forward additional hypotheses about the causes of the problem. Let's look at that paper now. First, the researchers considered the issue of wages. As the wage gap has grown between those with college degrees and those without, economists have suggested that men aren't as interested in taking some of the less lucrative jobs. While the authors of the paper found truth in this explanation, they assert that low wages can't be the only factor, as wages for men without college degrees, adjusting for inflation, haven't changed much since the 1960s, making it hard to see why fewer men seem willing to accept those wages.

This leads to the second theory, that more jobs require a college degree today than in the past. Indeed, that theory seems valid, because in America today, 2/3 of jobs are filled by workers with at least some college education. However, the authors of the paper argue that there are other factors amplifying the problem.

They identified two new potential explanations: the first being the tremendous decline in marriage among men without college degrees since the 1960s; and the second being the increase in women participating in the workforce that was concurrent with the decline in marriage. These two changes mean that men might not have families to support, or if they do, their wives might be doing more of the providing, both of which might remove the financial incentive to work. The authors of the paper concede that research on the subject isn't complete, but they argue that their work supports the value of a college education.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say has become something of a ritual?

options.text: To argue about the value of a college degree.
To debate the validity of current survey data.
To account for the drastic decline in employment among men.
To compare men without college degrees with those who have.

questions.shortExplanation: Now, it's become something of a ritual to debate the value of a college degree, but as Current Population Survey data show, there has been a sharp decline in employment among men without college degrees compared with those who have them.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） To argue about the value of a college degree.

【定位】 Now, it's become something of a ritual to debate the value of a college degree, but as Current Population Survey data show, there has been a sharp decline in employment among men without college degrees compared with those who have them.

如今，争论大学学历的价值已经几乎成了一种惯例，但正如"当前人口调查"的数据所显示的，没有大学学历的男性其就业出现了急剧下降，与有学历的人相比尤其如此。

【信号】 标志词 ritual 紧跟其定义。答案句里 it's become something of a ritual to debate the value of a college degree 中 ritual 后面紧接的 to debate… 就是"惯例"的具体内容，标志词后面紧跟的不定式就是要听的落点。

【替换】 ritual to debate the value of a college degree↔To argue about the value of a college degree.

debate 同义替换为 argue about

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

录音里确有 Current Population Survey data show，B 项 To debate the validity of current survey data. 借走 survey、data 让你"听到就想选"，但原文是"数据显示"，并非"争论数据是否可信"，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： Current Population Survey data show C) 张冠李戴

C 项 To account for the drastic decline in employment among men. 搬来了答案句后半的 a sharp decline in employment among men without college degrees，但"成为惯例的"是前半句"争论学历价值"，"解释就业下降"是全篇要做的事、不是被称作 ritual 的那件事，张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： a sharp decline in employment among men without college degrees D) 原词陷阱

D 项 To compare men without college degrees with those who have. 用了 men without college degrees compared with those who have them 的字眼，但 compared 在原文只是描述"下降"的对照背景，说话人意图并非"做对比"这件事本身，过度解读。 借⽤原⽂： men without college degrees compared with those who have them
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What did the researchers of a recent working paper consider first?

options.text: The increase in women taking up jobs.
The issue of changing job requirements.
The factor of wages.
The impact of inflation.

questions.shortExplanation: Let's look at that paper now. First, the researchers considered the issue of wages.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） The factor of wages.

【定位】 Let's look at that paper now. First, the researchers considered the issue of wages.

现在我们来看这篇论文。首先，研究者们考虑了工资这一问题。

【信号】 次序信号词 First 直接领出答案。First, the researchers considered the issue of wages. 里 First 就是"最先考虑"的信号，它后面紧跟的 the issue of wages 即答案落点。

【替换】 the researchers considered the issue of wages↔The factor of wages.

the issue of wages 概括为 The factor of wages

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

A 项 The increase in women taking up jobs. 对应录音 the increase in women participating in the workforce，但那是第 5 段"新增解释"里的内容，不是"首先考虑"的， 答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： the increase in women participating in the workforce B) 原词陷阱

B 项 The issue of changing job requirements. 指向 more jobs require a college degree today than in the past，但录音明说这是 the second theory，不是"首先"考虑的，次序错位。 借⽤原⽂： This leads to the second theory, that more jobs require a college degree today D) 原词陷阱 D 项 The impact of inflation. 借走录音 adjusting for inflation 里的 inflation，但 inflation 在原文只是"调整通胀后"的限定语，研究者首先考虑的是 wages，不是通胀，原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： adjusting for inflation
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What did the recent paper identify as a new potential explanation of the problem concerning men's employment?

options.text: Men's unwillingness to accept low wages in times of growing inflation.
The wage gap between those with college degrees and those without.
More jobs requiring their holders to have a college degree nowadays.
The sharp decline in marriage among men with no college degrees.

questions.shortExplanation: They identified two new potential explanations: the first being the tremendous decline in marriage among men without college degrees since the 1960s; and the second being the increase in women participating in the workforce that was concurrent with the decline in marriage.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） The sharp decline in marriage among men with no college degrees.

【定位】 They identified two new potential explanations: the first being the tremendous decline in marriage among men without college degrees since the 1960s; and the second being the increase in women participating in the workforce that was concurrent with the decline in marriage.

他们指出了两个新的可能解释：第一个是自上世纪六十年代以来，没有大学学历的男性婚姻率的剧烈下降；第二个是与婚姻下降同时出现的女性进入劳动力市场的增加。

【信号】 信号词 new、identified 领出两个新解释。They identified two new potential explanations 里 new、identified 就是"新提出"的信号，冒号后的 the tremendous decline in marriage among men without college degrees 即新解释之一。

【替换】 the tremendous decline in marriage among men without college degrees ↔ The sharp decline in marriage among men with no college degrees.

tremendous=sharp、without=with no 同义替换

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 项 Men's unwillingness to accept low wages in times of growing inflation. 拼接了 why fewer men seem willing to accept those wages 与 inflation，但这是第一个旧理论的内容，不是"新"解释，且原文说工资经通胀调整后"变化不大"，并非"通胀加剧"，既答非所问又与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： why fewer men seem willing to accept those wages

B) 原词陷阱

B 项 The wage gap between those with college degrees and those without. 几乎照抄录音 the wage gap has grown between those with college degrees and those without，但那是第 3 段已有的工资理论，不是第 5 段"新提出"的，原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： As the wage gap has grown between those with college degrees and those without C) 原词陷阱

C 项 More jobs requiring their holders to have a college degree nowadays. 对应 more jobs require a college degree today than in the past，但这是 the second theory（旧理论），不在"new potential explanations"之列，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： more jobs require a college degree today than in the past
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

items.title: 2023年12月六级第2套 · 讲座与讲话 2
items.transcript:
While an increasing number of people are trying to eat less meat, a market research team has found in its latest fashion and sustainability report that the trend is now spreading from kitchen to closet. It found animal welfare came top of a list of issues that people considered before buying clothes, with 42% saying it was important to them. The researchers of the team predicted that the next year would see a boom in animal-free shoe collections, since they heard shoppers of all ages say they would buy footwear designated as "vegan", meaning the goods were produced without using any animal or animal part.

As well as being on trend, and with a much better ring to it than synthetic leather, the vegan label does convey an important extra distinction. If you label something as vegan, then the whole product needs to be animal free. That means checking things like the glue that holds the shoe together, for example, and the chemicals used for finishing them. At the top end, some of the world-renowned fashion designers have avoided leather and fur for some time. In fact, some of the companies are now exploring a leather substitute and a silk replacement made from mushrooms.

The Animal Free Product Society says they've seen a boom in products registered with the vegan trademark. In 2018, there were 119. So far this year, it says an unprecedented 1,956 have been registered. New products are being added daily. There are fur coats that are vegan, plastic vegan belts and shoes made from tree bark or natural rubber labelled vegan. These new products aren't coming at an extra cost to consumers though. Vegan boots cost the same as the leather originals. New Look, one of the first reputable store chains to use the vegan trademark, prices ballet shoes at £7.99 and a vegan laptop handbag at £29.99, comparable with its other products.

This signifies a change. In the past, ethical products, whether they were fair trade or organic, came at a premium. However, it is unclear whether these new products can be considered ethical. The debate over durability, crop-growing impacts, pollution and recyclability is a complicated one, not to mention the ethics around the working conditions for people making the products, whatever the component materials. Environmental campaigners advise that the best approach is to buy less, never mind what the item is made of.

questions.prompt: What has a market research team found in its latest fashion and sustainability report?

options.text: More and more people attach importance to protecting endangered animals.
More and more people prioritize animal welfare when buying things to wear.
An increasing number of people demand to free animals being kept in cages.
An increasing number of people follow the latest trend of becoming vegetarians.

questions.shortExplanation: It found animal welfare came top of a list of issues that people considered before buying clothes, with 42% saying it was important to them. 调查发现，在人们买衣服前会考虑的诸多问题中，动物福利排在首位，有 42% 的人表示这点对他们很重要。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） More and more people prioritize animal welfare when buying things to wear.

【定位】 It found animal welfare came top of a list of issues that people considered before buying clothes, with 42% saying it was important to them. 调查发现，在人们买衣服前会考虑的诸多问题中，动物福利排在首位，有 42% 的人表示这点对他们很重要。

【信号】 主体 It found 直接领出发现。录音用 It found animal welfare came top of a list of issues that people considered before buying clothes 把调查主体的「发现」直接端出来，「It found」就是答案句的信号——题目问发现什么，跟着 found 后面那句走即可。

【替换】 animal welfare came top of a list of issues that people considered before buying clothes↔ prioritize animal welfare when buying things to wear

came top=prioritize、buying clothes=things to wear

【排除】 A) 偷换概念

录音通篇讲 animal welfare(动物福利)和 animal-free(无动物成分)产品，从没说 protecting endangered animals(保护濒危动物)，A 把「动物福利」偷换成「濒危动物保护」，是听到 animal 就想选的诱饵。

C) 未提及录音只字未提 free animals being kept in cages(放生笼中动物)，这是凭「动物」话题联想出来的内容，原文无据。 D) 原词陷阱

录音开头确有 an increasing number of people are trying to eat less meat，但那只是引出话题的背景，不是调查「发现」的内容；D becoming vegetarians 盗用了开头的「吃肉/吃素」原词来答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： While an increasing number of people are trying to eat less meat
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What have some world-renowned fashion designers done for some time?

options.text: Avoided the use of leather and fur.
Labelled all their products as vegan.
Refrained from using chemicals in their products.
Utilized a silk substitute made from mushrooms.

questions.shortExplanation: At the top end, some of the world-renowned fashion designers have avoided leather and fur for some time.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Avoided the use of leather and fur.

【定位】 At the top end, some of the world-renowned fashion designers have avoided leather and fur for some time.

在高端领域，一些世界知名的时装设计师已经有一段时间不用皮革和皮草了。

【信号】 主体词+for some time 原样复现。录音 some of the world-renowned fashion designers have avoided leather and fur for some time 把题干的主体词和 for some time 几乎原样念出，这种「题干主体词在原文复现」就是答案句信号，紧跟其后的动词 avoided 即所做之事。

【替换】 have avoided leather and fur for some time↔Avoided the use of leather and fur. 近乎原词、仅补 the use of

【排除】 B) 张冠李戴

录音里 vegan 标签是 products registered with the vegan trademark、由 The Animal Free Product Society 与 New Look 等做的，不是高端设计师；B Labelled all their products as vegan. 把别人做的事安到设计师头上，且加了原文没有的 all。 借⽤原⽂： products registered with the vegan trademark C) 原词陷阱

录音提到 the chemicals used for finishing them 是说做 vegan 产品要检查的环节，并未说设计师「拒用化学品」；C Refrained from using chemicals in their products. 盗用 chemicals 原词却编造了「拒用」这个原文没有的动作。 借⽤原⽂： the chemicals used for finishing them D) 原词陷阱

录音说 some of the companies are now exploring a leather substitute and a silk replacement made from mushrooms，主体是 some companies、动作是 now exploring(正在探索)，既非「设计师长期所做」也非已经 utilized；D Utilized a silk substitute made from mushrooms. 盗用了 mushrooms 这个抢眼原词，但主体和时态都错位。 借⽤原⽂： some of the companies are now exploring a leather substitute and a silk replacement made from mushrooms
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say is unclear concerning vegan products?

options.text: Whether they actually signify a substantial change.
Whether they effectively protect animals at large.
Whether they can be considered sustainable.
Whether they can be regarded as ethical.

questions.shortExplanation: However, it is unclear whether these new products can be considered ethical.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Whether they can be regarded as ethical.

【定位】 However, it is unclear whether these new products can be considered ethical.

然而，这些新产品是否能被视为合乎道德/伦理，尚不明确。

【信号】 However 转折后接 unclear。录音先说 This signifies a change，紧接 However, it is unclear whether these new products can be considered ethical——转折词 However 加存疑词 unclear 双重信号叠加，转折之后才是真意，存疑的对象 ethical 就在这句里。

【替换】 whether these new products can be considered ethical ↔ Whether they can be regarded as ethical. considered=regarded as 同义

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

录音说 This signifies a change——「这标志着一种改变」是肯定语气、已成定论，恰恰不是 unclear 的对象；A a substantial change 盗用了 change 原词，却把已确定的事说成尚不明确，正话反说。 借⽤原⽂： This signifies a change

B) 答非所问

录音整体讲 animal-free/animal welfare，但说 unclear 的那句问的是 ethical，不是 protect animals at large；B 借了全篇的「动物」话题来冒充存疑对象，原文没把「是否真护动物」列为不明确之事。

C) 原词陷阱

录音只在开头报告名 fashion and sustainability report 出现过 sustainability，从未说 「是否可持续」尚不明确；C sustainable 盗用了这个开头出现的原词来答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： fashion and sustainability report
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

items.title: 2023年12月六级第2套 · 讲座与讲话 3
items.transcript:
By the end of 2016, anyone who had been paying even passing attention to the news headlines was highly likely to conclude that everything was terrible, and that the world was going to hell. It was easy to feel depressed by the wars in different parts of the world, the spread of deadly viruses or terror attacks.

Yet, 2016 was the best year in the history of humanity. Child mortality was roughly half what it was as recently as 1990. And 300,000 more people gained access to electricity each day. Every single measure of material and environmental welfare in America, Europe, Asia, Africa and the world as a whole has improved rather than deteriorated. We are living in history's most peaceful era, with violence of all kinds in steep decline. Those are the facts. So why aren't we all optimists?

In a 2015 survey for YouGov, 65% of British people and 81% of the French said they thought the world was getting worse. However, according to numerous sensible statistics, these people are simply wrong. Nobody in their right mind should wish to have lived in a previous century. Yet people do. Why?

Our prevailing mood of despair is irrational. It says more about us than it does about how things really are. It is best explained as the result of various psychological biases that served a purpose for our evolutionary ancestors—but now, in a media-saturated era, constantly mislead us. Once upon a time, it was of great survival value to be worried about everything that could go wrong. This is what makes bad news especially compelling.

In our evolutionary past, it was a very good thing that our attention could be easily seized by negative information, since it might well indicate a dangerous risk to our own survival. The caveman who always assumed there was a lion behind the next rock would usually be wrong, but he'd be much more likely to survive and reproduce than one who always assumed the opposite. But that was all before newspapers, television and the internet. In today's hyper connected times, our addiction to bad news just leads us to vacuum up depressing or enraging stories from across the globe. Whether these news stories threaten us or not, we conclude that things are much worse than they actually are. Really good news, on the other hand, can be a lot harder to spot in a newspaper because predictable daily events by definition aren't news.

questions.prompt: What is one of the facts stated by the speaker?

options.text: The era we live in is the most peaceful in history.
The world has seen more violence in recent years.
The environmental welfare has worsened in the world.
The belief is less prevalent that the world is going to hell.

questions.shortExplanation: We are living in history's most peaceful era, with violence of all kinds in steep decline. Those are the facts. 我们正生活在历史上最和平的时代，各类暴力都在急剧下降。这些就是事实。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） The era we live in is the most peaceful in history.

【定位】 We are living in history's most peaceful era, with violence of all kinds in steep decline. Those are the facts. 我们正生活在历史上最和平的时代，各类暴力都在急剧下降。这些就是事实。

【信号】 'Those are the facts' 直接点明这是事实。演讲者紧接着用 Those are the facts. 给前面一串陈述盖章为'事实'，这就是答案信号；其中 history's most peaceful era 正对应题干要的那个 fact。

【替换】 history's most peaceful era↔ the most peaceful in history

同义改写：词序调换、词性微调

【排除】 B) 与原文相反

选项说 more violence in recent years，但录音明说 violence of all kinds in steep decline（各类暴力急剧下降），方向正好相反，是把'下降'听反成'增多'。 借⽤原⽂： violence of all kinds in steep decline C) 与原文相反

选项称 environmental welfare has worsened，但录音说每一项 environmental welfare…has improved rather than deteriorated（改善而非恶化），用 worsened 偷换了 improved，方向反了。 借⽤原⽂： Every single measure of material and environmental welfare…has improved rather than deteriorated D) 未提及

选项说'认为世界要完蛋的信念不那么流行了'，但录音恰恰描述这种悲观信念很普遍 （everything was terrible, and that the world was going to hell、第 3 段多数英法人觉得世界在变坏），从没说它在减弱，属凭空生造。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about most British and French people in a 2015 survey for YouGov?

options.text: They were actually not in their right mind.
They believed the world was deteriorating.
They did not wish to live in the previous century.
They were convinced by the statistics presented to them.

questions.shortExplanation: In a 2015 survey for YouGov, 65% of British people and 81% of the French said they thought the world was getting worse.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） They believed the world was deteriorating.

【定位】 In a 2015 survey for YouGov, 65% of British people and 81% of the French said they thought the world was getting worse.

在 2015 年一项 YouGov 的调查中，65% 的英国人和 81% 的法国人说他们认为世界正在变糟。

【信号】 专名 YouGov/2015 直接领出答案句。题干的专名锚点 In a 2015 survey for YouGov 在原文原样出现，紧跟其后的 said they thought the world was getting worse 就是这群人的看法，即答案信号。

【替换】 the world was getting worse↔ the world was deteriorating 同义改写：getting worse = deteriorating

【排除】 A) 张冠李戴

选项说这群人 not in their right mind，原文确有 Nobody in their right mind should wish to have lived in a previous century，但这是演讲者自己的评论，不是调查显示这群人神志不清；把演讲者的话安到调查对象头上。 借⽤原⽂： Nobody in their right mind should wish to have lived in a previous century. C) 张冠李戴

选项 did not wish to live in the previous century 同样取自 Nobody in their right mind should wish to have lived in a previous century，但这仍是演讲者的论断，且原文是说'没人该希望活在过去'，并非调查里这群人表达了此意愿。 借⽤原⽂： Nobody in their right mind should wish to have lived in a previous century. D) 与原文相反

选项说他们 convinced by the statistics presented to them，但原文说按 numerous sensible statistics, these people are simply wrong——统计数据恰恰证明他们错了，他们并未被数据说服，方向相反。 借⽤原⽂： according to numerous sensible statistics, these people are simply wrong
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does our prevailing mood of despair indicate?

options.text: The subjectivity of mass media.
The current state of affairs.
Our psychological biases.
Our ancestors' influence.

questions.shortExplanation: It is best explained as the result of various psychological biases that served a purpose for our evolutionary ancestors—but now, in a media-saturated era, constantly mislead us. 它最好被解释为种种心理偏见的结果——这些偏见曾对我们的进化祖先有用，但如今在一个被媒体充斥的时代，却不断误导我们。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Our psychological biases.

【定位】 It is best explained as the result of various psychological biases that served a purpose for our evolutionary ancestors—but now, in a media-saturated era, constantly mislead us. 它最好被解释为种种心理偏见的结果——这些偏见曾对我们的进化祖先有用，但如今在一个被媒体充斥的时代，却不断误导我们。

【信号】 归因信号 'explained as the result of'。演讲者用 It is best explained as the result of various psychological biases 明确把这股绝望情绪归因到'心理偏见'，explained as the result of 就是答案信号，其后名词即题目要的答案。

【替换】 various psychological biases↔ Our psychological biases. 近乎原词，仅限定词不同

【排除】 A) 偷换概念选项说 The subjectivity of mass media.，原文虽提到 in a media-saturated era（媒体充斥的时代），但那只是偏见'被放大'的背景，演讲者归因的根源是心理偏见，而非'媒体的主观性'，把背景偷换成根源。 借⽤原⽂： in a media-saturated era, constantly mislead us B) 与原文相反

选项说反映 The current state of affairs.，但原文明说这情绪 says more about us than it does about how things really are——它说的是我们自己，而非事情的真实状况，正好相反。 借⽤原⽂： It says more about us than it does about how things really are. D) 原词陷阱

选项 Our ancestors' influence. 盗用原文 served a purpose for our evolutionary ancestors 里的 ancestors，听到这个词很想选；但原文是说偏见曾对祖先有用，演讲者把绝望情绪直接归因到'心理偏见'本身，而非'祖先的影响'。 借⽤原⽂： that served a purpose for our evolutionary ancestors
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What was a very good thing in our evolutionary past?

options.text: Spreading exciting news around us far and wide.
Vacuuming up depressing or enraging stories.
Calculating dangerous risks to our survival.
Paying attention to negative information.

questions.shortExplanation: In our evolutionary past, it was a very good thing that our attention could be easily seized by negative information, since it might well indicate a dangerous risk to our own survival. 在我们的进化过去，注意力容易被负面信息攫取是一件很好的事，因为这很可能意味着对我们自身生存的危险威胁。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Paying attention to negative information.

【定位】 In our evolutionary past, it was a very good thing that our attention could be easily seized by negative information, since it might well indicate a dangerous risk to our own survival. 在我们的进化过去，注意力容易被负面信息攫取是一件很好的事，因为这很可能意味着对我们自身生存的危险威胁。

【信号】 原句直给 'a very good thing that…'。题干 a very good thing 在原文原样出现于 it was a very good thing that our attention could be easily seized by negative information，that 从句里的内容就是那件'好事'，即答案信号。

【替换】 our attention could be easily seized by negative information↔ Paying attention to negative information.

被动转主动 + 概括：被攫取注意 = 关注负面信息

【排除】 A) 与原文相反选项说 Spreading exciting news around us far and wide.，但原文说 Really good news…can be a lot harder to spot（好消息其实更难被注意到），且演讲者夸的是关注'坏'消息有生存价值，不是传播好消息，方向相反。 借⽤原⽂： Really good news…can be a lot harder to spot in a newspaper B) 原词陷阱

选项 Vacuuming up depressing or enraging stories. 几乎照搬原文 vacuum up depressing or enraging stories from across the globe，听到原词极想选；但原文说这是'当今超连接时代'我们对坏消息上瘾的恶果，而非'进化过去的好事'，时间与褒贬都对不上。 借⽤原⽂： our addiction to bad news just leads us to vacuum up depressing or enraging stories from across the globe C) 偷换概念

选项说 Calculating dangerous risks to our survival.，原文有 a dangerous risk to our own survival，但说的是负面信息可能'意味着'生存危险，故关注它是好事，并未说去'计算'风险；把'感知威胁'偷换成'计算风险'。 借⽤原⽂： it might well indicate a dangerous risk to our own survival

items.title: 2023年3月六级第1套 · 长对话 1
items.transcript:
M: Thanks for inviting me out tonight. I've been wanting to try this place for weeks. I usually pass it on my way home from work but never seem to have time to stop.

W: I've been dying to come here as well. I was worried that the menu might not be accommodating. But one of my close friends ate here last week. She's a vegetarian. She told me that there were a lot of options for her, and they offered alternative dishes.

M: But you're not vegetarian, are you?

W: Well, not entirely. I don't eat meat at all, but I don't have a problem eating fish, seafood or eggs.

M: Isn't that very difficult? I can't imagine giving up a premium juicy steak or bacon cheeseburgers.

W: I wouldn't know. My parents followed the same diet. Even when I was younger, we never had meat during meals, and I never really had a craving to try it. I bet it would be hard though, giving up something you're accustomed to eating. I tried cutting back on coffee in the morning, and it was awful. Come to think of it, it was probably even worse for my colleagues that had to deal with me at morning meetings.

M: That's even harder to imagine you, without coffee. So you say your parents also followed a partially vegetarian diet? Why did they decide to do that?

W: That's an interesting question. I never thought to ask them though. My best guess is for health reasons. They're not terribly active or knowledgeable about animal preservation efforts, but they're serious about their health. Both are in their 70s now, but eat organic as often as possible and take part in regular physical exercise. Neither of them has any health problems, and they hardly ever get sick.

M: In that case, I might give it a try someday.

W: Now back to the menu. What are you going to have?

questions.prompt: Where does the conversation most probably take place?

options.text: In a restaurant.
In a kitchen.
In a food store.
In a supermarket.

questions.shortExplanation: But one of my close friends ate here last week. She's a vegetarian. She told me that there were a lot of options for her, and they offered alternative dishes. 不过我一个好朋友上周在这儿吃过。她是素食者。她跟我说这里给她的选择很多，还提供替代菜品。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （推断题） In a restaurant.

【定位】 But one of my close friends ate here last week. She's a vegetarian. She told me that there were a lot of options for her, and they offered alternative dishes. 不过我一个好朋友上周在这儿吃过。她是素食者。她跟我说这里给她的选择很多，还提供替代菜品。

【信号】 menu、ate here、offered dishes 等餐厅标志词。环境标志词成串出现：第1段 I've been wanting to try this place、第2段 the menu 与 they offered alternative dishes、 第10段 What are you going to have?——「菜单、上菜、点什么」只可能发生在餐厅， 多个标志词共同锁定地点。

【替换】 the menu ↔ In a restaurant. 有菜单、有人上菜的场所即餐厅

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

kitchen（厨房）借的是 dishes、menu 引发的「跟做饭有关」联想，但全程是别人给两人上菜、问他们点什么，没人在自己下厨，地点不是厨房。 借⽤原⽂： they offered alternative dishes C) 原词陷阱

food store（食品店）只是蹭了满篇的食物话题，可对话里是坐下来看菜单、被问点什么， 没有任何挑选购买商品的情节，与食品店不符。 D) 原词陷阱

supermarket（超市）与 food store 错法相同，只因话题是吃就被列进来，但录音里 What are you going to have? 是点餐、不是购物，排除。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the woman?

options.text: She eats meat occasionally.
She enjoys cheeseburgers.
She is allergic to seafood.
She is a partial vegetarian.

questions.shortExplanation: Well, not entirely. I don't eat meat at all, but I don't have a problem eating fish, seafood or eggs.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） She is a partial vegetarian.

【定位】 Well, not entirely. I don't eat meat at all, but I don't have a problem eating fish, seafood or eggs.

嗯，不完全是。我完全不吃肉，但吃鱼、海鲜或蛋是没问题的。

【信号】 被问者应答 + not entirely 让步 + but 转折。男士问 you're not vegetarian, are you?， 女士的应答即落点；她先说 not entirely（不完全是），再用 but 把「不吃肉」和「吃鱼蛋」对接——这种「部分是、不完全是」正是 partial vegetarian 的定义。

【替换】 I don't eat meat at all, but I don't have a problem eating fish, seafood or eggs↔ She is a partial vegetarian.

「不吃肉但吃鱼蛋」概括为「部分素食者」 not entirely↔ partial vegetarian 「不完全是」对应「部分」

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

She eats meat occasionally.（偶尔吃肉）与原文 I don't eat meat at all（完全不吃肉） 正好相反，把「一点都不吃」反成了「偶尔吃」。 借⽤原⽂： I don't eat meat at all B) 张冠李戴

She enjoys cheeseburgers. 盗用了男士那句 bacon cheeseburgers，但说舍不得汉堡的是男士、不是女士，把男方的话安到了女方头上。 借⽤原⽂： bacon cheeseburgers C) 原词陷阱

She is allergic to seafood. 盗用了 seafood 一词，但原文是她「吃海鲜没问题」，根本没提过敏，allergic 系凭空捏造且与事实相反。 借⽤原⽂： eating fish, seafood or eggs
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What would be a difficult thing to do according to the woman?

options.text: Dealing with one's colleagues.
Changing one's eating habit.
Following the same diet for years.
Keeping awake at morning meetings.

questions.shortExplanation: I bet it would be hard though, giving up something you're accustomed to eating. 不过我敢说，要放弃一样你习惯了的吃食，是会很难的。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Changing one's eating habit.

【定位】 I bet it would be hard though, giving up something you're accustomed to eating. 不过我敢说，要放弃一样你习惯了的吃食，是会很难的。

【信号】 评价词 hard 直接修饰 giving up… eating。it would be hard 里的 hard（难）直接评价后面的 giving up something you're accustomed to eating——「放弃一样你已习惯吃的东西」，评价词紧贴的那件事就是答案，正是「改变饮食习惯」。

【替换】 giving up something you're accustomed to eating↔Changing one's eating habit. 「放弃习惯吃的东西」=「改变饮食习惯」

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

Dealing with one's colleagues. 盗用了 deal with me 旁边的 colleagues，但原文是「戒咖啡后同事得忍受我很难受」，难的是戒咖啡这件事，不是「处理同事」。 借⽤原⽂： deal with me at morning meetings C) 原词陷阱

Following the same diet for years. 蹭了 My parents followed the same diet，可那是在讲她从小随父母吃同样的饭、并不觉得难，不是被评为「难做」的事。 借⽤原⽂： My parents followed the same diet

D) 原词陷阱 Keeping awake at morning meetings. 借用了 morning meetings，但原文只说戒咖啡让她早会上状态差、同事难受，从没说「在早会保持清醒」是难事，系拼凑原词。 借⽤原⽂： morning meetings
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about her parents?

options.text: They enjoy perfect health.
They are both animal lovers.
They only eat organic food.
They are cutting back on coffee.

questions.shortExplanation: Both are in their 70s now, but eat organic as often as possible and take part in regular physical exercise. Neither of them has any health problems, and they hardly ever get sick.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） They enjoy perfect health.

【定位】 Both are in their 70s now, but eat organic as often as possible and take part in regular physical exercise. Neither of them has any health problems, and they hardly ever get sick.

他们俩现在都七十多岁了，但尽量常吃有机食品，也定期参加体育锻炼。两人都没有任何健康问题，也几乎从不生病。

【信号】 强否定 Neither…any + hardly ever 收束健康结论。落点在 Neither of them has any health problems 与 they hardly ever get sick——双重否定 + hardly ever 把父母身体状况推到「完全没病、几乎不生病」的极佳状态，这是对父母的总体定论。

【替换】 Neither of them has any health problems, and they hardly ever get sick↔ They enjoy perfect health. 「都没病、几乎不生病」=「身体极佳」

【排除】 B) 与原文相反

They are both animal lovers. 借了 animal preservation 一词，但原文说父母 not terribly active or knowledgeable about animal preservation efforts（对动物保护既不热心也不懂），与「都是爱动物者」相反。 借⽤原⽂： not terribly active or knowledgeable about animal preservation efforts C) 偷换概念

They only eat organic food. 盗用 eat organic，却把原文的 as often as possible（尽量常吃）偷改成 only（只吃），范围被绝对化，不符。 借⽤原⽂： eat organic as often as possible D) 张冠李戴

They are cutting back on coffee. 盗用了 cutting back on coffee，但戒咖啡的是女士自己（I tried cutting back on coffee），父母从未减咖啡，把女士的事安到了父母身上。 借⽤原⽂： I tried cutting back on coffee

items.title: 2023年3月六级第1套 · 长对话 2
items.transcript:
W: How did your annual performance evaluation meeting with your manager go? Did you get much in the way of praise?

M: Next to zero. When we came to the part about discussing my areas for growth, he bluntly told me that I had an attitude problem. But he wouldn't really expand on that description. He said it's the little things I do and say.

W: Did you ask him for a specific example?

M: I did ask him a few more questions to try and narrow it down. He said my constant questioning of him and his decisions was the most obvious example he could give. Then our conversation was swiftly brought to a close.

W: I had a similar experience once. My manager told me I was too honest. In most cases, I thought my honesty was helpful, as did my colleagues, but my manager thought otherwise. Some managers really adopt manipulative language to disguise the unreasonable choices they have made. They don't use the rational power of arguments to resolve issues of conflict or complaints about unfairness.

M: Right. Some employ their persuasive vocabulary and influential communication style to win workplace arguments by compelling people to perform the intended action.

W: Exactly. Too honest? Isn't that a good thing? I thought that's surely something we should have covered earlier in the section discussing strengths and talents, but no. Honesty was deemed to be more of a sin than a virtue, since it made people feel uncomfortable, or at least it made the most powerful folks feel uncomfortable.

M: Indeed. Rhetoric is viewed by many philosophers as the method through which the powerful accumulate more power. By virtue of having the loudest voice, they're able to command greater attention and to further assert their dominance, even when what they're saying doesn't really make much sense.

W: And retaining their power and prestige is their priority.

M: It's what makes the most sense to a lot of them.

questions.prompt: What was the manager's reason for giving little praise for the man's performance?

options.text: The man got a poor evaluation from his colleagues.
The man made little contribution to the company.
The man paid attention to trivial things.
The man had an attitude problem.

questions.shortExplanation: he bluntly told me that I had an attitude problem. 他直截了当地告诉我，我有态度问题。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） The man had an attitude problem.

【定位】 he bluntly told me that I had an attitude problem. 他直截了当地告诉我，我有态度问题。

【信号】 被问者复述经理原话的直接引述句。女士问考评结果后，男士应答里 he bluntly told me that I had an attitude problem 是对经理原话的直接转述，'他告诉我……'这种引述就是答案信号——经理给出的原因被原原本本复述在这句里。

【替换】 I had an attitude problem ↔ The man had an attitude problem.

原话第一人称 I，选项换成第三人称 The man，意思不变

【排除】 A) 张冠李戴

原文差评出自男士的 manager(见 your annual performance evaluation meeting with your manager)，A 却说 a poor evaluation from his colleagues'来自同事'，张冠李戴改了评价来源，故错。 借⽤原⽂： your annual performance evaluation meeting with your manager B) 未提及

经理给的理由是态度问题，全程没说男士 made little contribution to the company'贡献少'，这是凭'表扬少'常识脑补出的原因，原文无据。

C) 原词陷阱

原文经理说 it's the little things I do and say，C 的 paid attention to trivial things 用 trivial(琐碎)勾住这个 little things，听着像。但原文 little things 指'惹经理不快的琐碎言行 (即态度的体现)'，不是说男士'只关注琐事'，含义被偷换。 借⽤原⽂： it's the little things I do and say
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about some managers?

options.text: They make unhelpful decisions for solving problems.
They favor some employees' suggestions over others.
They use manipulative language to mask their irrational choices.
They reject employees' reasonable arguments for work efficiency.

questions.shortExplanation: Some managers really adopt manipulative language to disguise the unreasonable choices they have made. 有些经理确实会采用操控性的语言，来掩饰他们做出的那些不合理的选择。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） They use manipulative language to mask their irrational choices.

【定位】 Some managers really adopt manipulative language to disguise the unreasonable choices they have made. 有些经理确实会采用操控性的语言，来掩饰他们做出的那些不合理的选择。

【信号】 女士发言中直接评价经理的核心陈述句。女士这段以 Some managers really adopt manipulative language to disguise the unreasonable choices 直陈对经理的判断，主语 Some managers、动词 adopt…to disguise 把'手段+目的'说全，是承载答案的评价句。

【替换】 adopt manipulative language ↔ use manipulative language adopt 换成 use，同义动词替换 disguise the unreasonable choices↔ mask their irrational choices disguise→mask、unreasonable→irrational 双重同义替换

【排除】 A) 答非所问

原文批评的是经理'用话术掩盖不合理决定'，重点在'掩盖'这个语言行为；A 的 make unhelpful decisions for solving problems 只截取'决定不好'一层，丢了'操控语言'的核心，且 unhelpful 与原文 unreasonable 侧重不同，未答到点上。 借⽤原⽂： disguise the unreasonable choices they have made B) 未提及

原文没说经理 favor some employees' suggestions over others'偏心采纳某些建议'，这是凭'经理不公'的印象自造的指控，原文无对应句。

D) 原词陷阱

原文紧接的下一句是 They don't use the rational power of arguments to resolve issues'他们不用理性论证去解决问题'，D 的 reject employees' reasonable arguments for work efficiency 盗用 rational/arguments 这两个原词，并自添 for work efficiency(为了效率)的动机，原文既没说'否决员工合理论点'，更没提'效率'，原词在意思被改向。 借⽤原⽂： They don't use the rational power of arguments to resolve issues of conflict
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: According to the woman, what do some managers think of honesty?

options.text: It is a must for rational judgment.
It is more of a sin than a virtue.
It is a good quality in the workplace.
It is more important now than ever.

questions.shortExplanation: Honesty was deemed to be more of a sin than a virtue, since it made people feel uncomfortable. 诚实被认为更像是一种罪过而非美德，因为它让人感到不舒服。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （态度观点题） It is more of a sin than a virtue.

【定位】 Honesty was deemed to be more of a sin than a virtue, since it made people feel uncomfortable. 诚实被认为更像是一种罪过而非美德，因为它让人感到不舒服。

【信号】 评价动词 deemed 引出的定性，是态度落点。女士用 Honesty was deemed to be more of a sin than a virtue，deemed(被认为是)后面跟的 a sin(罪)就是这些经理对诚实的定性，评价性动词后的内容正是态度题答案信号。

【替换】 more of a sin than a virtue↔more of a sin than a virtue

此项罕见地原句照搬，反成正确项

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

原文把诚实判为 more of a sin than a virtue'更像罪'，是负面；A 的 It is a must for rational judgment'理性判断的必需品'是正面拔高，极性与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： Honesty was deemed to be more of a sin than a virtue C) 与原文相反

C 的 It is a good quality in the workplace'职场好品质'是正面评价，而原文这些经理把诚实看作 a sin(负面)，褒贬相反；workplace 虽是全篇高频词，但拿它包装的却是与原意相反的正面判断。 借⽤原⽂： Honesty was deemed to be more of a sin than a virtue D) 未提及

原文谈的是诚实被看作罪/还是美德，从没说它 more important now than ever'现在比过去更重要'，时间今昔的维度原文完全没出现。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the woman think is the priority of many managers?

options.text: Smoothing relationships in the workplace.
Making rational and productive decisions.
Focusing on employees career growth.
Preserving their power and prestige.

questions.shortExplanation: And retaining their power and prestige is their priority.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Preserving their power and prestige.

【定位】 And retaining their power and prestige is their priority.

而且，保住他们的权力和威望，才是他们的首要之务。

【信号】 对话收尾处带 priority 的结论句。临近结束，女士用 And retaining their power and prestige is their priority 直接点出 priority，以 And 收束全段批评、给出结论，正是答案信号——对话的总结判断落在这句。

【替换】 retaining their power and prestige↔Preserving their power and prestige. retaining 换成 preserving，同义动词替换

【排除】 A) 未提及

原文说经理首要是保权保威，从没说他们以 Smoothing relationships in the workplace'维系职场关系'为先，这是凭好印象自造的目标，原文无对应。

B) 原词陷阱

原文多处用到 rational(如 They don't use the rational power of arguments)，B 的 Making rational and productive decisions'做理性高效决定'正是拿这个高频词设套；但全篇批评经理不理性、靠话术保权，把'理性决策'当成他们的首要恰恰相反。 借⽤原⽂： They don't use the rational power of arguments to resolve issues C) 未提及

原文通篇批评经理只顾自己权威，绝无说他们以 Focusing on employees career growth'员工职业成长'为先，这与结论句的'保权'完全背离，原文无据。

items.title: 2023年3月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 1
items.transcript:
Athletes are seen as heroes because they can do things that most of us can't do. They can hit fastballs coming at them at nearly 100 miles an hour, and leap and hang in the air, seemingly defying gravity. They get paid millions of dollars for their efforts, and their names and faces appear on everything from running shoes to advertising boards.

Athletes who are champions also show qualities such as perseverance, dedication, and the ability to keep their cool under pressure. Many show those same qualities off the playing field, too. Stories about superstar athletes teach us about working hard and believing in ourselves and then being passionate about what we do. Although it's usually bad behavior that gets an athlete a spot on the six o'clock news, many high-profile players work hard to be positive role models to children. They raise money for charities and act as mentors, talking to student groups and volunteering their time to programs that help children keep off drugs and stay in school.

Still, even the greatest champions have flaws. Just because an athlete has the perfect golf swing doesn't mean he is the perfect parent, friend or spokesperson. They also make mistakes. Separating an athlete's professional and personal lives can be tough. When a sports star gets in trouble with the law, or does something wrong in their private life, fans are often left disappointed. Before he died, baseball star Mickey Mantle, who was plagued with alcohol problems, told young ballplayers and the fans who admired him "to play like me, don't be like me."

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker say athletes are often viewed as heroes?

options.text: They show genius which defies description.
They accomplish feats many of us cannot.
They create very high commercial value.
They bring great honor to their country.

questions.shortExplanation: Athletes are seen as heroes because they can do things that most of us can't do. 运动员被视为英雄，是因为他们能做到我们多数人做不到的事。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） They accomplish feats many of us cannot.

【定位】 Athletes are seen as heroes because they can do things that most of us can't do. 运动员被视为英雄，是因为他们能做到我们多数人做不到的事。

【信号】 because 后紧跟原因。答案信号是因果连词 because，它后面 they can do things that most of us can\'t do 正是录音给出的理由，因果词后那一句就是答案落点。

【替换】 do things that most of us can\'t do↔ accomplish feats many of us cannot

同义改写：do things=accomplish feats

【排除】 A) 未提及

They show genius which defies description. 的天赋/无法描述在录音里没有对应表述； 录音说的是做到常人做不到的事，并未夸张到天才到无法形容，属拔高式编造。

C) 原词陷阱

They create very high commercial value. 借了录音里 They get paid millions of dollars 和广告板出现这层商业画面来诱选，但那是顺带描述、并非说话人给出的成为英雄的原因； 题问 Why are they heroes，答案是能力而非商业价值，听到钱就选会中招。 借⽤原⽂： They get paid millions of dollars for their efforts D) 未提及

They bring great honor to their country. 的 country/为国争光在整段录音里没出现过， 是听力惯用的拔高型干扰，第一步预读时已提醒要警惕 country 是否真被提到。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say many high-profile players do?

options.text: They take part in kids' extra-curricular activities.
They work in spare time to teach children sports.
They try to be positive role models to children.
They serve as spokespersons for luxury goods.

questions.shortExplanation: They raise money for charities and act as mentors, talking to student groups and volunteering their time to programs that help children keep off drugs and stay in school. 他们为慈善募款、担任导师，与学生群体交流，并把时间投入到帮助孩子远离毒品、留在学校的项目中。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） They try to be positive role models to children.

【定位】 They raise money for charities and act as mentors, talking to student groups and volunteering their time to programs that help children keep off drugs and stay in school. 他们为慈善募款、担任导师，与学生群体交流，并把时间投入到帮助孩子远离毒品、留在学校的项目中。

【信号】 主语承接后的行为列举。答案句承接上句 many high-profile players work hard to be positive role models to children，紧接着用 volunteering their time to programs that help children keep off drugs and stay in school 具体列举其作为，行为列举处即题问的落点。

【替换】 help children keep off drugs and stay in school↔ Keeping athletes away from drug or alcohol problems keep off=keep away from 同义

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

They take part in kids\' extra-curricular activities. 借录音里频繁出现的 children/student groups 这层与孩子相关的画面诱选，但录音说的是 talking to student groups、volunteering，并非 take part in 课外活动，动作对不上。 借⽤原⽂： talking to student groups B) 未提及

They work in spare time to teach children sports. 利用录音里 children 一词及对孩子的帮助来诱选，但录音从未说他们利用业余时间教孩子体育，teach ... sports 与 spare time 都是录音没有的添加。 借⽤原⽂： help children keep off drugs and stay in school

D) 与原文相反 They serve as spokespersons for luxury goods. 把这群正面榜样说成代言奢侈品，方向与录音里 work hard to be positive role models to children 的公益形象相反，且 luxury goods 录音未提。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say can be difficult?

options.text: Separating an athlete's professional life from their personal life.
Preventing certain athletes from getting in trouble with the law.
Keeping athletes away from drug or alcohol problems.
Being super sports stars without appearing arrogant.

questions.shortExplanation: Separating an athlete's professional and personal lives can be tough. 把运动员的职业生活与私人生活分开，可能很难。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Separating an athlete's professional life from their personal life.

【定位】 Separating an athlete's professional and personal lives can be tough. 把运动员的职业生活与私人生活分开，可能很难。

【信号】 tough 这一难易判断词。答案信号是 can be tough 里的 tough，它正是题干 difficult 的同义词，与它搭配的 Separating an athlete\'s professional and personal lives 即题问的那件难事。

【替换】 Separating an athlete\'s professional and personal lives ↔ Separating an athlete\'s professional life from their personal life 几乎原句，仅句式微调 can be tough ↔ can be difficult tough=difficult

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

Preventing certain athletes from getting in trouble with the law. 直接搬录音里 gets in trouble with the law 的原话诱选，但录音是把触犯法律当作运动员会犯错的举例，并没说防止其触法是件难事，问的难事是分开两种生活。 借⽤原⽂： When a sports star gets in trouble with the law C) 原词陷阱

Keeping athletes away from drug or alcohol problems. 借录音 plagued with alcohol problems 的醒目词诱选，但那是 Mickey Mantle 个人遭遇的举例，录音没把远离毒品酒精说成困难，与 tough 搭配的并非此事。 借⽤原⽂： Mickey Mantle, who was plagued with alcohol problems D) 未提及

Being super sports stars without appearing arrogant. 的不显傲慢在录音里没有任何对应，arrogant 一词及相关意思整段未出现，属凭空编造的难处。

items.title: 2023年3月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 2
items.transcript:
We don't need to tell you that weddings can get expensive. Even with the most meticulous budgeting, a few unexpected costs are bound to occur. While most brides tend to accept this as fact, one Canadian woman, who is only known as Susan, attempted to avoid all wedding costs. She did this by asking her friends and family to pay up to attend her wedding. It went about as well as you'd expect. Susan is causing quite the debate online after posting a bizarre Facebook complaint about her now-cancelled wedding.

Yes, the couple called off the wedding just days before their wedding vows. Since their guests refused to pay the $1,500 attendance fee, the $60,000 dream wedding was put on permanent hold. In her long explanation filled with cursing and swearing, the bride accused her friends and family of ruining her marriage and her life. She stated that each guest would only need to pay $1,500 while she sacrificed everything for the day. Her maid of honor told her to stick to the budget, as she was asking too much from her guests. But Susan ignored her. Not surprisingly, only eight people responded positively to the wedding invitations and money requests.

Realizing they would not be able to afford their dream wedding, Susan's future husband suggested getting married in Las Vegas. The bride quickly shut down the idea, saying she did not want a wedding of gambling and heavy drinking. It seems her dream wedding has now become a nightmare.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about weddings?

options.text: They always cost more than expected.
They are joyous and exciting occasions.
They should be paid up by the attendees.
They are dreams coming true to the brides.

questions.shortExplanation: We don't need to tell you that weddings can get expensive. Even with the most meticulous budgeting, a few unexpected costs are bound to occur. 不用我们说你也知道，婚礼会变得很烧钱。哪怕预算做得再精细，也难免冒出一些意料之外的开销。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） They always cost more than expected.

【定位】 We don't need to tell you that weddings can get expensive. Even with the most meticulous budgeting, a few unexpected costs are bound to occur. 不用我们说你也知道，婚礼会变得很烧钱。哪怕预算做得再精细，也难免冒出一些意料之外的开销。

【信号】 开篇总起句直接定调。篇章第一句 weddings can get expensive 就是开门见山的总起，紧接着 a few unexpected costs are bound to occur 进一步坐实"花费会超出预料"。开头总起句是篇章题最常见的答案信号，听到第一句定性就该锁定。

【替换】 a few unexpected costs are bound to occur↔cost more than expected unexpected costs = cost more than expected

【排除】 B) 未提及 They are joyous and exciting occasions.（欢乐激动的场合）听起来像婚礼常识，很诱人，但说话人开篇的定性是"烧钱、超预算"，全篇也是讲婚礼黄掉的糟心事，根本没说婚礼欢乐。这是用生活常识代替原文的典型坑。

C) 原词陷阱

They should be paid up by the attendees.（该由出席者付费）盗用了原文 asking her friends and family to pay up to attend her wedding 里的 pay up、attend——但那是 Susan 一个人的荒唐做法，不是 speaker 对"婚礼"的普遍看法。听到 pay up 就选，正中原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： asking her friends and family to pay up to attend her wedding D) 原词陷阱

They are dreams coming true to the brides. 借用了原文反复出现的 dream wedding、 brides，听着顺耳。但原文的 dream wedding 是讽刺 Susan 那场最终变 nightmare 的婚礼，绝非说"婚礼是新娘美梦成真"。这是把后文的反讽细节误当成开篇定性。 借⽤原⽂： the $60,000 dream wedding was put on permanent hold
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the wedding of the Canadian woman Susan?

options.text: It cost $60,000.
It was cancelled.
It had eight guests only.
It was held in Las Vegas.

questions.shortExplanation: Yes, the couple called off the wedding just days before their wedding vows. Since their guests refused to pay the $1,500 attendance fee, the $60,000 dream wedding was put on permanent hold. 是的，这对新人在交换结婚誓言前几天取消了婚礼。由于宾客拒付 1500 美元的出席费，这场 6 万美元的梦想婚礼被永久搁置了。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） It was cancelled.

【定位】 Yes, the couple called off the wedding just days before their wedding vows. Since their guests refused to pay the $1,500 attendance fee, the $60,000 dream wedding was put on permanent hold. 是的，这对新人在交换结婚誓言前几天取消了婚礼。由于宾客拒付 1500 美元的出席费，这场 6 万美元的梦想婚礼被永久搁置了。

【信号】 结局动词 called off / put on permanent hold。答案落在表"取消"的动作上：the couple called off the wedding 与 put on permanent hold 直接交代了婚礼的最终结局。 问"这场婚礼怎么了"，结局性动词就是定位信号，盖过其中的数字干扰。

【替换】 the couple called off the wedding↔It was cancelled. called off = was cancelled

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 It cost $60,000. 里的 6 万美元录音确实念到了——the $60,000 dream wedding——但原文是说这场"标价 6 万的梦想婚礼被搁置"，并不是说它"真的花掉了 6 万"（婚礼根本没办成）。听到 $60,000 就选，正中数字原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： the $60,000 dream wedding was put on permanent hold C) 原词陷阱

It had eight guests only. 借了原文 only eight people responded positively 里的 eight。但那"八个人"是"积极回应邀请和付费要求的人数"，而婚礼根本取消了、压根没有出席的宾客。把"回应的八人"偷换成"到场八位宾客"，是细节偷换。 借⽤原⽂： only eight people responded positively to the wedding invitations and money requests D) 原词陷阱

It was held in Las Vegas. 盗用了原文地名 getting married in Las Vegas。但拉斯维加斯只是未婚夫"提议"的地点，且 Susan 当场否决了，婚礼根本没在那办、也没办成。地名被搬到错误的事实上，是张冠李戴式原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： Susan's future husband suggested getting married in Las Vegas
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What did Susan's maid of honor advise her to do?

options.text: Postpone her wedding.
Ask her friends for help.
Keep to her budget.
Invite more guests.

questions.shortExplanation: Her maid of honor told her to stick to the budget, as she was asking too much from her guests.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Keep to her budget.

【定位】 Her maid of honor told her to stick to the budget, as she was asking too much from her guests.

她的伴娘劝她守住预算，因为她对宾客的要求太过分了。

【信号】 建议信号 told her to。Her maid of honor told her to stick to the budget 中的 told her to 就是"建议"信号，信号后紧跟的动作 stick to the budget 即答案所在。听建议题， 认准 told sb to / advised 这类信号，落点就在其后的动词短语。

【替换】 stick to the budget↔Keep to her budget stick to = keep to

【排除】 A) 未提及

Postpone her wedding. 听着合理（婚礼出问题了，推迟很常见），但伴娘说的是守预算， 从没提推迟。婚礼最后是被取消（called off）而非推迟，考生易把"取消"的印象误当成伴娘建议"推迟"。 B) 与原文相反

Ask her friends for help. 恰恰反了：原文里 Susan 正是因为 asking too much from her guests（向宾客 / 朋友要太多）才闹崩，伴娘是劝她"别再这么要了、守预算"，而非劝她"找朋友帮忙"。方向完全相反。 借⽤原⽂： she was asking too much from her guests D) 与原文相反

Invite more guests. 与伴娘的本意相悖。伴娘嫌 Susan 对宾客要求太多、要她收着点（守预算），怎会让她再多邀客人？这是把建议方向取反的干扰项。 借⽤原⽂： Her maid of honor told her to stick to the budget
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: How did Susan respond to her future husband's suggestion?

options.text: She called it romantic.
She welcomed it with open arms.
She said she would think about it.
She rejected it flatly.

questions.shortExplanation: The bride quickly shut down the idea, saying she did not want a wedding of gambling and heavy drinking.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （态度观点题） She rejected it flatly.

【定位】 The bride quickly shut down the idea, saying she did not want a wedding of gambling and heavy drinking.

新娘很快否决了这个主意，说她不想要一场满是赌博和酗酒的婚礼。

【信号】 强否定动作 shut down + 理由。The bride quickly shut down the idea 里 shut down （直接否决）加上副词 quickly，语气强烈而干脆；后面 she did not want 的否定理由再次坐实拒绝。态度题就抓这种强否定动作 + 否定理由作为信号。

【替换】 quickly shut down the idea↔rejected it flatly

quickly shut down = rejected flatly

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

She called it romantic.（说它浪漫）是正面反应，与原文 shut down the idea 的干脆否决完全相反。原文里浪漫一词根本没出现，是凭"婚礼"联想出的诱选。 借⽤原⽂： The bride quickly shut down the idea B) 与原文相反

She welcomed it with open arms.（张开双臂欢迎）是强烈接受，恰与 Susan 的强烈拒绝相对。这是把态度光谱拨到了相反一端的干扰。 借⽤原⽂： quickly shut down the idea

C) 偷换概念 She said she would think about it.（说她会考虑）是夹在接受与拒绝之间的中间态度，最像"温和版"答案。但原文是 quickly shut down——又快又决绝，没有任何"再想想"的余地。把强否定弱化成"考虑"，是程度偷改。 借⽤原⽂： The bride quickly shut down the idea
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

items.title: 2023年3月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 1
items.transcript:
It has long been scientifically established that weather changes can affect people's moods. Now, a new study has provided evidence that temperature can influence people's personalities. This study of over 1.6 million people revealed that 22 degrees Celsius is the perfect air temperature to live in. A city with an average annual temperature closer to 22 tends to have a population who are more agreeable, conscientious, emotionally stable, and outgoing. It is the least taxing temperature for the body to regulate its own temperature.

The study was observational and didn't show cause and effect, but the scientists behind it theorized that better weather leads people to leave their home more often. This, in turn, leads to more social interaction, which encourages them to develop a friendlier and socially more acceptable personality. Warmer climates also make people feel more positive in general. They tend to be more agreeable and conscientious.

The findings might help explain why colder and warmer countries tend to produce people with different personalities. Roughly speaking, about 40% of a person's personality is determined by their genes, the other 60% by their environment. It was already well-known that personality traits vary across geographic regions. Scientists also knew that these geographic personality traits are associated with a broad range of consequential outcomes. These outcomes include economic activity, for example, entrepreneurial start-up rates, and also crime rates, health behaviors, and health outcomes.

And it is well established that personality traits differ between countries. The research team speculated the two might be linked. To test this, they gave online personality tests to 5,587 Chinese students and 1.66 million Americans. They then compared the results with the average annual temperature where they grew up. The tests measured personality along five well-studied characteristics. The five were agreeability, conscientiousness, emotional stability, outgoingness, and openness to new experiences. In both groups, the researchers found the closer a town's average annual temperature was to 22 degrees, the more its population exhibited those personality characteristics.

However, the findings were much stronger for the Chinese group than the Americans studied, which suggests that though temperature plays a role, it does not play a dominant role. The effects are fairly weak. It's unlikely to lead to many arguments over the temperature setting of the office air conditioner.

questions.prompt: What has a new study revealed about temperature?

options.text: It determines people's moods.
It can impact people's wellbeing.
It is closely related to people's emotions.
It can influence people's personalities.

questions.shortExplanation: Now, a new study has provided evidence that temperature can influence people's personalities.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） It can influence people's personalities.

【定位】 Now, a new study has provided evidence that temperature can influence people's personalities.

如今，一项新研究提供了证据，表明温度能够影响人的性格。

【信号】 Now 引出新结论。前一句说"天气影响情绪"早已是定论，紧接 Now, a new study has provided evidence 用 "Now"（如今）把新旧对照开来——"Now+新研究"正是答案信号，新研究的新发现就在这句，落点是 temperature can influence people's personalities。

【替换】 temperature can influence people's personalities↔It can influence people's personalities. 近乎原句对应

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

A"决定人的情绪 moods"盗用了原文 weather changes can affect people's moods 里的 moods，但那是"早已确立的旧定论"、且用的是 affect（影响）不是 determine（决定），并非"新研究的发现"，听到 moods 就选会掉进时间错位的坑。 借⽤原⽂： weather changes can affect people's moods B) 未提及

B 说温度"影响人的福祉 wellbeing"，可原文新研究讲的是影响"personalities 性格"，从没出现 wellbeing 这层；属凭"听着合理"硬填，原文无据。 C) 答非所问

C"与情绪密切相关 closely related to emotions"对应的是 weather changes can affect people's moods 那条"早已确立"的旧知识，不是"new study revealed"的新发现；既错在时间（旧非新），"closely"也夸大了原文 affect 的程度。 借⽤原⽂： It has long been scientifically established that weather changes can affect people's moods.

items.title: 2023年3月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 2
items.transcript:
Today, we are talking about loneliness. Loneliness and social isolation are growing public health concerns for people of all ages in the United States, from adolescence to the elderly. Public health experts are worried because loneliness seems to be on the rise, and studies have long found correlations between loneliness and an assortment of medical conditions that threaten health and longevity.

The problem of loneliness may be even greater than we thought. A new national poll found that about a third of older Americans are lonely, and almost as many seniors feel isolated. This is a serious problem as research shows that chronic loneliness is particularly harmful to senior citizens. That's because it can impair older adults' memory and damage their physical and mental health. Chronic loneliness even impacts the life expectancy of seniors, increasing their risk of early mortality.

Let's take a closer look at that poll now. More than a third of seniors in the poll said they felt lonely at least some of the time, and 27% said they sometimes or often felt isolated. This reflects how much time the seniors spent with others. Almost 30% said they socialized with friends, family or neighbors once a week or less. Women were more likely than men to report loneliness.

But there is good news. It looks like loneliness can be reversed. But researchers are still trying to determine the best way to do so. Why is that? Resolving the problem of loneliness among seniors often isn't as simple as getting them together with others or moving them in with their children. In fact, the poll found that seniors who lived with their children were more likely to report feeling lonely than those who didn't. This may be because loneliness refers to the discrepancy between actual and desired relationships. So it's possible that someone who lives alone doesn't meet that definition, while someone in a house full of busy people does.

How can we solve the problem? Well, the researchers assert that it's important to address each person's underlying cause of loneliness, whether it's the death of a spouse, medical problems, or social expectations that haven't been fulfilled. It's noteworthy that there is one general recommendation. While finding solutions for loneliness is highly personal, research suggests the best interventions are those that involve meaningful social contact at least once a week. Depending on the person, that could mean volunteering, seeing an old friend or something else.

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker say the finding of a new national poll reveals a serious problem?

options.text: The number of older Americans living alone is on the rise.
Chronic loneliness does harm to senior citizens in particular.
Correlations have been found between loneliness and ill health.
A growing number of US seniors face the risk of early mortality.

questions.shortExplanation: This is a serious problem as research shows that chronic loneliness is particularly harmful to senior citizens.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Chronic loneliness does harm to senior citizens in particular.

【定位】 This is a serious problem as research shows that chronic loneliness is particularly harmful to senior citizens.

这是个严重的问题，因为研究显示长期的孤独对老年人尤其有害。

【信号】 原句直说 serious problem 加 as 因果。录音里 This is a serious problem as research shows that chronic loneliness is particularly harmful to senior citizens 用 a serious problem 直接呼应题干的 serious problem，再用 as（因为）引出原因——题干问 Why， 答案就在这个 as 因果句里。

【替换】 chronic loneliness is particularly harmful to senior citizens↔ Chronic loneliness does harm to senior citizens in particular

近义改写：harmful 换 does harm，particularly 换 in particular

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

录音第1段确实念过 loneliness seems to be on the rise，选项 The number of older Americans living alone is on the rise 顺手借了 on the rise 制造耳熟，但录音说的是孤独在上升，不是独居老人人数在上升，且这不是题干问的为何是严重问题，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： loneliness seems to be on the rise C) 原词陷阱

第1段念过 correlations between loneliness and an assortment of medical conditions，选项 Correlations have been found between loneliness and ill health 借此造耳熟。但这是讲座开场的背景铺垫，题干问的是新民调揭示的严重问题，那条具体落在第2段的尤其伤害老人，C 答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： studies have long found correlations between loneliness and an assortment of medical conditions D) 原词陷阱

第2段念过 increasing their risk of early mortality，选项 A growing number of US seniors face the risk of early mortality 借走 early mortality 与 risk。但录音说的是长期孤独提高了老人早亡风险，并没说越来越多老人面临早亡风险（人数增长），D 把风险升高偷换成人数增多，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： increasing their risk of early mortality

questions.prompt: What is the good news the speaker talks about?

options.text: Medication is available for treating loneliness.

Being busy helps fight loneliness.
Loneliness is probably reversible.

questions.shortExplanation: But there is good news. It looks like loneliness can be reversed. 但有个好消息。看起来孤独是可以被逆转的。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Loneliness is probably reversible.

【定位】 But there is good news. It looks like loneliness can be reversed. 但有个好消息。看起来孤独是可以被逆转的。

【信号】 转折 But 加提示词 good news。录音 But there is good news 用转折 But 加题干同词 good news 双重提示，紧接的 loneliness can be reversed 就是好消息的内容——转折后/ 提示词后的那句才是真正落点。

【替换】 loneliness can be reversed↔Loneliness is probably reversible

词性转换：can be reversed 换 reversible

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

录音第5段提到 medical problems，选项 Medication is available for treating loneliness 借 medical 的耳熟造出有药可治。但录音只把 medical problems 列为孤独的诱因之一， 从没说有药物能治疗孤独，属无中生有的原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： medical problems B) 原词陷阱

第4段念过 someone who lives alone，选项 Loneliness rarely results from living alone 借 living alone 造耳熟。录音确实暗示独居未必孤独，但用 rarely（很少）把它说成了绝对判断，且这不是题干问的好消息那一句，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： someone who lives alone doesn't meet that definition C) 与原文相反

第4段念过 a house full of busy people，选项 Being busy helps fight loneliness 借 busy 造耳熟。可录音恰恰是说住在一屋子忙人中间的人反而可能孤独，busy 在原文是孤独的反例，C 把它反着用成忙碌能对抗孤独，与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： someone in a house full of busy people does

questions.prompt: What is the key to solving the loneliness problem according to the speaker?

options.text: Living with one's children.
Meeting social expectations.

questions.shortExplanation: While finding solutions for loneliness is highly personal, research suggests the best interventions are those that involve meaningful social contact at least once a week.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Meaningful social contact.

【定位】 While finding solutions for loneliness is highly personal, research suggests the best interventions are those that involve meaningful social contact at least once a week.

尽管为孤独寻找解决办法因人而异，但研究表明，最好的干预是那些每周至少有一次有意义社交接触的方式。

【信号】 推荐信号 research suggests the best。录音 research suggests the best interventions are those that involve meaningful social contact 用 suggests 加 the best（最佳）双重推荐信号点名办法——题干问 the key，答案就在这个给推荐的句子里。

【替换】 meaningful social contact at least once a week ↔ Meaningful social contact 概括截取：选项是原句的核心保留

【排除】 A) 与原文相反第4段念过 moving them in with their children，选项 Living with one's children 借 children 造耳熟。但录音明说和子女同住的老人反而更易孤独，把它当解决办法正好相反， 是听到熟词就选的陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： seniors who lived with their children were more likely to report feeling lonely B) 原词陷阱

第5段念过 social expectations that haven't been fulfilled，选项 Meeting social expectations 借 social expectations 造耳熟。但录音把它列为孤独的诱因之一，不是解决孤独的关键，B 答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： social expectations that haven't been fulfilled D) 原词陷阱

录音念过 the best interventions 和第5段的 medical problems，选项 Timely medical intervention 拼合 medical 与 intervention 造耳熟。但录音说最佳 intervention 是有意义的社交接触，不是医疗干预；medical 在原文是诱因，D 张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： the best interventions are those that involve meaningful social contact

items.title: 2023年3月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 3
items.transcript:
Hello, I'm co-founder of the popular female travel community We Are Travel Girls. We collect and publish stories from women traveling all over the world. We promote women's blogs; we host meetings and events and are getting ready to launch our Travel With Us trips in Bali, Japan and Malawi.

Before I started We Are Travel Girls, I had a successful 10-year career in finance in London, where I advised private clients on their investments. Having always had a huge love for travel, I finally took the leap and left finance to pursue my dream of starting a travel company.

For as long as I can remember, I wanted to be a travel writer. Before blogs existed and everything we read was online, I would go to travel writing seminars by writers who were published in travel magazines. I was desperate to write for one of those magazines, but didn't know how to break into that industry. After university, I ended up working in finance, but always had a desire to travel and write about it.

In 2015, I was looking at ways to leave finance, and my best friend Vanessa, who grew up on a ranch on the Central Coast of California, suggested starting a blog. But when we started creating it, we realized that was the same thing every girl was doing. So we turned our attention to creating a community among these women. This led us to start We Are Travel Girls, which has now grown into a community of over 200,000 followers.

To anyone thinking about becoming a travel writer, I would suggest they first try and look for a unique way to enter the industry. There are a lot of travel writers now and it can be hard to stand out from the crowd, which is really why we started We Are Travel Girls. Be prepared to work hard if you want to turn it into a full-time business, and try not to rush to selling advertising spaces before you have created a dedicated audience. The size of your audience doesn't necessarily need to be huge, but you want them to be engaged. If you post too many promotions early on, you will turn many people off.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the speaker before she created the community We Are Travel Girls?

options.text: She had a successful career in finance.

She invested in several private companies.

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） She had a successful career in finance.

【定位】 Before I started We Are Travel Girls, I had a successful 10-year career in finance in London, where I advised private clients on their investments.

在创办 We Are Travel Girls 之前，我在伦敦有过一段成功的、长达十年的金融职业生涯， 在那里我为私人客户提供投资建议。

【信号】 时间信号 Before…对上题干。答案句以 Before I started We Are Travel Girls 开头，与题干的 before she created the community 时间状语完全对应，这个『Before…』就是定位信号，它领出的那句正是讲她创办社区之前的身份。

【替换】 a successful 10-year career in finance↔a successful career in finance 几乎原句，只省去年限

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

选项 She wrote stories about women travelers. 盗用了录音第一段 We collect and publish stories from women traveling all over the world 里的 stories 与 women，但那是她现在做的社区业务、且是『收集发布』而非她个人『写』，题目问的是『创办社区之前』，时间和动作都对不上。 借⽤原⽂： We collect and publish stories from women traveling all over the world C) 原词陷阱

选项 She invested in several private companies. 盗用录音 I advised private clients on their investments 里的 private 和 invest，但原文是她『为私人客户提供投资建议』，主语和动作都被偷换成『她自己投资了几家私人公司』，意思已变。 借⽤原⽂： I advised private clients on their investments

【答案】 C （细节题） Avoiding too much advertising early on.

【定位】 Try not to rush to selling advertising spaces before you have created a dedicated audience. If you post too many promotions early on, you will turn many people off.

在你培养起一批忠实受众之前，不要急着去卖广告位。如果你早期发太多推广，会让很多人反感离开。

【信号】 否定建议 try not to + early on。答案句是 Try not to rush to selling advertising spaces before you have created a dedicated audience 和 If you post too many promotions early on, you will turn many people off，try not to 这个否定建议信号配合 early on（早期），正是讲如何留住受众的关键句。

【替换】 try not to rush to selling advertising spaces before you have created a dedicated audience↔ Avoiding too much advertising early on

try not to 等于 avoiding，时机对应 early on

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

选项 Attracting sufficient investment. 里 investment 让人联想第二段她的金融/投资背景 advised private clients on their investments，但讲『赢得受众』的这段从未谈吸引投资，属拿别处话题词来干扰。 借⽤原⽂： I advised private clients on their investments B) 未提及

选项 Creating an exotic corporate culture. 没有任何录音原句支撑，exotic corporate culture（异域企业文化）是凭旅行主题臆造出来的，与赢得受众的建议无关，属未提及。

D) 偷换概念

选项 Refraining from promoting similar products. 盗用录音 post too many promotions 里的 promotion，但原文劝的是『别在早期发太多推广』，问题在数量与时机，不是『别推类似产品』，similar products 是录音没有的偷换。 借⽤原⽂： If you post too many promotions early on, you will turn many people off
