items.title: 2023年6月六级第1套 · 长对话 1
items.transcript:
M: Hi, Lily, how's the new apartment?

W: It's okay.

M: What? How can it be just okay when last week you were thrilled about the place and kept posting photos of it online?

W: Well, last week when I moved in, the apartment seemed cozy, just the right size for one person. But now it just seems tiny, shabby and solitary.

M: Ah, that's the problem. You miss your roommates from university, don't you?

W: I'm going to sound like an idiot, because I used to complain to you all the time about how crowded our dormitory room was, and about all the things they did to irritate me, like watching movies late at night without headphones, or talking loudly early in the morning. But now I miss them terribly.

M: Of course you do. That's perfectly normal. When I got my first place I remember thinking I couldn't wait to live by myself and get away from my juvenile roommates and all their annoying habits. But then I began missing them and feeling lonely and thinking that our dormitory was like paradise, even though there were six of us guys in one small room.

W: I thought it was just me who felt like that.

M: Look, you lived at home with us, and then you had three roommates, and this is your first time living alone. So it's hard. But your first apartment is a milestone in your life, and you should celebrate it. Tell me about the apartment.

W: Actually, it's not bad. In fact, it's pretty adorable, now that I have decorated it and it has everything I need. I have a kitchen to cook in and a bathroom all to myself, and then another room with my bed at one end, and a sofa, a small table and chairs at the other end.

M: That does sound adorable and I can't wait to see it, and neither can mom and dad.

questions.prompt: What was the woman's first impression of the apartment?

options.text: It was spacious and tranquil.
It was warm and comfortable.
It was shabby and solitary.
It was tiny and noisy.

questions.shortExplanation: Well, last week when I moved in, the apartment seemed cozy, just the right size for one person. But now it just seems tiny, shabby and solitary.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） It was warm and comfortable.

【定位】 Well, last week when I moved in, the apartment seemed cozy, just the right size for one person. But now it just seems tiny, shabby and solitary.

嗯，上周我刚搬进来时，公寓显得很温馨，对一个人来说大小正合适。但现在它只让人觉得又小、又破、又孤单。

【信号】 时间对照 last week…But now 切出'第一印象'。答案句靠 last week when I moved in 与 But now 形成前后对照：转折前讲的是刚搬进来时（即第一印象），转折后才是现在的感受。题问 first impression，要取转折前那半句 the apartment seemed cozy, just the right size，别被 But now 后面的负面词带走。

【替换】 the apartment seemed cozy, just the right size for one person↔It was warm and comfortable. cozy=warm and comfortable 的同义概括

【排除】 A) 偷换概念

It was spacious and tranquil. 说'宽敞安静'，但录音只说 just the right size for one person（一人正合适），并非宽敞，tranquil 安静也无对应，属偷换概念。 借⽤原⽂： just the right size for one person C) 原词陷阱

shabby and solitary 两词录音确实念到，但出现在 But now it just seems tiny, shabby and solitary——是'现在'的感受，不是题问的'第一印象'，盗用原词答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： But now it just seems tiny, shabby and solitary

D) 原词陷阱

It was tiny and noisy. 中 tiny 是转折后'现在'的词（now it just seems tiny），noisy 录音根本没说；既错时间点又有未提及成分。 借⽤原⽂： now it just seems tiny

questions.prompt: Why does the woman say she is going to sound like an idiot?

options.text: She no longer hates people talking loudly in the dorm.
She misses her roommates she used to complain about.
She begins to enjoy the movies she once found irritating.
She finds the crowded dorm as cozy as her new apartment.

questions.shortExplanation: I'm going to sound like an idiot, because I used to complain to you all the time about how crowded our dormitory room was, and about all the things they did to irritate me… But now I miss them terribly.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） She misses her roommates she used to complain about.

【定位】 I'm going to sound like an idiot, because I used to complain to you all the time about how crowded our dormitory room was, and about all the things they did to irritate me… But now I miss them terribly.

我接下来说的会显得很傻，因为我以前老是跟你抱怨宿舍多么拥挤、室友们做的种种让我心烦的事……可现在我却特别想念他们。

【信号】 because 引出原因 + But now 给出反转落点。答案句由 because 直接引出'为何像傻瓜'的原因，又用 But now I miss them terribly 把态度反转到落点：以前抱怨、现在却想念，这一反差正是她说自己像傻瓜的缘由。because 与 But now 两个信号叠加锁定此句。

【替换】 I used to complain to you all the time about how crowded our dormitory room was↔ she used to complain about used to complain 原义保留、对象概括为 roommates But now I miss them terribly↔ She misses her roommates miss them=misses her roommates，代词还原

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

She no longer hates people talking loudly in the dorm. 盗用录音 talking loudly early in the morning 这个原词，但录音说的是'这曾让我心烦'，并没说'不再讨厌'，no longer 是凭空加的极性反转。 借⽤原⽂： talking loudly early in the morning C) 原词陷阱

She begins to enjoy the movies she once found irritating. 把录音 watching movies late at night without headphones 和 irritate 拼起来，但录音只说这些事曾让她心烦，从未说她现在'开始享受电影'，属答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： watching movies late at night without headphones D) 原词陷阱

She finds the crowded dorm as cozy as her new apartment. 借用 crowded、cozy 等词，但录音只说想念室友，从未把'拥挤的宿舍'与'新公寓'做'一样温馨'的比较，属无中生有。 借⽤原⽂： how crowded our dormitory room was

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the man when he left the dormitory to live on his own?

options.text: He found the apartment perfectly furnished.
He had a feeling of despair and frustration.
He had a similar feeling to the woman's.
He felt the new place was like paradise.

questions.shortExplanation: When I got my first place I remember thinking I couldn't wait to live by myself… But then I began missing them and feeling lonely and thinking that our dormitory was like paradise, even though there were six of us guys in one small room.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） He had a similar feeling to the woman's.

【定位】 When I got my first place I remember thinking I couldn't wait to live by myself… But then I began missing them and feeling lonely and thinking that our dormitory was like paradise, even though there were six of us guys in one small room.

我有了自己第一个住处时，记得当时心想终于可以一个人住了……可后来我开始想念他们、 感到孤单，觉得我们的宿舍简直像天堂，哪怕当时我们六个大男生挤在一间小屋里。

【信号】 But then 后的'想念、孤单'与女方感受平行。男方先说当初迫不及待独居，But then I began missing them and feeling lonely 转折后才是真实感受：想念室友、感到孤单。这与女方'now I miss them terribly'完全平行，正应了选项'与女方感受相似'。But then 是锁定真实感受的信号。

【替换】 But then I began missing them and feeling lonely↔He had a similar feeling to the woman's. 男方'想念+孤单'平行于女方同款感受=similar feeling

【排除】 A) 未提及

He found the apartment perfectly furnished. 录音里男方谈的是情绪（想念、孤单）， 从未说他的住处家具完美齐备，属未提及。

B) 过度推断

He had a feeling of despair and frustration. 把男方的 feeling lonely（孤单）夸大成 despair（绝望）、frustration（沮丧），情绪程度被大幅拔高，属过度推断。 借⽤原⽂： feeling lonely D) 张冠李戴

He felt the new place was like paradise. 盗用原词 paradise，但录音 thinking that our dormitory was like paradise 说的是'宿舍像天堂'，绝非'新住处像天堂'，把对象张冠李戴了。 借⽤原⽂： thinking that our dormitory was like paradise

questions.prompt: What does the man say he can't wait to do?

options.text: Go to see the woman's apartment.
Make a phone call to his parents.
Buy some furniture for the woman.
Decorate the woman's apartment.

questions.shortExplanation: That does sound adorable and I can't wait to see it, and neither can mom and dad.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Go to see the woman's apartment.

【定位】 That does sound adorable and I can't wait to see it, and neither can mom and dad.

那听起来确实很可爱，我都等不及要去看看了，爸妈也一样等不及呢。

【信号】 意愿标志 I can't wait to see it 直接给出动作。答案句的信号就是 I can't wait to see it， can't wait to 后面的 see it 即男方迫不及待要做的事；it 指上文女方的公寓。题干问 can't wait to do，顺着这个词在原文里一找即得。

【替换】 I can't wait to see it↔ Go to see the woman's apartment. see it→go to see the apartment，代词还原

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 Make a phone call to his parents. 借用录音 neither can mom and dad 里的父母，但男方说的是'爸妈也等不及（想看公寓）'，并非'要打电话给父母'，属答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： neither can mom and dad C) 未提及

Buy some furniture for the woman. 中 furniture 与女方描述公寓时提到的 sofa、table 沾边，但男方从未说要买家具，属未提及。

D) 张冠李戴

Decorate the woman's apartment. 盗用原词 decorate，但录音 now that I have decorated it 说的是女方已经装饰好了，并非男方迫不及待要去装饰，张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： now that I have decorated it

items.title: 2023年6月六级第1套 · 长对话 2
items.transcript:
W: Welcome to our program Book Talk. Our guest today is Frank Jones, a critic of our education system, and the author of a new book, How to Reform Our Universities.

M: Hello, Susan.

W: Frank, you support radically changing universities in America?

M: Yes, I believe that the purpose of higher education is to prepare young people to enter the workforce, and that our current system fails to do this. We're allocating too many resources to disciplines that don't match the needs of employers.

W: I think your attitude to education is a bit cynical, Frank. Surely the purpose of university is to prepare young people to participate fully in civic life, rather than just to find well-paid jobs.

M: Susan, many young graduates struggle to find any job, let alone a good one. The job market is grim, particularly for students who study the arts.

W: I agree that it isn't easy for young people to find work, but you propose closing down all departments that aren't directly related to science and technology. Is that really the solution?

M: You're overstating my point. My argument is that we need to use more of our budget on areas like science and engineering. To do that, we need to take money from subjects like literature and music.

W: But the arts have value. They're an important part of our culture. Studying literature or music or sculpture might not result in a job in that area, but it helps young people to think about the world in a deeper way, which makes them better citizens and makes for a better society.

M: I agree that the arts are valuable to society, but it's naive to think that not only the most talented, but all students should study them at university level. The arts are very competitive, and most graduates will end up with a great deal of debt, obtaining a degree that has little value on the job market.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the conversation about the man?

options.text: He works as a literary critic.
He hosts an educational program.
He has initiated a university reform.
He has published a book recently.

questions.shortExplanation: Our guest today is Frank Jones, a critic of our education system, and the author of a new book, How to Reform Our Universities. 我们今天的嘉宾是 Frank Jones，他是我国教育体制的一位批评者，也是一本新书《如何改革我们的大学》的作者。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） He has published a book recently.

【定位】 Our guest today is Frank Jones, a critic of our education system, and the author of a new book, How to Reform Our Universities. 我们今天的嘉宾是 Frank Jones，他是我国教育体制的一位批评者，也是一本新书《如何改革我们的大学》的作者。

【信号】 开场介绍嘉宾句。答案信号是主持人开篇介绍嘉宾的固定句式 Our guest today is Frank Jones，这类“今天的嘉宾是……，他是……的作者”的引荐句，必然交代人物身份，是细节题的天然落点。

【替换】 the author of a new book, How to Reform Our Universities↔He has published a book recently. “新书作者”=“最近出书”

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱录音确说他是 a critic of our education system（教育体制的批评者），A 盗这个 critic 改成 a literary critic.（文学评论家）——把“批评教育”偷换成“文学评论”，是听到 critic 就想选的原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： a critic of our education system B) 张冠李戴

He hosts an educational program.（他主持一档教育节目）说反了人物：主持节目的是女方 Susan（Welcome to our program Book Talk），男方只是受访嘉宾，把主持人的身份安到嘉宾头上。 借⽤原⽂： Welcome to our program Book Talk C) 过度推断

He has initiated a university reform.（他已发起一场大学改革）盗用了书名里的 reform （How to Reform Our Universities）。他只是写书“主张”改革，并未真的发起改革，把“写书谈改革”夸成“已发起改革”，属过度推断。 借⽤原⽂： How to Reform Our Universities
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the man believe is the problem with the current American system of higher education?

options.text: It fails to keep up with the radical changes of society.
It fails to ensure universities get sufficient resources.
It has not prepared young people for the job market.
It has not fostered the growth of the arts disciplines.

questions.shortExplanation: I believe that the purpose of higher education is to prepare young people to enter the workforce, and that our current system fails to do this. 我认为高等教育的目的是让年轻人为进入职场做好准备，而我们现行的体制没能做到这一点。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） It has not prepared young people for the job market.

【定位】 I believe that the purpose of higher education is to prepare young people to enter the workforce, and that our current system fails to do this. 我认为高等教育的目的是让年轻人为进入职场做好准备，而我们现行的体制没能做到这一点。

【信号】 被问者应答 + fails 否定。答案信号有二：一是这是男方对“你支持激进改革大学吗”的直接应答（被问者的回答处），二是句中 our current system fails to do this 的否定动词 fails，正点出“制度没做到的事”——即他眼中的问题。

【替换】 prepare young people to enter the workforce↔ It has not prepared young people for the job market. workforce=job market

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

It fails to keep up with the radical changes of society. 借用了原文 radically changing （radically changing universities）的 radical，但男方批的是“没对接就业”，并未说制度 “跟不上社会的剧变”，把原词拼到一个原文没说的归因上。 借⽤原⽂： radically changing universities

B) 与原文相反

It fails to ensure universities get sufficient resources. 盗用原文 resources（allocating too many resources）。男方说的是资源“分配错地方（过多给了不匹配需求的学科）”，不是大学“拿不到足够资源”，方向正相反。 借⽤原⽂： allocating too many resources to disciplines that don't match the needs of employers D) 与原文相反

It has not fostered the growth of the arts disciplines.（没扶持文科）与男方立场完全相反：他主张少投文科、多投理工（take money from subjects like literature and music），怎会嫌文科扶持不够。这是把他的对立面安到他头上。 借⽤原⽂： take money from subjects like literature and music
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: How should the education budget be allocated according to the man?

options.text: More of the budget should go to science and technology.
The underfunded music discipline should be prioritized.
Subdisciplines like sculpture should get more funding.
Literature should get as much funding as engineering.

questions.shortExplanation: My argument is that we need to use more of our budget on areas like science and engineering. To do that, we need to take money from subjects like literature and music. 我的主张是，我们需要把更多预算用在科学和工程这类领域。要做到这一点，我们就得从文学、音乐这类科目那里抽走经费。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） More of the budget should go to science and technology.

【定位】 My argument is that we need to use more of our budget on areas like science and engineering. To do that, we need to take money from subjects like literature and music. 我的主张是，我们需要把更多预算用在科学和工程这类领域。要做到这一点，我们就得从文学、音乐这类科目那里抽走经费。

【信号】 立论句 My argument is。答案信号是男方亮明主张的标志句 My argument is that we need to use more of our budget on areas like science and engineering——My argument is / we need to 是典型的“建议 / 主张”信号，其后内容即他的真实立场。

【替换】 use more of our budget on areas like science and engineering↔ More of the budget should go to science and technology. “多用预算于”=“更多预算应给”

【排除】 B) 与原文相反

The underfunded music discipline should be prioritized. 盗用原文 music（literature and music）。男方恰恰主张从 music 抽钱（take money from），而非优先扶持 music，方向完全相反。 借⽤原⽂： take money from subjects like literature and music

C) 张冠李戴

Subdisciplines like sculpture should get more funding. 借用女方后文提到的 sculpture （literature or music or sculpture）。但这是女方为艺术辩护时举的例，男方的主张是给理工加钱、从文科抽钱，绝不会主张给雕塑这类细分文科加经费，既张冠李戴又方向相反。 借⽤原⽂： Studying literature or music or sculpture D) 偷换概念

Literature should get as much funding as engineering. 盗用 literature、engineering 两个原词，却把男方“偏向理工、从文学抽钱”的不均等主张，偷换成“文学与工程经费同等”。男方要的是倾斜，不是均分。 借⽤原⽂： take money from subjects like literature and music
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say the arts can do?

options.text: Build a prosperous nation.
Make skilled professionals.
Create ingenious artists.
Cultivate better citizens.

questions.shortExplanation: Studying literature or music or sculpture might not result in a job in that area, but it helps young people to think about the world in a deeper way, which makes them better citizens and makes for a better society. 学习文学、音乐或雕塑，也许不会带来该领域的工作，但它能帮助年轻人更深入地思考世界，从而让他们成为更好的公民、造就更好的社会。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Cultivate better citizens.

【定位】 Studying literature or music or sculpture might not result in a job in that area, but it helps young people to think about the world in a deeper way, which makes them better citizens and makes for a better society. 学习文学、音乐或雕塑，也许不会带来该领域的工作，但它能帮助年轻人更深入地思考世界，从而让他们成为更好的公民、造就更好的社会。

【信号】 转折 but 后才是真意。答案信号是转折词 but——but it helps young people to think about the world in a deeper way, which makes them better citizens。but 之前的 might not result in a job 是让步铺垫，but 之后才是女方真正要强调的艺术功效。

【替换】 which makes them better citizens ↔ Cultivate better citizens. “使其成为更好公民”=“培养更好公民”

【排除】 A) 偷换概念 Build a prosperous nation. 听上去接近原文 makes for a better society，但 prosperous nation（繁荣国家）与 better society（更好的社会）并不等同，且题问“艺术能做什么”的核心落点是 better citizens；把“更好的社会”拔成“建设繁荣国家”是偷换加拔高。 借⽤原⽂： makes for a better society B) 未提及

items.title: 2023年6月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 1
items.transcript:
Do you ever have the annoying feeling that you don't have time to really think anymore? You are not alone. A variety of factors have conspired to rob us of time for reflection about ourselves and our lives. Today, our preoccupied minds are rarely silent. The average person receives hundreds of texts and voice messages a day, and holidays for many of us are action-packed weeks more likely full of family activities than opportunities for tranquility and contemplation.

Regular reflection, however, underlies all great professionals. It's a prerequisite for you to recharge your mental batteries, see things in a new light and tap into your creativity. Almost all of the great advisors that I have studied have found ways to get away from it all and contemplate their life and work. Some researchers in the field of creativity, in fact, believe that insight occurs during the reflection and relaxation that follows a period of intense activity.

Schedule time for reflection about your work or a particular project you're engaged in. I usually block out half an hour. Don't answer the phone. Push your papers to the side. Sketch, make lists, draw "mind maps" of ideas that come to you. At the end, write down any emerging ideas.

When you're alone, stop worrying and think. A lot of our down time is spent worrying about troublesome things in our lives or fantasizing about how we'd like our lives to be. Revisit things during moments of relaxation after a period of intense work. This is when we are the most creative.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the feeling that one doesn't have time to think anymore?

options.text: It is quite common.

questions.shortExplanation: Do you ever have the annoying feeling that you don't have time to really think anymore? You are not alone.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） It is quite common.

【定位】 Do you ever have the annoying feeling that you don't have time to really think anymore? You are not alone.

你是否曾有那种烦人的感觉——觉得自己再也没时间好好思考了？你并不是一个人（很多人都这样）。

【信号】 应答式呼应 You are not alone。录音先抛出 "没时间思考" 的感受，紧接一句 You are not alone.——"你不是一个人" 是对前面感受的直接回应与定性，等于说 "这事很多人都有"， 这种自问自答后的定性句就是答案信号。

【替换】 You are not alone. ↔ It is quite common. 换说法表 "普遍"

【排除】 B) 与原文相反

items.title: 2023年6月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 2
items.transcript:
Even before Colorado was a state, it had post offices. The first opened in 1859, in a settlement founded by migrants searching for gold. Life could be unpredictable out west—gold failed to appear, drought ruined farmers and settlers clashed with Native Americans. On the settlement's location now stands a sprawling university campus. Amid all the changes, one feature remained constant—the postal service.

The maps tracing America's westward expansion are telling. In 1864, there were few postal branches on land controlled by Native Americans, which still accounted for most of the West. Over the next 25 years, post offices grew quickly. Colonization of the West could be regarded as a result of big government rather than pioneers. As federal subsidies and land grants tempted people into the deserts and plains, the post kept them connected.

In the mid-19th century, the Post Office Department was far from a centralized bureaucracy. To keep up with migration patterns, postal services were added to existing businesses. The federal government commissioned private wagons to carry the mail. Short-term contracts were granted to local businessmen to act as postmasters. These partnerships enabled the mail to quickly follow migrants, helping knit together remote parts of the country.

Mr. Blevins, a digital historian, wrote a book on the history of the US postal service. He used data science to analyze historical trends. Most strikingly, he built an accompanying website, complete with interactive maps. They show readers how, within a generation, the postal service helped colonize a continent. These online interactive maps illustrate the formative power of snail mail.

items.title: 2023年6月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 1
items.transcript:
In last week's lecture, we discussed reasons why people forget things. This week, we will discuss a surprising reason why we might remember some things—anxiety.

Think about something as simple as buying a coffee. That may not seem like an experience that would make a deep impression on your memory, but anxiety could change that. In fact, a new study suggests that people with higher anxiety levels might remember certain information better than people with lower anxiety levels. That's because higher levels of anxiety may make people more susceptible to negative feelings, putting them in a more negative state of mind. That in turn may make them able to better remember some events.

Let's take a closer look at that new study now. In the study, the researchers started by giving 80 undergraduate students an anxiety test. The test measured the participants' anxiety levels over the preceding two weeks. Then, to test memory, the participants were shown a series of neutral words, one at a time. Some of the words were printed on to photos of negative scenes, meaning images that could affect their emotions negatively, such as a photo of a car accident or a cemetery. The rest of the words were printed on to photos of neutral scenes, such as a photo of a lake or trees. Neutral words included words like "table" or "desk" that don't elicit emotion. Later, the participants were asked to think back to the words they were shown earlier, which caused them to reenter either a negative or a neutral mindset. The participants were then presented with another set of neutral words, and their memory of these new words was tested.

The researchers found that the new words presented to people in a negative mindset were better remembered by people with higher levels of anxiety than those with lower levels of anxiety. In other words, when highly anxious individuals took in otherwise emotionally neutral information that was presented to them, it became colored by their negative mindset, making them remember the information better. But these same effects were not seen in people with low levels of anxiety.

Previous studies have found that extreme levels of anxiety, such as those experienced by people diagnosed with an anxiety disorder, can be quite detrimental to memory and cognitive performance. But the highly anxious people in this study represent individuals who are managing their anxiety and for whom anxiety is not a serious problem.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say the new study suggests?

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Higher levels of anxiety may improve people's memory.

【定位】 In fact, a new study suggests that people with higher anxiety levels might remember certain information better than people with lower anxiety levels. 事实上，一项新研究表明，焦虑水平较高的人，可能比焦虑水平较低的人更能记住某些信息。

【信号】 提示词 a new study suggests 后即结论。录音里 a new study suggests that 是明确的结论引出语，凡听到"研究表明"这类话，紧跟其后的整句就是答案句，本句把 higher anxiety 与 remember…better 直接挂钩，正是研究结论。

【替换】 people with higher anxiety levels might remember certain information better↔ Higher levels of anxiety may improve people's memory

"记得更好"改写成"提升记忆" people with higher anxiety levels↔Higher levels of anxiety

名词化平移

【排除】 D) 原词陷阱

Simple things may leave a deep impression 盗用了录音 make a deep impression on your memory 里的 deep impression，但原文说的是"买咖啡这种简单事本来不会留下深刻印象"，是用来引出焦虑可改变这一点的铺垫反例，并非研究结论，听到 deep impression 就选会中招。 借⽤原⽂： make a deep impression on your memory C) 未提及

Most people tend to remember things selectively 说"多数人有选择地记忆"，但录音只说高焦虑者"记得更好"(remember…better)，从没说"有选择地"(selectively)，也没说 most people，范围和限定词都是凭空加的。 B) 答非所问

Some experiences are easier to remember than others（有些经历比另一些更易记）听上去对，但它只说"经历有难易之分"，完全没提研究的关键——是 anxiety 在起作用，把研究最核心的变量丢了，等于答非所问。

items.title: 2023年6月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 2
items.transcript:
Over the past 20 years, the internet has gradually become a dominant feature of our lives. It has changed how we communicate with each other, and it has definitely transformed the way we do business with each other. Marketing has also changed in a number of ways. For instance, in the past, consumers had to call a phone number and patiently wait on hold, in order to get the information they wanted. Today, they want the information immediately. They'll go to the company's social media page and post comments and questions, expecting to receive an immediate response. If they don't get their questions answered soon, they'll move on to another company that will answer them quickly.

Marketing departments today need to follow technological development. For example, this year's smartphone is smarter than last year's; self-driving cars are now on the road. Marketers have to do research on which technologies are coming into being. Otherwise, they risk being left behind in the virtual dust. Marketing has also changed due to the importance of video. People don't just want to read text; they want to watch things happening. Companies now have to explore how they can use video on a consistent basis to share information about their businesses. Fortunately, it's extremely easy to shoot something these days. All you need is a smartphone.

But what's the result of all this? Shorter attention spans. We aren't the same people that we were 20 years ago. Not only have we grown accustomed to getting the information we want instantaneously, our attention spans are much shorter. If something doesn't capture our attention within a few seconds, we're on to the next piece of content. Marketers need to figure out ways to speak directly to the customers' emotions, and they need to figure out how to do that as quickly as possible. Once people are emotionally engaged, they'll stick with you.

If marketing has changed this much in the past 20 years, imagine what the next 20 years will bring. In a recent survey, only 9% of marketers could say with confidence that their marketing efforts were actually working. Their confidence is being shaken, because the rules of the game change every year. That's why it's important for marketers to pay attention to the latest technological developments and consider collaborating with technological innovators. That way, they'll be moving at the same pace as the tech industry.

items.title: 2023年6月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 3
items.transcript:
You might be surprised to learn that the benefits of friendships extend beyond people's social life and into their work, which is interesting when considering the extent to which people sacrifice friendships, or at least the time they spend with friends, because of the extended hours they're devoting to work. Just last week, I was remarking to a colleague that I'm content with only one social engagement per week. But according to recent research, that's evidently not enough.

In an initial study of more than 700 respondents, scholars from an American university analyzed the impact that friends, as opposed to family, have on self-esteem and well-being. Friends came out substantially on top. That's because to be someone's mate is a voluntary act, unlike family who people rarely get to choose. The researchers found that when people choose to cultivate and maintain supportive friendships with an individual, it means that the person is valued and worthy of their limited time. Such sentiments of value and worthiness boost our self-esteem.

The second study comprised more than 300 participants. It proved that the better we feel about ourselves, the more likely we'll perform our job confidently and competently. This follow-up study found that non-work friends even improve people's job satisfaction. They have as much of an impact on how much they love their jobs as do the friends they have at work, despite not actually being at our place of work. These types of friends tend to be our preferred outlet for venting about work-related matters. This is an avenue that may not be available at the office.

So even though friendships can be easy to neglect when confronted by pressures at work, or even pressures at home, neglecting our friends can turn out to be harmful and counterproductive. That's why, when determining how to create a better work-life balance, we need to consider not only how to balance work and family demands, but also how to cultivate and sustain supportive friendships. It's for this reason that managers should never discriminate when it comes to requests from employees for flexible work arrangements. It's irrelevant whether their need for a desired schedule is due to, say, parenting responsibilities, or a craving to hang out with a best mate. What matters is the opportunity to engage in a nourishing activity outside of work. That will definitely have a follow-on effect at work.

【定位】 You might be surprised to learn that the benefits of friendships extend beyond people's social life and into their work, which is interesting when considering the extent to which people sacrifice friendships … because of the extended hours they're devoting to work.

你或许会惊讶地发现，友谊的好处不止于社交生活，还延伸进了工作之中；考虑到人们为了延长工作时间而牺牲友谊，这一点尤其有意思。

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Allow employees to have a flexible work schedule.

【定位】 It's for this reason that managers should never discriminate when it comes to requests from employees for flexible work arrangements. 正因如此，管理者在面对员工提出的弹性工作安排请求时，绝不应区别对待。

【信号】 managers should never… 直接的建议句。录音 managers should never discriminate when it comes to requests from employees for flexible work arrangements 用 managers should never 直陈对管理者的建议，并落到 flexible work arrangements，正是题干 suggest managers do 所要的那句，建议句信号明确。

【替换】 managers should never discriminate when it comes to requests from employees for flexible work arrangements ↔ Allow employees to have a flexible work schedule.

『绝不区别对待弹性请求』正面化为『允许弹性安排』

【排除】 B) 答非所问

B:Encourage employees to be friends with colleagues. 把建议窄化成『鼓励和同事交朋友』，但录音 non-work friends even improve people's job satisfaction 一直强调非工作朋友的价值，讲者给管理者的建议是弹性安排，从没让管理者撮合同事交友，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： non-work friends even improve people's job satisfaction C) 原词陷阱

C:Help employees balance work and family responsibilities. 搬用录音 how to balance work and family demands 的原词，但那是讲者谈 work-life balance 时的铺垫；他给管理者的落地建议是别歧视弹性安排请求，C 把铺垫当成了建议本身。 借⽤原⽂： how to balance work and family demands D) 原词陷阱 D:Organize activities to nourish friendships outside of work. 把录音 the opportunity to engage in a nourishing activity outside of work 的 nourishing、outside of work 原词搬来，听上去最耳熟，但录音说的是『员工有机会参与工作外的滋养性活动』，并没让管理者去『组织活动』；管理者要做的是别歧视弹性请求，张冠李戴又偷换了动作。 借⽤原⽂： What matters is the opportunity to engage in a nourishing activity outside of work
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

items.title: 2023年6月六级第2套 · 长对话 1
items.transcript:
M: Have you decided what you wish to study?

W: Yes, professor. I wish to study architecture.

M: Ah, that's a wonderful profession. Why did you choose it?

W: I gave a lot of thought to things you said during our last discussion, and I decided architecture made the most sense for me. In particular, I'm attracted to the marriage of design and engineering.

M: That's great, but I seem to remember you were preoccupied with all the lofty mathematics. You no longer think this aspect will be too hard for you?

W: No. I was doing some online research and I think I should be able to manage. Math might be the toughest subject I encounter in the curriculum, but I'll simply put in the work required. I'm certain the fruits of my labor will pay off.

M: I'm sure that's true. Due to its material nature, architecture is one field where you will be able to clearly witness the contribution you make to a city. And the legacies you build will last much longer than any of us mortals.

W: Yeah, I guess that's true too. So what subjects do you think I should start brushing up on in preparation? I have the whole summer.

M: These days, architecture is a very diverse and dynamic degree. Most universities will encourage you to learn different things from fields as wide-ranging as philosophy and economics. Nevertheless, I would suggest you start with computer science because there will be many intricate visuals you will have to produce as part of your projects.

W: Any software in particular you think I should start with?

M: Photoshop is a good place. If you aren't yet, try to become as proficient as you can with it. And another thing that I would recommend you learn as much as you can is fine arts, in particular, the history of Western art.

questions.prompt: Why does the woman wish to study architecture?

options.text: She is attracted to the beauty of modern buildings.
She is preoccupied with her dream to be an architect.
She is influenced by her father who teaches architecture.
She is drawn to its integration of design and engineering.

questions.shortExplanation: In particular, I'm attracted to the marriage of design and engineering.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） She is drawn to its integration of design and engineering.

【定位】 In particular, I'm attracted to the marriage of design and engineering.

尤其是，我被设计与工程的结合所吸引。

【信号】 被问者直接应答动机。教授先问 Why did you choose it?，她的回答里用 I'm attracted to 直接给出动机，且以 In particular 加重强调——"问因 + 被问者亲口应答 + 加重语气"三重信号锁定此句。

【替换】 the marriage of design and engineering↔its integration of design and engineering marriage=integration同义改写

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

录音确有 I'm attracted to，A 项 She is attracted to the beauty of modern buildings. 借用了 attracted 这个原词，但她被吸引的是"设计与工程的结合"，不是"现代建筑的美"——美这一点录音从未说，属听到 attracted 就想选的陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： I'm attracted to the marriage of design and engineering B) 原词陷阱

preoccupied 一词录音里出现在教授口中 you were preoccupied with all the lofty mathematics，指她曾为数学发愁，根本不是"痴迷当建筑师的梦想"。B 项 She is preoccupied with her dream to be an architect. 盗了 preoccupied 又改了对象，与问"动机"无关。 借⽤原⽂： you were preoccupied with all the lofty mathematics C) 未提及

C 项 She is influenced by her father who teaches architecture. 牵出一个"教建筑的父亲"，但整段录音从未提到她父亲，更没说受其影响——是预读时就警惕的"凭空多出一个人物"的诱选。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: How does the woman say she will overcome the difficulty in learning mathematics?

options.text: Through hard work.
With the professor's help.
By studying the subject online.
By taking prerequisite courses.

questions.shortExplanation: Math might be the toughest subject I encounter in the curriculum, but I'll simply put in the work required. 数学可能是我在课程里遇到的最难的科目，但我会直接付出所需的努力。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Through hard work.

【定位】 Math might be the toughest subject I encounter in the curriculum, but I'll simply put in the work required. 数学可能是我在课程里遇到的最难的科目，但我会直接付出所需的努力。

【信号】 转折 but 后才是真应对。她先承认 Math might be the toughest subject，紧接 but I'll simply put in the work required——转折词 but 之后才是她真正给出的克服办法，前半只是铺垫难处。"but 后是落点"是听力定位的硬信号。

【替换】 put in the work required↔Through hard work put in work=hard work同义概括

【排除】 B) 未提及对话里确有 professor 这个人，B 项 With the professor's help. 借"现场有教授"诱你选， 但她讲克服数学的办法时只字未提靠教授，靠的是自己出力——属"同场有这人就误以为靠他"的陷阱。

C) 原词陷阱

录音里 I was doing some online research 确实出现 online，C 项 By studying the subject online. 盗了 online。但她上网只是"做了点调研"判断自己应付得来，并非"靠网上学数学"来克服难点——原词在、用途被偷换。 借⽤原⽂： I was doing some online research D) 未提及

D 项 By taking prerequisite courses. 说靠"修先修课"克服，但录音从未提到 prerequisite 或先修课程这回事——是凭空安上的办法。

questions.prompt: What does the man say about architects' contribution to a city?

options.text: It is groundbreaking.
It is long-lasting.
It is immaterial.
It is immortal.

questions.shortExplanation: And the legacies you build will last much longer than any of us mortals. 而且你所建造的那些遗产，会比我们这些凡人存续得久得多。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） It is long-lasting.

【定位】 And the legacies you build will last much longer than any of us mortals. 而且你所建造的那些遗产，会比我们这些凡人存续得久得多。

【信号】 男士对城市贡献的直接断言。男士谈到 the contribution you make to a city 后，紧接断言 the legacies you build will last much longer——这句直接定性"建筑师留下的东西能存续很久"，是他对该话题的正面陈述句，定位于此。

【替换】 will last much longer than any of us mortals↔It is long-lasting last much longer=long-lasting同义

【排除】 A) 未提及

A 项 It is groundbreaking."具开创性"在录音里毫无对应——男士谈的是贡献能"长久存续"，不是"开天辟地"，属凭空贴标签。

C) 与原文相反

录音里 Due to its material nature 出现 material（实体的），C 项 It is immaterial. 恰好取了它的反义 immaterial（非物质/无关紧要）。建筑明明是"实体"，选项却说"无形"， 是"盗原词又反极性"的诱选。 借⽤原⽂： Due to its material nature D) 原词陷阱

录音 longer than any of us mortals 用 mortals（凡人）作对比，D 项 It is immortal. 盗这个词根改成 immortal（不朽）。原文只说贡献"比凡人活得久"，是相对的"更久"，并非"永不灭"——把相对的久夸成绝对不朽，程度过头。 借⽤原⽂： will last much longer than any of us mortals
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What subject does the man suggest the woman start with?

options.text: Economics.
Philosophy.
Computer science.
Western art.

questions.shortExplanation: Nevertheless, I would suggest you start with computer science because there will be many intricate visuals you will have to produce as part of your projects.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Computer science.

【定位】 Nevertheless, I would suggest you start with computer science because there will be many intricate visuals you will have to produce as part of your projects.

不过，我建议你从计算机科学开始，因为你的项目里会有很多复杂的图像需要你来制作。

【信号】 Nevertheless 转折 + suggest start with。前句先泛举 philosophy and economics 等领域，再用 Nevertheless 一转，紧跟 I would suggest you start with computer science ——转折后的"建议 + start with"双信号，直指真正要先学的那门。

【替换】 I would suggest you start with computer science↔Computer science 原句点名即选项学科

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

philosophy and economics 里 economics 被念到，但那是男士泛举"大学会鼓励你学的各类领域"，A 项 Economics. 盗这个原词冒充答案；题问的是 start with（先学），经济学并非他建议起步的那门。 借⽤原⽂： fields as wide-ranging as philosophy and economics B) 原词陷阱

B 项 Philosophy. 同样来自 philosophy and economics 的泛举，philosophy 被念到却不是"建议先学"的那门——与 A 一样是"听到学科名就想划"的原词诱选。 借⽤原⽂： fields as wide-ranging as philosophy and economics D) 答非所问

录音末尾 the history of Western art 确出现"西方艺术"，D 项 Western art. 盗了它。但那是男士另起一句"还建议你尽量多学美术"，与本题问的 start with（最先入手）不是同一件事——位置和性质都对不上。 借⽤原⽂： another thing that I would recommend you learn as much as you can is fine arts, in particular, the history of Western art

items.title: 2023年6月六级第2套 · 长对话 2
items.transcript:
W: So as I mentioned over the phone, we are looking for someone who is very discreet, I can't stress this enough.

M: I fully understand.

W: As we all know, being such a famous football player at Real Madrid, Mr. Sanchez has a very high public profile. This means he cannot leave the house without being recognized and harassed.

M: Yes, I completely understand how imperative it would be to respect Mr. Sanchez's private life.

W: Good. As his personal assistant, you would be required to run common everyday chores for Mr. Sanchez, things he cannot do himself due to his fame, like going to the supermarket or post office. So, well, at first sight it may appear that working for a celebrity is very glamorous. Nothing could be further from the truth. I'm telling you this so that you don't get any false expectations of what the job has to offer you.

M: Thanks. I understand this too. This is my first job after graduating from university. So frankly, I don't have much prior working experience. I am, however, very excited about the prospect of joining this company and very keen to start from the bottom in whatever capacity I may be of use.

W: That's good to hear. You sound very energetic. Tell me why you think you are well suited for this job?

M: Well, firstly, I love football. I'm a lifelong Real Madrid supporter and go to their games every weekend I can. I would simply love to have a job where I'm involved in some capacity with Real Madrid, regardless of the position and salary. And secondly, I think what this company does in sports consultancy is very cool. And I think my language skills could prove very useful down the road.

W: Please tell me more about your language skills.

M: I am fully fluent in English and Spanish and have a working proficiency in French.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the conversation about Mr. Sanchez?

options.text: He has occasionally been harassed by his fans.
He has been guarded by a discreet assistant.
He is well known to the public.
He is a famous football coach.

questions.shortExplanation: As we all know, being such a famous football player at Real Madrid, Mr. Sanchez has a very high public profile. This means he cannot leave the house without being recognized and harassed.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） He is well known to the public.

【定位】 As we all know, being such a famous football player at Real Madrid, Mr. Sanchez has a very high public profile. This means he cannot leave the house without being recognized and harassed.

众所周知，作为皇马一名如此有名的足球运动员，桑切斯先生有着很高的公众知名度。这意味着他一出门就会被认出、被骚扰。

【信号】 直接的身份介绍句。女士用 being such a famous football player at Real Madrid 一句话给桑切斯定了身份，再用 has a very high public profile 说明其名气之大——这种"客观介绍人物"的陈述句就是身份细节题的答案句。

【替换】 has a very high public profile ↔ well known to the public 「高公众知名度」=「被公众熟知」

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

He has occasionally been harassed by his fans. 借了录音 recognized and harassed 里的 harassed 一词，但录音说的是"一出门就"被骚扰、且并未限定"被粉丝"，更没说"偶尔"。题问的是"我们了解到什么"，最核心是他名气大，A把附带后果当主答案、还加了 occasionally,fans 这些原文没有的限定。 借⽤原⽂： recognized and harassed B) 张冠李戴

He has been guarded by a discreet assistant. 把开头 we are looking for someone who is very discreet 里的 discreet 拿来，安成"他被一位谨慎的助理护卫"。但 discreet 是对应聘者（男方）的要求，不是说桑切斯有这样一个助理——人物对应被搬错，且题问的是桑切斯本人，不是他的助理。 借⽤原⽂： someone who is very discreet D) 偷换概念 He is a famous football coach. 借用了录音 famous football player 里的 famous football，却把 player（球员）偷换成 coach（教练）。一字之差、身份全错，这正是预读时圈出"coach 是差异点"要防的偷换。 借⽤原⽂： famous football player
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What will the man do if he gets the job?

options.text: Serve as a personal assistant.
Play a key role in Real Madrid.
Run common daily chores for the woman.
Help promote Mr. Sanchez's public profile.

questions.shortExplanation: As his personal assistant, you would be required to run common everyday chores for Mr. Sanchez, things he cannot do himself due to his fame, like going to the supermarket or post office.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Serve as a personal assistant.

【定位】 As his personal assistant, you would be required to run common everyday chores for Mr. Sanchez, things he cannot do himself due to his fame, like going to the supermarket or post office.

作为他的私人助理，你将被要求为桑切斯先生跑日常琐事，那些他因名气太大而无法自己做的事，比如去超市或邮局。

【信号】 招聘者直接交代岗位。女方用 As his personal assistant 一句明确点出岗位名，这种由招聘方直接交代"你将担任什么"的句子，就是"他将做什么"的答案句。

【替换】 As his personal assistant↔Serve as a personal assistant.

「作为私人助理」=「担任私人助理」

【排除】 B) 过度推断

Play a key role in Real Madrid. 借了第7、8段反复出现的 Real Madrid，把"跑腿助理"夸成"在皇马担任关键角色"。录音清楚说他要做的是 run common everyday chores（跑日常琐事），与"key role"完全相反，是过度拔高。 借⽤原⽂： run common everyday chores for Mr. Sanchez C) 张冠李戴

Run common daily chores for the woman. 几乎照搬录音 run common everyday chores，只把"for Mr. Sanchez"换成"for the woman"。跑腿是为桑切斯、不是为这位招聘的女士，服务对象被掉包——正是预读时圈 for the woman 要防的张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： run common everyday chores for Mr. Sanchez D) 与原文相反 Help promote Mr. Sanchez's public profile. 拿了 high public profile 里的 public profile，编成"帮桑切斯提升公众形象"。但录音说的是因他名气太大、助理替他做他没法做的事（things he cannot do himself due to his fame），是"避开曝光"，绝非"提升曝光"，方向相反。 借⽤原⽂： has a very high public profile
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the man say about himself?

options.text: He is honest and always tells the truth.
He once worked part-time in university.
He cares little about his working hours.
He has little previous work experience.

questions.shortExplanation: This is my first job after graduating from university. So frankly, I don't have much prior working experience.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） He has little previous work experience.

【定位】 This is my first job after graduating from university. So frankly, I don't have much prior working experience.

这是我大学毕业后的第一份工作。所以坦白说，我没有多少之前的工作经验。

【信号】 第一人称的自我坦白。男方用 This is my first job after graduating from university 加 I don't have much prior working experience 直陈自身处境，这种"I/my"领起的自述句即本题答案落点。

【替换】 I don't have much prior working experience↔He has little previous work experience. 「没多少经验」=「几乎没经验」

【排除】 A) 过度推断

He is honest and always tells the truth. 大概由录音里 frankly（坦白说）联想而来，但 frankly 只是说话的语气词，男方并未谈自己"诚实、总说真话"。把一个口头副词夸成性格优点，属无中生有的推断。 借⽤原⽂： So frankly, I don't have much prior working experience B) 未提及

He once worked part-time in university. 用了 university 这个录音确实出现的词（after graduating from university），但男方只说"大学毕业"，从未提"在校期间打过工"。借眼熟的 university 编出一段没说过的经历，属未提及。 借⽤原⽂： after graduating from university C) 未提及 He cares little about his working hours. 听起来像呼应他"愿从底层做起"（keen to start from the bottom）的谦逊，但他谈的是不计职位与薪水，从没说"不在乎工作时长 （working hours）"。working hours 是录音里完全没出现的话题。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: Why does the man think he is a very competitive candidate?

options.text: He has a strong ability to connect with people.
He has a high proficiency in several languages.
He has a sound knowledge of sports consultancy.
He has a natural capacity to cooperate with others.

questions.shortExplanation: And I think my language skills could prove very useful down the road. 而且我觉得我的语言能力日后会很有用。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） He has a high proficiency in several languages.

【定位】 And I think my language skills could prove very useful down the road. 而且我觉得我的语言能力日后会很有用。

【信号】 他自陈的优势落点。在列举理由的段落里，男方以 I think my language skills could prove very useful 把"语言能力"点为自己的可用之长——这种"I think my … useful"的自夸句就是优势题的答案句。第10段又用 fully fluent in English and Spanish 坐实他确有多语能力。

【替换】 my language skills could prove very useful↔He has a high proficiency in several languages.

「语言能力有用」=「精通几门语言」

【排除】 A) 未提及

He has a strong ability to connect with people. 描述的人际沟通能力，录音通篇没有提及。他列的是爱足球、觉得公司酷、语言能力，没有任何一句谈"与人连接"，属凭"助理该会沟通"的常识脑补。 C) 张冠李戴

He has a sound knowledge of sports consultancy. 盗用了录音 what this company does in sports consultancy 里的 sports consultancy。但这是他在夸"公司做的体育咨询很酷"，说的是公司的业务，不是他本人懂体育咨询——把公司的事安成了他的能力。 借⽤原⽂： what this company does in sports consultancy is very cool D) 未提及

He has a natural capacity to cooperate with others. 和A一样属人际类能力，与他亲口列的"语言能力"无关，录音没说他"善于与人协作"。它和A刻意做得相像（connect with people/cooperate with others），用来分散对正确项B的注意。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

items.title: 2023年6月六级第2套 · 听力篇章 1
items.transcript:
Adventure sports are undeniably attractive to many energetic and thrill-seeking kids. Sports like rock climbing, surfing, skiing, and mountain biking, thus have lots of appeal. They don't have many of the rules and pressures of traditional team sports, but they still have all the benefits of outdoor physical activity.

When properly supervised, extreme sports can be a part of a healthy, balanced life. Some adventure sports may be associated with high risks of injury, so it's important for kids to figure out when to take risks, and when not to. Risk-free activities deprive kids of the opportunity to test themselves and overcome their fears. But to some, these very risks are what makes these sports a bad choice. They say that extreme sports can often lead to devastating injuries, especially as young thrill-seekers may attempt feats that are too advanced for them.

But let's be real. Most kids do all kinds of dangerous stuff whether you want them to or not. Adventure sports have many of the same risks and dangers, but they have an additional sense of adventure, courage and autonomy that is important to foster in young children. As always, it's up to parents to decide what's best for their kids. But if you do decide that adventure sports are a bit too much, do try to introduce other forms of outdoor adventures into their lives. Camping under the stars, fishing, stargazing or even just playing in the woods can help a lot in building the same sense of self-confidence and risk-taking as in adventure sports.

questions.prompt: Why do extreme sports appeal to many kids?

options.text: They bring more benefits to young people.
They require less supervision and training.
They are more suitable to young people.
They have fewer rules and pressures.

questions.shortExplanation: They don't have many of the rules and pressures of traditional team sports, but they still have all the benefits of outdoor physical activity. 它们没有传统团队运动那么多的规则和压力，但仍然具备户外体育活动的全部益处。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） They have fewer rules and pressures.

【定位】 They don't have many of the rules and pressures of traditional team sports, but they still have all the benefits of outdoor physical activity. 它们没有传统团队运动那么多的规则和压力，但仍然具备户外体育活动的全部益处。

【信号】 对照句"没有……但仍有……"。这句用 They don't have many of the rules and pressures of traditional team sports 与后面 but they still have all the benefits 做对照，前半把"规则和压力少"点了出来——这正是这类运动区别于传统运动、吸引孩子的卖点，是承载答案的句子。

【替换】 don't have many of the rules and pressures ↔ have fewer rules and pressures don't have many = fewer

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

A 用了录音同句里的原词 benefits，但录音说的是"仍具备户外活动的全部益处"，并非"带来更多益处"；more 是选项硬加的，题目问的是"吸引力来自哪"，benefits 只是顺带提及， 不是吸引点。 借⽤原⽂： they still have all the benefits of outdoor physical activity B) 原词陷阱

B 的 less supervision and training 借用了第二段的 When properly supervised 制造熟耳感，但录音从没说这类运动"需要的监管和训练更少"；相反第二段强调"需要妥善监管"， 与 B 相反。 借⽤原⽂： When properly supervised, extreme sports can be a part of a healthy, balanced life. C) 未提及 C 说这类运动"更适合"年轻人，录音只说它们对孩子"有吸引力（attractive/appeal）"，从未做"更适合/更不适合"的比较判断，属于原文未提及的拔高。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about risk-free activities?

options.text: They prevent kids from enjoying adventure sports.
They help kids guard against any possible injuries.
They rob kids of the chance to cultivate their courage.
They deprive kids of the opportunity to develop team spirit.

questions.shortExplanation: Risk-free activities deprive kids of the opportunity to test themselves and overcome their fears.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） They rob kids of the chance to cultivate their courage.

【定位】 Risk-free activities deprive kids of the opportunity to test themselves and overcome their fears.

无风险的活动剥夺了孩子自我考验、克服恐惧的机会。

【信号】 对象词 risk-free 直接现身。录音里 Risk-free activities deprive kids of the opportunity to test themselves and overcome their fears 正面点出题干对象 risk-free activities，并紧跟一个负面动词 deprive，这一句就是对该对象的直接评价，是答案句。

【替换】 deprive kids of the opportunity to test themselves and overcome their fears↔ rob kids of the chance to cultivate their courage deprive=rob、克服恐惧=培养勇气

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

A 的 prevent kids from enjoying adventure sports 借了录音常出现的 adventure sports，但录音说"剥夺机会"的是 risk-free activities 对"自我考验"，并非"阻止孩子享受冒险运动"，把对象和内容都换了。 借⽤原⽂： Adventure sports have many of the same risks and dangers B) 与原文相反

B 说无风险活动"帮孩子防受伤"，听上去像好事，但录音对 risk-free activities 的态度是负面的（deprive 剥夺机会），B 把贬义说成了褒义，方向相反；injuries 一词来自录音第二段对 devastating injuries 的描述。 借⽤原⽂： extreme sports can often lead to devastating injuries D) 偷换概念 D 把录音"克服恐惧"偷换成 develop team spirit（团队精神）。录音里"团队"概念只与 traditional team sports 沾边，从没说无风险活动剥夺了"团队精神"，是把尾词悄悄换掉。 借⽤原⽂： traditional team sports
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What should parents do if they decide adventure sports are a bit too much for their kids?

options.text: Help them take up these sports when they are more mature.
Let them participate in some less risky outdoor activities.
Ask them to try some forms of indoor sports.
Introduce them to these sports step by step.

questions.shortExplanation: But if you do decide that adventure sports are a bit too much, do try to introduce other forms of outdoor adventures into their lives.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Let them participate in some less risky outdoor activities.

【定位】 But if you do decide that adventure sports are a bit too much, do try to introduce other forms of outdoor adventures into their lives.

但如果你确实觉得冒险运动有点过头，那就一定要试着把其他形式的户外探险引入他们的生活。

【信号】 建议句"do try to…"加重语气。这句用 do try to introduce other forms of outdoor adventures，do 加在动词前是强调语气的建议，且与题干条件 adventure sports are a bit too much 逐字对上，是承载答案的建议句。

【替换】 introduce other forms of outdoor adventures↔participate in some less risky outdoor activities 其他户外探险 = 风险更低的户外活动

【排除】 A) 未提及

A 说"等孩子更成熟再让他们玩这些运动"，录音从没建议"等长大再玩"，only 提到引入别的户外活动；mature 一词录音也未出现，属凭空添加的方案。

C) 与原文相反

C 让孩子"试室内运动"，但录音建议的是 outdoor adventures（户外探险），并举露营、 观星等户外例子，方向与"室内"相反。 借⽤原⽂： introduce other forms of outdoor adventures into their lives D) 原词陷阱

D 的"step by step / 循序渐进地把这些运动介绍给孩子"盗用了录音原词 introduce，但录音的 introduce 接的是 other forms of outdoor adventures（别的户外活动），不是"循序渐进地引入冒险运动本身"；step by step 是选项硬加，且与"觉得太过头就别玩"的前提矛盾。 借⽤原⽂： do try to introduce other forms of outdoor adventures into their lives

items.title: 2023年6月六级第2套 · 听力篇章 2
items.transcript:
The shiny gadgets of today will be waste tomorrow. Manufacturers don't talk much about this when they announce the big new thing that will replace your mostly just as good old thing. In fact, technology firms often purposely design devices that will not last long and cannot be repaired so that consumers will have to spend their money on a new one.

This year, the French government began requiring tech manufacturers to list a repairability score. If a device can be repaired, then its life can be extended, saving consumers money and the planet the burden of so many trashed gadgets. Equipped with this knowledge, consumers can make better choices about which products to buy.

Some 59 million tons of old TVs, computers, screens, smartphones, washers and other electronics are discarded every year. This waste is dangerous. Batteries explode in recycling facilities. Toxic substances like mercury leak into soil and groundwater and disperse in the air. Manufacturing flat screens adds greenhouse gases to the atmosphere. We need tech companies to take the lead to solve this problem. If they won't, governments must make them do so.

Although tech companies will often speak of environmental sustainability, many lobby against repair legislation, fearful it will eat into their profits. Sustainability matters, but marketable design appears to matter more to these companies. Consumers should support right-to-repair legislation. In this world, damage is a certainty. But we cannot leave things broken: A problem of our creation is a problem that can be fixed.

questions.prompt: Why do new tech products soon become waste?

options.text: Consumers often have a craving for the latest model.
Such products tend to comprise parts that are irreplaceable.
Tech firms intentionally design products to have short lifespans.
Manufacturers use effective strategies to promote fancier products.

questions.shortExplanation: In fact, technology firms often purposely design devices that will not last long and cannot be repaired so that consumers will have to spend their money on a new one. 事实上，科技公司常常故意把设备设计成用不长久、又无法维修，好让消费者不得不掏钱买新的。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Tech firms intentionally design products to have short lifespans.

【定位】 In fact, technology firms often purposely design devices that will not last long and cannot be repaired so that consumers will have to spend their money on a new one. 事实上，科技公司常常故意把设备设计成用不长久、又无法维修，好让消费者不得不掏钱买新的。

【信号】 强调词 In fact + 因果连词 so that。In fact 把语气加重、引出真意，紧接的 so that consumers will have to spend their money on a new one 是明确因果，正是 Why 题要锁定的那一句。

【替换】 purposely design devices that will not last long ↔ intentionally design products to have short lifespans purposely=intentionally，短命换说法

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

录音确实提到 spend their money on a new one 里有 "买新" 的影子，但那是厂商设计造成的结果，不是说消费者主动 "渴望新款"；A 盗用 "new" 的语感把原因偷换到消费者欲望上。 借⽤原⽂： consumers will have to spend their money on a new one B) 答非所问

录音说 cannot be repaired，B 据此说零件 irreplaceable，但题问的是 "为何变废" 的根因 ——厂商故意，而非单纯零件不可换；B 抓了枝节当主因。 借⽤原⽂： cannot be repaired D) 偷换概念

录音批评厂商 purposely design devices that will not last long，D 却说厂商用有效策略推广更高端产品，语气由贬转中、且 "fancier products" 录音根本没说，是改了立场的无中生有。 借⽤原⽂： purposely design devices that will not last long and cannot be repaired
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What did the French government require tech companies to do to help consumers make better choices?

options.text: Indicate the competitiveness of their products.
List a repairability score of their products.
Specify the major parts of their products.
Detail the lifecycle of their products.

questions.shortExplanation: This year, the French government began requiring tech manufacturers to list a repairability score.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） List a repairability score of their products.

【定位】 This year, the French government began requiring tech manufacturers to list a repairability score.

今年，法国政府开始要求科技制造商列出一个可维修性评分。

【信号】 题干主体 French government 在原文复现，紧跟其后动作即答案。录音 the French government began requiring tech manufacturers to list a repairability score 与题干主体逐字对上，requiring 后的动作就是要求内容，是顺序定位的标准信号。

【替换】 list a repairability score↔List a repairability score of their products

近乎原句对应，list 与评分逐词吻合

【排除】 A) 未提及

录音通篇没说要标 "竞争力"，A 的 competitiveness of their products 是凭 "产品" 话题臆造出的方向，与政府要求无关。

C) 张冠李戴

录音第一段说设备 cannot be repaired 时隐含零件问题，C 借 major parts 之名说政府要求 "列出主要零件"，但政府要求的是评分不是列零件，把别处的词安到这道题上。 借⽤原⽂： cannot be repaired D) 原词陷阱

录音后句提到 its life can be extended，D 的 lifecycle of their products 借这点说要求 "详述生命周期"，但那是评分带来的好处，不是政府要求标注的内容，方向被带偏。 借⽤原⽂： its life can be extended
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What should tech companies do to help ensure environmental sustainability?

options.text: Take the initiative to reduce electronic waste.
Take due caution in upgrading their products.
Invest in constructing more recycling facilities.
Substitute all toxic substances with non-toxic ones.

questions.shortExplanation: We need tech companies to take the lead to solve this problem.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Take the initiative to reduce electronic waste.

【定位】 We need tech companies to take the lead to solve this problem.

我们需要科技公司带头来解决这个问题。

【信号】 主张句信号 We need…to take the lead。We need tech companies to take the lead to solve this problem 用 We need…to 直陈主张，take the lead 是 "应做" 动作的核心， 正是 should 题要锁的句。

【替换】 take the lead to solve this problem↔Take the initiative to reduce electronic waste

take the lead=take the initiative；this problem=electronic waste

【排除】 B) 未提及

Take due caution in upgrading their products 谈升级要谨慎，录音只在第一段批评厂商频出新品，从未要求厂商 "升级时谨慎"，是顺着话题臆造的对策。

C) 原词陷阱

录音 Batteries explode in recycling facilities 是在讲危害，C 借 recycling facilities 这个原词说应 "投资建更多回收设施"，但录音没把建设施当对策，把危害描述里的词挪来当答案。 借⽤原⽂： Batteries explode in recycling facilities D) 过度推断

录音 Toxic substances like mercury leak into soil 只在说毒物危害，D 借 toxic substances 拔高成 "用无毒物替换全部毒物"，substitute all 录音根本没主张，绝对词 all 更是过满。 借⽤原⽂： Toxic substances like mercury leak into soil and groundwater
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker think of the problem of waste?

options.text: It can be solved.
It is certain to worsen.
It will be fixed by tech companies.
It is unavoidable in the long run.

questions.shortExplanation: But we cannot leave things broken: A problem of our creation is a problem that can be fixed.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （态度观点题） It can be solved.

【定位】 But we cannot leave things broken: A problem of our creation is a problem that can be fixed.

但我们不能让问题就这么烂着：我们自己造成的问题，是能够被解决的。

【信号】 转折 But + 末句定调 can be fixed。But we cannot leave things broken 的 But 是态度反转信号，前句 damage is a certainty 是铺垫，转折后的 a problem that can be fixed 才是说话人真正的乐观结论。

【替换】 a problem that can be fixed↔ It can be solved.

can be fixed=can be solved，主被动同形

【排除】 B) 与原文相反

录音 damage is a certainty 只说损害必定存在，B 借 certainty 这个词头偷换成 certain to worsen（必然变糟），把 "必定有损害" 曲解为 "必定恶化"，与说话人乐观结论相反。 借⽤原⽂： damage is a certainty C) 张冠李戴

录音说问题 can be fixed 是 "我们" 共同的事，C 却说 fixed by tech companies，把解决主体单独安到科技公司头上；录音前文还说很多厂商 lobby against repair，正说明不能指望它们独力解决。 借⽤原⽂： many lobby against repair legislation D) 与原文相反

unavoidable in the long run 借的是 damage is a certainty 的悲观语气，但说话人紧接 But 就反转为问题能解决，D 取了被否定掉的那一半，与最终乐观态度相反。 借⽤原⽂： damage is a certainty
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

items.title: 2023年6月六级第2套 · 讲座与讲话 1
items.transcript:
On average, US workers spend about 10% of their workday surfing the internet, emailing friends or shopping online. This behavior, called cyberloafing, is believed to cost employers up to $85 billion a year in lost productivity.

The majority of cyberloafing research focuses on ways to prevent employees from engaging in this behavior through interventions such as internet monitoring and computer use policies. But it turns out, such behaviors may not be a sign that a worker is lazy or just wasting time. Social media use at work has been linked to higher levels of employee engagement and job satisfaction. New research suggests cyberloafing can help workers cope with an exceptionally stressful work environment.

But is cyberloafing actually effective at reducing employee stress levels? That's the question my research team wanted to answer in our new study. Our hypothesis was that cyberloafing may serve as a mini-break, giving employees an opportunity to recover from stressful work situations. To test this, we asked workers to complete an online survey and rank how much time they spent cyberloafing, checking non-work emails and shopping. We also asked them to rank job satisfaction, their desire to quit, and how often they've experienced mistreatment at work, such as being bullied, threatened or yelled at. As you might expect, we found that overall, more mistreatment at work was correlated with lower levels of job satisfaction and a greater desire to quit. More interestingly, we found that cyberloafing effectively buffered this connection. That is, mistreated workers who spent more time surfing the web and checking emails reported higher job satisfaction and were less likely to want to quit than similar participants who didn't cyberloaf as much. This suggests that cyberloafing acts as a sort of relief valve for workers, helping them recover from stressful experiences.

While we did not directly assess how cyberloafing affects worker performance, we believe by relieving stress it may not only reduce worker turnover, but also ultimately bolster productivity. This fits with other recent research that suggests taking short breaks is associated with higher levels of daily job performance. That isn't to say cyberloafing is always good. Too much time spent on non-work activities likely causes performance to suffer. All in all, managers should be more lenient with employees. We believe a bit of online shopping or surfing the internet at work could make workers more productive in the long run.

questions.prompt: What does most cyberloafing research focus on?

options.text: How internet monitoring can be implemented.
How to encourage productive internet surfing.
How cyberloafing affects overall productivity.
How to prevent employees from cyberloafing.

questions.shortExplanation: The majority of cyberloafing research focuses on ways to prevent employees from engaging in this behavior through interventions such as internet monitoring and computer use policies.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） How to prevent employees from cyberloafing.

【定位】 The majority of cyberloafing research focuses on ways to prevent employees from engaging in this behavior through interventions such as internet monitoring and computer use policies.

大多数关于摸鱼上网的研究关注的是如何通过网络监控、电脑使用规定等干预手段来防止员工从事这种行为。

【信号】 原话直述 research focuses on。录音直接说 The majority of cyberloafing research focuses on ways to prevent employees from engaging in this behavior，与题干 research focus on 几乎同词，是直述型答案句，听到 research focuses on 立刻锁定其后的宾语。

【替换】 ways to prevent employees from engaging in this behavior↔ How to prevent employees from cyberloafing

this behavior 即 cyberloafing，prevent 原词对应

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱录音确实念了 internet monitoring，但它是研究焦点（防止摸鱼）下面举的干预手段之一，不是研究本身关注的对象；A 把举例升格成焦点，且原文没说研究关注它如何被 implemented。 借⽤原⽂： internet monitoring and computer use policies B) 与原文相反

原文研究关注的是防止摸鱼，B 却说成鼓励高效上网（encourage productive internet surfing），方向相反，录音从未说大多数研究关注怎么鼓励上网。 借⽤原⽂： prevent employees from engaging in this behavior C) 张冠李戴

cyberloafing 对效率的影响是讲者自己团队后续探讨的内容，而本题问的是大多数已有研究关注什么——答案句明说那聚焦于 prevent；C 张冠李戴，把后文结论安到大多数研究头上。 借⽤原⽂： is cyberloafing actually effective at reducing employee stress levels?
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What was the hypothesis of the speaker's research team?

options.text: Cyberloafing is a sign of workers' laziness.
Cyberloafing may relieve employees of stress.
Employee engagement is closely related to job satisfaction.
Overuse of social media may lead to decline in productivity.

questions.shortExplanation: Our hypothesis was that cyberloafing may serve as a mini-break, giving employees an opportunity to recover from stressful work situations.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Cyberloafing may relieve employees of stress.

【定位】 Our hypothesis was that cyberloafing may serve as a mini-break, giving employees an opportunity to recover from stressful work situations.

我们的假设是：摸鱼上网或许能充当一次短暂的休息，给员工一个从高压工作处境中恢复过来的机会。

【信号】 标志词 Our hypothesis was that 引出答案。录音用 Our hypothesis was that cyberloafing may serve as a mini-break 直接点出假设，hypothesis 与题干同词，是标志词引导的答案句，听到 hypothesis was that 后面那句就是答案。

【替换】 recover from stressful work situations↔relieve employees of stress 从压力中恢复＝缓解压力，同义改写 serve as a mini-break↔ may relieve employees of stress 充当短歇＝起到减压作用，功能等值

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

录音确实念了 a sign that a worker is lazy，但前面有 may not be，是讲者要否定的旧观念，不是其团队的假设；A 取了被否定的那一极，正话反取。 借⽤原⽂： such behaviors may not be a sign that a worker is lazy C) 张冠李戴

higher levels of employee engagement and job satisfaction 是录音引用的他人研究背景，且原文是说社媒使用与二者相关，并未说 engagement 与 job satisfaction 互相关联；C 既错置主体又乱搭关系。 借⽤原⽂： Social media use at work has been linked to higher levels of employee engagement and job satisfaction D) 原词陷阱录音多处提到 productivity，但本团队的假设是摸鱼减压，而非过度用社媒会降低效率；D 取了一个原文别处的话题词拼成假设，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： cost employers up to $85 billion a year in lost productivity

【信号】 fits with other recent research 直接挂钩。录音用 This fits with other recent research that suggests taking short breaks is associated with higher levels of daily job performance，fits with other recent research 与题干 agree with other recent research 直接呼应，that 从句即两方一致之处。

items.title: 2023年6月六级第2套 · 讲座与讲话 2
items.transcript:
When Julius Morton moved to Nebraska City in 1854, he faced a problem shared by many settlers in the territory: It was a treeless plain. That meant no trees for building materials, or for fuel. But Morton was one of the world's first conservationists, stating, "For prosperity, we ought to plant as many forests as we have exhausted and consumed". So he started planting trees, beginning with his own land. By 1860 Morton possessed a forest of more than 300 trees. A few years later, he had more than 1,000.

As the forest grew, so did Morton's influence in Nebraska. This was largely because Morton founded the Nebraska City News, the state's first newspaper, in which he frequently wrote editorials about the practical and aesthetic benefits of tree planting. He also organized the Nebraska State Gardening Society and served on the Nebraska State Board of Agriculture. While serving on the Board, Morton came up with an idea to spread his belief in tree planting statewide.

On January 4, 1872, Morton drafted a resolution that April 10 be designated day for the planting of trees in the State of Nebraska and urged people to go out and plant trees themselves. Morton called the special event Arbor Day as "arbor" is Latin for "tree". The state government agreed. And on April 10, 1872, the first unofficial Arbor Day was celebrated throughout Nebraska. Prizes were awarded to counties, cities, and individuals who planted the largest number of trees. That day, an astounding one million trees were planted in Nebraska—an average of more than six for every man, woman and child in the state. Since 1885, Nebraska has planted more than 700,000 acres of trees, earning it the nickname "the Tree Planters State".

Arbor Day became a legal, civic holiday in the state in 1885. It was held on April 22—Julius Morton's birthday. In addition to a parade in Nebraska City, Morton introduced what has since become a long-standing Arbor Day tradition: School children went outside and planted trees together.

In 1970, nearly a century after Arbor Day was first celebrated, President Richard Nixon declared the last Friday of every April to be observed as National Arbor Day. All 50 states recognize the April observance, although many hold an additional state Arbor Day in a month more suited to local tree planting.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about Nebraska City in 1854 when Julius Morton moved there?

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） There were no trees.

【定位】 When Julius Morton moved to Nebraska City in 1854, he faced a problem shared by many settlers in the territory: It was a treeless plain. That meant no trees for building materials, or for fuel. 当朱利叶斯·莫顿于1854年迁居内布拉斯加城时，他面临着该地区许多移民共有的一个问题：这是一片没有树的平原。这意味着没有树木可作建筑材料，也没有树木可作燃料。

【信号】 时间词后的状况交代。录音开头复述了题干同样的时间地点 When Julius Morton moved to Nebraska City in 1854，紧跟着的 It was a treeless plain 就是对当地状况的直接交代，这种"时间地点重现+随即说明情况"是答案句的信号。

【替换】 It was a treeless plain↔There were no trees. treeless = no trees

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

录音确实念到 no trees for building materials（没有树作建筑材料），A 把它偷换成 There were no wooden buildings.（没有木建筑）。原文说的是缺"建材来源"而非"已无木建筑"，听到 building 这个原词就选会上当。 借⽤原⽂： no trees for building materials

B) 过度推断

D) 原词陷阱录音念到 a problem shared by many settlers（许多移民共有的问题），D 盗用 settlers 这个原词编出 There were few settlers.（移民很少）。原文是说移民"多"且共有难题，并未说移民少，方向正相反。 借⽤原⽂： a problem shared by many settlers

【定位】 As the forest grew, so did Morton's influence in Nebraska. This was largely because Morton founded the Nebraska City News, the state's first newspaper, in which he frequently wrote editorials about the practical and aesthetic benefits of tree planting.

【替换】 Morton founded the Nebraska City News, the state's first newspaper↔He founded a newspaper 专名概括成普通名词 he frequently wrote editorials about the practical and aesthetic benefits of tree planting↔ used it to promote his ideas 撰文宣传=推广理念

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

录音说他 served on the Nebraska State Board of Agriculture（在董事会任职），A 改成 served as chairman of the Nebraska State Board of Agriculture（任董事会主席）。原文只说"任职"未说"任主席"，且这件事并非影响力增大的原因，既偷换身份又答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： served on the Nebraska State Board of Agriculture B) 原词陷阱录音说他 organized the Nebraska State Gardening Society（组织了园艺学会），B 盗用该机构名却把动作换成 urged the state to start the Nebraska State Gardening Society（敦促州里去创办）。原文是他亲自组织、并非"敦促州政府创办"，且此事也非影响力之源，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： organized the Nebraska State Gardening Society

C) 原词陷阱

录音里 aesthetic 只是修饰社论内容（讲植树的实用与审美益处），C 把它拼成 engaged himself in a large number of aesthetic projects（投身大量审美项目）。原文根本没说他搞了一堆审美项目，属盗用原词后无中生有。 借⽤原⽂： the practical and aesthetic benefits of tree planting

items.title: 2023年6月六级第2套 · 讲座与讲话 3
items.transcript:
Modern humans arose in Africa about 200,000 years ago. They then spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago. This is the "Out of Africa" model, as it's commonly known. In the 1990s, the hypothesis found widespread acceptance. But this popular idea is in need of revision, particularly given the number of important findings across Asia over the past few decades.

For instance, many new human fossils found, particularly in China, are now dated as older than 60,000 years. This calls into question the idea that modern humans migrated out of Africa only 60,000 years ago. Take the recent discovery of two modern human teeth found in the Luna cave in China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. When my research team and I dated these teeth, we found they were more than 70,000 years old—a situation clearly impossible if modern humans moved out of Africa only 60,000 years ago.

So with such findings, what happened exactly? Where does the most current data suggest we came from?

The first question we should ask is why did modern humans leave Africa to begin with? If a population is perfectly adapted to a particular environment and has access to an abundance of resources, then there really is no reason to move or change. For instance, some monkeys in Africa have a set of teeth that has hardly changed over the course of millions of years, indicating that they found a place that has worked for them.

So what happened with humans? Some researchers have suggested that population density increased to the point where smaller human groups were forced to explore new lands. Other researchers have suggested that due to major environmental events in East Africa, humans were prompted to find greener pastures. Yet another explanation could simply be that early modern human hunters were following the large animals that they relied on, and so they moved out of Africa without realizing that they were actually moving from one continent to another.

Humans need daily access to reliable fresh water, which appears to be absent from many coastal areas. This brings us to another question: by which route did modern humans move out of Africa? No clear route across the Mediterranean from North Africa appears to be present, so the earlier dispersals out of Africa and into Europe and Asia might have been across the Arabian Peninsula.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about modern humans according to the hypothesis commonly accepted in the 1990s?

options.text: They spread across Europe and Asia in a few decades.
They lived mostly in Africa for about 200,000 years.
They preferred to live in Europe rather than in Asia.
They moved out of Africa about 60,000 years ago.

questions.shortExplanation: Modern humans arose in Africa about 200,000 years ago. They then spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago. This is the "Out of Africa" model, as it's commonly known. In the 1990s, the hypothesis found widespread acceptance.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） They moved out of Africa about 60,000 years ago.

【定位】 Modern humans arose in Africa about 200,000 years ago. They then spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago. This is the "Out of Africa" model, as it's commonly known. In the 1990s, the hypothesis found widespread acceptance.

现代人大约在二十万年前起源于非洲。随后在距今约六万年后的某个时期扩散到欧洲和亚洲。这就是众所周知的『走出非洲』模型。上世纪九十年代，这一假说获得了广泛接受。

【信号】 时间状语锁定旧假说内容。题干限定 in the 1990s 的旧假说，录音里 In the 1990s, the hypothesis found widespread acceptance. 把前文 spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago 这段表述归到了那个旧假说名下，因此前面讲迁徙时间的那几句就是答案句。

【替换】 spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago↔ They moved out of Africa about 60,000 years ago.

扩散到欧亚=走出非洲

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

选项 They spread across Europe and Asia in a few decades. 直接搬用录音原词 spread across Europe and Asia，听到就想选；但 in a few decades（几十年内）是录音根本没说的速度，讲者只说在六万年后扩散、并未说扩散只花几十年。 借⽤原⽂： spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago B) 偷换概念

选项 They lived mostly in Africa for about 200,000 years. 偷换了 arose in Africa about 200,000 years ago 里的 200,000：录音说的是『二十万年前起源于非洲』这个时间点，不是『在非洲住了二十万年』这个时长，听到 200,000 + Africa 就选会落坑。 借⽤原⽂： Modern humans arose in Africa about 200,000 years ago. C) 未提及选项 They preferred to live in Europe rather than in Asia. 借用了原词 Europe 和 Asia， 但录音只把欧洲与亚洲并列为扩散去向（Europe and Asia），从未比较二者、更没说『偏好欧洲胜过亚洲』，属凭空添加的偏好。 借⽤原⽂： spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago

questions.prompt: What has called into question the "Out of Africa" model?

options.text: The discovery of two modern human teeth in China.
The traces of human migration out of Africa to Asia.
The human fossils discovered most recently in Africa.
The Luna cave in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.

questions.shortExplanation: Take the recent discovery of two modern human teeth found in the Luna cave in China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. When my research team and I dated these teeth, we found they were more than 70,000 years old—a situation clearly impossible if modern humans moved out of Africa only 60,000 years ago.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） The discovery of two modern human teeth in China.

【定位】 Take the recent discovery of two modern human teeth found in the Luna cave in China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. When my research team and I dated these teeth, we found they were more than 70,000 years old—a situation clearly impossible if modern humans moved out of Africa only 60,000 years ago.

以最近在中国广西壮族自治区娄洞发现的两颗现代人牙齿为例。当我和我的研究团队给这些牙齿测年时，我们发现它们已有七万多年的历史——如果现代人直到六万年前才走出非洲， 这种情况显然是不可能出现的。

【信号】 Take…例子+测年结果证伪旧说。讲者用 Take the recent discovery of two modern human teeth 引出一个具体例子，并以 more than 70,000 years old 这个测年结果说明它与旧模型矛盾，正是这个『两颗牙齿』的发现 called into question 了该模型，故定位到这例子。

【替换】 the recent discovery of two modern human teeth found in the Luna cave in China↔ The discovery of two modern human teeth in China.

近乎原句的浓缩

【排除】 B) 答非所问选项 The traces of human migration out of Africa to Asia. 用的是全篇大主题词 migration out of Africa，听起来很对题；但题目问的是『具体什么动摇了模型』，动摇模型的是那个测年超七万年的牙齿发现，而非泛泛的『迁徙痕迹』，B 笼统得答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： the idea that modern humans migrated out of Africa only 60,000 years ago C) 原词陷阱

选项 The human fossils discovered most recently in Africa. 借了录音的 recent / discovery 和 fossils 等原词，但把地点改成了 in Africa；动摇模型的发现明明在中国 （Luna cave in China），不在非洲，听到 recent + discovered 就选会被骗。 借⽤原⽂： many new human fossils found, particularly in China D) 原词陷阱

选项 The Luna cave in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. 把录音里原样念出的专有地名整段照搬，最易『听到原词就想选』；但动摇模型的是『在该洞发现的牙齿超七万年』 这一发现，洞穴本身只是地点，并非动摇模型的证据，D 偷换了概念。 借⽤原⽂： found in the Luna cave in China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region
