questions.prompt: What does the speaker want to show with the example of some monkeys in Africa?

options.text: There must have been some reason for human migration.
There have been changes in animals' living conditions.
Humans adapted themselves to the environment there.
Humans had access to abundant food sources there.

questions.shortExplanation: The first question we should ask is why did modern humans leave Africa to begin with? If a population is perfectly adapted to a particular environment and has access to an abundance of resources, then there really is no reason to move or change. For instance, some monkeys in Africa have a set of teeth that has hardly changed over the course of millions of years, indicating that they found a place that has worked for them. 我们首先该问的是：现代人当初究竟为什么要离开非洲？如果一个种群完美适应了某个特定环境、又能获得充足的资源，那就真的没有理由迁移或改变了。比如，非洲的一些猴子，其牙齿在数百万年里几乎没有变化，这表明它们找到了一处适合自己的栖身之地。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） There must have been some reason for human migration.

【定位】 The first question we should ask is why did modern humans leave Africa to begin with? If a population is perfectly adapted to a particular environment and has access to an abundance of resources, then there really is no reason to move or change. For instance, some monkeys in Africa have a set of teeth that has hardly changed over the course of millions of years, indicating that they found a place that has worked for them. 我们首先该问的是：现代人当初究竟为什么要离开非洲？如果一个种群完美适应了某个特定环境、又能获得充足的资源，那就真的没有理由迁移或改变了。比如，非洲的一些猴子，其牙齿在数百万年里几乎没有变化，这表明它们找到了一处适合自己的栖身之地。

【信号】 例子前的论点句+indicating回扣。猴子例子由 For instance 引出，它服务的论点写在前一句 then there really is no reason to move or change，又被例子末尾 indicating that they found a place that has worked for them 回扣——合起来说明：环境好就没理由迁，反过来人类迁徙必有原因，故答案句锁定这组论点而非猴子牙齿细节。

【替换】 there really is no reason to move or change↔ There must have been some reason for human migration.

正话反说的等值推论

【排除】 B) 与原文相反

选项 There have been changes in animals' living conditions. 蹭了 animals（猴子是动物）这一关联，但录音说猴子牙齿 hardly changed、环境一直 worked for them，恰恰是 『没变化』，B 把『没变』说成『有变』，与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： some monkeys in Africa have a set of teeth that has hardly changed C) 原词陷阱

选项 Humans adapted themselves to the environment there. 借了原文 adapted、 environment 等原词，但 perfectly adapted 在录音里说的是『假设种群（以猴子为例） 适应了就不会迁』，是用来反衬人类要迁的前提，并非讲者想证明『人类适应了那里』，C 张冠李戴又答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： If a population is perfectly adapted to a particular environment

D) 原词陷阱

选项 Humans had access to abundant food sources there. 盗用原文 access to an abundance of resources 的近义词，但原文说的是『若有充足资源就没理由迁』这一假设前提，讲者举猴子恰是要说明人类迁了说明并非如此，D 把反衬前提错当成结论，且把 resources 窄化成 food sources。 借⽤原⽂： has access to an abundance of resources, then there really is no reason to move

questions.prompt: What question does the speaker raise close to the end of the talk?

options.text: How humans settled down on the Arabian Peninsula.
When modern humans started to disperse out of Africa.
What path modern humans took to migrate out of Africa.
Why fresh water is so important for human survival.

questions.shortExplanation: This brings us to another question: by which route did modern humans move out of Africa?
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） What path modern humans took to migrate out of Africa.

【定位】 This brings us to another question: by which route did modern humans move out of Africa?

这就把我们引向另一个问题：现代人究竟是沿哪条路线走出非洲的？

【信号】 another question引出的自问句。结尾段用 This brings us to another question 明确抛出讲者临近结尾的那个问题，冒号后的 by which route did modern humans move out of Africa 就是该问题本体，by which route 即问『路线』，故答案锁定此句。

【替换】 by which route did modern humans move out of Africa↔ What path modern humans took to migrate out of Africa. by which route=what path

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

选项 How humans settled down on the Arabian Peninsula. 借了结尾出现的地名 Arabian Peninsula，听到就想选；但讲者只是把阿拉伯半岛作为可能路线的推测，并没有把『如何在阿拉伯半岛定居』当作他提出的那个问题，A 答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： the earlier dispersals out of Africa and into Europe and Asia might have been across the Arabian Peninsula B) 偷换概念

选项 When modern humans started to disperse out of Africa. 用了 disperse out of Africa 等原词，问的是『何时』；但『何时走出非洲』是前文（第二段牙齿测年）已讨论的旧问题，结尾真正抛出的是 by which route（哪条路线），B 把疑问词从 route 偷换成 when。 借⽤原⽂： by which route did modern humans move out of Africa D) 原词陷阱

选项 Why fresh water is so important for human survival. 盗用结尾出现的 fresh water 原词；但讲者提 Humans need daily access to reliable fresh water 只是引出路线问题的铺垫，并未把『为何淡水重要』作为他提出的问题，D 把铺垫句错当成所提问题。 借⽤原⽂： Humans need daily access to reliable fresh water

items.title: 2024年12月六级第1套 · 长对话 1
items.transcript:
M: OK then, this here is your yearly performance review. You've been with the company for 3 years and under my direct supervision for the past 12 months. Your report is mostly good. But there are a couple of issues we must discuss. The report is yours to take with you. We'll go through the main points together now. And you can come through it in greater detail later. Do you have any questions before we start?

W: No, sir.

M: I'll get straight to it then. It is evident that you are a hard worker. You are punctual and industrious. Furthermore, you have strong analytical skills and attention to detail. The company, myself included, is happy with your productivity and overall performance.

W: Thank you. I appreciate the recognition.

M: Do you agree, then, with this depiction so far?

W: Yeah, it's a little simplistic perhaps. But that's to be expected from this kind of evaluation.

M: Sure. Would you want to add anything? Your comments can be added to the report if you wish.

W: Oh, there's no need. It's a flattering portrayal really. Thank you, though.

M: OK. This leads me to the not-so-good part. This mostly centers around one behavioral aspect— your ability to work with others.

W: I see.

M: Yes. As you already know, over the last several months, there have been some complaints raised about your communication style.

W: Of course, we already had like three meetings about this. Look, all I'm going to say is that it was never my intention to offend anyone. Simply put, I don't like to write long emails, because, frankly, I think they're a waste of time. Conciseness is efficiency. I feel that writing long emails hurts that same productivity you praised me for just a minute ago. And I already apologized if anyone was offended. But to be perfectly honest, I think anyone who was offended was being a little too sensitive.

questions.prompt: What are the speakers most probably doing?

options.text: Preparing for a job interview.
Writing a work report together.
Going through a couple of issues the company faces.
Discussing the woman's annual performance review.

questions.shortExplanation: OK then, this here is your yearly performance review. You've been with the company for 3 years and under my direct supervision for the past 12 months.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （主旨题） Discussing the woman's annual performance review.

【定位】 OK then, this here is your yearly performance review. You've been with the company for 3 years and under my direct supervision for the past 12 months.

那好，这是你的年度绩效评估。你在公司已经三年，过去十二个月在我的直接管理之下。

【信号】 开头场景定调句。对话第一句 this here is your yearly performance review 就开门见山点出场合，是典型的“开头定调”信号：主旨情境题的答案往往就埋在第一句对场合的交代里。

【替换】 this here is your yearly performance review↔ Discussing the woman's annual performance review yearly等于annual

【排除】 A) 未提及

录音是上司给在职三年的下属做评估，全程没有应聘、招人的内容，Preparing for a job interview. 凭“职场”联想硬套，属未提及。

B) 原词陷阱

录音里 report 是指已经写好的评估报告(Your report is mostly good)，男方说 the report is yours to take，并非两人“一起写报告”。Writing a work report together. 盗用了原词 report 却把“一起过报告”偷换成“一起写报告”。 借⽤原⽂： Your report is mostly good C) 原词陷阱

男方确实说了 there are a couple of issues we must discuss，但那只是这次绩效面谈的一部分(后半段才谈问题)，并非两人整体“只在过几个公司问题”。Going through a couple of issues the company faces. 盗用 a couple of issues 把局部当成了全局，且 issues 是关于“她”的，不是“公司面临的问题”。 借⽤原⽂： there are a couple of issues we must discuss

questions.prompt: What does the woman say she appreciates?

options.text: The overall culture of the company.
The instruction from her supervisor.
The honesty of the manager.
The recognition of her merits.

questions.shortExplanation: Thank you. I appreciate the recognition. 谢谢，我很感激这份认可。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） The recognition of her merits.

【定位】 Thank you. I appreciate the recognition. 谢谢，我很感激这份认可。

【信号】 被问者的直接应答。男方刚夸完她勤奋、有分析力、令公司满意，女方紧接着应答 I appreciate the recognition，这句“道谢 + appreciate”正是与题干 appreciate 直接对应的应答句，信号极明确。

【替换】 I appreciate the recognition↔The recognition of her merits.

认可即对优点的认可

【排除】 A) 未提及

The overall culture of the company. 录音从未谈“公司文化”，只是借 company 一词(男方多次提 the company)制造“职场”联想，属未提及。 B) 原词陷阱

The instruction from her supervisor. 借男方自称 supervisor(under my direct supervision)制造干扰，但女方感激的是“认可”而非“上级的指示”，盗用 supervision 一词答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： under my direct supervision

C) 偷换概念

The honesty of the manager. 中“经理诚实”录音并未作为她感激的内容提及；女方后文虽说 to be perfectly honest，但那是她自述坦率，与“感激经理诚实”无关，属偷换概念。 借⽤原⽂： to be perfectly honest

questions.prompt: What has given rise to some complaints about the woman?

options.text: Her inadequate language proficiency.
Her inability to interact with colleagues properly.
Her inappropriate behavior at company meetings.
Her simplistic approach to dealing with others.

questions.shortExplanation: This leads me to the not-so-good part. This mostly centers around one behavioral aspect— your ability to work with others. 这就引到不太好的部分了。它主要集中在一个行为方面——你与他人合作的能力。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Her inability to interact with colleagues properly.

【定位】 This leads me to the not-so-good part. This mostly centers around one behavioral aspect— your ability to work with others. 这就引到不太好的部分了。它主要集中在一个行为方面——你与他人合作的能力。

【信号】 转折后才是落点。男方用 the not-so-good part 把话题从表扬转向批评，这是明确的转向信号；转折之后点出的 your ability to work with others 才是抱怨的真正所指，前半的表扬都是铺垫。

【替换】 your ability to work with others↔Her inability to interact with colleagues properly. 合作能力即与同事互动

【排除】 A) 偷换概念 Her inadequate language proficiency. 录音从未说她“语言能力不足”；抱怨针对的是 communication style(沟通方式)，与“语言水平”是两回事，属偷换概念。 借⽤原⽂： complaints raised about your communication style C) 原词陷阱

Her inappropriate behavior at company meetings. 盗用了 meetings(女方说 we already had like three meetings about this)，但 meetings 是“就此事开过的三次会”，不是“她开会时行为不当”。抱怨的内容是沟通方式，与开会表现无关。 借⽤原⽂： we already had like three meetings about this D) 张冠李戴

Her simplistic approach to dealing with others. 借第6段女方自评报告 it's a little simplistic perhaps 里的 simplistic 一词制造干扰，但那句是她评价“这份评估”有点简单， 与“她待人方式简单”无关，张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： it's a little simplistic perhaps

questions.prompt: Why doesn't the woman like to write long emails?

options.text: To avoid offending the recipients.
To show her unique writing style.
To save time.
To be frank.

questions.shortExplanation: I don't like to write long emails, because, frankly, I think they're a waste of time. Conciseness is efficiency. 我不喜欢写长邮件，因为说实话，我觉得那是浪费时间。简洁就是效率。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） To save time.

【定位】 I don't like to write long emails, because, frankly, I think they're a waste of time. Conciseness is efficiency. 我不喜欢写长邮件，因为说实话，我觉得那是浪费时间。简洁就是效率。

【信号】 因果because直给原因。她说 I don't like to write long emails, because… I think they're a waste of time，because 之后就是她亲口给出的理由——“浪费时间”，因果信号直白， 是最干净的答案句。

【替换】 I think they're a waste of time↔To save time.

不浪费时间即省时间

【排除】 A) 答非所问

To avoid offending the recipients. 盗用她说的 it was never my intention to offend anyone，但“无意冒犯”是她对抱怨的辩解，不是她“不写长邮件”的原因。她不写长邮件的理由明确是“浪费时间”，A 答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： it was never my intention to offend anyone B) 未提及

To show her unique writing style. 录音从未说她不写长邮件是为“展示独特文风”，纯属凭 “写邮件”话题臆造，属未提及。

D) 原词陷阱

To be frank. 盗用她话里的 frankly(frankly, I think they're a waste of time) 与 to be perfectly honest，但 frankly 只是她说话的口吻插入语，不是“不写长邮件”的目的。真正原因在 frankly 之后的 a waste of time，D 把语气词错当成了动机。 借⽤原⽂： frankly, I think they're a waste of time

items.title: 2024年12月六级第1套 · 长对话 2
items.transcript:
M: So tell me, why do you wish to study medicine?

W: I've always wanted to be a doctor. I come from a small town where healthcare was never the best. And I think that had a profound effect on me. As a child, I remember thinking how great it would be to serve the community and cure people!

M: What other people or events in your life have shaped your interest in becoming a doctor?

W: Well, that's hard to say. I would certainly say my parents have been a key factor. They always pushed me to study hard. And I certainly wouldn't be here without their support. I guess I was also immensely fortunate to have good teachers and friends around me. At the end of the day, I've always been surrounded by a positive environment conducive to my working hard and pursuing my dreams.

M: Is there any medical branch that you would like to specialize in?

W: I haven't decided yet. It's still early days. However, if I had to say, internal medicine.

M: Why internal medicine?

W: I know it's no picnic. But I find it the most intriguing, because it covers so much and ties together so many other specialties.

M: Thank you. Now I'd like to address your academic history and projected grades. We like to think of ourselves as a prestigious institution with a highly competitive and promising student body. As you know, to get into our programmes, you need at least 85% score in the entrance exam. Do you think you can attain this?

W: I think so. Yes.

M: I'm looking at your school grades now and I'll be honest. It's a bit of a mixed bag. You do get top grades here and there, but you are not very… Shall we say "consistent"? I see no problem in making you a conditional offer, but consider yourself warned, our entrance exam is, to use your own words, no picnic.

questions.prompt: What does the woman say she has always wanted to do since childhood?

options.text: Provide medical service to the community.
Make healthcare in her hometown the best.
Obtain a doctoral degree in internal medicine.
Have a profound impact on people around her.

questions.shortExplanation: As a child, I remember thinking how great it would be to serve the community and cure people! 小时候，我就记得自己在想：能服务社区、治病救人该有多好啊！
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Provide medical service to the community.

【定位】 As a child, I remember thinking how great it would be to serve the community and cure people! 小时候，我就记得自己在想：能服务社区、治病救人该有多好啊！

【信号】 As a child 提示童年愿望。信号是时间状语 As a child——它直接对应题干的 since childhood，把"从小的愿望"标了出来；紧跟其后的 to serve the community and cure people 就是她从小想做的事。

【替换】 serve the community ↔ Provide medical service to the community

serve=provide service cure people↔ medical service

cure people 概括为 medical service

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

B 用了录音里 I come from a small town where healthcare was never the best 中的 healthcare 与"家乡"概念，但录音说的是"家乡医疗从来不算好"，她的愿望是去服务，并没有说要"把家乡医疗变成最好"。这是把原词拼成一个原文没说的目标。 借⽤原⽂： I come from a small town where healthcare was never the best C) 未提及

C 说"拿内科博士学位"，但录音里她只说想当医生、想专攻内科，从没提过"博士学位"。这是把后文的 internal medicine 嫁接到一个没出现过的"读博"目标上。

D) 与原文相反

D"对身边人产生深远影响"借了录音 that had a profound effect on me 的 profound effect，但原文是"家乡医疗状况对她产生了深远影响"——是别的事影响"她"，不是她要去影响别人。方向被调了个个儿。 借⽤原⽂： that had a profound effect on me
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the woman's parents from the conversation?

options.text: They have constantly urged her to study hard.
They have worked hard to finance her education.
They have tried to create a positive learning environment.
They have pursued the family's dreams together with her.

questions.shortExplanation: I would certainly say my parents have been a key factor. They always pushed me to study hard.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） They have constantly urged her to study hard.

【定位】 I would certainly say my parents have been a key factor. They always pushed me to study hard.

我肯定会说，我父母是关键因素。他们总是督促我努力学习。

【信号】 被问者应答里的 my parents。信号是被问者直接点名 my parents have been a key factor——对话题答案落在回答方，她一提到 parents，下一句 They always pushed me to study hard 就是关于父母的核心信息。

【替换】 always pushed me to study hard↔ constantly urged her to study hard pushed=urged，always=constantly

【排除】 B) 偷换概念

B"努力挣钱供她读书"利用了录音 I certainly wouldn't be here without their support 里的 support，但 support 只是泛指"支持"，录音从未说是"经济上出钱（finance）"。这是把一个泛词坐实成具体的金钱资助。 借⽤原⽂： I certainly wouldn't be here without their support C) 张冠李戴

C"营造积极学习环境"盗用了录音 a positive environment conducive to my working hard，但说这环境的是"老师、朋友等她周围的人"带来的，原文并没把"营造环境"安在父母头上。这是张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： surrounded by a positive environment conducive to my working hard D) 未提及 D 说父母"和她一起追求家庭梦想"，录音只说追梦是"她自己的"（pursuing my dreams），并无父母与她"共同追梦"之说。属凭空添加。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: Why does the woman say she wants to choose internal medicine as her specialty?

options.text: It is a key medical branch conducive to realizing her dreams.
It connects many other specialties with its broad coverage.
It has a long history in the man's prestigious institution.
It is a medical branch both of her parents specialize in.

questions.shortExplanation: But I find it the most intriguing, because it covers so much and ties together so many other specialties. 但我觉得它最有意思，因为它覆盖面很广，又把许多其他专科串联在一起。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） It connects many other specialties with its broad coverage.

【定位】 But I find it the most intriguing, because it covers so much and ties together so many other specialties. 但我觉得它最有意思，因为它覆盖面很广，又把许多其他专科串联在一起。

【信号】 because 领出真正理由。信号是因果连词 because——它后面 it covers so much and ties together so many other specialties 才是她选内科的真正原因；before because 的 most intriguing 只是感受，理由在 because 之后。

【替换】 it covers so much ↔ its broad coverage covers so much=broad coverage ties together so many other specialties↔connects many other specialties ties together=connects

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

A"有助于实现她的梦想"里的 dreams 确在录音别处出现过（pursuing my dreams），但她解释"为何选内科"时给的理由是"覆盖广、连专科"，从未说内科"有助于实现梦想"。这是把别处的词搬来当本题理由。 借⽤原⽂： pursuing my dreams C) 原词陷阱

C 说内科"在这所名校历史悠久"，录音里 prestigious institution（名校）确出现过，但谈的是"学校的声望与竞争"，根本没说内科"历史悠久"。把名校话题硬接到"内科有历史"上。 借⽤原⽂： prestigious institution D) 未提及

D"父母都专攻这一科"，录音里父母只"督促她学习"，从没说过父母是医生、更没说专攻内科。这是把 parents 与 internal medicine 两个真词强行拼成一个假关系。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: How does the man describe the woman's school grades?

options.text: Problematic.
Competitive.
Inconsistent.
Trustworthy.

questions.shortExplanation: You do get top grades here and there, but you are not very… Shall we say "consistent"?
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （态度观点题） Inconsistent.

【定位】 You do get top grades here and there, but you are not very… Shall we say "consistent"?

你确实这儿那儿拿过一些顶尖成绩，但你不太……怎么说呢，"稳定"？

【信号】 转折 but 后才是真评价。信号是转折词 but——but 之前的 You do get top grades 是先扬，but 之后 you are not very… consistent 才是男方真正的评价：成绩不够稳定。态度题的落点在转折后。

【替换】 you are not very… Shall we say "consistent"?↔Inconsistent

not consistent=inconsistent a bit of a mixed bag↔Inconsistent

mixed bag=时好时坏=inconsistent

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

items.title: 2024年12月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 1
items.transcript:
Logging into your email account can sometimes feel like trying to hack into the Pentagon. If you follow all of the guidelines, you need to use a different password for every one of your accounts; use an incomprehensible variety of letters, numbers, and symbols; sign up for two-step verification; and change every password every time one of them is compromised. More often than not, you then have to choose photos that include a street sign, as this apparently provides solid evidence to your computer that you are, in fact, a human being.

It's no small wonder most of us forget our passwords more often than our keys. Now a new peer-reviewed study by researchers at Aalto University in Finland is attempting to figure out why we forget our passwords in order to help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon. Their findings suggest that how likely you are to remember your password has less to do with the password itself and more to do with how often you anticipate using it. Which is to say: you are far more likely to remember a complicated password if you know you'll frequently be using it to log into an account than you are to remember a simple password for an account that you don't expect to log into very often. The researchers advise websites to include more of an incentive for users to log in more often in order to help them remember their secret codes.

questions.prompt: Why do we often have to choose photos that include a street sign to log into our email accounts?

options.text: To prevent hackers from cracking our secret codes.
To show that all the guidelines are being followed.
To provide evidence that passwords are forgotten.
To convince our computer that we are human.

questions.shortExplanation: More often than not, you then have to choose photos that include a street sign, as this apparently provides solid evidence to your computer that you are, in fact, a human being. 你往往还得去选那些含有街道标志的照片，因为这显然能向你的电脑提供确凿的证据，证明你其实是一个人类。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） To convince our computer that we are human.

【定位】 More often than not, you then have to choose photos that include a street sign, as this apparently provides solid evidence to your computer that you are, in fact, a human being. 你往往还得去选那些含有街道标志的照片，因为这显然能向你的电脑提供确凿的证据，证明你其实是一个人类。

【信号】 原因信号 as 引出真意。答案就在 as this apparently provides solid evidence to your computer that you are, in fact, a human being 里的 as 之后——as 在这里是『因为』， 专门交代前面『选含街道标志照片』这个动作的目的，是典型的原因信号。

【替换】 provides solid evidence to your computer that you are, in fact, a human being↔ To convince our computer that we are human

提供证据=使信服，同义改写

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

选项里的 hackers 让人联想原文开头 hack into the Pentagon，但那只是开篇打比方说登录难，与『选街道标志照片是为了什么』无关，属听到 hack 就想选的原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： trying to hack into the Pentagon B) 原词陷阱

all the guidelines are being followed 借用原文 If you follow all of the guidelines，但原文那句是在罗列守规则有多麻烦，并非解释选照片的目的，词对了、对应错了。 借⽤原⽂： If you follow all of the guidelines

C) 未提及 passwords are forgotten 把后文『人会忘密码』这个话题硬塞进本题，但选照片是为了证明你是人，跟『提供忘记密码的证据』毫无关系，原文也没这么说。

questions.prompt: What do researchers at a university in Finland aim to do in their new study?

options.text: Put an end to the hacking phenomenon.
Help people remember their passwords.
Reduce the intricacy of the password itself.
Explain the need for different email accounts.

questions.shortExplanation: Now a new peer-reviewed study by researchers at Aalto University in Finland is attempting to figure out why we forget our passwords in order to help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （目的题） Help people remember their passwords.

【定位】 Now a new peer-reviewed study by researchers at Aalto University in Finland is attempting to figure out why we forget our passwords in order to help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon.

如今，芬兰阿尔托大学研究者开展的一项新的同行评审研究，正试图弄清我们为什么会忘记密码，以期帮助终结这一令人沮丧的现象。

【信号】 目的信号 in order to help。研究者的真正目标由 in order to help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon 中的 in order to 引出——in order to 是直白的目的信号，它后面才是研究的最终意图。

【替换】 help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon↔Help people remember their passwords 代词 this 指回忘密码，概括等值

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

Put an end to the hacking phenomenon 直接搬原文 put an end to this frustrating phenomenon 的 put an end to，却把对象偷换成 hacking（黑客）；原文要终结的是 『忘密码』这一令人沮丧的现象，不是黑客现象。 借⽤原⽂： in order to help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon C) 原词陷阱

Reduce the intricacy of the password itself 借了原文反复出现的 the password itself， 但研究的发现是『记不记得住与密码本身关系不大』，从未说要降低密码复杂度，是把原词拼成原文没有的目标。 借⽤原⽂： less to do with the password itself D) 原词陷阱 Explain the need for different email accounts 让人想到原文 a different password for every one of your accounts，但那是开篇讲守规则的麻烦，与芬兰研究的目标无关， accounts 这个词被挪用来骗选。 借⽤原⽂： a different password for every one of your accounts

研究者建议网站多设置一些激励，促使用户更频繁地登录，以帮助他们记住自己的密码。

【信号】 建议信号 advise 直接给出对策。答案由 The researchers advise websites to include more of an incentive for users to log in more often 里的 advise 直接引出——advise 是建议信号，它后面 websites to... 的内容就是研究者给出的对策。

【替换】 include more of an incentive for users to log in more often↔ Take steps to encourage users to log in more often

设激励=采取措施鼓励，同义改写

【排除】 A) 过度推断

Innovate technologies to ensure the safety of users' accounts 蹭全篇的安全 / accounts 话题，但研究者的建议是加登录激励，从未让网站去『创新技术保障账户安全』，是凭话题耳熟编出的拔高项。 B) 原词陷阱

Explore the possibility of using simpler secret codes 借了原文结尾的 secret codes，但原文那句是说激励的目的（帮人记住密码），研究者并没建议用更简单的密码，词对、意思不对。 借⽤原⽂： help them remember their secret codes

items.title: 2024年12月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 2
items.transcript: Four years ago, Jenny Weiner was in a fitness slump. She wanted to improve her physical and mental health. However, her workouts lacked intensity without a proper training programme to follow. When she went to the gym, her daily ritual predominantly involved easy exercise options like jogging; she avoided more formidable exercises like lifting weights. A personal trainer who might push her was out of the question. The extravagant cost was just unaffordable. She then discovered the fitness phone app Slimmeretics. To use the app, you first input your profile about your previous training experiences and preferences, as well as your desired goals. A virtual coach then uses that information to suggest a personalised training regime. After the workout, the app's artificial intelligence software system gives feedback from Ms. Weiner and its other 53 million users around the world to adjust future training sessions. Now Ms. Weiner finds the workouts exciting. This is because no two are ever the same. As a result, the app has helped her to lose more than 25 kilograms. The app's mathematical approach can arrange a more meticulous workout schedule. This has led to optimal results. However, some experts think that apps cannot replace human personal trainers. An app cannot understand human behavior. It will not comprehend that there are competing interests outside of health and fitness. Additionally, a human trainer can add compassion to the workout. He can also make exercise fun and sustainable. Trainers can monitor whether a person is doing exercises correctly. This can safeguard against injuries. An app cannot perceive such subtleties.

items.title: 2024年12月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 1
items.transcript:
All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules, which include deferring to superiors and respecting the property of others, Oxford University has concluded. Although many cultures are moving towards more liberal, less hierarchical organizations, the new research suggests that traditional power structures and basic values of charity and brotherhood are the cornerstones of successful societies.

The huge study of 60 different cultures around the world found that all communities operate under seven basic moral codes. Those universal rules are: help your family, help your group, return favors, be brave, defer to superiors, divide resources fairly, and respect the property of others. The character traits held for every kind of community, be they traditional hunter gatherers or advanced civilizations, helping to uphold civilized society and foster social cooperation, researchers found. "Everyone everywhere shares a common moral code," said Dr. Oliver Scott Curry, lead author and senior researcher at Oxford. "These seven moral rules appear to be universal across cultures, because people face the same social problems. Even if some of these traits look right-wing or conservative, for example, deferring to authority, left-wing people will still have a group loyalty and deference to someone or something. This shows there really is more that unites us than divides us."

The study published in Current Anthropology is the largest and most comprehensive and widespread survey of morals ever conducted and aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality. The team accessed the world's best archives to analyze accounts from more than 600 sources of 60 societies around the world. They found that the seven rules were considered morally good in all societies and were observed across all continents, religions and politics. However, some communities valued certain rules more highly than others. Dr. Curry hopes that this research helps to promote mutual understanding between people of different cultures and appreciation of what we have in common and how and why we differ. Co-author professor Harvey Whitehouse said social scientists should now set about testing the theory in the field, rather than relying on old data. "This study was based on historical descriptions of cultures around the world," he said. "These descriptions were made independent of and prior to the theory we're testing. In future, if social scientists are serious about testing theories of morality, they will need to gather new data, more systematically, out in the field."

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the conclusion of the Oxford University researchers?

options.text: All societies are built upon the cornerstones of basic values.
Everyone everywhere demonstrates seven character traits.
All societies are kept together by seven basic moral rules.
Everyone everywhere shares a universal moral standard.

questions.shortExplanation: All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules, which include deferring to superiors and respecting the property of others, Oxford University has concluded.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） All societies are kept together by seven basic moral rules.

【定位】 All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules, which include deferring to superiors and respecting the property of others, Oxford University has concluded.

牛津大学得出结论：所有社会都靠七条普世道德规则维系在一起，其中包括服从尊长、尊重他人财物。

【信号】 结论标志词 concluded。句末的 Oxford University has concluded 是明确的结论信号， 加之这句出现在篇章开头点题处，正是篇章独白把核心论点摆在开头的典型位置，听到 concluded 就该锁定这句是答案句。

【替换】 All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules↔ All societies are kept together by seven basic moral rules

held together 同义改写为 kept together

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

All societies are built upon the cornerstones of basic values. 把第一段后文的 basic values of charity and brotherhood are the cornerstones of successful societies 的原词 cornerstones、basic values 搬了过来，但那句讲的是成功社会的基石，并非研究的总结论本身，听到熟词就选会落进这个陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： basic values of charity and brotherhood are the cornerstones of successful societies B) 偷换概念

Everyone everywhere demonstrates seven character traits. 借了原文出现过的 seven 和第二段的 The character traits held for every kind of community，但研究的结论说的是七条道德规则（rules），而非七种性格特质，把 rules 偷换成 character traits 就跑偏了。 借⽤原⽂： The character traits held for every kind of community D) 偷换概念 Everyone everywhere shares a universal moral standard. 用了第二段 Everyone everywhere shares a common moral code 的熟悉句式，但原文说的是共享一套七条规则的道德准则（code），D 把它笼统说成 a universal moral standard，丢掉了结论里七条规则这一核心，不如 C 精确对应题干问的结论。 借⽤原⽂： Everyone everywhere shares a common moral code
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What did the new study by Oxford researchers aim to do?

options.text: Ascertain whether deferring to authority was confined to right-wing people.
Find out whether different societies had different versions of morality.
Make clear whether all societies faced the same moral issues.
Find out whether left-wing people still had a group loyalty.

questions.shortExplanation: The study published in Current Anthropology is the largest and most comprehensive and widespread survey of morals ever conducted and aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （目的题） Find out whether different societies had different versions of morality.

【定位】 The study published in Current Anthropology is the largest and most comprehensive and widespread survey of morals ever conducted and aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality.

这项发表于《当代人类学》的研究是有史以来规模最大、最全面、覆盖最广的道德调查，旨在弄清不同社会是否有不同版本的道德观。

【信号】 意图标志 aimed to find out。句中的 aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality 用 aimed to 直陈研究目的，这是目的题最直接的信号，听到 aimed to 即可锁定。

【替换】 aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality↔ Find out whether different societies had different versions of morality

近乎原句，仅去掉 aimed to

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Ascertain whether deferring to authority was confined to right-wing people. 把第二段 Dr. Curry 那句里的 deferring to authority 和 right-wing 原词搬来，但那是他举例说明规则的普世性，并非这项研究本身要弄清的目标，听到熟词就选会被带偏。 借⽤原⽂： deferring to authority C) 偷换概念

Make clear whether all societies faced the same moral issues. 听上去和研究目的沾边，但原文目的是查不同社会是否有不同版本的道德，C 反向说成所有社会是否面对相同道德问题，方向被改了。 借⽤原⽂： whether different societies had different versions of morality D) 原词陷阱

Find out whether left-wing people still had a group loyalty. 借了第二段 left-wing people will still have a group loyalty 的原话，但那是 Dr. Curry 论证规则普世性的例子， 不是研究要查明的目标，属典型的盗用原句却答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： left-wing people will still have a group loyalty
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does Harvey Whitehouse think social scientists should do to theories of morality?

options.text: Make independent descriptions of cultures around the world.
Strive to understand the basic differences between peoples.
Appreciate the foundational value of the existing data.
Carry out systematic field studies to gather new data.

questions.shortExplanation: In future, if social scientists are serious about testing theories of morality, they will need to gather new data, more systematically, out in the field. 今后，社会科学家若真要检验道德理论，就需要更系统地到实地去采集新数据。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （目的题） Carry out systematic field studies to gather new data.

【定位】 In future, if social scientists are serious about testing theories of morality, they will need to gather new data, more systematically, out in the field. 今后，社会科学家若真要检验道德理论，就需要更系统地到实地去采集新数据。

【信号】 建议信号 will need to + 转折 rather than。Whitehouse 先说 should now set about testing the theory in the field, rather than relying on old data，再用 they will need to gather new data, more systematically, out in the field 点明做法；need to 是建议信号，rather than relying on old data 则用对比把落点推向新数据。

【替换】 gather new data, more systematically, out in the field ↔ Carry out systematic field studies to gather new data.

systematically 名词化、out in the field 转为 field studies

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Make independent descriptions of cultures around the world. 搬了原文 These descriptions were made independent of and prior to the theory we're testing 的原词 independent、descriptions，但那是在说本研究所依据的旧资料的来历，不是 Whitehouse 主张今后该做的事，时间方向相反。 借⽤原⽂： These descriptions were made independent of and prior to the theory we're testing

B) 张冠李戴

Strive to understand the basic differences between peoples. 借了第三段 Dr. Curry 那句 appreciation of what we have in common and how and why we differ 的差异话题，但那是 Curry 的期望，且题干问的是 Whitehouse 的主张，张冠李戴又跑了题。 借⽤原⽂： appreciation of what we have in common and how and why we differ C) 与原文相反

Appreciate the foundational value of the existing data. 里的 existing data 恰是 Whitehouse 用 rather than relying on old data 明确否定的对象，他主张采集新数据，C 取了被否定的旧数据一侧，方向反了。 借⽤原⽂： rather than relying on old data

items.title: 2024年12月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 2
items.transcript:
When it comes to food, color is money. Food companies know that better color gives better prices, so they ensure that their products are attractive in color to bolster earnings. Oranges, for example, have to meet specific color standards. And oranges are just the beginning. There are color standards for foods including French fries, tomatoes, pumpkins, olives, honey and cherries.

The attention to color is for good reason. For all the talk of the tongue, our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience. A great number of our brain functions are dedicated to processing vision, while only a percent or two is given over to taste faculties, and the result is that color actually changes how we taste food.

Scientists have demonstrated many times the importance of color to taste. In a 1980s study, for example, test participants were asked to name the flavor of the beverage they were drinking without being able to see that beverage. Only one in five was able to identify it as orange. But when they were allowed to see what they were drinking which was orange in color, each of them identified the orange flavor. And when a drink that was lime flavor was colored orange, nearly half of respondents identified the flavor of the beverage as orange. None made that mistake when the beverage was green in color. What's happening when someone fails to identify the flavor of a beverage they can't see or that has an abnormal color? Is it that participants can't discern what the flavor is, and so rely on visual cues? Or does color actually change the experience of taste? The key to these questions is the effect of color on expectation. The brain makes predictions using color. These predictions rely on expectations that come from experience. Research shows that we're all born liking sweet things and desire to eat them, but we aren't born knowing what the sweet things we crave look like. So we need to learn this over time. The brain gets information from the environment. And we learn, for example, that fruits go from green and sour to red and ripe and sweet. Thus, if we see a green berry, we equate its color with a sour taste, and just looking at a red fruit will activate our expectations that it will taste sweet and delicious.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about our eyes?

options.text: They might be the most important part of our eating experience.
They can activate our brain functions in a most direct fashion.
They can be viewed as the windows to our soul.
They could mislead us in more ways than one.

questions.shortExplanation: For all the talk of the tongue, our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience. 尽管人们老在谈论舌头（的味觉），我们的眼睛或许才真正是吃这件事里最重要的部分。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） They might be the most important part of our eating experience.

【定位】 For all the talk of the tongue, our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience. 尽管人们老在谈论舌头（的味觉），我们的眼睛或许才真正是吃这件事里最重要的部分。

【信号】 让步 For all… + 强调 really might。信号是句首让步结构 For all the talk of the tongue （"尽管都在说舌头"）后面才抛出真正主张，再加 our eyes really might be the most important part 里的 "really" 加重语气——让步之后、被强调的那句才是说话人的落点， 正是答案句。

【替换】 our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience↔ They might be the most important part of our eating experience.

近乎原句、They 替 our eyes

【排除】 B) 偷换概念

B 盗用了第 2 段原词 brain functions。原文说 A great number of our brain functions are dedicated to processing vision——是 "很多脑功能用于处理视觉"，主语是脑功能、 用来佐证 eyes 重要；B 把它倒过来说成 "眼睛激活脑功能"，还加了原文没有的 "in a most direct fashion"，是偷换概念，且没回答 "说话人对 eyes 的核心论断"。 借⽤原⽂： A great number of our brain functions are dedicated to processing vision C) 未提及

C 借用了关于眼睛的常见俗语 "心灵的窗户"，听着像常识、最易顺口选中，但整篇录音只把眼睛和 "eating experience（吃的体验）" 挂钩，从未说眼睛是 "心灵的窗户"，属原文未提及，凭常识选它就中招。 D) 与原文相反

D 说眼睛会 mislead us（误导我们），是贬义。但答案句对眼睛是高度肯定——our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience，说话人在抬高眼睛而非贬低。D 的态度与原文相反，故排除。 借⽤原⽂： our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does color actually do according to this lecture?

options.text: It attracts food companies' growing attention.
It adversely impacts one's eating experience.
It invariably determines how food sells.
It changes the way people taste food.

questions.shortExplanation: And the result is that color actually changes how we taste food.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） It changes the way people taste food.

【定位】 And the result is that color actually changes how we taste food.

其结果就是，颜色实际上改变了我们品尝食物的方式。

【信号】 结果词 the result is + actually。信号是因果收束词 the result is that（"其结果是"）领出全段结论，又叠加 color actually changes how we taste food 里的 "actually"，与题干 "actually do" 直接呼应——结果句 + actually 强调，这就是答案句。

【替换】 color actually changes how we taste food↔It changes the way people taste food.

how we taste = the way people taste

【排除】 A) 答非所问

A 盗用第 1 段背景里的 "food companies"。原文确说 Food companies know that better color gives better prices，但那是讲公司在意颜色的背景，不是回答 "color actually do（颜色实际起什么作用）"；且原文是公司已经关注，A 说 "growing attention （关注在增长）" 也无依据，属答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： Food companies know that better color gives better prices B) 与原文相反

B 借 eating experience 这个原文反复出现的词（第 2 段就有 the eating experience）， 却安上 "adversely impacts（负面影响）"。原文从头到尾把颜色讲成 "改变味觉、帮助判断" 的中性甚至有用的作用，从没说颜色 "负面影响" 吃的体验，态度相反，排除。 借⽤原⽂： the most important part of the eating experience C) 过度推断

C 盗用第 1 段 "color is money / better prices" 的卖钱话题，推成 It invariably determines how food sells.。原文只说 better color gives better prices（更好的颜色卖更好的价），是 "有助于"，C 用绝对词 "invariably（无一例外地决定）" 把话说死，超出原文，属过度推断。 借⽤原⽂： better color gives better prices
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the brain use color to do?

options.text: Enhance the taste.
Make predictions.
Identify distinct flavors.
Enrich the eating experience.

questions.shortExplanation: The brain makes predictions using color.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Make predictions.

【定位】 The brain makes predictions using color.

大脑利用颜色来做出预测。

【信号】 brain + color 同现的机制句。信号是录音第一次把 The brain 和 using color 放进同一句、直接给出动作的机制句 The brain makes predictions using color——题干问 "大脑用颜色做什么"，正是这句把主语、工具、动作三者一次说全，即答案句。

【替换】 The brain makes predictions using color↔Make predictions.

makes predictions = Make predictions

【排除】 A) 未提及

A 说 Enhance the taste.（增强味道），听着像 "颜色让吃更好" 的常识，但录音讲的是颜色让大脑做预测、形成对甜/酸的预期，从没说颜色 "增强" 味道本身，属原文未提及。

C) 张冠李戴

C 盗用第 3 段实验里的原词 "identify the flavor"。原文 each of them identified the orange flavor 说的是 "实验参与者借助看到颜色去辨认味道"，是讲颜色影响味觉的证据； 题问的是 "大脑用颜色做什么"，答案是 "做预测"，C 把实验现象当成大脑机制本身，属张冠李戴、答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： each of them identified the orange flavor D) 未提及

D 说 Enrich the eating experience.（丰富吃的体验），借用了贯穿全篇的 "eating experience" 话题词，但原文说大脑用颜色是去 "做预测、形成味觉预期"，从没说颜色用来 "丰富" 吃的体验，属原文未提及。

items.title: 2024年12月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 3
items.transcript:
Searching for meaning is something many of us experience throughout our lives. For some, this meaning is religious, some political and some interpersonal. And having a sense of meaning can bring us happiness.

A new study looks at the relationship between meaning and happiness in the context of financial resources. Rhea Catapano from the University of Toronto and colleagues find meaning is a far weaker predictor of happiness for rich people than poorer people, suggesting economic resources can impact how we experience meaning. The team analysed data from over 500,000 people across 123 countries. The first study used data from a daily poll of US residents collected between 2013 and 2015. Well-being was tracked using measures of positive affect—whether, during the day before they were surveyed, participants had smiled or laughed a lot or experienced a lot of happiness. Meaning was measured through a daily "purpose index", which explored the extent to which participants felt that they like what they do every day and are motivated to achieve their goals. Finally, income levels were assessed. The results showed that the correlation between meaning and happiness was strongest among those in lower income brackets. But as income levels increased, the correlation became weaker. The second study looked at worldwide data. Happiness was measured using the same questions as in the first study, while meaning was measured using the single question: "Do you feel your life has an important purpose or meaning?" Again, the strength of the relationship between meaning and happiness depended on participants' income: meaning had a greater influence on happiness for those on lower incomes compared to those in higher brackets. In the final study, French participants indicated the extent to which they felt they led a purposeful and meaningful life and how much they considered themselves a happy person. Finally, rather than using specific income brackets, they placed themselves on a "social ladder", representing where they stand in society with regard to wealth, education, and career. The results from the study duplicated those of the first two.

So overall, meaning and happiness had a stronger relationship in those with fewer resources than those with more. This might be the case because rich individuals have more access to other sources of happiness—many of which will be external, like lack of stress or community. Thus, a focus on an internal sense of satisfaction, purpose or meaning is less important.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say many of us search for throughout our lives?

options.text: Social status.
Financial resources.
Meaning.
Happiness.

questions.shortExplanation: Searching for meaning is something many of us experience throughout our lives.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Meaning.

【定位】 Searching for meaning is something many of us experience throughout our lives.

追寻意义，是我们许多人一生中都会经历的事。

【信号】 开篇点题句即答案。录音第一句 Searching for meaning is something many of us experience throughout our lives 与题干 throughout our lives 逐词呼应，是典型的‘开篇点题’信号——篇章独白常把核心对象放在第一句领出，这里把 meaning 摆在句首作主语， 正是答案所在。

【替换】 Searching for meaning↔ Meaning 动名词短语取其宾语名词

【排除】 D) 原词陷阱

录音紧接着说 having a sense of meaning can bring us happiness，happiness 在这里是‘意义带来的结果’，不是‘人们追寻的东西’。选项 Happiness 盗用了这个刚听到的原词， 但答非所问——题目问的是 search for 的对象。 借⽤原⽂： having a sense of meaning can bring us happiness B) 原词陷阱

in the context of financial resources 里 financial resources 是这项研究的考察背景/变量，全篇没说它是‘人们一生追寻的东西’。选项 Financial resources 盗用了后文反复出现的财富一词来诱选。 借⽤原⽂： in the context of financial resources A) 未提及 For some, this meaning is religious, some political and some interpersonal 列举的是意义的种类（宗教、政治、人际），通篇并未把 social status（社会地位）说成人们追寻的东西，属无中生有。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What do Rhia Catapano and colleagues find about economic resources?

options.text: Their effect on people's happiness has long been overstated.
Their influence on people's life varies with social contexts.
They can affect people's experience of meaning.
They can ensure people's overall well-being.

questions.shortExplanation: Rhea Catapano from the University of Toronto and colleagues find meaning is a far weaker predictor of happiness for rich people than poorer people, suggesting economic resources can impact how we experience meaning. 多伦多大学的 Rhea Catapano 及其同事发现，对富人而言，意义对幸福的预测作用远弱于穷人，这表明经济资源会影响我们体验意义的方式。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） They can affect people's experience of meaning.

【定位】 Rhea Catapano from the University of Toronto and colleagues find meaning is a far weaker predictor of happiness for rich people than poorer people, suggesting economic resources can impact how we experience meaning. 多伦多大学的 Rhea Catapano 及其同事发现，对富人而言，意义对幸福的预测作用远弱于穷人，这表明经济资源会影响我们体验意义的方式。

【信号】 find…suggesting 引出结论。录音用 find meaning is a far weaker predictor of happiness…suggesting economic resources can impact how we experience meaning 把研究结论端出来：动词 find 直接对应题干的 find，而 suggesting 之后那半句正是对‘经济资源起什么作用’的定性回答，是结论信号最集中处。

【替换】 economic resources can impact how we experience meaning ↔ They can affect people's experience of meaning

impact=affect 同义替换 economic resources ↔ They 代词回指经济资源

【排除】 D) 偷换概念

录音说财富影响的是 how we experience meaning（体验意义的方式），并未说它能‘保证整体幸福’。选项 They can ensure people's overall well-being 借用了全篇高频词 happiness 的近义概念 well-being，还把‘影响’夸大成‘保证（ensure）’，对象与程度都改了。 借⽤原⽂： economic resources can impact how we experience meaning A) 未提及

meaning is a far weaker predictor of happiness for rich people than poorer people 谈的是‘穷富之间预测力强弱不同’，从未说‘财富对幸福的影响被长期夸大’。选项 Their effect on people's happiness has long been overstated 凭空造出一个‘被夸大’的评价， 是无中生有，正应了预读对 overstated 这个程度词的预警。

B) 原词陷阱

录音说差异取决于 income（收入高低），而非 social contexts（社会环境）。第三项研究里虽有 social ladder（社会阶梯）一词，但那是测量财富地位的工具，不是‘随社会环境而变’。选项 Their influence on people's life varies with social contexts 盗用了 social 这个原词来制造熟悉感。 借⽤原⽂： they placed themselves on a "social ladder"
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about Rhia Catapano and colleagues' second study?

options.text: It used questions totally different from those in their first study.
It focused on the sense of meaning of French participants.
It analysed cases from a daily poll of US residents.
It examined data collected from multiple countries.

questions.shortExplanation: The second study looked at worldwide data.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） It examined data collected from multiple countries.

【定位】 The second study looked at worldwide data.

第二项研究考察的是全球范围的数据。

【信号】 序数词 second 直接定位。录音用序数词把三项研究串起来：first study…second study… final study。题干问 second study，就听 The second study looked at worldwide data 这句——worldwide data（全球数据）是这项研究区别于前后两项的核心特征，序数词是最干净的定位信号。

【替换】 worldwide data ↔ data collected from multiple countries worldwide=multiple countries

【排除】 C) 张冠李戴

The first study used data from a daily poll of US residents 明说‘分析美国居民每日民调’ 的是第一项研究，不是第二项。选项 It analysed cases from a daily poll of US residents 盗用了 daily poll of US residents 这串原话，但安到了错的研究上。 借⽤原⽂： The first study used data from a daily poll of US residents B) 张冠李戴

In the final study, French participants indicated 表明‘聚焦法国被试’的是最终那项研究， 而非第二项。选项 It focused on the sense of meaning of French participants 盗用 French participants 这一原词，错配到第二项研究上。 借⽤原⽂： In the final study, French participants indicated A) 与原文相反

录音说第二项研究 Happiness was measured using the same questions as in the first study，幸福度用的是与第一项‘相同’的问题；选项 It used questions totally different from those in their first study 恰好把 same（相同）反说成 totally different（全然不同），正话反说。 借⽤原⽂： Happiness was measured using the same questions as in the first study

questions.prompt: Why do meaning and happiness have a weaker relationship in those with more resources?

options.text: They might have more access to external sources of happiness.
They might focus on an individual sense of satisfaction or meaning.
They might be less easily affected by a community's overall feeling.
They might be less adversely impacted by failure to achieve a purpose.

questions.shortExplanation: This might be the case because rich individuals have more access to other sources of happiness—many of which will be external, like lack of stress or community.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） They might have more access to external sources of happiness.

【定位】 This might be the case because rich individuals have more access to other sources of happiness—many of which will be external, like lack of stress or community.

之所以如此，可能是因为富人能接触到更多其他的幸福来源——其中许多是外部的，比如没有压力、或拥有社群。

【信号】 because 引出原因。录音用 This might be the case because rich individuals have more access to other sources of happiness 给出解释，because 是最直接的因果信号， 其后那句正是‘富人为何关系更弱’的答案；后面 many of which will be external 进一步点明这些来源是‘外部的’。

【替换】 rich individuals have more access to other sources of happiness↔ They might have more access to external sources of happiness

near-原词复现+补 external

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱录音末句 a focus on an internal sense of satisfaction, purpose or meaning is less important 说‘对内部满足/意义的关注变得不那么重要’，这是‘外部来源多’导致的结果，且方向是‘内部变次要’，并非‘富人聚焦内部满足’。选项 They might focus on an individual sense of satisfaction or meaning 盗用 internal/satisfaction/meaning 这串原词，却把因果与方向都说反了。 借⽤原⽂： a focus on an internal sense of satisfaction, purpose or meaning is less important C) 偷换概念

录音的 like lack of stress or community 把 community（社群）举例为‘外部幸福来源之一’，而选项 They might be less easily affected by a community's overall feeling 把 community 改造成‘群体的整体情绪’并说富人‘不易受其影响’，与原文‘社群是一种幸福来源’ 完全不是一回事。 借⽤原⽂： like lack of stress or community D) 未提及

录音通篇没说富人‘较少受目标未达成的负面打击’。选项 They might be less adversely impacted by failure to achieve a purpose 借 purpose 一词（录音里 purpose 多次出现）拼出一个原文未提的因果，属无中生有。

items.title: 2024年12月六级第2套 · 长对话 1
items.transcript:
W: Hi, Alan. Sorry for not calling you back sooner. You said on the phone you had something you needed to discuss with me?

M: Well, to get right down to it, I'm having second thoughts about my major. With my family situation getting more complicated and the end of my university education nearing, persisting with Art History just doesn't seem the right choice.

W: Alan, in the last 3 years, I have heard nothing but how passionate you are about the Art History programme. You often told fellow classmates how fabulous the instructors were and that you finally felt accepted. What would cause you to abandon it?

M: My father's current financial situation has helped me realize that a more financially viable employment opportunity is not necessarily a bad thing. Art History nourishes my soul, but does nothing to put food on my plate.

W: What about all the work opportunities I discussed with you last month? Have you gone to those places of business to investigate whether any legitimate positions might be available for someone with your background?

M: Ah, well…

W: Look, Alan, if your heart is set on working in the art industry, you need to be more assertive and start talking with people. Networking is key if you want to become a celebrity in the world of museums and galleries.

M: Time is a very precious commodity right now. My social life does not exist. I can barely keep up with my studies and thesis is due by the end of this year. When can I find time to research jobs when I have so much to do as it is?

W: What you do now will determine your future options. Now is the optimum time to put forth your best effort.

M: I will take what you said into consideration. The advice is much appreciated.

questions.prompt: What did the man want to discuss with the woman?

options.text: Changing his major.
His family situation.
Revising his graduation thesis.
His passion for Art History.

questions.shortExplanation: Well, to get right down to it, I'm having second thoughts about my major.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Changing his major.

【定位】 Well, to get right down to it, I'm having second thoughts about my major.

嗯，直说吧，我对自己的专业起了动摇 / 想重新考虑了。

【信号】 开门见山引出语。to get right down to it（直奔主题地说）是典型的点题信号，紧跟其后的 I'm having second thoughts about my major 就是他要谈的核心，这正是开篇定主话题的落点。

【替换】 having second thoughts about my major↔ Changing his major. 动摇=想换

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

录音确有 With my family situation getting more complicated，但家庭状况只是促使他动摇的背景诱因，不是他『想讨论』的主题；听到原词 family situation 就选会上当。 借⽤原⽂： With my family situation getting more complicated C) 原词陷阱 thesis（毕业论文）确实在后文 thesis is due by the end of this year 被提到，但那是讲他没时间的论据，与他开头要谈的『换专业』无关，更没说要 revise（修改）论文。 借⽤原⽂： thesis is due by the end of this year

D) 与原文相反

passion for Art History 出自女方回忆 how passionate you are about the Art History programme，那是男生过去的热爱；他现在恰恰是要放弃，方向相反，不是他想讨论的事。 借⽤原⽂： how passionate you are about the Art History programme

options.text: He doesn't think it legitimate to depend on his father.

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） He doesn't think it will provide him with a living.

【定位】 Art History nourishes my soul, but does nothing to put food on my plate.

艺术史滋养我的灵魂，却完全没法让我糊口 / 养活自己。

【信号】 转折 but 后是真意。but does nothing to put food on my plate 中的 but 是关键信号： 前半 nourishes my soul 是让步，转折之后才是他放弃的真正理由——这门专业养不活自己。转折后才是落点。

【替换】 does nothing to put food on my plate↔ He doesn't think it will provide him with a living.

糊口=谋生

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

录音出现过 My father's current financial situation 和别处的 legitimate，但他从没说 『依赖父亲不正当』；这是把不同句的原词拼成一个似是而非的理由。 借⽤原⽂： My father's current financial situation has helped me realize B) 张冠李戴

My father's current financial situation 是『父亲的』经济状况让他醒悟，并非『他自己的经济状况变了』；选项把主语和含义都改了。 借⽤原⽂： My father's current financial situation has helped me realize D) 偷换概念

nourishes 确实念到了，但原文是 Art History nourishes my soul——艺术史滋养灵魂是他舍不得它的地方，不是放弃的理由；选项把它说成『只滋养经济无虞者』，纯属歪曲。 借⽤原⽂： Art History nourishes my soul

questions.prompt: What does the woman advise the man to do?

options.text: Try his best to socialize and build a network in the art industry.
Seek financially viable employment opportunities after graduation.

questions.shortExplanation: if your heart is set on working in the art industry, you need to be more assertive and start talking with people. Networking is key if you want to become a celebrity in the world of museums and galleries.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Try his best to socialize and build a network in the art industry.

【定位】 if your heart is set on working in the art industry, you need to be more assertive and start talking with people. Networking is key if you want to become a celebrity in the world of museums and galleries.

如果你一心想在艺术行业工作，就得更主动些，开始去和人交谈。如果你想成为博物馆和画廊界的名人，建立人脉至关重要。

【信号】 建议句 you need to / is key。you need to be more assertive and start talking with people 用 you need to 直接发出建议，Networking is key 又以『…至关重要』强调要点 ——这两处劝告语气正是建议题的答案信号。

【替换】 start talking with people↔ Try his best to socialize and build a network in the art industry. 和人交谈=社交 Networking is key ↔ build a network in the art industry

networking=build a network

【排除】 B) 张冠李戴

financially viable employment 是男方在 a more financially viable employment opportunity is not necessarily a bad thing 说的想法，不是女方的建议；女方反而劝他坚持艺术行业。 借⽤原⽂： a more financially viable employment opportunity is not necessarily a bad thing C) 偷换概念

录音里 become a celebrity in the world of museums and galleries 是『成名』这一目标，女方建议的手段是建人脉；选项把它说成『研究怎样成名』，把目标当成了建议的动作。 借⽤原⽂： become a celebrity in the world of museums and galleries D) 未提及 Strike a balance between intellectual pursuits and financial security. 听上去最稳妥， 但女方通篇没说『要在理想与现实间平衡』，她是明确劝他坚持艺术、去建人脉；这是录音没提及的折中说法。

options.text: Money.

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Time.

【定位】 Time is a very precious commodity right now. My social life does not exist. I can barely keep up with my studies and thesis is due by the end of this year. When can I find time to research jobs when I have so much to do as it is?

时间现在是非常稀缺的东西。我根本没有社交生活，连学业都快跟不上，论文今年底就要交。我本就忙得不可开交，哪还能挤出时间去找工作？

【信号】 稀缺信号 precious / barely。Time is a very precious commodity right now 中的 precious（珍贵稀缺）直接点出匮乏，后面 I can barely keep up 和 When can I find time 反复诉说时间不够——这一连串稀缺信号都指向时间。

【排除】 A) 答非所问

金钱话题（financial、food on my plate）出现在前文谈放弃专业时，但他在被问『缺什么』的这段里抱怨的是时间不是钱；把别处的 money 话题搬过来就答偏了。 借⽤原⽂： does nothing to put food on my plate

C) 未提及录音没说他缺决心；他缺的是时间，决心与原文无对应。

D) 原词陷阱

女方说过 Now is the optimum time，optimum（最佳的）与 optimism（乐观）形近易混，但这是女方的话、且讲的是『最佳时机』，与他缺什么无关。 借⽤原⽂： Now is the optimum time to put forth your best effort

items.title: 2024年12月六级第2套 · 长对话 2
items.transcript:
M: Have you decided yet what your end-of-semester business project will be on?

W: Yes. How about you?

M: Yes. Go on. You go first.

W: I am going to do it about beef.

M: Beef?

W: Yeah, beef. I'm going to design a business case study for a cow farm that supplies beef for the domestic market.

M: Well, that sounds very interesting and original. Wherever did you get that idea?

W: I don't know. It just came to me, I guess. But think about it. Beef consumption has been rising strongly over the past 20 years. As the economy continues to grow, consumer demand is expected to continue to increase for the foreseeable future. And currently, most of the beef is imported, which brings with it added fees. So why not raise cattle here?

M: Of course. Makes perfect sense. There's plenty of land out west. So, if done right, it should be very profitable to raise our own cattle.

W: Exactly.

M: Seriously, that sounds like a great idea. You should genuinely look into it once we get our degrees.

W: Thanks. So, your turn now. What are you doing your case study on?

M: I was thinking about a car wash, but it now seems like such a boring notion after hearing your brilliant idea.

W: That's cool. I could see that working. After all, there's plenty of cars about and those aren't going away any time soon. While many people don't care how their car looks, many other people do. You got yourself a vast and continual market.

M: Right. So the idea is a large self-cleaning car wash, but I mean really big and well-outfitted like they have in America. I was thinking of having it cater to high-end consumers in large cities. It could charge a profitable markup by offering just a bit more technical equipment and professional service than competitors.

questions.prompt: What are the speakers mainly talking about in the conversation?

options.text: Their decision on investigating beef consumption.
Their original ideas about the domestic market.
Their different approaches to a case study.
Their end-of-semester business projects.

questions.shortExplanation: M: Have you decided yet what your end-of-semester business project will be on? ... W: I'm going to design a business case study for a cow farm... M: What are you doing your case study on? M: I was thinking about a car wash...
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （主旨题） Their end-of-semester business projects.

【定位】 M: Have you decided yet what your end-of-semester business project will be on? ... W: I'm going to design a business case study for a cow farm... M: What are you doing your case study on? M: I was thinking about a car wash...

男：你定下来期末商业项目做什么了吗？……女：我打算给一个供应国内市场牛肉的养牛场设计一个商业案例……男：你的案例研究做什么？男：我本来在想做洗车……

【信号】 首句点题且全程围绕。开头第一句 what your end-of-semester business project will be on 就点出话题，之后两人轮流介绍各自的 project（女的牛肉、男的洗车），话题从头贯到尾——主旨就靠"开头点题 + 全程不离"判定。

【替换】 end-of-semester business project↔Their end-of-semester business projects 几乎原词照搬

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Their decision on investigating beef consumption 盗用了录音里 Beef consumption has been rising strongly 的 beef consumption，但那只是女方项目内的一个论据，既非"两人"共谈、也非全程主旨，以偏概全。 借⽤原⽂： Beef consumption has been rising strongly over the past 20 years B) 原词陷阱

Their original ideas about the domestic market 借了 the domestic market 的原词，但对话主谈的是"做什么项目"，domestic market 只是女方方案里的一个限定，不能代表整段。 借⽤原⽂： supplies beef for the domestic market C) 过度推断

Their different approaches to a case study 听上去合理，因为两人确实各做 case study，但录音中两人是"各做各的不同生意"，并没有讨论"做案例的不同方法"， approaches 是无中生有。 借⽤原⽂： What are you doing your case study on?

【答案】 C （细节题） Raising cattle domestically.

【定位】 M: Of course. Makes perfect sense. There's plenty of land out west. So, if done right, it should be very profitable to raise our own cattle. 男：当然。完全说得通。西部有大片土地。所以，只要做得对，自己养牛应该很赚钱。

【替换】 to raise our own cattle↔Raising cattle domestically

our own=domestically

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

Expanding farmland out west 盗用了男方 plenty of land out west 的 land out west， 但他是用"西部有地"来论证自养可行，并非主张"扩张西部农田"，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： There's plenty of land out west B) 与原文相反

Importing most of the beef 借了女方 most of the beef is imported 的原词，但 imported 在录音里是"现状的弊端、要被自养取代"的对象，绝不是 makes sense 的对象， 取的恰是反面。 借⽤原⽂： most of the beef is imported, which brings with it added fees D) 原词陷阱

Continuing to boost economic growth 盗用了 the economy continues to grow 的 economy/grow，但经济增长在录音里是"需求会涨"的大背景，男方认可的是"自养"这个做法，不是"继续推动经济增长"。 借⽤原⽂： As the economy continues to grow, consumer demand is expected to continue to increase

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

Technical equipment 盗用了后文 a bit more technical equipment 的原词，但那是男方靠它"加价"的卖点，不是"市场大"的对象，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： offering just a bit more technical equipment and professional service B) 未提及

questions.prompt: Who would the man's imagined business cater to?

Consumers craving for professional service.

questions.shortExplanation: M: I was thinking of having it cater to high-end consumers in large cities. It could charge a profitable markup by offering just a bit more technical equipment and professional service than competitors.

【定位】 M: I was thinking of having it cater to high-end consumers in large cities. It could charge a profitable markup by offering just a bit more technical equipment and professional service than competitors.

男：我本想让它面向大城市的高端消费者。靠比对手多提供一点技术设备和专业服务，就能收取可观的利润加价。

items.title: 2024年12月六级第2套 · 听力篇章 1
items.transcript:
Increased television time for young children has long been linked with poorer progress in some areas of development. One possible way to counter those negative effects is talking while watching the screen. As a new study suggests, the more parents engaged in conversation with preschoolers during TV time, the more likely those children were to have higher curiosity levels when they reached kindergarten. This was particularly true for children with socioeconomic disadvantages.

"Our findings reinforce the importance of parent conversation to promote early childhood development and curiosity," said lead author Prachi Shah at University of Michigan Health C.S. Mott Children's Hospital. Researchers assessed hours of daily television exposure and frequency of parent-screen-time conversation among 1,500 preschoolers, and then measured early childhood curiosity in kindergarten. The study specifically focused on curiosity levels, which are associated with enhanced learning and higher academic achievement in reading and math at kindergarten, and behavioral-developmental benefits, especially for children from families with lower socioeconomic status. While many young children are now growing up with digital media exposure through mobile devices like tablets and phones, television remains a dominant screen activity, accounting for 72% of all screen time. TVs are in 98% of all homes, keeping television exposure a relevant developmental context in young children.

Excessive media exposure, including television, can displace exploratory activities such as play and parent-child interactions, which are believed to be key to cultivating curiosity in kids. "Our findings suggest the importance of parents finding opportunities to foster conversational exchanges in daily routines with their young children—including while watching television," Shah said.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from a new study about young children?

options.text: Parents' talking with them during TV time raises their curiosity levels.
Their daily television exposure cuts parent-child conversation time.
The more TV they watch the poorer their progress in development.
Their socioeconomic levels impact their academic achievement.

questions.shortExplanation: As a new study suggests, the more parents engaged in conversation with preschoolers during TV time, the more likely those children were to have higher curiosity levels when they reached kindergarten. 正如一项新研究所示，家长在看电视时与学龄前儿童交谈得越多，这些孩子上幼儿园时拥有更高好奇心水平的可能性就越大。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Parents' talking with them during TV time raises their curiosity levels.

【定位】 As a new study suggests, the more parents engaged in conversation with preschoolers during TV time, the more likely those children were to have higher curiosity levels when they reached kindergarten. 正如一项新研究所示，家长在看电视时与学龄前儿童交谈得越多，这些孩子上幼儿园时拥有更高好奇心水平的可能性就越大。

【信号】 研究结论标志语 a new study suggests。录音用 As a new study suggests 这个明确的结论引出语点题，紧跟其后的 the more… the more… 句式正是新研究的核心结论，听到 study suggests 就该锁定其后那句为答案句。

【替换】 the more parents engaged in conversation with preschoolers during TV time, the more likely those children were to have higher curiosity levels

↔ Parents' talking with them during TV time raises their curiosity levels

the more…the more 改写为 raises engaged in conversation with preschoolers during TV time↔ talking with them during TV time engaged in conversation = talking

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

B 借用了录音第二段念到的 daily television exposure 这个原词，编出看电视会减少亲子对话时间的说法，但录音从未说看电视削减对话，反而强调看电视时家长要多陪聊，属于听到原词就想选的原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： Researchers assessed hours of daily television exposure and frequency of parent-screen-time conversation C) 答非所问

C 用了录音开头 poorer progress in some areas of development 的原词，说成看得越多发展越差的递进因果，但录音只说看电视时间增多长期与发展较差相关联，是个背景前提、 并非本研究的新发现，新发现是陪聊提升好奇心，故 C 答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： Increased television time for young children has long been linked with poorer progress in some areas of development. D) 偷换概念

D 借用录音里的 socioeconomic disadvantages 一词，说成经济水平影响学业成就，但录音只把社会经济弱势作为陪聊效果尤其明显的人群补充，并未把它当作研究的主结论，属于把次要信息偷换成主结论。 借⽤原⽂： This was particularly true for children with socioeconomic disadvantages.

C 照搬录音原词 reading and math，但 reading and math 是好奇心相关联的学业成就领域，属于延伸好处，不是研究聚焦的对象，同样是听到具体学科词就想选的原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： higher academic achievement in reading and math at kindergarten D) 原词陷阱

包括电视在内的过度媒体接触，会挤占诸如游戏和亲子互动这样的探索性活动，而这些活动被认为是培养孩子好奇心的关键。

【信号】 主体加负面谓语 can displace。录音第三段开头 Excessive media exposure, including television, can displace exploratory activities 中，主体 excessive media exposure 后紧跟负面谓语 can displace（挤占），这就是直接回答其后果的答案句，听到题目主体原词加一个动词就锁定该句。

displace 改写为 cut into time

【排除】 A) 未提及

A 说过度媒体接触会妨碍孩子与同伴相处（get on with their peers），但录音通篇只说挤占游戏和亲子互动，从未提到与同伴相处或交友受阻，属录音根本没说的内容。 C) 与原文相反

C 说能激发孩子对真实人际互动的兴趣，是正面后果，而录音 can displace exploratory activities such as play and parent-child interactions 借用了 interactions 这个原词却把方向说反了：原文是挤占亲子互动这一负面结果，C 却说成激发兴趣，方向完全相反。 借⽤原⽂： can displace exploratory activities such as play and parent-child interactions D) 原词陷阱

D 借用了录音里反复出现的社会经济地位概念（lower socioeconomic status），说成会拉大不同经济地位孩子间的差距，但录音从未说过度媒体接触会扩大经济差距，只把经济弱势作为陪聊受益尤其明显的人群，属于听到熟悉术语就想选的原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： especially for children from families with lower socioeconomic status

items.title: 2024年12月六级第2套 · 听力篇章 2
items.transcript:
Humans are aspirational goal-seeking beings. Each of us, according to research, has an inborn drive to acquire. The "dark side" of this drive to acquire is being mindlessly driven to possess more and more "things" and to socially compare our "stuff" with all the stuff other people have in their lives. So the question is, how do we ensure we tap into our drive to acquire in positive ways that will benefit our well-being?

One way is to become more intentionally aspirational. To be intentionally aspirational includes consciously aspiring to be the person you need to be to succeed in your professional and personal life. It also includes consciously aspiring to acquire things in your life that will positively impact your sense of well-being. If you're not consciously, mindfully and intentionally harnessing this inborn drive to acquire, you might be mindlessly pursuing all the wrong things.

While your intentional aspirational goals will include pursuit of acquiring things that will increase your sense of well-being, they ought to also include goals to help other people in your various life roles. Your intentional aspirational goals will also include striving to be your personal best—a person of "good" character, integrity, and trustworthiness.

Think about this from a practical, rather than theoretical viewpoint. If you're not pursuing intentional aspirational goals, you have nothing to strive for. If you have nothing to strive for, you're putting yourself in the dangerous position of simply drifting through life, and you will not be able to experience, live and enjoy all that life has to offer.

questions.prompt: What is the dark side of our inborn drive to acquire?

options.text: Exerting ourselves too hard in order to attain our life's goals.
Being possessed with a single thought of professional success.
Trying every means to beat others in terms of personal aspirations.
Being mindlessly driven to possess more and more material things.

questions.shortExplanation: The "dark side" of this drive to acquire is being mindlessly driven to possess more and more "things" and to socially compare our "stuff" with all the stuff other people have in their lives. 这种获取欲的"阴暗面"就是：被盲目地驱使着去占有越来越多的"东西"，并把自己的"物品"和别人生活里拥有的所有物品作社会性比较。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Being mindlessly driven to possess more and more material things.

【定位】 The "dark side" of this drive to acquire is being mindlessly driven to possess more and more "things" and to socially compare our "stuff" with all the stuff other people have in their lives. 这种获取欲的"阴暗面"就是：被盲目地驱使着去占有越来越多的"东西"，并把自己的"物品"和别人生活里拥有的所有物品作社会性比较。

【信号】 题干原词在原文复现。原文 The "dark side" of this drive to acquire is 和题干用了同样的 dark side、drive to acquire，是"原词定位"信号——听到题干念到的词，原文这一句就是答案句。

【替换】 being mindlessly driven to possess more and more "things" ↔ Being mindlessly driven to possess more and more material things things 具体化为 material things

【排除】 A) 未提及

Exerting ourselves too hard in order to attain our life's goals. 谈"为目标过度用力"，但原文 dark side 指的是盲目占有物质，并非"努力过头"，属未提及。

B) 原词陷阱

Being possessed with a single thought of professional success. 借了原文后文出现的 success（succeed in your professional and personal life）来诱选，但那处讲的是"有意识地追求成功"的正面建议，不是 dark side。 借⽤原⽂： succeed in your professional and personal life C) 过度推断

Trying every means to beat others in terms of personal aspirations. 说"想方设法胜过别人"，原文谈的是"和别人比较自己的物品"（compare），并非"击败别人"，把 compare 夸大成 beat。 借⽤原⽂： socially compare our "stuff" with all the stuff other people have

questions.prompt: What might happen if we do not harness our inborn drive to acquire?

options.text: We might isolate ourselves from our fellow beings.
We might acquire an incorrect sense of well-being.
We might end up pursuing all the wrong things.
We might make a mess of our personal lives.

questions.shortExplanation: If you're not consciously, mindfully and intentionally harnessing this inborn drive to acquire, you might be mindlessly pursuing all the wrong things.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） We might end up pursuing all the wrong things.

【定位】 If you're not consciously, mindfully and intentionally harnessing this inborn drive to acquire, you might be mindlessly pursuing all the wrong things.

如果你不是有意识地、用心地、有目的地去驾驭这种与生俱来的获取欲，你可能就会盲目地去追求一切错误的东西。

【信号】 条件句 If…you might 的结果半句。原文 If you're not...harnessing this inborn drive to acquire, you might be... 是 If…you might 结构，转折点在逗号后——后半句才是"会发生什么"的落点。

【替换】 you might be mindlessly pursuing all the wrong things↔ We might end up pursuing all the wrong things

you 换 We、加 end up 不改义

【排除】 A) 未提及

We might isolate ourselves from our fellow beings. 说"把自己和同类隔离"，原文从未讲会孤立自己，属凭常识脑补的未提及项。

B) 原词陷阱

We might acquire an incorrect sense of well-being. 借了原文高频词 well-being 来诱选，但原文 well-being 都用在"如何正向利用获取欲、提升幸福感"，并非"不驾驭就会得到错误的幸福感"。 借⽤原⽂： benefit our well-being D) 原词陷阱

We might make a mess of our personal lives. 借 personal（原文有 personal life）造出"搞砸私人生活"的后果，但原文只说会"追错东西"，没说生活会一团糟。 借⽤原⽂： succeed in your professional and personal life

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about our intentional aspirational goals?

options.text: They should be based on solid theoretical concepts.
They should take personal interests into account.

questions.shortExplanation: While your intentional aspirational goals will include pursuit of acquiring things that will increase your sense of well-being, they ought to also include goals to help other people in your various life roles.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） They should include goals to help other people.

【定位】 While your intentional aspirational goals will include pursuit of acquiring things that will increase your sense of well-being, they ought to also include goals to help other people in your various life roles.

虽然你那些有意识的人生目标会包含"去获取能提升幸福感的东西"这一追求，但它们还应当包含"在你各种人生角色中去帮助他人"的目标。

【信号】 让步 While + ought to also 的递进落点。原文 While...will include..., they ought to also include goals to help other people 用 While 让步开头、真正主张在 ought to also 之后——递进"还应当"处才是落点。

【替换】 they ought to also include goals to help other people↔ They should include goals to help other people ought to=should，其余照搬

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

They should be based on solid theoretical concepts. 借了原文 theoretical 一词，但原文是叫你"从实践而非理论角度看"（practical, rather than theoretical），态度恰好相反。 借⽤原⽂： from a practical, rather than theoretical viewpoint B) 偷换概念

They should take personal interests into account. 说"应考虑个人兴趣"，原文谈的是 personal best、personal life，从没说 goals 要照顾"个人兴趣"，属偷换。 借⽤原⽂： striving to be your personal best

D) 原词陷阱 They should increase our sense of worthiness. 仿照原文 increase your sense of well-being 的句式，把 well-being 换成 worthiness（价值感），但那句讲的是"获取能提升幸福感的东西"，且不是本题问的"还应当包含什么"的落点。 借⽤原⽂： increase your sense of well-being

questions.prompt: What will you end up doing without pursuing intentional aspirational goals?

options.text: Drifting through life aimlessly.
Giving up the chance to fulfill yourself.
Abandoning all that life has to offer.
Spoiling your character and integrity.

questions.shortExplanation: If you have nothing to strive for, you're putting yourself in the dangerous position of simply drifting through life, and you will not be able to experience, live and enjoy all that life has to offer.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Drifting through life aimlessly.

【定位】 If you have nothing to strive for, you're putting yourself in the dangerous position of simply drifting through life, and you will not be able to experience, live and enjoy all that life has to offer.

如果你没有什么可为之奋斗的，你就把自己置于一个危险的境地——只是漫无目的地随波逐流地过一生，而且你将无法去体验、去活出、去享受生活所能给予的一切。

【信号】 文末 dangerous position 的警示结论。原文 you're putting yourself in the dangerous position of simply drifting through life 用 dangerous 加重语气点出"危险结局"，是文末收束的警示落点。

【替换】 simply drifting through life↔ Drifting through life aimlessly simply=aimlessly 同义改写

【排除】 B) 未提及

Giving up the chance to fulfill yourself. 说"放弃自我实现的机会"，原文文末讲的是"漂泊度日、无法享受生活"，并未提到"放弃自我实现"，属未提及。

C) 原词陷阱

Abandoning all that life has to offer. 直接借了原文 all that life has to offer 来诱选，但原文是说你"将无法享受 all that life has to offer"，是"无法享受"而非主动"abandon（抛弃）"，意思错位。 借⽤原⽂： enjoy all that life has to offer D) 张冠李戴

Spoiling your character and integrity. 借了第 3 段 character, integrity, and trustworthiness 的词，但那处讲的是"目标应包含做有品格的人"这一正面主张，不是"不追目标会毁品格"的结局，张冠李戴到本题。 借⽤原⽂： a person of "good" character, integrity, and trustworthiness

items.title: 2024年12月六级第2套 · 讲座与讲话 1
items.transcript:
It's revision time for exams and dissertations. The pressure is on, so you want all the help you can get to aid your memory and raise your grades. As a nutrition expert, I want to say that eating well can make a real difference to your revision regime—so what brain-boosting food and drink would I recommend?

Coffee can have numerous benefits. However, while coffee may make you more alert, individuals can build up a tolerance, meaning this is short-lived. Coffee can also increase blood sugar and eventually cause lack of focus and energy. It's also worth noting that people react differently to coffee. Some people can drink it at midnight and go straight to sleep, whereas others get feelings of anxiety after a small amount. Also remember that coffee from a coffee shop may be stronger than coffee made at home. So stop drinking coffee by 2 pm and have a maximum of 2 cups of coffee a day, but be aware of your own reaction to it.

Whole grain foods will ward off hunger. Examples include porridge and whole wheat bread. Combining whole grain foods with protein will help keep your blood sugar levels balanced, which is essential for mood and concentration. Berries and nuts are a convenient and nutritious snack. Blueberries, like many dark colored fruits and vegetables, can slow down brain damage and age-related decline. Frozen berries are also a good choice. They are usually cheap, last longer and don't lose their nutrients when frozen. But flavored and coated nuts are less healthy as they contain added oil, salt, and sugar.

Doctors often recommend taking vitamin supplements to top up on the nutrients you need. But I would say food should always come before supplements and the key to getting as many nutrients as possible is to eat a varied diet with lots of different colors such as frozen berries and dark green vegetables. It's better to get everything you need from food and drink. For example, oranges contain not only vitamin C which boosts the immune system, but also fiber and other components that you can't get packaged together in a tablet.

Don't forget to drink a proper amount of water, which can boost attention by almost 25 percent and can elevate your mood as well.

Finally, don't skip meals. Eating regularly will help keep blood sugar balanced and feed the brain with the fuel it needs.
