questions.prompt: What is the feeling about the problem around the woman's workplace?

options.text: Frustration.
Intimidation.
Desperation.
Indignation.

questions.shortExplanation: Well, I'll have you know, my manager is rather indignant that it's taken you this long to come.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （态度观点题） Indignation.

【定位】 Well, I'll have you know, my manager is rather indignant that it's taken you this long to come.

这么说吧，我得让你知道，我的经理对你们拖这么久才来相当愤慨。

【信号】 评价性形容词 indignant。女士说 my manager is rather indignant that it's taken you this long to come，indignant 是直接的情绪形容词，又被 rather 加重，正是描述工作场所对这件事感受的答案句。

【替换】 my manager is rather indignant↔Indignation 形容词 indignant 转成名词 Indignation

【排除】 A) 未提及

Frustration 是常见情绪词的合理猜测，但原文用的明确是 indignant（愤慨），二者程度和指向不同：indignant 是对怠慢的气愤，不是单纯的受挫，原文并未表达 frustration。

B) 未提及

Intimidation 指被威胁、被吓住，对话里女方是在抱怨对方来得慢，没有任何被恐吓的内容，与原文情绪不符，属未提及。

C) 过度推断

Desperation 表示绝望、走投无路，程度远超原文。女方只是不满拖延、表达气愤，并未到绝望地步，属过度推断。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say her manager would know?

options.text: Whether the contents have been backed up.
Whether they can find help somewhere else.
Whether all data stored on the hard drive has got lost.
Whether they need to wipe the system directories clean.

questions.shortExplanation: M: Do you know if it's backed up? ... W: My manager would know. Let me go get him. 男：你知道它有没有做备份吗？……女：我的经理会知道，我去把他叫来。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Whether the contents have been backed up.

【定位】 M: Do you know if it's backed up? ... W: My manager would know. Let me go get him. 男：你知道它有没有做备份吗？……女：我的经理会知道，我去把他叫来。

【信号】 一问一答的指代承接。男士先问 Do you know if it's backed up?，他随后解释 it 指 its contents have been copied and saved somewhere else；女士最后说 My manager would know，这句 would know 承接的正是前面备份这个问题，所以经理会知道的就是有没有备份。

【替换】 Do you know if it's backed up?↔Whether the contents have been backed up if it's backed up 改写成 whether…backed up

【排除】 B) 未提及

对话里没有任何关于到别处找帮助的内容，女士只说叫经理来确认备份情况，find help somewhere else 是无中生有，属未提及。

C) 原词陷阱

选项盗用男士那句 all data that was stored on its hard drive will be forever lost，但那是他对不备份后果的假设性说明，并不是女士说经理会知道的内容；经理会知道的是有没有备份，不是数据是否已全丢，属答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： all data that was stored on its hard drive will be forever lost D) 原词陷阱

wipe the system directories clean 直接取自 if I need to wipe the system directories clean，那是男士对自己后续可能操作的描述，是他要不要做的事，不是女士说经理会知道的内容，属答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： if I need to wipe the system directories clean in order to reconfigure default protocols

items.title: 2025年6月六级第1套 · 长对话 2
items.transcript:
M: Have you given more thought to studying law?

W: I've been thinking about it a lot, yes. In fact, this is why I wished to speak to you. I wanted to hear more about what it's like.

M: A career in law is a beautiful thing in my opinion. Many people will say it's a boring field, but I disagree. The thing is there are many different branches of law and many different jobs.

W: You are involved with buildings and construction, right?

M: Correct. I'm a solicitor, specializing in real estate. Most of my work involves mediating land disputes.

W: Do you mind giving me an example?

M: Sure. So in many cases I am employed to arbitrate between two clashing parties. Let's say for example, there are two landowners who are in a thorny disagreement about something like the borders of their adjacent plots. Someone may employ me to break the deadlock and resolve the dispute. Often my work involves negotiating agreements, plain and simple.

W: So you are saying that a lot of what you do is fix people's legal issues, like you try to find a solution that benefits everyone and that prevents a problem from escalating.

M: Exactly, well put. You need to remember that courts, like all bureaucracies really, can be very messy, frustrating, and expensive. For this reason, it's usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible.

W: I see. So besides knowing the law inside out, you need good people skills, right?

M: Of course. Any job that involves people requires good interpersonal skills, and any law professional needs to be very eloquent at articulating that argument.

W: Right. So I've been thinking about studying criminal law. I think it sounds very interesting.

M: Mm-hmm, yes. I'd say there's more money in property law, but the stakes are higher in criminal law. I can see how you would find it more interesting.

questions.prompt: What will many people say about a career in law?

options.text: It's boring.
It's challenging.
It's a beautiful thing.
It's unlike most jobs.

questions.shortExplanation: A career in law is a beautiful thing in my opinion. Many people will say it's a boring field, but I disagree.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （态度观点题） It's boring.

【定位】 A career in law is a beautiful thing in my opinion. Many people will say it's a boring field, but I disagree.

在我看来，从事法律是件美好的事。许多人会说这是个枯燥的领域，但我不同意。

【信号】 归属信号 Many people will say。答案落点不在 a beautiful thing in my opinion，而在 Many people will say it's a boring field 这句——题干问的是 many people，必须抓住 Many people will say 这个明确的归属信号，它后面跟的才是『许多人』的说法。

【替换】 a boring field↔It's boring. 同义浓缩

【排除】 C) 张冠李戴

It's a beautiful thing. 盗用了录音原话 a beautiful thing in my opinion，但那是男士『我个人』的看法，题干问的是 many people 怎么说——把说话人的观点安到『许多人』头上，归属错位。 借⽤原⽂： a beautiful thing in my opinion B) 未提及

It's challenging. 听上去合理，但录音里无论是 many people 还是说话人，都没说过从事法律『有挑战性』，属凭常识脑补、原文无据。

D) 未提及

It's unlike most jobs. 在录音中找不到对应，男士只说了 many people 觉得 boring、自己觉得 beautiful，从未拿它和『多数工作』作比较。
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the man say most of his work involves?

options.text: Arbitrating between disagreeing solicitors.
Preventing disputes from escalating.
Buying and selling property.
Mediating land disputes.

questions.shortExplanation: I'm a solicitor, specializing in real estate. Most of my work involves mediating land disputes. 我是一名事务律师，专攻房地产。我的工作大部分涉及调解土地纠纷。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Mediating land disputes.

【定位】 I'm a solicitor, specializing in real estate. Most of my work involves mediating land disputes. 我是一名事务律师，专攻房地产。我的工作大部分涉及调解土地纠纷。

【信号】 限定信号 Most of my work。录音 Most of my work involves mediating land disputes 与题干的 most of his work 用词几乎一致，Most of my work 就是定位信号，它后面跟的动作即答案。

【替换】 mediating land disputes↔Mediating land disputes.

近乎原词对应

【排除】 C) 原词陷阱

Buying and selling property. 蹭了录音 specializing in real estate 的房地产话题，听到 『房产』就想选；但男士说的主要工作是 mediating land disputes，不是买卖房产，属答非所问的原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： specializing in real estate A) 偷换概念

Arbitrating between disagreeing solicitors. 借用了后文 arbitrate between two clashing parties 的 arbitrate，但把对象偷换成 disagreeing solicitors(意见不合的律师)； 录音里仲裁的对象是两个地主/当事人，不是律师，对象错位。 借⽤原⽂： arbitrate between two clashing parties B) 答非所问 Preventing disputes from escalating. 对应后文 prevents a problem from escalating， 但那是女士事后归纳男士工作意义的话，且题干问的是 most of his work 的具体内容；用 『防止问题升级』这个意义层面的概括来答『主要做什么』，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： prevents a problem from escalating

questions.prompt: Why does the man say it's usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible?

options.text: Courts are intended for fixing major legal disputes.
Courts are getting too bureaucratic to function.
Courts can be frustrating and expensive.
Courts can be frightening and arbitrary.

questions.shortExplanation: You need to remember that courts, like all bureaucracies really, can be very messy, frustrating, and expensive. For this reason, it's usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Courts can be frustrating and expensive.

【定位】 You need to remember that courts, like all bureaucracies really, can be very messy, frustrating, and expensive. For this reason, it's usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible.

你要记住，法庭和所有官僚机构一样，可能非常混乱、令人沮丧而且昂贵。正因如此，能在庭外解决问题通常更好。

【信号】 因果信号 For this reason。For this reason 是明确的因果连接词，它前面那句 courts...can be very messy, frustrating, and expensive 就是『为什么庭外解决更好』的原因，顺着 For this reason 往前一句即定位到答案。

【替换】 frustrating, and expensive↔ Courts can be frustrating and expensive.

原词提取，去掉多余特征

【排除】 D) 偷换概念

Courts can be frightening and arbitrary. 与正确项仅差两个形容词，但录音说的是 frustrating(沮丧)和 expensive(昂贵)，不是 frightening(可怕)和 arbitrary(武断)；这两个词录音根本没念，是替换掉真实形容词的近形陷阱。 A) 答非所问

Courts are intended for fixing major legal disputes. 说的是法庭的用途，录音里男士并没有用『法庭是用来解决重大纠纷的』来解释为何庭外更好，方向不符。 B) 过度推断

Courts are getting too bureaucratic to function. 蹭了录音 like all bureaucracies 的 bureaucracy，但录音只是把法庭比作官僚机构、说它混乱昂贵，从没说法庭『过于官僚以致无法运转』，属由原词过度推断。 借⽤原⽂： like all bureaucracies
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the man think is required of any law professional?

options.text: The ability to make arguments in a unique way.
The skill of preventing conflicts between parties concerned.
The skill of foreseeing any potential stakes in their work.
The ability to express themselves clearly and forcefully.

questions.shortExplanation: Any job that involves people requires good interpersonal skills, and any law professional needs to be very eloquent at articulating that argument. 任何与人打交道的工作都需要良好的人际交往能力，而任何法律从业者都需要非常善于清楚地表达论点。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） The ability to express themselves clearly and forcefully.

The skill of preventing conflicts between parties concerned. 蹭了前文 prevents a problem from escalating 与调解纠纷的整段话题，听上去和这职业最贴；但题干问 any law professional 被要求的能力，录音对此的回答是 eloquent at articulating，不是预防冲突，属答非所问的原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： prevents a problem from escalating A) 偷换概念

The ability to make arguments in a unique way. 借了录音 articulating that argument 的 argument，但录音只说要 eloquent(善于表达)，从未说要『以独特的方式』论辩， unique 是凭空加上的限定。 借⽤原⽂： articulating that argument C) 张冠李戴

The skill of foreseeing any potential stakes in their work. 盗用了结尾 the stakes are higher in criminal law 的 stakes，但那是男士比较两类法律时说的话，与『法律从业者被要求的能力』无关，且录音从没说要『预见潜在利害』。 借⽤原⽂： the stakes are higher in criminal law

items.title: 2025年6月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 1
items.transcript:
When a person tries to access a memory, their brains quickly examine everything stored in it to find the relevant information. But as we age, many of us have difficulty retrieving memories.

In a review published in the journal *Trends in Cognitive Sciences* on February 11th, researchers propose an explanation for why this might be happening: the brains of older adults allocate more space to accumulated knowledge and have more material to navigate when attempting to access memories. While this wealth of prior knowledge can make memory retrieval challenging, the researchers say it has its upsides—this life experience can aid with creativity and decision-making.

Researchers Tarek Amer, Jordana Wynn and Lynn Hasher looked at several behavioral and brain imaging studies, which show that older adults have difficulty suppressing information that is no longer relevant and that when searching for a specific memory, they often retrieve other, irrelevant memories along with it. The studies also showed that when given a cognitive task, older adults rely more heavily on previous knowledge than younger adults do.

While the researchers focus primarily on the difficulties that these disorderly, crowded memories may pose, they also highlight a few situations in which these same memory patterns may be useful. "Evidence suggests that older adults show preserved, and at times enhanced, creativity as a function of enriched memories," the researchers write. They further hypothesize that older adults may be well served by their prior knowledge when it comes to decision-making, where they can pull on their accumulated wisdom.

questions.prompt: What did the researchers do in their review in the journal Trends in Cognitive Sciences?

options.text: They looked into the relationship between one's prior knowledge and creativity.
They offered novel ways to help older adults to keep their memories from aging.
They proposed an explanation for old people's difficulty in retrieving memories.
They advanced a new model concerning human information storage and retrieval.

questions.shortExplanation: researchers propose an explanation for why this might be happening: the brains of older adults allocate more space to accumulated knowledge and have more material to navigate when attempting to access memories.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

They proposed an explanation for old people's difficulty in retrieving memories.

【定位】 researchers propose an explanation for why this might be happening: the brains of older adults allocate more space to accumulated knowledge and have more material to navigate when attempting to access memories.

研究人员提出了一个解释，说明为什么会发生这种情况：老年人的大脑把更多空间分配给积累的知识，因而在试图提取记忆时要导航的材料更多。

【信号】 研究行为动词 propose。定位信号是描述研究者行为的那个动词 propose an explanation for why this might be happening——题干问 do（做了什么），原文里紧跟 researchers 的那个动作动词 propose 就是答案句标志。

【替换】 propose an explanation for why this might be happening↔ proposed an explanation

近乎同词的动作 why this might be happening ↔ old people's difficulty in retrieving memories

指代还原为具体所指

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

A 项 looked into the relationship between one's prior knowledge and creativity 盗用了原文确实出现过的 prior knowledge 与 creativity（见第四段 enhanced, creativity）， 但那是后文讲记忆模式的好处时顺带提到的，研究综述本身做的核心动作是 propose an explanation，不是去研究知识与创造力的关系，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： older adults may be well served by their prior knowledge

B) 未提及 B 项 offered novel ways to help older adults to keep their memories from aging 借用了 older adults、memories 等话题词，但原文从头到尾只是提出解释、分析现象，没有任何研究者提供新方法去防止记忆衰老的内容，属未提及。

D) 偷换概念

D 项 advanced a new model concerning human information storage and retrieval 用 retrieval 这个原文反复出现的词制造熟悉感，但原文研究者做的是 propose an explanation（提出一个解释），不是 advance a new model（提出一个新模型）；一个解释和一个新模型不是同一层级的成果，属偷换概念。 借⽤原⽂： propose an explanation for why this might be happening
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What do several behavioral and brain imaging studies show?

options.text: Young adults rely on memory while older adults keep notes as a reminder.

questions.shortExplanation: studies, which show that older adults have difficulty suppressing information that is no longer relevant and that when searching for a specific memory, they often retrieve other, irrelevant memories along with it. 这些研究显示，老年人难以抑制不再相关的信息，并且在搜寻某一具体记忆时，常常连带提取出其他无关的记忆。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Older adults often retrieve irrelevant memories along with what they want.

【定位】 studies, which show that older adults have difficulty suppressing information that is no longer relevant and that when searching for a specific memory, they often retrieve other, irrelevant memories along with it. 这些研究显示，老年人难以抑制不再相关的信息，并且在搜寻某一具体记忆时，常常连带提取出其他无关的记忆。

【信号】 show that 引出研究结论。信号是 which show that——题干问 studies show，原文里 studies which show that 之后的内容就是答案句，紧跟其后列出的 retrieve other, irrelevant memories 正是落点。

【替换】 they often retrieve other, irrelevant memories along with it↔ Older adults often retrieve irrelevant memories along with what they want 代词还原后近乎同句

【排除】 A) 未提及

A 项 Young adults rely on memory while older adults keep notes as a reminder 听着像在讲两类人记忆方式，但原文只说老年人更依赖旧知识，从没说老年人靠记笔记提醒、也没说年轻人靠记忆，属未提及。 C) 原词陷阱

C 项 Young adults accumulate knowledge much more quickly than older adults 盗用了原文的 accumulated knowledge（见第二段 accumulated knowledge），但原文讲的是老年人积累的知识多、要导航的材料多，从没比较谁积累得更快，选项凭空加了 much more quickly 的速度比较，属过度推断兼偷换。 借⽤原⽂： allocate more space to accumulated knowledge D) 原词陷阱 D 项 Older adults generally perform cognitive tasks much slower than young adults 盗用了原文的 cognitive task（见第三段 when given a cognitive task），但原文只说做认知任务时老年人更依赖旧知识，根本没提速度更慢，选项擅自加了 much slower 的速度论断，属原词陷阱加无中生有。 借⽤原⽂： when given a cognitive task, older adults rely more heavily on previous knowledge

questions.shortExplanation: "Evidence suggests that older adults show preserved, and at times enhanced, creativity as a function of enriched memories," the researchers write.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） They show preserved, and sometimes enhanced, creativity.

【定位】 "Evidence suggests that older adults show preserved, and at times enhanced, creativity as a function of enriched memories," the researchers write.

研究人员写道：证据表明，由于记忆更丰富，老年人的创造力得以保留、有时甚至得到增强。

【信号】 Evidence suggests 引出证据结论。信号是 Evidence suggests that——题干用的就是 evidence suggest，原文这处 Evidence suggests that 之后说的 older adults show preserved, and at times enhanced, creativity 即答案句。

【替换】 older adults show preserved, and at times enhanced, creativity ↔ They show preserved, and sometimes enhanced, creativity 仅换一个程度词

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

B 项 They frequently suffer from disorderly crowded memories 盗用了原文的 disorderly, crowded memories（见第四段 disorderly, crowded memories），但原文那处是讲这些记忆模式带来的困难，而本题问的是 evidence suggests 那句的正面发现（创造力），方向与问点都不对，属原词陷阱兼答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： these disorderly, crowded memories may pose C) 偷换概念

C 项 They can rely on their accumulated wisdom in an emergency 盗用了原文的 accumulated wisdom（见第四段 accumulated wisdom），但原文说的是在 decision-making（决策）时可借助积累的智慧，并非 in an emergency（紧急情况），选项把决策场景偷换成应急场景，属偷换概念。 借⽤原⽂： may be well served by their prior knowledge when it comes to decision-making

D) 与原文相反

D 项 They may well be served by forgetting their prior knowledge 盗用了原文 may be well served by 与 prior knowledge 的近原句（见第四段 may be well served by their prior knowledge），但原文说老年人是靠旧知识 served，选项却改成靠忘掉旧知识 served，把方向反了，属与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： older adults may be well served by their prior knowledge

items.title: 2025年6月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 2
items.transcript:
There are at least four major problems with work in America today.

First, work can be alienating. Workers are often not in control of how they work, when they work, what is done with the goods and services they produce, and what is done with the profits made from their work.

Second, workers are not paid the full value of their labor. Real wages have not kept pace with productivity, driving economic inequality and a decline in labor's share of income.

Third, people are time poor. In the U.S., full time employees work an average of 8.72 hours per day despite productivity increases. Long working hours contribute to the feeling of "time poverty", which has an adverse effect on psychological well-being.

Fourth, automation puts jobs and wages at risk. Technological innovation could in theory liberate people from the 40-hour work week. But unless changes are made to the structure of work, automation will simply exert downward pressure on wages and further diminish work opportunities.

So, what can be done to alleviate these problems? There are competing visions of the best way to arrive at a solution. One vision is what's known as the "post-work" position. The post-work theorists believe that work should not hold a central position in our lives or take up so much of our time. They assert that although doing some work might be necessary, meaning, purpose and social value reside in the communities and relationships built and sustained outside of the workplace. Thus, life should be seen as an end in itself.

【信号】 分点首句"First"后的解释句。本段以 First, work can be alienating. 起头点出第一个问题，紧接着的这句 Workers are often not in control of 就是对该问题的展开说明，是承载答案的句子。

items.title: 2025年6月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 1
items.transcript:
Recent studies show that self-control and persistence increase academic outcomes, independence of IQ. Even our personal beliefs about efforts can affect academic outcomes. Children who think effort leads to achievement outperform those who believe ability is a fixed trait. Given the link between persistence and academic success, decisions about efforts are particularly important in childhood.

Yet, relatively little research has explored how young children learn what's worth the effort. We all know that infants are keen observers of the social world, but they're not just idly watching; they are tiny learning machines. They can generalize such abstract concepts as causal relationships and social roles from just a few examples. Even a 15-month-old infant can outperform a high level computer in such tasks. Could infants also make broad generalizable inferences from a few examples when it comes to effort? If so, then maybe persistence isn't simply a character trait. Maybe it's flexible and adaptable based on social context.

To explore this question, we showed 15-month-old babies one of two things—an experimenter working hard to achieve two different goals, or an experimenter who effortlessly reached each goal. Then we introduced the baby to a novel music toy that seemed as if it could be activated by pushing a big button on top. The button could be pressed down, but didn't actually activate anything. Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button so that they heard the toy making music. We gave the babies the music toy and left the room. Then analysts who didn't know which condition each baby was in, watched video tapes of the experiment and counted how many times babies tried to activate the toy by pressing the button.

Across one study and a pre-registered duplication, babies who had seen an adult persist and succeed push the button about twice as many times as those who saw an adult effortlessly succeed. In other words, babies learned that effort was valuable after watching just two examples of an adult working hard and succeeding. Part of what's exciting about this finding is that the babies didn't just imitate the adult's actions. Instead, they generalized the value of effort to a novel task. The experimenter never demonstrated pushing a button or trying to make music. Instead, the babies learned from different examples of effortful actions that the new toy probably also required persistence.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say even our personal beliefs about effort can do?

options.text: Affect our attitude to novel tasks.
Distinguish us in the social world.
Outweigh IQ in importance.
Impact academic achievements.

questions.shortExplanation: Even our personal beliefs about efforts can affect academic outcomes.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Impact academic achievements.

【定位】 Even our personal beliefs about efforts can affect academic outcomes.

甚至连我们对努力的个人信念，都能影响学业成果。

【信号】 题干原词复现 + Even 强调。录音 Even our personal beliefs about efforts can affect academic outcomes. 几乎照搬了题干的 personal beliefs about effort，又用 Even 加重语气提示"这点尤其值得注意"——题干关键词原样出现加上 Even 的强调，就是答案句的信号。

【替换】 affect academic outcomes↔ Impact academic achievements. 近义词整体替换

【排除】 A) 张冠李戴

Affect our attitude to novel tasks. 盗用了录音后文 a novel music toy / a novel task 里的 novel（新的）一词，但那是讲婴儿对"新玩具 / 新任务"，和本题"个人信念能做什么"无关，属张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： a novel music toy B) 原词陷阱

Distinguish us in the social world. 借了录音 keen observers of the social world 里的 social world，但原文是说"婴儿是社会世界的敏锐观察者"，根本没说个人信念能"在社会中区分我们"，是盗用原词的答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： keen observers of the social world C) 偷换概念

Outweigh IQ in importance. 抓住了录音里的 IQ，但原文说自控力与坚持是 independence of IQ（独立于 IQ、与 IQ 无关），并没有说"比 IQ 更重要"，把"无关"偷换成了"更重要"，是与原文不符的偷换。 借⽤原⽂： independence of IQ

questions.prompt: How did the researchers turn on the music toy in their experiment?

options.text: By pressing a hidden button.
By pushing a big button on top.
By pressing two buttons at the same time.
By helping the babies push the right button.

questions.shortExplanation: Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button so that they heard the toy making music.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） By pressing a hidden button.

【定位】 Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button so that they heard the toy making music.

在婴儿看不到的地方，我们用一个隐藏的按钮打开了音乐玩具，好让他们听到玩具发出音乐。

【信号】 题干动词 turned on 原样复现。录音 we turned on the music toy with a hidden button 把题干的 turn on the music toy 原样念出，紧跟 with a hidden button 交代方式 ——题干动作短语原样出现的那句，就是答案句。

【替换】 turned on the music toy with a hidden button↔By pressing a hidden button. with a hidden button 概括为 by pressing it

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 By pushing a big button on top. 整句盗自录音 pushing a big button on top，但原文说这个顶上的大按钮"按得下去却其实不启动任何东西"（didn't actually activate anything），它是给婴儿试的假按钮，不是研究者打开玩具的方式，是典型原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： a big button on top, but didn't actually activate anything C) 未提及

By pressing two buttons at the same time. 里"同时按两个按钮"在录音中完全没有出现 ——原文只有一个隐藏按钮和一个假的大按钮，没有"两个一起按"的说法，属未提及。 D) 与原文相反

By helping the babies push the right button. 与录音相反：原文是研究者 Out of sight of the babies（背着婴儿）自己用隐藏按钮打开，并非"帮婴儿按对按钮"，把"偷偷开"歪曲成"协助婴儿按"，与原文不符。 借⽤原⽂： Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button

questions.prompt: What could the infants do in the experiment according to the speaker?

options.text: Perform difficult tasks successfully just by observing how adults acted.
Make generalizable inferences about persistence from a few examples.
Adapt themselves to different social contexts.
Work hard to interact with experimenters.

questions.shortExplanation: They can generalize such abstract concepts as causal relationships and social roles from just a few examples. Could infants also make broad generalizable inferences from a few examples when it comes to effort?
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Make generalizable inferences about persistence from a few examples.

【定位】 They can generalize such abstract concepts as causal relationships and social roles from just a few examples. Could infants also make broad generalizable inferences from a few examples when it comes to effort?

他们能仅凭少数几个例子，就归纳出因果关系、社会角色这类抽象概念。那么，当涉及努力时，婴儿是否也能从少数例子中做出宽泛而可推广的推断呢？

【信号】 选项长句原话复现 generalizable inferences from a few examples。录音 make broad generalizable inferences from a few examples 几乎照搬了选项 B 的措辞，from just a few examples 又反复强调"只凭少数例子"——选项学术长句在录音原话里成段复现，就是答案信号；第4段 they generalized the value of effort 进一步证实婴儿确实做到了这种推广。

【替换】 make broad generalizable inferences from a few examples ↔ Make generalizable inferences about persistence from a few examples. 近乎原词复现 + persistence 同义补足

【排除】 A) 过度推断

Perform difficult tasks successfully just by observing how adults acted. 借了录音 keen observers / observing 的"观察"之意，但原文说的是婴儿从观察中"做出推断、推广努力的价值"，并没说他们"光靠看就成功完成难任务"；successfully、just by 把原意夸大了一截，是过度推断。 借⽤原⽂： infants are keen observers of the social world C) 偷换概念

Adapt themselves to different social contexts. 盗用录音 based on social context 的 social context，但原文是说"坚持也许是灵活的、随社会情境而变"（指坚持这一特质的性质），不是说"婴儿能让自己适应不同社会情境"，主体和意思都被偷换。 借⽤原⽂： it's flexible and adaptable based on social context D) 张冠李戴

Work hard to interact with experimenters. 借了录音里反复出现的 experimenter（实验者）和 effort / work hard 之意，但原文说"努力工作"的是录像里的成人 an adult working hard，婴儿是观察者，录音从没说婴儿"努力去和实验者互动"，是张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： an adult working hard

items.title: 2025年6月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 2
items.transcript:
If chronic lateness has taken over your life and turned into a defining trait of who you are, it's likely that you're losing out on job offers, recreational opportunities, friendships, and more. If you are showing up late to your own life, get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes.

When you have to be somewhere, try to arrive 15 to 30 minutes before you need to. If you always run late, that means you must be failing to account for something you always do. Anticipate that by giving yourself extra time to arrive. Keep track of whether or not you actually do arrive early. You might find that leaving early gets you to places exactly on time.

Set two alarms. Set one alarm that lets you know it's time to drop what you're doing and a second alarm that means you need to walk out the door. Obey the alarms. As soon as the first alarm goes off, stop what you're doing. If it's something you'll be coming back to, like a project for work, make a note to remind yourself where you left off. Grab everything you need and make sure you know how to get where you're going. Aim to be out the door and on your way before the second alarm rings. This will only work if you take the alarms seriously, so make sure you react as soon as you hear them.

Prepare for the day ahead. Have all of your notes and materials organized well in advance of each event, so that all you have to do is grab them and go when it's the actual day. If mornings are a struggle for you, do as much as you can to ready yourself the night before. Before you go to bed, lay out your clothes and pack your bag for the next day.

Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings. It soon becomes unbearable to shift between one meeting and another without space in between. If you overschedule yourself, however, you'll arrive late as soon as you hit a bump. As well as giving you space, this time also acts as a buffer between events, which can be borrowed from, should you be held up in a prior meeting, allowing you to still get to the next one on time. Calculate transit time between activities and then add 10 to 30 minutes for unexpected delays.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's purpose of giving this talk?

options.text: Offering advice on overcoming habitual lateness.
Exemplifying various recreational opportunities.
Scrutinizing individuals' defining traits.
Suggesting ways for setting priorities.

questions.shortExplanation: If chronic lateness has taken over your life and turned into a defining trait of who you are, it's likely that you're losing out on job offers, recreational opportunities, friendships, and more. If you are showing up late to your own life, get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （目的题） Offering advice on overcoming habitual lateness.

【定位】 If chronic lateness has taken over your life and turned into a defining trait of who you are, it's likely that you're losing out on job offers, recreational opportunities, friendships, and more. If you are showing up late to your own life, get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes.

如果长期迟到已经占据了你的生活、变成你这个人的一个鲜明特征,那你很可能正在失去工作机会、休闲机会、友谊等等。如果你连自己的人生都总是迟到,那就把自己安排好、把准时放在首位、并解决背后的根本原因。

【信号】 篇首点题句。目的题的答案信号是"开头的总起句":首段先点出"chronic lateness"(长期迟到) 的危害,再用祈使句 get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes 给出全篇要教的方向,后面各段(设两个闹钟、前一晚准备、中间留时间)都是这句的展开,故它统领全篇、就是目的所在。

【替换】 chronic lateness↔ habitual lateness

同义词替换 get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes↔ Offering advice on overcoming 详述概括为"给建议"

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

Exemplifying various recreational opportunities. 盗用了首段的原词 recreational:录音里 recreational opportunities 只是迟到会"失去"的东西之一,被一笔带过,讲话根本不是在"举例各种休闲机会",属于把局部细节当主旨。 借⽤原⽂： recreational opportunities C) 原词陷阱

Scrutinizing individuals' defining traits. 盗用了首段的 a defining trait of who you are: 录音只是说"长期迟到会变成你的一个鲜明特征",并非要去"剖析人的个性特质",方向完全跑偏。 借⽤原⽂： a defining trait of who you are

D) 偷换概念

Suggesting ways for setting priorities. 借了 prioritize punctuality(把准时放首位)里的"priorit-"做文章:录音只把"优先准时"作为众多建议中的一句,全篇并非教"如何排优先级", 以偏概全。 借⽤原⽂： prioritize punctuality

questions.prompt: What should you do if mornings are a struggle for you?

options.text: Make the breakfast simpler.
Take the alarms seriously.
Ready yourself in the early dawn.
Get prepared the night before.

questions.shortExplanation: If mornings are a struggle for you, do as much as you can to ready yourself the night before. Before you go to bed, lay out your clothes and pack your bag for the next day.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Get prepared the night before.

【定位】 If mornings are a struggle for you, do as much as you can to ready yourself the night before. Before you go to bed, lay out your clothes and pack your bag for the next day.

如果早晨对你来说很吃力,那就尽量在前一晚把自己准备好。睡觉前,把衣服摆好、把第二天的包收拾好。

【信号】 条件句原话复现+其后应对。答案信号是题干条件句在录音里的几乎原话复现:录音 If mornings are a struggle for you 与题干一字不差,紧跟其后的 do as much as you can to ready yourself the night before 就是给出的做法,据"条件句之后即答案"锁定此句。

【替换】 ready yourself the night before↔Get prepared the night before.

近义短语替换

【排除】 A) 未提及

Make the breakfast simpler. 听着像应对"早晨吃力"的合理办法,但录音讲早晨那段只说"前一晚摆衣服、收包",从未提及早餐或把它简化,属凭常识脑补、原文未提。 B) 张冠李戴

Take the alarms seriously. 盗用了第三段的 take the alarms seriously:那是"设两个闹钟"那条建议里的话,和本题"早晨吃力怎么办"不是同一条,被错接到这道题上。 借⽤原⽂： take the alarms seriously C) 与原文相反 Ready yourself in the early dawn. 把 ready yourself 的时间偷改成"清晨(early dawn)", 而录音明说是 ready yourself the night before(前一晚),时间点正好相反,正中第一步预读标出的 C/D 对立陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： ready yourself the night before

questions.prompt: According to the speaker, what can we do to combat unexpected delays?

options.text: Finish the prior task 30 minutes earlier.
Keep ourselves from hitting a bump.
Leave time in between activities.
Try to avoid possible hold-ups.

questions.shortExplanation: Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings. As well as giving you space, this time also acts as a buffer between events, which can be borrowed from, should you be held up in a prior meeting, allowing you to still get to the next one on time.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Leave time in between activities.

【定位】 Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings. As well as giving you space, this time also acts as a buffer between events, which can be borrowed from, should you be held up in a prior meeting, allowing you to still get to the next one on time.

学会在各项任务和会议之间留出时间。这段时间除了给你余地,还在各项活动之间起到缓冲作用——万一前一场会议把你拖住了,可以从这段时间里挪用,让你仍能准时赶到下一场。

【信号】 段首主张句+buffer 缓冲解释。答案信号是第五段段首的核心主张 Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings,其后用 acts as a buffer(充当缓冲)解释它正好能对付"被前一场拖住"的意外延误,与题干 combat unexpected delays 对上,据此锁定段首这句主张。

【替换】 leave time in between tasks and meetings ↔ Leave time in between activities. 上位词概括替换 acts as a buffer between events ↔ Leave time in between activities. 缓冲机制印证该做法

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

Finish the prior task 30 minutes earlier. 盗用了末句的数字 add 10 to 30 minutes for unexpected delays 里的"30 minutes":录音是说"为意外延误额外加留 10 到 30 分钟",并不是"把前一项任务提前 30 分钟完成",数字念到了、事却拼错了。 借⽤原⽂： add 10 to 30 minutes for unexpected delays B) 与原文相反

Keep ourselves from hitting a bump. 盗用了 you'll arrive late as soon as you hit a bump 里的"hit a bump":录音是说"一旦把日程排太满,碰到颠簸就会迟到",讲的是过度排期的后果,而非教你"避免碰到颠簸";颠簸是无法避免的,要做的是留缓冲,选项把原意拧反了。 借⽤原⽂： you'll arrive late as soon as you hit a bump D) 偷换概念

Try to avoid possible hold-ups. 只是把题干目标"应对意外延误"换个说法重述一遍(avoid hold-ups),并未给出录音真正提出的可操作做法;且录音 should you be held up 把"被拖住"当成会发生、需用缓冲化解的事,而非教你"避免"它,这是空泛复述目标的陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： should you be held up

items.title: 2025年6月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 3
items.transcript:
Do you think Bostonians put out the welcome mat? Do you find other cities to be more or less polite? Different cities have different feels for visitors. Some are friendly and open; some are formal and distant. Boston tends to seem hurried and sometimes a little rude. That's what some tourists have said. One study found that people here are less willing to volunteer to help strangers than those residents of other U.S. cities. Take a close look next time you're in Boston, and here are some of the things you'll probably see: people smoking in the subway stations despite the frequent reminders not to do so; pedestrians walking when the crosswalk lights say not to do so, ignoring the cars; car drivers speeding, making a loud noise with the horn and occasionally cursing at each other. Drivers who can't be bothered to find a place to park, but instead simply turn on their blinker and stop in the middle of the street.

Sometimes Bostonians seem like they're just too busy to be polite. Why is their city like that? Former U.S. representative Chester Atkins says it's because the Puritan founding fathers were themselves impatient and bad-tempered, and had little time for courtesy. That culture has carried down to the present day, he believes. Boston College professor Thomas O'Connor thinks a contributing factor is Boston's history as a city where each new group of immigrants was treated with suspicion and exclusion. That's given Boston a sense of clannishness and reserve, he thinks. The idea of a stranger greeting another stranger is simply not part of the local culture, he says. People will begin a conversation with someone they know, but not with a stranger. Ralph Whitehead, a professor of journalism at the University of Massachusetts at Amherst, thinks it's because Boston's upper class used manners to make class distinctions. By being snobbish about manners, Proper Bostonians made other people scornful of courtesy, he says.

Some say that's just the way Boston is and that the city will never change. Still, other cities with reputations for worse rudeness are trying hard to change their images. Paris is one example where people are trying to be friendly. New York City is another. There, the city is trying to persuade subway riders to be more considerate. If those cities can make the effort, maybe Boston should as well.

questions.prompt: What do visitors find about the cities they've been to?

options.text: Their lifestyles vary.
Their traits vary.
They have different customs.
They have different feels.

questions.shortExplanation: Different cities have different feels for visitors.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） They have different feels.

【定位】 Different cities have different feels for visitors.

不同的城市带给游客不同的感受。

【信号】 开篇点题句。这是第一段抛出两个问句后给出的第一句陈述 Different cities have different feels for visitors.，独白常在开头先点主题，它直接对应题干问的"游客的发现"，是答案句。

【替换】 different feels for visitors↔They have different feels. 近乎原句保留 feels

【排除】 A) 偷换概念

Their lifestyles vary. 把"feels"偷换成 lifestyles（生活方式），原文谈的是"感受"不是"生活方式"，属偷换概念。

B) 偷换概念

Their traits vary. 用 traits（特征）顶替原文的 feels，原文从未说城市"特征"不同，是换词制造的干扰。 C) 未提及

They have different customs. 的 customs（习俗）原文没有出现，属无中生有的替换项。

questions.prompt: What did one study find about Bostonians compared with residents of other U.S. cities?

options.text: They are not as willing to help strangers.
They are not as patient with one another.
They violate traffic rules more frequently.
They become more easily irritated in public.

questions.shortExplanation: One study found that people here are less willing to volunteer to help strangers than those residents of other U.S. cities. 一项研究发现，与美国其它城市的居民相比，这里的人更不愿意主动帮助陌生人。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） They are not as willing to help strangers.

【定位】 One study found that people here are less willing to volunteer to help strangers than those residents of other U.S. cities. 一项研究发现，与美国其它城市的居民相比，这里的人更不愿意主动帮助陌生人。

【信号】 study found 信号词。句首 One study found that 是题干 one study 的直接对应锚点， 其后跟的就是研究结论，是答案句。

【替换】 less willing to volunteer to help strangers↔They are not as willing to help strangers.

less=not as 同义改写

【排除】 B) 答非所问

not as patient with one another 里的 patient 来自后文 too busy to be polite 的语境联想，但研究句说的是"帮陌生人"不是"彼此有无耐心"，把别处内容安到研究结论上，属答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： Sometimes Bostonians seem like they're just too busy to be polite. C) 原词陷阱

violate traffic rules more frequently 盗用第一段后半罗列的现象——pedestrians walking when the crosswalk lights say not to、car drivers speeding，但这些是说话人列举的所见，不是 one study 的结论，属原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： car drivers speeding, making a loud noise with the horn D) 过度推断

more easily irritated in public 由后文 cursing、rude 的氛围引申而来，但研究句并未说波士顿人"更易动怒"，是顺着语气过度推断。 借⽤原⽂： occasionally cursing at each other

questions.prompt: What does Thomas O'Connor say about the idea of strangers greeting one another?

options.text: It was practiced by Boston's founding fathers.
It is not deemed exotic by Proper Bostonians.
It was adopted by Boston's upper class.
It is not part of Boston's local culture.

questions.shortExplanation: The idea of a stranger greeting another stranger is simply not part of the local culture, he says.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） It is not part of Boston's local culture.

【定位】 The idea of a stranger greeting another stranger is simply not part of the local culture, he says.

他说，陌生人跟陌生人打招呼这种事，根本就不属于本地文化。

【信号】 he says 归属信号。这句以 he says 收尾，he 回指本段正在论述的 Thomas O'Connor， 把观点准确归到他名下；其内容直接回答"陌生人打招呼"与文化的关系，是答案句。

【替换】 simply not part of the local culture↔It is not part of Boston's local culture. near-原句对应

【排除】 A) 张冠李戴

practiced by Boston's founding fathers 盗用了 the Puritan founding fathers，但那是 Chester Atkins 的说法、且讲的是性情急躁，与 O'Connor 谈"陌生人打招呼"无关，属张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： the Puritan founding fathers were themselves impatient and bad-tempered B) 原词陷阱

not deemed exotic by Proper Bostonians 把 Proper Bostonians 这个原词拼到不存在的 exotic 上，Proper Bostonians 出自 Whitehead 谈"以礼仪划阶级"的论述，原文从无"是否异域风"之说，属原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： Proper Bostonians made other people scornful of courtesy C) 张冠李戴 adopted by Boston's upper class 盗用 Boston's upper class used manners to make class distinctions，那是 Whitehead 的说法、讲的是上层用礼仪划分阶级，并非 O'Connor 论"陌生人打招呼"，属张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： Boston's upper class used manners to make class distinctions

questions.prompt: What does the speaker think Boston should do?

options.text: Stick to its own way of showing courtesy to strangers.
Follow the examples set by Paris and New York City.
Learn from the world's major cities in promoting tourism.
Take pride in its history and adhere to its cultural tradition.

questions.shortExplanation: Paris is one example where people are trying to be friendly. New York City is another. There, the city is trying to persuade subway riders to be more considerate. If those cities can make the effort, maybe Boston should as well.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （推断题） Follow the examples set by Paris and New York City.

【定位】 Paris is one example where people are trying to be friendly. New York City is another. There, the city is trying to persuade subway riders to be more considerate. If those cities can make the effort, maybe Boston should as well.

巴黎就是一个例子，那里的人在努力变得友善。纽约也是，那座城市正设法说服地铁乘客多为他人着想。如果这些城市都能努力，那么也许波士顿也应该这么做。

【信号】 末句 maybe…should 表态。结尾 If those cities can make the effort, maybe Boston should as well. 用条件句含蓄给出说话人的建议——既然巴黎、纽约都在努力改，波士顿也应仿效，是承载态度的答案句。

【替换】 Paris is one example ↔ Follow the examples set by Paris and New York City. 举例即榜样 maybe Boston should as well ↔ Follow the examples

should as well=该照做

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

Stick to its own way of showing courtesy to strangers 是"保持原样"，恰与说话人"也该努力改"的劝告相反；它呼应的是上文 the city will never change，但那是"some say"的观点、被 Still 一转否掉了。 借⽤原⽂： Some say that's just the way Boston is and that the city will never change. C) 未提及

Learn from the world's major cities in promoting tourism 借用了"向大城市学"的影子， 但原文谈的是变友善、有礼，从未提"promoting tourism（推广旅游）"，属未提及。

D) 与原文相反

Take pride in its history and adhere to its cultural tradition 盗用前文 Boston's history 等词，主张"守住历史与传统"，与说话人"该像巴黎纽约一样去改"正好相反，属与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： Boston's history as a city where each new group of immigrants was treated with suspicion

items.title: 2025年6月六级第2套 · 长对话 1
items.transcript:
W: We are down to two candidates for one position, and we need to decide by the end of the day in order to finalize this whole procedure.

M: Yes, but it isn't an easy choice to make. Both applicants are quite strong.

W: Let's get to it, then. Both of them went to good universities, and both of them studied business-related subjects. So academically, I'd say they're pretty much the same. What do you think?

M: I would agree, yes. The only difference worth noting, perhaps, is that it looks like Rachel scored moderately stronger grades throughout high school and university. But as I said, only a tiny bit higher than Peter.

W: That's true, and worth noting. Thank you. In addition, Rachel interviewed very well. I thought she came across as bright and alert.

M: Yes. She asked some very good questions about the position and the company, which made me think she is very keen about the job.

W: I thought so, too. Now, let's look at Peter's interview performance. I thought he also did very well. He came across as respectful and professional, wouldn't you say? Calm and poised. Very mature for his age.

M: Exactly. In my notes, I wrote that he seemed composed and in control of his emotions. I think he definitely looked more mature than Rachel.

W: Interesting. So, we agree that Rachel appeared inexperienced and less mature than Peter, even though both candidates are the same age and have practically no work experience.

M: When comparing them side by side, yes, Peter seemed more self-assured somehow. Maybe it was something about their body language.

W: Sure. Maybe he was simply less nervous.

M: Maybe. Who knows? To be honest, I think I like Rachel better.

W: Hmm. Really? I think I like Peter.

M: Ah, well. If there's a tie, and we can't come to an agreement, then we'll take it to John and let him cast the deciding vote.

questions.prompt: Why does the man think it is difficult to make the decision?

options.text: They have to make a choice by the end of the day.
Both candidates are very keen on getting the job.
They hold different views on the procedure.
Both candidates are quite competitive.

questions.shortExplanation: M: Yes, but it isn't an easy choice to make. Both applicants are quite strong.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Both candidates are quite competitive.

【定位】 M: Yes, but it isn't an easy choice to make. Both applicants are quite strong.

男：是啊，但这不是个容易做的选择。两位申请者都相当强。

【信号】 男士应答里的转折 + 给因。这是男士对女士「今天得定」的直接应答，but it isn't an easy choice to make 用 but 转出「不好选」，紧接 Both applicants are quite strong 给出原因——两人都很强，正是「难选」的答案句。

【替换】 Both applicants are quite strong↔Both candidates are quite competitive 近义改写 strong→competitive、applicants→candidates

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

A 取自女士开场 we need to decide by the end of the day 的「by the end of the day」，但那是「期限」而非「难以抉择的原因」；问的是 Why difficult，时间紧不是男士给出的理由，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： we need to decide by the end of the day B) 张冠李戴

「很想要这份工作」对应录音后面 she is very keen about the job，那是评价 Rachel 的，且只针对一人；本题问男士为何觉得难选，他给的因是「两人都强」，不是「都很想要」，B 张冠李戴又答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： she is very keen about the job

C) 未提及录音里两人对「流程」并无分歧，finalize this whole procedure 只是说要走完流程，并没有说「对 procedure 持不同看法」；C 借 procedure 一词虚构了一个原文没有的分歧。 借⽤原⽂： finalize this whole procedure
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What do the speakers say may be worth noting?

options.text: Both Rachel and Peter came across as respectful and professional.
Rachel scored moderately higher grades than Peter at school.
Both Rachel and Peter excelled in their academic pursuit.
Peter appeared slightly stronger than Rachel physically.

questions.shortExplanation: M: The only difference worth noting, perhaps, is that it looks like Rachel scored moderately stronger grades throughout high school and university. But as I said, only a tiny bit higher than Peter. 男：唯一也许值得一提的差别，是看起来 Rachel 在整个高中和大学的成绩略好一些。但正如我说的，只比 Peter 高出一点点。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Rachel scored moderately higher grades than Peter at school.

【定位】 M: The only difference worth noting, perhaps, is that it looks like Rachel scored moderately stronger grades throughout high school and university. But as I said, only a tiny bit higher than Peter. 男：唯一也许值得一提的差别，是看起来 Rachel 在整个高中和大学的成绩略好一些。但正如我说的，只比 Peter 高出一点点。

【信号】 明示标记 difference worth noting。男士直接说 The only difference worth noting， 与题干 worth noting 字面对应，是教科书式的答案信号；其后 Rachel scored moderately stronger grades 加上 only a tiny bit higher than Peter 就是要抓的内容。

【替换】 Rachel scored moderately stronger grades throughout high school and university↔ Rachel scored moderately higher grades than Peter at school

stronger grades=higher grades，程度词原样保留 only a tiny bit higher than Peter↔moderately higher grades than Peter

a tiny bit higher印证「略高」

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

A 的 respectful and professional 直接取自女士评 Peter 的 He came across as respectful and professional，是真听到的原词；但那是夸 Peter 一人的面试表现，并非两人都如此，且不是被点为「worth noting」的那点，属原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： He came across as respectful and professional C) 与原文相反

录音强调 only a tiny bit higher，仅是「略高」；C 的 excelled（出类拔萃）且说「两人都」学业杰出，把程度从「略」拔高到「极」、把范围从「Rachel 略胜」改成「两人皆优」，与原文程度相反。 借⽤原⽂： only a tiny bit higher than Peter D) 未提及

录音通篇比的是成绩、面试表现、成熟度，从未提到 physically（体格）；D 把 stronger 偷换成「身体上更强」，是录音根本没说的维度。

questions.prompt: According to the man, what might account for Peter appearing somewhat more self-assured than Rachel?

options.text: His use of body language.
His accumulation of experience.
His unusual state of mind.
His knowledge about the company.

questions.shortExplanation: M: When comparing them side by side, yes, Peter seemed more self-assured somehow. Maybe it was something about their body language. 男：把他们并排比较时，是的，Peter 不知怎的显得更自信。也许跟他们的肢体语言有关。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） His use of body language.

【定位】 M: When comparing them side by side, yes, Peter seemed more self-assured somehow. Maybe it was something about their body language. 男：把他们并排比较时，是的，Peter 不知怎的显得更自信。也许跟他们的肢体语言有关。

【信号】 男士的归因句 Maybe it was…。这是男士亲口给出的归因——Peter seemed more self-assured somehow 之后紧跟 Maybe it was something about their body language，用 Maybe it was… 引出原因，正是 account for 所问的答案句。

【替换】 Maybe it was something about their body language↔His use of body language

body language原词同指其运用

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

B 的 experience 来自录音 practically no work experience，但原文说的是「两人几乎都没有工作经验」，恰恰不是经验造成差异；B 把「没有经验」偷成「经验的积累」，听到 experience 就选即落坑。 借⽤原⽂： practically no work experience C) 偷换概念

录音说 Peter 显得 composed and in control of his emotions（沉着、控制情绪），是正面的镇定，并非 unusual state of mind（异常心态）；C 把镇定歪曲成「异常」，且不是男士给的归因，原文未提此因。 借⽤原⽂： composed and in control of his emotions D) 张冠李戴

D 的 knowledge about the company 化用录音 asked some very good questions about the position and the company，但那是说 Rachel 问了好问题、显得很想要这份工作，针对的是 Rachel、回答的是「是否 keen」，与本题问 Peter 自信的归因无关。 借⽤原⽂： asked some very good questions about the position and the company
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the man say they will do if they can't reach an agreement?

options.text: Compare the candidates side by side again.
Ask the board to cast the deciding vote.
Find a way to break the tie next time.
Let John make the final decision.

questions.shortExplanation: M: Ah, well. If there's a tie, and we can't come to an agreement, then we'll take it to John and let him cast the deciding vote. 男：啊，好吧。如果出现平局、我们没法达成一致，那我们就把它交给 John，让他来投决定票。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Let John make the final decision.

【定位】 M: Ah, well. If there's a tie, and we can't come to an agreement, then we'll take it to John and let him cast the deciding vote. 男：啊，好吧。如果出现平局、我们没法达成一致，那我们就把它交给 John，让他来投决定票。

【信号】 条件句 If…then 的对策落点。男士用 If there's a tie, and we can't come to an agreement, then we'll take it to John 给出明确的 If…then 对策；句中专有人名 John 是强定位信号，then 后的动作即答案。

【替换】 take it to John and let him cast the deciding vote↔Let John make the final decision cast the deciding vote=make the final decision

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

A 的 compare side by side 取自男士早前的 When comparing them side by side，确是原词；但那是描述他们之前已做的对比，而非「谈不拢时的对策」，问的是 if can't agree 怎么办，A 时态与问点都不符。 借⽤原⽂： When comparing them side by side B) 偷换概念

B 的 cast the deciding vote 正是录音原词 cast the deciding vote，极具迷惑；但录音里投决定票的是 John 一个人，B 却说交给 the board（董事会）投票，把「个人 John」偷换成「集体 board」。 借⽤原⽂： take it to John and let him cast the deciding vote C) 偷换概念

C 的 break the tie 借用录音 If there's a tie 的 tie 一词，但录音对平局的对策是「这次就交给 John」，C 却说「找办法在下次打破平局」，把「当下交 John」偷改成「留待下次」，时点与做法都对不上。 借⽤原⽂： If there's a tie, and we can't come to an agreement

items.title: 2025年6月六级第2套 · 长对话 2
items.transcript:
M: We're here with Clementine Ortega, head designer of the private fashion label L'Orange, to discuss her latest collection. Ms. Ortega, how would you describe this season's look?

W: To be honest, my preferred style has always been on the ambiguous side, and I think this collection is even more so. I try not to adhere to social norms and expectations. Rather, I always try to incorporate something slightly absurd into my aesthetic.

M: The assortments of accessories in this collection have had quite the impact on critics. The dazzling cape deployed at the end of the show, for example, bewildered many in the audience. What was your inspiration for this piece?

W: Over the summer, I traveled through rural mountain villages throughout Asia in search of handicrafts to decorate my new studio with. The embroidery done by the women in a particular village was so exquisite. I couldn't stop thinking about it. Trying to recreate their designs would have been futile. So instead, I applied my own eccentric approach. Using glitter, I drew similar intricate patterns onto the velvet cape. This ended up in the glamorous, luminous look that concluded the show.

M: It was indeed majestic, and yet, dare I say, masculine at the same time.

W: Well, yes, that was intentional. I like to merge styles that are often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum. Hence, the sparkling cape was paired with a traditional power suit you would typically see in a business setting. It was sensational, if I do say so myself.

M: Spectacular for sure! A stunning show all around. Going against stereotypes, the incorporation of indigenous aspects, along with your underlying signature touch, made this collection a statement of the season. You have proven yourself a formidable young designer, and we can't wait to see what creations you come up with next.

questions.prompt: What are the speakers mainly talking about?

options.text: The private label "L'Orange".
The woman's latest collection.
This season's new fashion.
The head designer's role.

questions.shortExplanation: We're here with Clementine Ortega, head designer of the private fashion label L'Orange, to discuss her latest collection. 我们今天请到了私人时装品牌 L'Orange 的首席设计师 Clementine Ortega，来聊聊她的最新系列。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （主旨题） The woman's latest collection.

【定位】 We're here with Clementine Ortega, head designer of the private fashion label L'Orange, to discuss her latest collection. 我们今天请到了私人时装品牌 L'Orange 的首席设计师 Clementine Ortega，来聊聊她的最新系列。

【信号】 开场引入语点题。记者开场白 to discuss her latest collection 直接交代了"今天来谈什么"，访谈类对话的中心话题几乎都由开场引入句给出，这就是答案句。

【替换】 to discuss her latest collection↔The woman's latest collection.

her=the woman 指代对应

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

录音确实念到品牌名 the private fashion label L'Orange，但它只是介绍设计师身份时的背景，全程没有围绕"这个品牌"展开，是听到原词就想选的原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： the private fashion label L'Orange C) 偷换概念

记者后面问过 this season's look，C 借这个词把话题偷换成"本季新潮流"这种行业泛论； 可对话谈的始终是"她个人的这一系列"，不是整个时尚界的趋势。 借⽤原⽂： this season's look D) 未提及

录音用 head designer 介绍她的职位，D 借此说成"首席设计师的职责"；但全段没有一句在谈"这个职位要干什么"，是抓住头衔词的过度发挥。 借⽤原⽂： head designer

questions.prompt: What does the woman say she always tries to incorporate into her aesthetic?

questions.shortExplanation: Rather, I always try to incorporate something slightly absurd into my aesthetic.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Something slightly absurd.

相反，我总是试着把一点略显荒诞的东西融入我的审美。

【信号】 I always try to 是直接应答。被问者女设计师用 I always try to incorporate something slightly absurd 直接讲出她总加入的东西，主语+always 的自述句正是题干所问，是答案句。

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

录音里 I try not to adhere to social norms 是她要"避开"的东西，A 却说她要加入"反映社会规范"的东西，正好把否定听成了肯定。 借⽤原⽂： I try not to adhere to social norms B) 与原文相反

D) 原词陷阱录音里 my preferred style has always been on the ambiguous side 说的是她整体风格偏"含糊"，D 借 ambiguous 这个原词来答"她加入了什么"，但题问的是 incorporate 进去的具体东西（absurd），答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： my preferred style has always been on the ambiguous side

options.text: Merge styles often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum.

questions.shortExplanation: I like to merge styles that are often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum. 我喜欢把那些常常处于时尚光谱两端的风格融合到一起。

【信号】 I like to 直陈偏好。I like to merge styles that are often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum 用 I like to 直接说出她的偏好，正中题干，是答案句。

majestic 和 masculine 是男主持人 masculine at the same time 给出的观感评价，C 盗用这两个原词，把"别人对作品的评价"伪装成"她喜欢做的事"，张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： masculine at the same time D) 原词陷阱

【定位】 we can't wait to see what creations you come up with next. 我们迫不及待想看看你接下来会创作出什么新作品。

【信号】 结尾 can't wait 表期待。男方在结尾说 we can't wait to see what creations you come up with next，can't wait to see 就是"期待"的强信号，是答案句。

【替换】 to see what creations you come up with next↔ Seeing the woman's new creations.

items.title: 2025年6月六级第2套 · 听力篇章 1
items.transcript:
Pet dogs can often readily understand a wide range of their owners' commands and gestures, but are these abilities inborn or are they exclusively learned through training? To find out, a new study examined whether stray dogs could understand human gestures. The study revealed that 80% of participating dogs successfully followed pointing gestures to a specific location despite having never received prior training. The results suggest that dogs can understand complex gestures by simply watching humans. This could have implications in reducing conflict between stray dogs and humans.

Dogs were domesticated 10,000 to 15,000 years ago. This means they are probably the oldest domesticated animals on the planet. Humans then bred dogs with the most desirable and useful traits so that they could function as companions and workers. This resulted in domesticated dogs that are highly responsive to human commands and gestures. However, it was not clear whether dogs understand us through training alone, or whether this was an inherent ability. Why does this matter?

Stray dogs are a common feature in cities around the world. They may observe and occasionally interact with people, but such dogs have never been trained, and are behaviorally "wild". Conflicts between stray dogs and humans are a problem. Understanding how humans shape stray dogs' behavior may help alleviate this problem. According to the researchers of the new study, stray dogs are intelligent creatures. They closely observe humans and use their understanding of us to make a decision. Treating stray dogs with sensitivity and respect, and giving them space, the researchers assert, can reduce much conflict.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about 80% of participating dogs in the new study?

options.text: They could readily recognize their owner simply by looking.
They could understand the implications of human commands.
They could be domesticated to act as our companions.
They could follow pointing gestures without training.

questions.shortExplanation: The study revealed that 80% of participating dogs successfully followed pointing gestures to a specific location despite having never received prior training. 研究表明，80% 参与实验的狗在从未接受过任何训练的情况下，成功跟随指点手势找到了特定地点。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） They could follow pointing gestures without training.

【定位】 The study revealed that 80% of participating dogs successfully followed pointing gestures to a specific location despite having never received prior training. 研究表明，80% 参与实验的狗在从未接受过任何训练的情况下，成功跟随指点手势找到了特定地点。

【信号】 数字 80% 即定位锚点。录音念到 80% of participating dogs 这个数字就是定位信号，紧跟其后的 successfully followed pointing gestures to a specific location despite having never received prior training 即承载答案的那句，听到数字就该锁定后半句。

【替换】 followed pointing gestures ↔ follow pointing gestures 近乎原词的同动作对应 despite having never received prior training ↔ without training

让步从句压缩成介词短语

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

A readily recognize their owner simply by looking 借了录音第 1 段开头 readily understand 里的 readily 一词，但录音说的是'轻易理解命令手势'，从未说'看一眼就认出主人'，是把听到的熟词嫁接到没说过的事上。 借⽤原⽂： readily understand a wide range of their owners' commands and gestures B) 偷换概念

B understand the implications of human commands 用了录音里的 commands，但 80% 那句讲的是'跟随手势找到地点'，并非'理解命令的言外之意（implications）'； implications 一词录音另有出处（讲研究意义），被挪来制造混淆。 借⽤原⽂： This could have implications in reducing conflict C) 张冠李戴 C domesticated to act as our companions 的 domesticated、companions 都出自录音第 2 段讲'家养狗被驯化成伴侣'，但第 9 题问的是新研究里的 80% 流浪狗，C 把'家养狗'的事安到了'实验流浪狗'头上。 借⽤原⽂： they could function as companions and workers

items.title: 2025年6月六级第2套 · 听力篇章 2
items.transcript:
Think your refrigerator is just one big box of evenly cold air? Not so! The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies from front to back, bottom to top and everywhere in between. Because of this, food product placement within the appliance is far more important than you probably realize.

The whole purpose of the modern refrigerator is to slow the growth of bacteria, which thrive in temperatures from 4.4 to 60 degrees Celsius. As a result, refrigerators are typically set at or below that low end to protect foods against bacteria. Although it might seem like time spent organizing the fridge will spoil your day, doing so will actually make it more user-friendly, easier to clean and food safety-conscious.

Those little bins on the inside of refrigerator doors are convenient, but they don't maintain a consistent temperature, so definitely refrain from putting perishable foods in there. The top area is not as cold as the bottom of the fridge, so save it for the foods that don't need extra-chilly temperatures. Store foods that are ready to eat or already cooked on the top shelf. The middle shelf is the most temperature-controlled part of the fridge, so place eggs here. Drinks and prepared foods can also live on the middle shelf if you ran out of room up top. The back of the bottom shelf is the coldest spot in the fridge, so store perishable dairy products here to keep them edible longer. Never store foods with high water content here, because the water within them can and will freeze, effectively ruining them.

questions.prompt: Why is food product placement within the fridge very important?

options.text: The temperature inside it varies from place to place.
Proper placement facilitates access to food products.
Its different shelves are designed for different purposes.
The space in an average fridge changes from top to bottom.

questions.shortExplanation: The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies from front to back, bottom to top and everywhere in between. Because of this, food product placement within the appliance is far more important than you probably realize.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） The temperature inside it varies from place to place.

【定位】 The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies from front to back, bottom to top and everywhere in between. Because of this, food product placement within the appliance is far more important than you probably realize.

普通冰箱内部的温度实际上从前到后、从下到上以及中间各处都不一样。正因如此，食物在冰箱内的摆放位置远比你以为的重要得多。

【信号】 Because of this 因果回指。Because of this 是答案信号：this 回指前一句讲的温度处处不同，紧接着说正因如此摆放才重要，所以前一句 The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies 就是位置重要的原因。

【替换】 The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies from front to back, bottom to top and everywhere in between

↔ The temperature inside it varies from place to place. 处处不同概括为因地而异

【排除】 B) 未提及

Proper placement facilitates access to food products. 说摆放是为了方便取放，但录音解释的原因只有温度因位置而异，全程没提取放是否方便，属于录音未提及的角度。

C) 原词陷阱

Its different shelves are designed for different purposes. 听起来很对，但它说的是层架被设计成不同用途，而录音第一段给的原因是温度因位置而异；它借后文反复出现的 shelf 字眼制造听到就想选的诱惑，却答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： The middle shelf is the most temperature-controlled part of the fridge D) 偷换概念

The space in an average fridge changes from top to bottom. 几乎照搬录音句式，却把变化的主语从温度换成了空间 space；录音说的是 The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies，变的是温度不是空间，属偷换核心概念。 借⽤原⽂： The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies from front to back, bottom to top and everywhere in between

To slow the rising of temperature in it. 借用了录音里反复出现的 temperature 字眼，把目的说成减缓升温；但录音明说目的是 to slow the growth of bacteria，减缓的是细菌生长不是温度上升，盗词却答错对象。 借⽤原⽂： to slow the growth of bacteria B) 与原文相反

Not so! D) 未提及 To keep the food cold as long as possible. 是凭常识容易选的诱饵，听起来冰箱不就是保冷吗；但录音点明的目的是抑制细菌生长，没说根本目的是尽量久保冷，属未提及的常识陷阱。

items.title: 2025年6月六级第2套 · 讲座与讲话 1
items.transcript:
My current research is mainly looking at factors like stress and how it affects our immune system. So the current projects that I'm quite excited about are looking at older people and factors that are important to them.

In one project we are looking at hip fracture in older people, which is a common event and we're trying to understand the impact of depression. Often people in hospital with a hip fracture develop depression, and these are the people that then go on to become feeble a lot more quickly than others. They get infections. Often these infections lead to death. So we're trying to slow down that progression to feebleness. So if we can better understand how these factors interact, then we can actually start doing something about it.

The impact that my research will have in Birmingham, first of all, is obviously for older people because these are the people that are having hip fractures and developing depression, and we're trying to improve their health and their quality of life. But this isn't just a problem in Birmingham or even in the UK. This is a problem globally. People are aging. There's a lot more people in the older generation who are living for longer but not necessarily staying healthy for a large part of their lives. So the last part of their life can often be full of ill health, and we're trying to understand factors that can contribute to the quality of life later on.

I think the thing that excites me most about my research is that it feels real and relevant. Lots of academics are probably very excited about their research, but it might not be that relevant to those around them. Whereas I feel that the work I do is relevant to everyone because everyone is aging. Health is an issue for everyone, regardless of their age, and what I'm trying to do is understand the factors that affect health and how we can improve the quality of life in people. So that's one of the things that really excites me about it. One of the other things is, rather than just taking one perspective, so rather than looking at aging and health just from the perspective of the psychologist, we are now bringing together a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints to actually look at the sort of different factors affecting health.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say is quite common among older people?

options.text: Chronic depression.
Growing feebleness.
Hip fracture.
Fatal infections.

questions.shortExplanation: In one project we are looking at hip fracture in older people, which is a common event and we're trying to understand the impact of depression. 在一个项目里，我们研究老年人的髋部骨折，这是一种常见的情况，我们想弄清抑郁对它的影响。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Hip fracture.

【定位】 In one project we are looking at hip fracture in older people, which is a common event and we're trying to understand the impact of depression. 在一个项目里，我们研究老年人的髋部骨折，这是一种常见的情况，我们想弄清抑郁对它的影响。

【信号】 which is a common event 直接点"常见"。答案句里 which is a common event（这是一种常见的情况）紧跟在 hip fracture in older people 之后，which 指代的正是 hip fracture，这个"常见"信号词把答案锁死在髋部骨折上。

【替换】 hip fracture in older people, which is a common event↔Hip fracture.

原词直接对应＋common 坐实

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

录音确实念到 depression，A 的 Chronic depression. 借此勾人，但原文说的是"骨折后常发展出抑郁"，抑郁是骨折带来的结果，且并未被 common 修饰，也没说是"chronic（慢性）"，答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： these are the people that then go on to become feeble a lot more quickly B) 原词陷阱

录音说 become feeble a lot more quickly，B 的 Growing feebleness. 取了这个 feeble，但原文讲的是骨折＋抑郁导致"更快变虚弱"这一恶化进程，并非在说"老年人中常见的是虚弱"，对不上题干的"常见"。 借⽤原⽂： become feeble a lot more quickly than others D) 原词陷阱

录音说 They get infections. Often these infections lead to death.，D 的 Fatal infections. 拼合了 infections 和"致命"，但原文 often 修饰的是"感染导致死亡"这一后续后果，处于"骨折→抑郁→虚弱→感染→死亡"链条末端，不是题干问的"常见之事"本身。 借⽤原⽂： Often these infections lead to death.

【信号】 excites me most 直接领出答案。答案句 the thing that excites me most about my research is that it feels real and relevant 里 excites me most 与题干 excites her most 是同一表态信号，is that 后面那句就是她给出的理由，定位精准。

【替换】 it feels real and relevant↔It feels real and relevant. 几乎原句搬入选项

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

录音确有 from the perspective of the psychologist，B 的 It contributes to psychology. 借 psychology 勾人，但原文是说"不再只从心理学家的单一视角看"，恰恰在强调超越心理学，而非"为心理学做贡献"，意思反向。 借⽤原⽂： rather than looking at aging and health just from the perspective of the psychologist C) 过度推断

录音说 Lots of academics are probably very excited about their research, but it might not be that relevant，C 的 It outcompetes lots of academics' research. 借 academics 勾人，但原文只是用别的学者作对比来突出"自己的研究更切身相关"，从未说"胜过／ outcompete"别人，属过度拔高。 借⽤原⽂： Lots of academics are probably very excited about their research, but it might not be that relevant to those around them

D) 原词陷阱

Birmingham 是录音里反复出现的地名（见 The impact that my research will have in Birmingham），D 的 It wins recognition outside of Birmingham. 借它勾人，但录音从没说研究"在伯明翰之外赢得认可"，只说这是"全球性问题"，把"问题是全球的"偷换成"研究在外地获认可"。 借⽤原⽂： But this isn't just a problem in Birmingham or even in the UK. This is a problem globally.

questions.prompt: How does the speaker approach her research project?

options.text: By bringing together experts old and young.
By counting on advanced modern technology.
By making full use of her expertise.
By combining multiple perspectives.

questions.shortExplanation: rather than just taking one perspective, so rather than looking at aging and health just from the perspective of the psychologist, we are now bringing together a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints to actually look at the sort of different factors affecting health. 与其只采取单一视角，与其只从心理学家的角度看待衰老与健康，我们现在汇集了许多不同的技术和许多不同的观点，来真正审视影响健康的各种因素。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） By combining multiple perspectives.

【定位】 rather than just taking one perspective, so rather than looking at aging and health just from the perspective of the psychologist, we are now bringing together a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints to actually look at the sort of different factors affecting health. 与其只采取单一视角，与其只从心理学家的角度看待衰老与健康，我们现在汇集了许多不同的技术和许多不同的观点，来真正审视影响健康的各种因素。

【信号】 rather than… we are now bringing together 对比转折。答案句用 rather than just taking one perspective 先否定"单一视角"，再以 we are now bringing together a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints 给出真正做法，"不是A而是B"的对比让 B 半句成为答案落点。

【替换】 a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints ↔ By combining multiple perspectives.

different viewpoints＝multiple perspectives 同义改写 bringing together ↔ combining

bring together＝combine 同义动词

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

录音确有 bringing together，A 的 By bringing together experts old and young. 借此勾人，但原文汇集的是 different techniques and viewpoints（技术与观点），不是"老少专家"，old and young 是套用别处的 older／young 之类印象，张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： we are now bringing together a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints B) 过度推断

录音说 a lot of different techniques（多种不同的技术手段），B 的 By counting on advanced modern technology. 借 techniques 勾人，但原文只说"多种技术手段"，从没说"依赖先进的现代科技"，advanced modern 是凭空添加的拔高。 借⽤原⽂： bringing together a lot of different techniques

C) 与原文相反

By making full use of her expertise. 即"充分用她自己（心理学家）的专长"，这正是录音用 rather than… just from the perspective of the psychologist 明确否定的单一视角做法，选项取了被否定的那一半，与原文意思相反。 借⽤原⽂： rather than looking at aging and health just from the perspective of the psychologist

items.title: 2025年6月六级第2套 · 讲座与讲话 2
items.transcript:
Americans are obsessed with celebrity chefs. We talk about them and try to eat like them. But could we learn something more from them than recipes and techniques?

According to market data enterprises, Americans spend nearly 10 billion dollars a year on self-help and personal-organization products. The market is huge, partly because most colleges and graduate schools don't teach basic organization, but cooking schools and professional kitchens do.

Perhaps the principles of cooking organization can be extended to help even those of us who aren't top chefs. The system that makes kitchens function is called "mise-en-place", or literally "put in place". It's a French phrase that means to gather and arrange the ingredients and tools needed for cooking.

But for many professional cooks, the phrase means something deeper. Some cooks call it their religion. It helps them coordinate vast amounts of labor and material, and transforms the lives of its practitioners through focus and self-discipline. Students at the culinary institute of America view it as a way of life. It's a way of concentrating their mind to only focus on the aspects that they need to be working on at the moment, to kind of rid themselves of distractions. And it's a habit that some students carry with them even when they're not in the kitchen. They mise-en-place their life. They set up their books for class. They set up their chef whites. They shine their shoes. They know everything that they need every step of the day.

Then how does one attain this level of organization? The key to high-level organization is the mindset. Cooks can easily do six hours of preparation for a three-hour dinner shift. "Mise-en-place forces cooks to account for every minute of their time and every movement. Every component of one single dish is in one single corner, so their hand literally moves inches," explains Dwayne Lipuma, an instructor at the culinary institute of America. "Once students set up their station, I should be able to cover up their eyes. And they should know that their knives are always here, their oil is always right here, their salt and pepper is always right here."

But practiced at its highest level, mise-en-place says that time is precious, resources are precious, space is precious, your self-respect and the respect of others are precious. Use them wisely. Isn't that a philosophy for our time?

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about most colleges and graduate schools in America?

options.text: They don't teach basic organization.
They don't focus on teaching techniques.
They attach little importance to recipes.
They hire very few distinguished chefs.

questions.shortExplanation: The market is huge, partly because most colleges and graduate schools don't teach basic organization, but cooking schools and professional kitchens do.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） They don't teach basic organization.

【定位】 The market is huge, partly because most colleges and graduate schools don't teach basic organization, but cooking schools and professional kitchens do.

这个市场之所以巨大，部分原因在于大多数大学和研究生院并不教授基本的组织方法，而烹饪学校和专业厨房却教。

【信号】 原因状语 because 引出的因果句。答案句由 partly because most colleges and graduate schools don't teach basic organization 这个 because 因果结构托出，讲者在解释“市场为何巨大”时正面说出了学校“不教什么”，这种交代原因的从句往往就是细节答案所在。

【替换】 most colleges and graduate schools don't teach basic organization↔ They don't teach basic organization.

把主语换成代词，其余几乎照搬

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

选项 They don't focus on teaching techniques. 借了录音开头 recipes and techniques 里的 techniques 制造熟耳感，但讲者从没说学校“不重视教技巧”，学校被说成不教的是 organization，不是 techniques，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： recipes and techniques C) 原词陷阱

选项 They attach little importance to recipes. 取了开头 recipes and techniques 的 recipes，但录音并未说学校“不重视食谱”，更没把 recipes 和大学挂钩，是借原词编出的无中生有。 借⽤原⽂： recipes and techniques D) 未提及

选项 They hire very few distinguished chefs. 用了贯穿全篇的 chefs 蹭话题，但录音通篇没提“学校聘用名厨多少”，hire very few distinguished chefs 完全是没听到的内容。 借⽤原⽂： celebrity chefs

questions.prompt: How do students of the culinary institute of America view "mise-en-place" or "put in place"?

options.text: It's unique to celebrity chefs.
It's a way of transformation.
It's too demanding for them.
It's a way of life to them.

questions.shortExplanation: Students at the culinary institute of America view it as a way of life.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （态度观点题） It's a way of life to them.

【定位】 Students at the culinary institute of America view it as a way of life.

美国烹饪学院的学生把它视为一种生活方式。

【信号】 被点名群体后紧跟的“view it as…”态度句。讲者点出 Students at the culinary institute of America 这一群体后，紧接 view it as a way of life 直接给出他们的看法，这种“某群人 + view/see it as……”的句子就是态度题的标准答案落点。

【替换】 view it as a way of life↔It's a way of life to them. view it as A 改写成 It's A to them

【排除】 A) 偷换概念

选项 It's unique to celebrity chefs. 借了开头 celebrity chefs 的熟词，但录音说把它当生活方式的是学生，不是名厨独有；unique（独有）这个范围限定录音根本没说，属偷换概念加原词诱选。 借⽤原⽂： celebrity chefs B) 答非所问

选项 It's a way of transformation. 取自录音 transforms the lives of its practitioners 的 transform，听起来很耳熟，但那句是讲者总述 mise-en-place 的功效，不是“学生怎么看它”的答案；题问的是学生的 view，答案句明确是 a way of life。 借⽤原⽂： transforms the lives of its practitioners

C) 过度推断选项 It's too demanding for them. 利用 focus and self-discipline 让人联想“很苛刻”，但录音从未说学生觉得它“太苛刻”，反而把它当生活方式正面接纳，too demanding 是凭印象的过度推断。 借⽤原⽂： focus and self-discipline

questions.prompt: What does the speaker advise us to do at the end of the talk?

options.text: Respect others so as to be respected.
Use time and resources in a wise way.
Cultivate a habit of self-discipline.
Learn from philosophers earnestly.

questions.shortExplanation: But practiced at its highest level, mise-en-place says that time is precious, resources are precious, space is precious, your self-respect and the respect of others are precious. Use them wisely.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） Use time and resources in a wise way.

【定位】 But practiced at its highest level, mise-en-place says that time is precious, resources are precious, space is precious, your self-respect and the respect of others are precious. Use them wisely.

但在最高层次上去实践，mise-en-place 告诉我们：时间是宝贵的，资源是宝贵的，空间是宝贵的，你的自尊和对他人的尊重都是宝贵的。要明智地使用它们。

【信号】 结尾的祈使劝告句“Use them wisely”。整段在罗列 time is precious, resources are precious 之后，以祈使句 Use them wisely. 收束，这句独立成句的劝告正是讲者在结尾给出的建议，是答案的落点。

【替换】 time is precious, resources are precious↔ Use time and resources in a wise way. 把要珍惜的对象同义搬进祈使句 Use them wisely. ↔ in a wise way wisely 改写成 in a wise way

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

选项 Respect others so as to be respected. 借了 your self-respect and the respect of others are precious 里的 respect，但录音只把“尊重”列为“宝贵之物”之一，最后的劝告是 Use them wisely（明智使用），并非“尊重别人以换取被尊重”，且 so as to be respected 是录音没有的因果，属原词陷阱加过度推断。 借⽤原⽂： your self-respect and the respect of others are precious C) 原词陷阱

选项 Cultivate a habit of self-discipline. 取自第四段 focus and self-discipline 的 self-discipline，这是前文描述 mise-en-place 作用时的词，不是结尾劝告；题问 at the end， 结尾讲者劝的是明智使用时间资源，不是培养自律。 借⽤原⽂： focus and self-discipline D) 偷换概念

选项 Learn from philosophers earnestly. 利用结尾 Isn't that a philosophy for our time? 的 philosophy 设套，但那只是反问“这难道不是我们时代的一种哲理吗”，并非叫人 “认真向哲学家学习”，philosophers 与 learn from 都是录音没有的捏造。 借⽤原⽂： Isn't that a philosophy for our time?
