items.title: 2025年6月六级第2套 · 讲座与讲话 3
items.transcript:
Why do we stop making goals for ourselves and stop progressing in life? One reason is the belief that we should accept who we are and not constantly strive to improve ourselves. The mistake we make with this is that whilst self-acceptance is imperative, it should actually be used as the basis for growth. When we're not growing, learning and seeking improvements in our lives, we tend to stagnate, accepting what is, and stop believing we can be better.

A key tool for creating goals and progressing, is using our imagination. Yet as is so often the case, by the time we've reached midlife, we've stopped dreaming about what we want to achieve and feel quite negatively about goal setting. Instead of feeling confidence, happiness and satisfaction from achieving our goals, we feel we are always falling short. That leads to disappointment, and we stop dreaming. We stop imagining the life we'd like to have or the person we'd like to be, quickly finding ourselves shattered by the pain of our reality.

Up until now, unless we work in the creative industry, we've found the idea of using "play" a bit childish. In the West, we're mostly operating from our heads, the rational mind. But it's beginning to be better understood, because using our imagination is actually one of the most powerful things we could ever do.

The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal is because the goal always changes and we're always adapting, whether we realize it or not. What happens, therefore, is that we end up feeling like we're never going to reach our goals. And herein lies one of the biggest misconceptions and reasons for failure, dissatisfaction and unhappiness. We measure against the goal, rather than where we've come from. Dan Sullivan calls this "the gap and the gain". We measure always against the goal, which we never feel we're reaching, rather than the gain, that is where we've come from. In measuring where we've come from, rather than where we're trying to get to, we see results. We see things we've taken for granted, or not noticed. It's a simple, yet profound change in perception, and what I love about it is the power it has to instantly shift us up a gear. It's so, so simple, yet has an immediate, positive impact on our thinking.

questions.prompt: What should self-acceptance be used as according to the speaker?

options.text: The motive for hard work.
The reason for stagnation.
The basis for self-improvement.
The justification for self-confidence.

questions.shortExplanation: The mistake we make with this is that whilst self-acceptance is imperative, it should actually be used as the basis for growth.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） The basis for self-improvement.

【定位】 The mistake we make with this is that whilst self-acceptance is imperative, it should actually be used as the basis for growth.

我们在这件事上犯的错误是：尽管自我接纳至关重要，但它其实应当被用作成长的基础。

【信号】 转折 whilst + 定性结构 used as。答案句先用让步 whilst self-acceptance is imperative （尽管自我接纳重要）退一步，再用 it should actually be used as the basis for growth 给出真正主张，actually 加重了转折后的落点，正是这句对 self-acceptance 做了定性。

【替换】 used as the basis for growth↔ The basis for self-improvement. growth = self-improvement 同义替换

【排除】 A) 未提及

The motive for hard work. 把 self-acceptance 说成『努力工作的动机』，原文只讲它是成长的基础，从未提 hard work，也未提 motive，属无中生有。

B) 原词陷阱 The reason for stagnation. 借用了原文 we tend to stagnate 的同根词 stagnation 制造耳熟，但原文说『不成长才会停滞』，stagnation 是不接纳成长的后果，绝非 self-acceptance 被用作的角色，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： we tend to stagnate

D) 偷换概念 The justification for self-confidence. 利用 self- 前缀与 C 的 self-improvement 混淆，但原文落点是 growth/improvement，不是 self-confidence，且 justification（理由）也非原文的 basis，属偷换概念。 借⽤原⽂： the basis for growth
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What do people tend to do when they have reached midlife?

options.text: Feel confidence, happiness and satisfaction.
Believe they have achieved their life goals.
Use a key tool for setting ambitious goals.
Stop imagining further progress in life.

questions.shortExplanation: Yet as is so often the case, by the time we've reached midlife, we've stopped dreaming about what we want to achieve and feel quite negatively about goal setting. ... We stop imagining the life we'd like to have or the person we'd like to be.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Stop imagining further progress in life.

【定位】 Yet as is so often the case, by the time we've reached midlife, we've stopped dreaming about what we want to achieve and feel quite negatively about goal setting. ... We stop imagining the life we'd like to have or the person we'd like to be.

然而正如常见的那样，到我们步入中年时，我们已经不再梦想自己想要实现什么，并对设定目标抱有相当负面的感受。……我们不再去想象自己想过的生活或想成为的人。

【信号】 转折 Yet + midlife 时间锚 + 重复 stop。Yet as is so often the case, by the time we've reached midlife 用 Yet 转折并点出时间锚 midlife，随后 we've stopped dreaming 与 We stop imagining the life we'd like to have 两次出现 stop，反复强调的负向行为正是答案落点。

【替换】 We stop imagining the life we'd like to have or the person we'd like to be↔ Stop imagining further progress in life.

stop imagining 原词 + 概括化 we've stopped dreaming about what we want to achieve↔ Stop imagining further progress in life. stop dreaming = stop imagining progress

【排除】 A) 与原文相反

Feel confidence, happiness and satisfaction. 三个词全部来自原文 Instead of feeling confidence, happiness and satisfaction from achieving our goals，但原文前面是 Instead of（而不是），意思恰恰是人们没有这些感受，选项却取了被否定的内容，是典型听到原词就选的陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： Instead of feeling confidence, happiness and satisfaction from achieving our goals B) 与原文相反

Believe they have achieved their life goals. 说人们相信已达成人生目标，而原文说中年时人们 feel we are always falling short（总觉得没达到），方向完全相反，属无中生有又反向。 借⽤原⽂： we feel we are always falling short C) 张冠李戴

Use a key tool for setting ambitious goals. 里 a key tool 来自第 2 段开头 A key tool for creating goals and progressing, is using our imagination，但那是作者讲『工具是什么』，并非说中年人会去用它；原文恰恰说中年时人们停止了想象，选项张冠李戴。 借⽤原⽂： A key tool for creating goals and progressing, is using our imagination
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: Why do we find ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal?

options.text: We feel we are always falling behind others.
We have to adapt to the ever-changing goal.
There are various misconceptions about goal setting.
There are always problems with the goal originally set.

questions.shortExplanation: The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal is because the goal always changes and we're always adapting, whether we realize it or not. 我们因没达成目标而恼火，问题在于：目标总在变化，而无论我们是否意识到，我们也总在不断适应。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） We have to adapt to the ever-changing goal.

【定位】 The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal is because the goal always changes and we're always adapting, whether we realize it or not. 我们因没达成目标而恼火，问题在于：目标总在变化，而无论我们是否意识到，我们也总在不断适应。

【信号】 因果结构 The problem with … is because。The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal is because the goal always changes 用 The problem … is because 直接给出原因，because 后的 the goal always changes and we're always adapting 就是答案句核心。

【替换】 the goal always changes and we're always adapting↔ We have to adapt to the ever-changing goal. always changes + always adapting → ever-changing + adapt

【排除】 A) 偷换概念

We feel we are always falling behind others. 借了原文反复出现的 always 与 falling 的语感（如 we feel we are always falling short），但加了 others（落后于他人）。原文讲的是和自己的目标比、和来路比，从未说和别人比，others 是凭空添加。 借⽤原⽂： we feel we are always falling short C) 原词陷阱

There are various misconceptions about goal setting. 搬用了原文 herein lies one of the biggest misconceptions 的 misconceptions，听着耳熟，但题目问的是『恼火的原因』，原因是 the goal always changes，而非泛泛地说『存在各种误解』，属听到原词就选的陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： herein lies one of the biggest misconceptions D) 偷换概念

There are always problems with the goal originally set. 借了原文 The problem with… 的 problem 一词，但原文说的是『恼火这件事的问题在于目标在变』，不是说『当初设的目标本身有毛病』，把问题归错了对象。 借⽤原⽂： The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say has an immediate positive impact on our thinking?

options.text: A noticeable change in the number of goals to achieve.
Measuring always against the gap rather than the gain.
Measuring where we've come from instead of measuring against the goal.
A proper conception of what we fail to notice in trying to achieve our goals.

questions.shortExplanation: We measure against the goal, rather than where we've come from. ... In measuring where we've come from, rather than where we're trying to get to, we see results. ... It's a simple, yet profound change in perception ... yet has an immediate, positive impact on our thinking.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Measuring where we've come from instead of measuring against the goal.

【定位】 We measure against the goal, rather than where we've come from. ... In measuring where we've come from, rather than where we're trying to get to, we see results. ... It's a simple, yet profound change in perception ... yet has an immediate, positive impact on our thinking.

我们对着目标来衡量，而不是衡量自己走过了多远。……当我们衡量自己走过了多远、而非衡量离要去的地方还差多少时，我们就看到了成果。……这是一种简单却深刻的认知转变…… 却对我们的思维有着即时而正面的影响。

【信号】 正面评价 profound/positive impact 指向 measuring where we've come from。has an immediate, positive impact on our thinking 这句的『它』回指前文反复强调的 In measuring where we've come from, rather than where we're trying to get to，作者用 profound、positive impact 正面定性的正是这种衡量来路的做法。

【替换】 measuring where we've come from, rather than where we're trying to get to ↔ Measuring where we've come from instead of measuring against the goal.

rather than = instead of，goal = where we're trying to get to

【排除】 A) 未提及

A noticeable change in the number of goals to achieve. 说『要达成的目标数量发生明显变化』，原文谈的是衡量基准的转变（量来路 vs 量目标），从未提目标的数量变化，属未提及。 B) 与原文相反

Measuring always against the gap rather than the gain. 搬用了原文术语 We measure always against the goal 与 gap/gain，但作者批评的恰恰是『总对着 gap/goal 量』、推崇的是量 gain（来路）。选项说『量 gap 而非 gain』正好取了被否定的一面，与原文相反。 借⽤原⽂： We measure always against the goal D) 偷换概念

A proper conception of what we fail to notice in trying to achieve our goals. 借了原文 things we've taken for granted, or not noticed 的 not noticed，拼成『对我们没注意到之物的正确认知』，但原文说有即时正面影响的是『衡量来路这一做法』本身，不是某种 conception，属偷换概念/过度拼凑。 借⽤原⽂： things we've taken for granted, or not noticed

items.title: 2026年6月六级第1套 · 长对话 1
items.transcript:
M: Welcome to "Business Matters". Today we have invited career development consultant Lucy Williams to talk about how to get ahead at work. Hi, Lucy. Many of us never seem to get promoted. Why is that? And what can we do about it?

W: One mistake people make is to limit communication only to their bosses. It's important to expand your network and include your co-workers.

M: But some of our co-workers are less senior to us. Is it really necessary to connect with them?

W: It's important not to underestimate your colleagues. Sometimes a job title might not clearly demonstrate the influence they may have.

M: Now many of us think that working hard creates a good impression, but this isn't always true, is it?

W: That's right. We should avoid trying to take on too much work and constantly staying late, just to show that you are committed.

M: I see. So setting expectations too high at the beginning can make us look bad if we don't maintain them.

W: Yeah, it's better to make sure you are putting in quality time instead of just a large quantity of time. And these efforts can easily be demonstrated by the results we achieve.

M: What about helping others at work? Should you try and go beyond your normal responsibilities and offer to help people with their projects?

W: Extend your assistance to those who need it, but only as long as your own work will not go unattended. If someone can benefit from your assistance or advice, help them out to gain their respect and trust.

M: But it goes without saying that you shouldn't act like a know-it-all, otherwise you'll appear arrogant.

W: Absolutely. Be humble, and you'll get a lot of time later on to show your genius.

items.transcript:
W: I think we first need to decide how to divide up the presentation responsibilities. From what I recall, the presentation consists of five parts, not including the introduction and conclusion. That would mean altogether, we need to allocate seven parts between the two of us.

M: So, we have the abstract, background research, the project design, the results and the discussion portions. As the abstract section only applies to the article, we needn't include it in the presentation. How would you suggest we dole out the rest?

W: How do you feel about handling the background bit? In this way, we can both discuss the part of the project that we devoted most of our time to.

M: Hold on a minute. You want me, the one who did the bulk of the task, to also do the majority of the presentation? The background research which was so meticulous took more than a month.

W: OK. OK. I get it. Quit your moaning. I appreciate the rigorous work ethic you applied to the research, but not the sarcasm that comes up every time I mention it. What do you think would be a fair arrangement?

M: I think the best arrangement would be to split the research into two parts: before-1980 and afterward. I would take the before-portion and you would be assigned the after-1980, leaving the project and results. I volunteer to describe the project. But as I struggled a bit with the statistics in the results section, how about you handling that?

W: That's agreeable to me. I propose we both handle the discussion section in parts along with the question and answer afterward, leaving only the introduction and conclusion.

M: I will take responsibility for the conclusion and put you in charge of the introduction. This will make it so that we alternate presenting, so as to avoid sounding monotonous to the audience.

items.title: 2026年6月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 1
items.transcript:
Makeup can do more than just change your appearance—it can also alter others' perceptions of you, for better or for worse. According to new research from the University of Stirling in Scotland, although both men and women perceive women who wear makeup as being of a higher status, men associate makeup with prestigious, positive qualities, while women view other women wearing makeup as being dominant and a potential threat.

The research showed that men and women both rated the faces with cosmetics as being more attractive, but only women rated made-up faces as being more dominant, while only men rated made-up faces as being higher in prestige.

A follow-up study investigated the root cause behind these differences in perception, and found that female-on-female jealousy seemed to be the main cause of the differences in perception. Women rating women with makeup said they would be more jealous of them and thought they would be more attractive to men than their non-makeup wearing counterparts.

Cosmetic products are good for more than just giving you a pretty face. It can be particularly useful for women to understand how wearing makeup alters others' perceptions of them in situations where they are trying to gain others' trust and admiration. At a job interview, knowing whether the hiring committee will consist of men or women might influence a female candidate's decision about wearing makeup. Whether the interviewers will view her as attractive, dominant and prestigious can affect the interviewers' actions and perhaps the outcome of the interview itself.

questions.prompt: What can makeup do according to new research from the University of Stirling in Scotland?

options.text: Alter others' perceptions of the wearer.
Win others' admiration for the wearer.
Enhance the wearer's confidence.
Change the wearer's appearance.

questions.shortExplanation: Makeup can do more than just change your appearance—it can also alter others' perceptions of you, for better or for worse. According to new research from the University of Stirling in Scotland, although both men and women perceive women who wear makeup as being of a higher status, men associate makeup with prestigious, positive qualities, while women view other women wearing makeup as being dominant and a potential threat.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Alter others' perceptions of the wearer.

【定位】 Makeup can do more than just change your appearance—it can also alter others' perceptions of you, for better or for worse. According to new research from the University of Stirling in Scotland, although both men and women perceive women who wear makeup as being of a higher status, men associate makeup with prestigious, positive qualities, while women view other women wearing makeup as being dominant and a potential threat.

化妆不仅能改变你的外貌——它还能改变他人对你的看法，无论好坏。根据苏格兰斯特林大学的新研究，尽管男性和女性都认为化妆的女性地位更高，但男性将化妆与有声望的积极品质联系在一起，而女性则认为化妆的其他女性更具主导性且是一种潜在威胁。

【信号】 主题句 + 研究来源句。答案信号来自段落开头的主题句 'Makeup can do more than just change your appearance—it can also alter others' perceptions of you'，其中 'it can also alter others' perceptions of you' 直接回应题干 'What can makeup do'；随后 'According to new research from the University of Stirling in Scotland' 进一步给出具体研究发现。

【替换】 alter others' perceptions of you↔Alter others' perceptions of the wearer.

同义改写：第二人称转第三人称

items.title: 2026年6月六级第1套 · 听力篇章 2
items.transcript:
You may have seen advertisements trumpeting methods of changing a habit that require absolutely no willpower whatsoever. But can you really change a bad habit or create a good one without willpower? To answer this question, we first have to ask: "What is willpower?" Most people, sadly, think of it only as the ability to clench their teeth and resist attractive temptations. In this view, willpower means self-denial and no fun. No wonder people hope to make changes without it.

I define willpower as "using only the thought of your motivators to control your actions." Let's say your motivators are "prevent diabetes" and "reach a healthy weight". So if you are at the all-you-can-eat buffet, you think about your motivator—avoid diabetes through weight loss—and you take small portions and avoid the dessert table.

So, amazingly enough, willpower begins with a thought—a bright idea—some way to improve your life or contribute to others. This bright idea is your motivator.

Doctor Walter Mischel, an expert on willpower skills, uses the expressive term "a burning goal". Whether you call it a motivator, a burning goal, or a bright idea, this idea is the force behind your willpower.

What sort of bright ideas—motivators—make for effective willpower? In fact, any goal that you value strongly counts. The list may include good health, self-respect, a better future for your family, a personal mission and being a role model for your child. All these can certainly drive a positive change.

【信号】 开篇直接陈述广告内容。录音开头用 advertisements trumpeting methods of changing a habit that require absolutely no willpower whatsoever 直接抛出广告的说法，随后才设问反驳，故首句即答案句。

【替换】 require absolutely no willpower whatsoever ↔ Those requiring no willpower at all. 同义替换：absolutely no ... whatsoever = no ... at all

【排除】 A) 未提及选项 Those involving no self-recognition. 中的 self-recognition 在录音中完全没有出现，属于无中生有。

B) 原词陷阱

items.title: 2026年6月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 1
items.transcript:
For many pregnant women, understanding what seafood is safe and healthy and what should be avoided because of mercury concerns comes with a lot of worrying. In part, that's because the federal government's advice on the matter, first issued in 2004, has long been criticized as vague. That guidance has included advice on how much seafood to eat, and which species pregnant and breastfeeding women should avoid over concerns about mercury contamination. But critics say the government advisory has done more harm than good, scaring many pregnant and breastfeeding women away from eating seafood altogether.

The problem is real. According to a spokesman for the Food and Drug Administration, or FDA for short, the agency analyzed fish consumption data from more than 1,000 pregnant women in the US and found that 21 per cent of them ate no fish whatsoever in the previous month. And those who did eat fish consumed far less than recommended by the dietary guidelines. Some 50 per cent ate less than two ounces a week and 75 per cent ate less than four ounces.

This week the FDA issued an update to the advice, listing more than sixty species in a chart that ranks fish as A Best Choice, Good Choice and Choices to Avoid. The goal is to make it easier for mothers-to-be to feel confident about the type of seafood they include in their diets. The new advice recommends consumers choose a variety of fish to eat, and it comes with an easy-to-understand illustration of what an appropriate portion size should be—four ounces for an adult and two ounces for children aged four to seven.

And while expectant mothers have long been warned to stay away from shark and four other particular types of fish from the Gulf of Mexico, now there are three new species on the list of what to avoid. But not everyone is thrilled with the new advice. Critics say the new advice doesn't always agree with the agency's own scientific findings. While mercury is of great concern when people are talking about pregnant women and seafood, it's not the only factor contributing to anxiety.

The FDA maintains that its final consumption recommendations were based on thorough scientific analysis. Agency spokesman Cassell says the FDA believes their recommendations will increase confidence, not uncertainty. But critics disagree. They think the FDA's advice is not based on the evidence in its own detailed report, and so it confuses everyone.

items.title: 2026年6月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 2
items.transcript:
I know you're busy with work, but you also need to take some time off to recharge those batteries. So, should you plan one big vacation for the year, or should you take multiple short vacations throughout? Quantity can sometimes beat quality. First and foremost, regardless of how you use your vacation days, you need to be using them, and soon. The longer you put off your time off, the worse you're making things for yourself.

One 9-year-long study published in Psychosomatic Medicine suggests not taking at least one vacation a year may increase your risk of mortality due to heart disease. So, not only are you killing your joy, you're possibly killing yourself. Give yourself a break, folks.

When you should take those breaks, however, depends on a few factors: how many days you have available to use, what activities bring you joy, whether you have a family or not, and other variables come into play. Because of that, there's no perfect formula that works for everyone, but there are still a few things everyone can try to shoot for. We know that in terms of maximizing relaxation, you should aim for vacations that range somewhere between 7 and 11 days long. That gives you enough time to let go of your stress at work, completely loosen up, and achieve full-on calm.

That above-mentioned study also recommends you space out your vacations evenly instead of using up all of your days at once. Eight days might sound like a lot for someone who only gets 10 days of vacation a year. But if you frame them with weekends, you can manage two evenly spaced 8-day vacations a year. If you have 14 days of paid leave, that's almost three separate 8-day vacations you can use to split your year into thirds.

As tempting as it might be to use all your days to take one long summer break, your overall goal should be to achieve the perfect balance between length plus joy and frequency. Vacation frequency is important because planning multiple breaks throughout the year means you always have something to look forward to. Planning things and the anticipation that comes with it tend to make us happier. If you only take one long vacation every year, the excitement builds much more slowly and seems so far off that it can actually lead to feelings of despair.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about people not taking any vacation?

options.text: They will suffer a breakdown soon.
They will be losing both joy and life.
They will be putting themselves and family at risk.
They will make things worse for people around them.

questions.shortExplanation: One 9-year-long study published in Psychosomatic Medicine suggests not taking at least one vacation a year may increase your risk of mortality due to heart disease. So, not only are you killing your joy, you're possibly killing yourself.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） They will be losing both joy and life.

【定位】 One 9-year-long study published in Psychosomatic Medicine suggests not taking at least one vacation a year may increase your risk of mortality due to heart disease. So, not only are you killing your joy, you're possibly killing yourself.

《心理医学》发表的一项长达9年的研究表明，每年至少不休假一次可能会增加死于心脏病的风险。所以，你不仅扼杀了自己的快乐，还可能葬送自己的性命。

【信号】 研究结论 + so 递进。录音先用 One 9-year-long study suggests... 抛出研究结论，再用 So, not only are you killing your joy, you're possibly killing yourself 递进强调后果，其中 not only...but（also）结构把 joy 和 life（killing yourself）并置，正是答案句。

【替换】 not only are you killing your joy, you're possibly killing yourself↔ They will be losing both joy and life

同义替换：killing joy → losing joy；possibly killing yourself → losing life

【排除】 A) 未提及

录音从未出现 breakdown；P1 只说 the worse you're making things for yourself，指 “让自己情况更糟”，并非 suffer a breakdown soon。

C) 偷换概念录音说 increase your risk of mortality due to heart disease 与 killing yourself，风险对象是自己；选项加入 family，把原句中的 risk 曲解为“自己和家人”。 借⽤原⽂： may increase your risk of mortality due to heart disease D) 原词陷阱

录音 the worse you're making things for yourself 说的是“让自己情况更糟”，选项把对象改为 people around them，制造了“影响周围人”的错觉。 借⽤原⽂： the worse you're making things for yourself
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What does the 9-year study recommend people do when planning vacations?

options.text: Spend 14 days for vacation every year.
Aim for three separate vacations yearly.
Space out their vacations evenly instead of taking one long vacation.
Use all their days off for a long summer break to achieve full-on calm.

questions.shortExplanation: That above-mentioned study also recommends you space out your vacations evenly instead of using up all of your days at once. 上述研究还建议你不要把假期一次性用完，而是均匀地分散开来安排。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Space out their vacations evenly instead of taking one long vacation.

【定位】 That above-mentioned study also recommends you space out your vacations evenly instead of using up all of your days at once. 上述研究还建议你不要把假期一次性用完，而是均匀地分散开来安排。

【信号】 recommends + instead of 建议结构。录音中 recommends you space out your vacations evenly instead of using up all of your days at once 直接给出研究建议， recommends 与 instead of 的对照标志答案落点。

【替换】 space out your vacations evenly instead of using up all of your days at once↔ Space out their vacations evenly instead of taking one long vacation 同义改写：space out evenly 直接对应；using up all days at once 转述为 taking one long vacation

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

录音 If you have 14 days of paid leave, that's almost three separate 8-day vacations... 只是假设举例，并非建议“每年必须休14天”。 借⽤原⽂： 14 days of paid leave B) 偷换概念

录音说如果只有14天带薪假“几乎可以分成三次8天假期”，这是基于假设的算法，不是研究对所有人的统一建议。 借⽤原⽂： almost three separate 8-day vacations you can use to split your year into thirds D) 与原文相反

录音 instead of using up all of your days at once 明确否定一次性休完，且 As tempting as it might be to use all your days to take one long summer break 也指出这是 temptation，D 项把它当成建议。 借⽤原⽂： using up all of your days at once
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: Why is vacation frequency important according to the speaker?

options.text: Expecting to have more vacations in a year will boost one's work efficiency.
Anticipating more vacations would reduce one's feelings of despair at work.
Taking more than three vacations yearly would prolong one's excitement.
Planning multiple breaks throughout the year will add to one's happiness.

questions.shortExplanation: Vacation frequency is important because planning multiple breaks throughout the year means you always have something to look forward to. Planning things and the anticipation that comes with it tend to make us happier.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Planning multiple breaks throughout the year will add to one's happiness.

【定位】 Vacation frequency is important because planning multiple breaks throughout the year means you always have something to look forward to. Planning things and the anticipation that comes with it tend to make us happier.

休假频率之所以重要，是因为一年中计划多次休息意味着你总有盼头。计划事情以及随之而来的期待往往会让我们更快乐。

【信号】 because 直接解释原因 + 评价词 happier。录音先以 Vacation frequency is important because planning multiple breaks throughout the year means you always have something to look forward to 点明因果，再用 the anticipation that comes with it tend to make us happier 给出积极评价，because 后内容即答案。

【替换】 planning multiple breaks throughout the year means you always have something to look forward to ↔ Planning multiple breaks throughout the year will add to one's happiness

同义改写：planning multiple breaks throughout the year 原样对应；have something to look forward to + make us happier → add to one's happiness the anticipation that comes with it tend to make us happier ↔ Planning multiple breaks throughout the year will add to one's happiness 同义改写：anticipation/tend to make us happier 对应 add to one's happiness

【排除】 A) 未提及录音讨论的是期待、快乐、despair，从未提到工作效率，属于无中生有。

B) 偷换概念

录音说如果一年只休一次长假，兴奋感太远才会 lead to feelings of despair；选项把“减少绝望”说成是期待更多休假的好处，但原文只用它衬托多次休假的好处，且对象也有偏差。 借⽤原⽂： it can actually lead to feelings of despair C) 过度推断

录音未说“超过三次”能延长兴奋；P4 的 three separate vacations 只是 14 天假期的算法举例，P5 的 excitement builds much more slowly 是批评一年一次，不是支持三次以上。 借⽤原⽂： three separate 8-day vacations you can use to split your year into thirds

items.title: 2026年6月六级第1套 · 讲座与讲话 3
items.transcript:
Autonomous cars that can take over from drivers if they are tired or caught in the heat of an argument are being developed in Sweden. Researchers working as part of the European Union's €77 billion research program are developing sensor-based systems that monitor whether a driver is distracted, anxious or tired. If a driver is not in a fit state to be on the road, the car automatically takes control of the wheel to prevent accidents. Doctor Anna Anund from the Swedish National Road and Transport Research Institute, who is leading the project, said a driver's state can be measured using a number of sensors, including heart rate monitors and eye sensors, which track where a driver's gaze is. She said the aim was to really make sure that the transition from the driver to the vehicle is done in a safe way, so we can take into consideration the driver's state, and so we do not give control to a driver who is under pressure of fatigue, stress, anxiety, and so on.

According to data from the European Commission, Sweden has the safest roads in the EU, with the UK a close second. However, the number of road accidents in both has largely levelled out since 2010. Driver fatigue is thought to be responsible for as many as a fifth of road crashes across the EU, although there are certain times of the day when more accidents happen. At 6:00 a.m., for example, drivers are said to be 20 times more likely to have an accident than at 10:00 a.m. While most experts agree driverless technology should help bring down accident numbers in the long term, some have questioned whether it is safe.

The researchers have said the technology they are developing is seeking to bridge the gap between Level 3 on the autonomy scale, in which drivers have to be ready to take control of the car at any point, and Level 4, in which driving is automated.

Daniel Ruiz, the chief executive of the UK's connected and autonomous vehicle programme Meridian, said: "there is a strong debate going on about how it is possible to make a Level 3 car completely safe." Despite advances in technology, we still have some way to go in shifting public sentiment. With an increase in attention-grabbing accidents recently, drivers now view self-driving cars as less safe than they used to.

questions.prompt: What are researchers doing in Sweden?

options.text: Surveying when drivers are caught in the heat of arguments.
Designing devices to prevent drivers from being distracted.
Testing models for monitoring drivers easily getting tired.
Developing sensor-based systems for autonomous vehicles.

questions.shortExplanation: Researchers working as part of the European Union's €77 billion research program are developing sensor-based systems that monitor whether a driver is distracted, anxious or tired. 作为欧盟 770 亿欧元研究项目的一部分，研究人员正在开发传感系统，用以监测驾驶员是否分心、焦虑或疲劳。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题） Developing sensor-based systems for autonomous vehicles.

【定位】 Researchers working as part of the European Union's €77 billion research program are developing sensor-based systems that monitor whether a driver is distracted, anxious or tired. 作为欧盟 770 亿欧元研究项目的一部分，研究人员正在开发传感系统，用以监测驾驶员是否分心、焦虑或疲劳。

【信号】 题干关键词原词复现+直接动作句。题干中的 researchers 与 doing 在 Researchers working as part of the European Union's €77 billion research program are developing sensor-based systems 中原词出现，developing 直接回答“做什么”，因此该句即为答案句。

【替换】 developing sensor-based systems that monitor whether a driver is distracted, anxious or tired↔ Developing sensor-based systems for autonomous vehicles. 核心动宾原词复现+目的同义

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

选项 Surveying when drivers are caught in the heat of arguments. 中的 caught in the heat of arguments 在 caught in the heat of an argument 中确实出现，但原文是说自动驾驶汽车在驾驶员情绪激动时接管，而非 researchers 在 survey/调查，动作被换。 借⽤原⽂： caught in the heat of an argument

B) 偷换概念选项 Designing devices to prevent drivers from being distracted. 用了原文 distracted 和 prevent accidents 两个词，但原文传感器是监测 distraction 并防止事故，不是 design devices 专门 prevent distraction。 借⽤原⽂： distracted C) 原词陷阱

选项 Testing models for monitoring drivers easily getting tired. 用了 tired，但原文是 developing sensor-based systems，不是 testing models；monitoring 是系统功能，不是测试模型。 借⽤原⽂： tired
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What did the researchers' project aim to do according to Dr. Anna Anund?

options.text: Make sure the autonomous vehicle operates in the simplest manner.
Ensure the transition from the driver to the vehicle is safely made.
Alleviate the driver's pressure as much as possible.
Record the driver's state as accurately as possible.

questions.shortExplanation: She said the aim was to really make sure that the transition from the driver to the vehicle is done in a safe way, so we can take into consideration the driver's state, and so we do not give control to a driver who is under pressure of fatigue, stress, anxiety, and so on. 她说，项目的目标是真正确保从驾驶员到车辆的接管过程以安全方式完成，从而把驾驶员状态纳入考量，避免把控制权交给处于疲劳、压力、焦虑等状态下的驾驶员。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （目的题） Ensure the transition from the driver to the vehicle is safely made.

【定位】 She said the aim was to really make sure that the transition from the driver to the vehicle is done in a safe way, so we can take into consideration the driver's state, and so we do not give control to a driver who is under pressure of fatigue, stress, anxiety, and so on. 她说，项目的目标是真正确保从驾驶员到车辆的接管过程以安全方式完成，从而把驾驶员状态纳入考量，避免把控制权交给处于疲劳、压力、焦虑等状态下的驾驶员。

【信号】 the aim was to 目的信号+make sure 强调。the aim was to really make sure that the transition from the driver to the vehicle is done in a safe way 中，the aim was to 直接对应题干 aim，make sure 强调目标，其后内容即为答案。

【替换】 the transition from the driver to the vehicle is done in a safe way↔ Ensure the transition from the driver to the vehicle is safely made.

同义改写+主被动转换

【排除】 A) 未提及

选项 Make sure the autonomous vehicle operates in the simplest manner. 中的 simplest 在原文未出现，且把 “safe” 偷换为 “simplest”。 C) 偷换概念

选项 Alleviate the driver's pressure as much as possible. 盗用 under pressure of fatigue, stress, anxiety, and so on，但原文是说不要把车交给有压力的驾驶员，而不是以 “减轻压力”为项目目的。 借⽤原⽂： under pressure of fatigue, stress, anxiety, and so on

D) 答非所问

选项 Record the driver's state as accurately as possible. 对应 a driver's state can be measured using a number of sensors, including heart rate monitors and eye sensors, which track where a driver's gaze is，但 measuring the state 是实现安全接管的手段，不是项目 aim。 借⽤原⽂： a driver's state can be measured using a number of sensors, including heart rate monitors and eye sensors, which track where a driver's gaze is
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: What is thought to be responsible for a fifth of road accidents across the European Union?

options.text: Driver fatigue.
Dreadful traffic.
Drunk driving.
Driving time.

questions.shortExplanation: Driver fatigue is thought to be responsible for as many as a fifth of road crashes across the EU, although there are certain times of the day when more accidents happen.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Driver fatigue.

【定位】 Driver fatigue is thought to be responsible for as many as a fifth of road crashes across the EU, although there are certain times of the day when more accidents happen.

据认为，驾驶员疲劳导致了欧盟多达五分之一的道路撞车事故，尽管一天中某些时段事故更多。

【信号】 题干关键词原词复现+主语即答案。responsible for as many as a fifth of road crashes across the EU 与题干 responsible for a fifth of road accidents across the European Union 几乎原词对应，其主语 Driver fatigue 就是答案。

【替换】 Driver fatigue is thought to be responsible for as many as a fifth of road crashes across the EU↔ Driver fatigue.

主语直接对应，其余为题干已知信息

【排除】 B) 未提及

选项 Dreadful traffic. 是交通事故的常见原因，但录音原文从未出现 traffic 相关表述。

C) 未提及选项 Drunk driving. 同样是常见事故原因，但原文没有 drunk/drinking/alcohol 等信息。

D) 偷换概念

选项 Driving time. 对应 there are certain times of the day when more accidents happen，但原文只说某些时段事故更多，并未把 driving time 当作 responsible for a fifth of accidents 的原因。 借⽤原⽂： there are certain times of the day when more accidents happen

questions.prompt: Why do drivers now view self-driving cars as less safe than they used to?

options.text: There has been a strong debate on the feasibility of Level 3 cars.
There have been few remarkable advances in auto technology.
There has been a rise in attention-grabbing accidents recently.
There have been few feasible ways to shift public sentiment.

questions.shortExplanation: With an increase in attention-grabbing accidents recently, drivers now view self-driving cars as less safe than they used to.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） There has been a rise in attention-grabbing accidents recently.

【定位】 With an increase in attention-grabbing accidents recently, drivers now view self-driving cars as less safe than they used to.

随着近期引人注目的交通事故增多，驾驶员现在认为自动驾驶汽车不如以前安全。

【信号】 With 引导原因状语，直接解释结果。With an increase in attention-grabbing accidents recently 位于结果句 “drivers now view self-driving cars as less safe than they used to” 之前，with 短语说明原因。

【替换】 an increase in attention-grabbing accidents recently↔ There has been a rise in attention-grabbing accidents recently.

同义替换：increase→rise

【排除】 A) 答非所问

选项 There has been a strong debate on the feasibility of Level 3 cars. 对应 there is a strong debate going on about how it is possible to make a Level 3 car completely safe.，但这是在讨论技术可行性，不是 drivers 觉得更不安全的原因。 借⽤原⽂： there is a strong debate going on about how it is possible to make a Level 3 car completely safe. B) 与原文相反

选项 There have been few remarkable advances in auto technology. 与 Despite advances in technology 相反，原文明确说技术有进步。 借⽤原⽂： Despite advances in technology D) 偷换概念

选项 There have been few feasible ways to shift public sentiment. 盗用 shifting public sentiment，但原文是说我们在转变公众情绪方面还有路要走，并非说缺乏可行方法，也不是驾驶员态度变化的原因。 借⽤原⽂： we still have some way to go in shifting public sentiment.

items.title: 2026年6月六级第2套 · 长对话 1
items.transcript:
W: Hi, Frank, are you working through your lunch hour again?

M: No, not at all. It's my 10th wedding anniversary next week, and I promised Jane that I would book a city break for us, as I have annual leave to take, and it would be nice to celebrate somewhere warm. So, I'm trying to book something in Barcelona.

W: That sounds so romantic. I adore Barcelona. It's such a fabulous cosmopolitan city. There's so much to do there, excellent food, and that cathedral that they are still building after about 150 years. Very cool.

M: I know. But the anniversary is looming, and I'm still scrambling to find accommodation. Everything is either wildly expensive or already fully booked. I'm starting to feel a bit frantic.

W: Well, if you are going for a whole week, why don't you do a couple of nights in somewhere really glamorous, and then do the rest of the week a bit further up the coast, where the accommodation is cheaper, and that will offset the cost of the expensive place?

M: That might be a good plan. It's not too expensive to rent a car, so we could still drive into the city. Yes, there are lots of places outside the city that have pools and are all inclusive, so we wouldn't even need to pay for food or drinks. I'll send a query now about the dates we're interested in.

W: That sounds perfect. I'm sure that Jane will be absolutely thrilled to bits. I really do recommend visiting that cathedral. You can go all the way up to the top of it, but you need to go up a really steep spiral staircase to get there.

M: Considering Jane is terrified of heights, I think if I tried to make her do that, I would come back divorced. Thanks for the help though; it was turning into a logistical nightmare.

questions.prompt: What is the man planning to do?

options.text: Celebrate his 10th wedding anniversary.
Celebrate his promotion in Barcelona.
Give his wife a pleasant surprise.
Ask for leave to visit Barcelona.

questions.shortExplanation: It's my 10th wedding anniversary next week, and I promised Jane that I would book a city break for us, as I have annual leave to take, and it would be nice to celebrate somewhere warm.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Celebrate his 10th wedding anniversary.

【定位】 It's my 10th wedding anniversary next week, and I promised Jane that I would book a city break for us, as I have annual leave to take, and it would be nice to celebrate somewhere warm.

下周是我结婚十周年纪念日，我答应 Jane 会给我们订一次城市短途旅行，因为我有年假要休，而且去个暖和的地方庆祝会很好。

【信号】 承诺句+原因铺陈。男士用 I promised Jane that I would book a city break for us 直接说明自己的计划，后面 as 引出原因；这是典型的'被问者应答'，直接承载答案。

【替换】 It's my 10th wedding anniversary next week↔ Celebrate his 10th wedding anniversary. 事件同义概括 I promised Jane that I would book a city break for us↔Celebrate his 10th wedding anniversary.

计划句→事件目的

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

Celebrate his promotion in Barcelona. 盗用了原文 in Barcelona，但录音说的是去 Barcelona 庆祝周年纪念，而非庆祝升职，promotion 未提及。 借⽤原⽂： in Barcelona C) 过度推断

Give his wife a pleasant surprise. 把原文 I promised Jane 的浪漫氛围曲解为 surprise， 录音中男士是答应订旅行，并未说是惊喜。 D) 原词陷阱

Ask for leave to visit Barcelona. 盗用原文 as I have annual leave to take，但录音说'有年假要休'，并非'申请请假'，动作被偷换。 借⽤原⽂： as I have annual leave to take
questions.hint: 回听对应对话或篇章，留意题干关键词、转折和同义表达。

questions.prompt: Why is the man starting to feel a bit frantic?

options.text: He is unable to find some inexpensive accommodation.
There are few warm places to go at this time of the year.
There is so much for him to do before going on vacation.
He is afraid Barcelona may not be so fabulous as expected.

questions.shortExplanation: But the anniversary is looming, and I'm still scrambling to find accommodation. Everything is either wildly expensive or already fully booked. I'm starting to feel a bit frantic. 但纪念日越来越近，我还在拼命找住宿。要么贵得离谱，要么已经订满。我开始有点慌了。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） He is unable to find some inexpensive accommodation.

【定位】 But the anniversary is looming, and I'm still scrambling to find accommodation. Everything is either wildly expensive or already fully booked. I'm starting to feel a bit frantic. 但纪念日越来越近，我还在拼命找住宿。要么贵得离谱，要么已经订满。我开始有点慌了。

【信号】 问题铺陈+情绪词。I'm still scrambling to find accommodation 点明困难，Everything is either wildly expensive or already fully booked 具体说明，I'm starting to feel a bit frantic 直接回应题干情绪。

【替换】 I'm still scrambling to find accommodation ↔ He is unable to find some inexpensive accommodation. 动作+结果同义改写 Everything is either wildly expensive or already fully booked ↔ He is unable to find some inexpensive accommodation.

反向同义替换

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 There are few warm places to go at this time of the year. 盗用原文 somewhere warm，但原文说想找个暖和地方庆祝，没说暖和地方少，属原词陷阱。 借⽤原⽂： somewhere warm C) 过度推断

There is so much for him to do before going on vacation. 把找住宿的困难扩大为'很多事要做'，录音未提及其他事务，属过度推断。

D) 与原文相反

W: Hey there, Paul. How's it going?

M: Hi, Suzanne. Just keeping busy with the usual stuff, filling prescriptions, talking to patients about their medications, that kind of thing. How about you?

W: Same here, although I did have an interesting case come in this morning. A patient came in, inquiring about a medication that had a potential interaction with another medication she was already taking.

M: Oh, that's always tricky. What did you do?

W: I explained the issue to her as best I could, and recommended she double-check with her doctor. And you know what? She actually followed my advice, and the doctor ended up switching the patient's medication.

M: Ah, that's great. You must feel quite accomplished.

W: Totally. These moments are the highlights of my routine work, employing my pharmaceutical expertise to the benefit of people's health and well-being.

M: I fully agree. Unfortunately, the opposite is true when the patient is too stubborn and they refuse to listen to us.

W: So true. In other developments, we've had a lot of people coming in to get their flu shots, which is always good to see.

M: Good, good. I've been working on a new medication therapy management program for our patients with chronic conditions. It helps patients manage their medications more effectively.

W: That sounds interesting.

M: We review all of their medications, and make sure that they're taking them as prescribed. We also look for any potential drug interactions or side effects. Patient response has so far been very positive. Some have reported seeing improvements in their health, which is really rewarding to see.

W: That's great to hear. Do you use text message reminders?

M: Yes, absolutely.

W: It's a great idea. Medication non-adherence is a big problem, especially for older patients.

M: We're still in the early stages of the program, but I'm hopeful that it will make a real difference for our patients.

items.title: 2026年6月六级第2套 · 听力篇章 1
items.transcript:
In America, at least, passion is a word that often comes up on job descriptions and in interviews. On the whole, passionate people are thought of in a positive light and considered likely to achieve their goals. But when it comes to predicting achievement, has the importance of passion been overstated?

According to a new study from Stanford University, passion may be less important in certain cultures, and the fact that passion is often seen as a key to achievement may reflect a distinctly Western model of motivation. The chief factor explored in the study was how individualistic a society was. In individualistic cultures, the researchers assert, people are more motivated by pursuing paths related to their passions, but those in collectivistic cultures are more likely to see themselves as part of a network. They often place fulfilling obligations to others above focusing on their own interests.

The researchers looked at data from nearly 60 countries. They found that in science subjects, passion was positively correlated with academic achievements. Higher levels of enjoyment and interest also bolstered test scores.

But the strength of this correlation wasn't the same across cultures. Those in individualistic societies such as the U.S., Australia, and the UK showed a stronger link between passion and achievement. The effect of passion on performance was more subtle for those in more collectivistic societies such as Colombia or Thailand.

These findings were mirrored in achievement in both mathematics and reading. It's clear from the findings that passion isn't the only thing that motivates people to achieve their goals.

View things positively.

Dominate job interviews.

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题） Accomplish their goals.

【定位】 On the whole, passionate people are thought of in a positive light and considered likely to achieve their goals.

总体而言，有热情的人被认为形象正面，且被认为很可能实现他们的目标。

【信号】 直接描述句。passionate people are thought of in a positive light and considered likely to achieve their goals是对passionate people的直接定义式描述，题干中的 『considered likely to』几乎原文复现了该句结构。

【替换】 achieve their goals ↔ Accomplish their goals.

同义词替换

【排除】 B) 原词陷阱

录音确实提到positive light，但题干问的是『considered likely to do』（做什么），不是 『被认为怎么样』（态度如何）；选项B把positive换个说法变成positively，看似用了原词，实则答非所问。 借⽤原⽂： passionate people are thought of in a positive light C) 偷换概念

录音末尾有has the importance of passion been overstated?，但这是作者抛出的质疑问题，并非passionate people『夸大自己的重要性』；选项C把『热情的重要性被高估』偷换成『他们夸大自己的重要性』，主语和对象都错了。 借⽤原⽂： has the importance of passion been overstated? D) 原词陷阱录音开头提到in interviews，但只说明passion这个词常在面试中出现，并未说passionate people『主导面试』；『dominate』是无中生有，利用『job interviews』这个原词制造 『听到就选』的诱惑。 借⽤原⽂： in job descriptions and in interviews

items.transcript:
Why does nature create patterns? The reason patterns often appear in nature is simple: the same basic physical or chemical processes occur in many pattern substances and organisms as they form. Whether in plants and animals or rocks, foams and ice crystals, the intricate patterns that happen in nature come down to what's happening at the level of atoms and molecules.

A pattern in nature is any regularly repeated arrangement of shapes or colors. Some of the most striking examples include the six-sided arrays of rocks at Giant's Causeway in the United Kingdom, and the colorful stripes and spots on tropical fish. Patterns like these begin to form at a small scale when materials undergo processes like drying, freezing, wrinkling, diffusing and reacting. Those changes then give rise to complex patterns at a larger scale that people can see.

Imagine delicate frozen crystals on a window during winter. What creates that pattern? When water freezes, its molecules begin clustering together. Water molecules have a particular bent shape that causes them to stack into clusters as they freeze. As the cluster grows, many outside factors, including humidity and temperature, begin to affect its overall shape. If the water is freezing on a window, for example, random imperfections on the glass surface affect the stacking and create the larger pattern.

But scientists do not always know the purpose of a pattern, or even if there is one. The molecular processes involved are simple enough that they might generate a pattern by coincidence.

items.title: 2026年6月六级第2套 · 讲座与讲话 1
items.transcript:
Many people, myself included, have multiple areas of life they would like to improve. For example, I would like to reach more people with my writing, to lift heavier weights at the gym, and to start practising mindfulness more consistently. Those are just a few of the goals I find desirable, and you probably have a long list yourself. The problem is, even if we are committed to working hard on our goals, our natural tendency is to return to our old habits at some point. Making a permanent lifestyle change is really difficult.

Recently I've come across a few studies that will make these difficult lifestyle changes a bit easier. As you'll see, however, the approach to mastering many areas of life is somewhat counterintuitive. Research has shown that you are two to three times more likely to stick with your habits if you make a specific plan for when, where, and how you will perform the behavior. For example, in one study, scientists asked people to fill out a sentence to specify during the next week they would do at least 20 minutes of vigorous exercise on which day, at what time of day, and at or in what place. Researchers found that people who filled out this sentence were two to three times more likely to actually exercise compared to a control group who did not make plans for their future behavior. Psychologists call these specific plans implementation intentions because they state when, where, and how you intend to implement a particular behavior.

However, follow-up research has discovered implementation intentions only work when you focus on one thing at a time. In fact, researchers found that people who tried to accomplish multiple goals were less committed and less likely to succeed than those who focused on a single goal.

Another science-based reason to focus on one thing at a time is that when you begin practising a new habit, it requires a lot of conscious effort to remember to do it. After a while, however, the pattern of behavior becomes easier. Eventually, your new habit becomes a normal routine, and the process is more or less mindless and automatic. The most important thing to note is that there is some tipping point at which new habits become more or less automatic. The time it takes to build a habit depends on many factors, including how difficult the habit is, your genetics, and more.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say is really difficult?

问题是，即使我们致力于努力实现目标，我们的自然倾向还是在某个时刻回到旧习惯。永久改变生活方式真的很难。

【信号】 题眼词复现 + 总结句。题干中的 difficult 在 Making a permanent lifestyle change is really difficult 中直接复现；这是段落末尾的总结句，前面用 The problem is 铺垫，信息落点在 really difficult 上。

【替换】 Making a permanent lifestyle change is really difficult↔Making a permanent lifestyle change 同义复现

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

Realizing all the life goals one has set 把 working hard on our goals 和 the goals I find desirable 改成“实现所有既定目标”，但原文只说“努力追求目标”，并未说实现所有目标，all 也过于绝对。 借⽤原⽂： the goals I find desirable

items.title: 2026年6月六级第2套 · 讲座与讲话 2
items.transcript:
It was a lazy, hazy, crazy day on the dwarf planet Pluto when New Horizons, a spacecraft from Earth, flew by at a speed of 31,000 mph (miles per hour) two years ago. The spacecraft took a bunch of photos, made some quick measurements of Pluto's atmosphere, and sent them all back here, giving planetary scientists their first up-close look of the distant dwarf planet.

One of the more bizarre things they found was that the haze in Pluto's atmosphere was much thicker than previously thought. The planet also had an atmosphere much cooler than earlier estimates, topping out at −333.4°F.

Now, a study published in Nature links those two atmospheric observations. A computer model developed by planetary scientist Xi Zhang and colleagues shows the haze of tiny droplets in the upper atmosphere is likely scattering light from the Sun, preventing heat from reaching the planet below. We see hazy skies on Earth too, from time to time, whenever solid particles get suspended in the air—from water-based fogs, to ash from fires, to the toxic droplets that make up a thick smog. But on Earth, the overall temperature of the planet is dominated by the distribution of gases in our atmosphere.

On Pluto, the authors suggest, haze might be more influential. Particles can reflect light from the Sun here on Earth: It happens after volcanoes erupt, emitting clouds of particles that reflect the Sun's rays into the atmosphere. Some people even propose imitating this phenomenon to alleviate the effects of climate change. But our planet isn't dominated by that process, or at least it hasn't been for a few billion years.

If Pluto's atmosphere is very different from ours and from that of other nearby planets, it could help scientists expand their understanding of planetary atmospheres. But right now, this is just a good guess based on data from New Horizons and a sophisticated computer model, not direct observations of the haze's composition.

There are other theories floating around to explain Pluto's cool temperatures, including blaming the cold air on gases in the atmosphere.

Luckily, the authors will get a chance to test their notions when the James Webb Space Telescope launches later. That observatory can detect different spectrums of light, which the hazy Plutonian atmosphere would be positively glowing with as it scattered sunlight. The researchers just have to wait and see if the light from the telescope validates their bright idea.

B 项说‘如果冥王星的霾层能被更容易观测’，但录音并未讨论观测难度是否 easier；原文只提到未来有机会用 James Webb 验证，没有 easier 这一比较。

items.title: 2026年6月六级第2套 · 讲座与讲话 3
items.transcript:
Parents have a small window where they can influence their 8- to 10-year-old children's music taste, researchers have concluded. The 24-month time frame comes at an age when youngsters are old enough to appreciate poetic lyrics and snappy tunes, but have not yet started to be embarrassed by their mother and father's preferences. Dr. Hauke Egermann, a lecturer in music at the University of York, carried out a literature review into more than a dozen studies looking at parental musical influence. "Children have an openness to new music, and this means parents have an important role to play in developing the musical preferences of their kids," he said.

However, time is of the essence as parental influence is most likely to be effective during the critical time period before age ten. During adolescence, children tend to gravitate away from their parents' choices and are more influenced by their peers. A separate survey of 2,000 British parents by music streaming service Deezer also found that nearly four-fifths of parents agreed that their children were far more receptive to their musical suggestions before the age of ten. In contrast, just 10 percent of parents reported positive reactions from their teenage children when they shared their favorite music. Some 79 percent of fathers said they had tried to influence their children's music, but just 69 percent of mothers. However, mothers were more effective, with 38 percent reporting that their kids loved the tunes they shared, compared to 30 percent of dads who, in some cases, said their children cried or even fell asleep.

Dr. Egermann claims introducing children to a variety of musical styles is the key to fostering good taste in later life. "By playing children a variety of genres before this critical period, research on familiarization suggests they will enjoy lots of different types of music as adults," he added. The benefits of having a wider taste in music include the ability to manage their emotions more effectively, socialize and bond with others more easily, and to have a better understanding of other cultures as well.

Dr. Egermann advises parents not to push their favorite music too hard on their children, but instead play it as background music while a child is playing. They can also help create positive memories about artists and bands by going to concerts and live music events together.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from researchers' conclusion at the beginning of the talk?

options.text: Parents can play a decisive role in cultivating their children's musical talent.
Children are embarrassed by parents' failure to appreciate their music.
Parents can mould their 8- to 10-year-old children's music taste.
Children aged 8 to 10 are old enough to produce poetic lyrics.

questions.shortExplanation: Parents have a small window where they can influence their 8- to 10-year-old children's music taste, researchers have concluded. 研究人员得出结论：父母有一个短暂的窗口期，可以影响8到10岁孩子的音乐品味。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题） Parents can mould their 8- to 10-year-old children's music taste.

【定位】 Parents have a small window where they can influence their 8- to 10-year-old children's music taste, researchers have concluded. 研究人员得出结论：父母有一个短暂的窗口期，可以影响8到10岁孩子的音乐品味。

【信号】 研究结论标志词。答案句以researchers have concluded结尾，是典型的研究结论标志；同时句首直接给出结论内容，符合篇章开头'先给结论'的常见结构。

【替换】 influence their 8- to 10-year-old children's music taste↔ mould their 8- to 10-year-old children's music taste influence与mould同义替换 Parents have a small window where they can ↔ Parents can small window限定为可能性

【排除】 A) 原词陷阱

选项中的musical talent在原文中从未出现，原文讲的是music taste；同时decisive role把原文a small window夸大成'决定性作用'，与原文程度不符。 借⽤原⽂： Parents have a small window where they can influence their 8- to 10-year-old children's music taste

B) 原词陷阱

原文have not yet started to be embarrassed by their mother and father's preferences说的是'还不会因父母的偏好感到尴尬'，而选项说成'Children are embarrassed by parents' failure to appreciate their music'，既把对象从'父母的偏好'偷换成'父母不欣赏孩子的音乐'，又把否定'not yet'变成了肯定。 借⽤原⽂： have not yet started to be embarrassed by their mother and father's preferences D) 原词陷阱

原文old enough to appreciate poetic lyrics说的是'足够大去欣赏富有诗意的歌词'，选项却改成'produce poetic lyrics'，把appreciate偷换成produce，动作主体和方向都错了。 借⽤原⽂： old enough to appreciate poetic lyrics

questions.prompt: What does Dr. Hauke Egermann say about adolescents?

options.text: They start to show their own musical preference.
They tend to be more influenced by their peers.
They tend to gravitate away from their homes.
They are more open to new genres of music.

questions.shortExplanation: During adolescence, children tend to gravitate away from their parents' choices and are more influenced by their peers. 在青春期，孩子们往往会偏离父母的选择，更受同龄人的影响。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题） They tend to be more influenced by their peers.

【信号】 题干关键词复现+比较级。原文During adolescence与题干adolescents直接对应，句中 more influenced by their peers用比较级点明影响来源的变化，是答案信号。

【替换】 During adolescence ↔ adolescents

名词化同义 are more influenced by their peers ↔ tend to be more influenced by their peers be动词添加趋向性

【排除】 A) 未提及

原文说的是孩子'偏离父母的选择'，并未说他们开始展示自己的musical preference；选项把'父母的选择'偷换成'自己的偏好'，属于无中生有。

C) 原词陷阱

选项盗用了原文gravitate away from这一短语，但把对象从their parents' choices偷换成 their homes，语义完全改变。 借⽤原⽂： gravitate away from their parents' choices D) 张冠李戴

原文Children have an openness to new music说的是儿童（8-10岁）对新音乐的开放态度，选项把它安到adolescents头上，属于群体错位。 借⽤原⽂： Children have an openness to new music

埃格曼博士称，让孩子接触多种多样的音乐风格是培养其日后良好品味的关键。

【信号】 专家观点+the key to结构。原文Dr. Egermann claims是专家观点标志，紧接着出现is the key to fostering good taste in later life，与题干中的the key to fostering good taste in later life完全对应。
